Cardinals Defend Decision to Sit Jeremiyah Love in Final Moments
full_text:
ARIZONA — With the game on the line, the Arizona Cardinals ' heftiest offseason investment was nowhere to be found.
The Cardinals' 36-24 loss to the New York Giants came down to the wire, with Jacoby Brissett and the team's offense being stonewalled near the goal line in the final moments of Week 4 action at MetLife Stadium.
The Cardinals, down 30-24, had first-and-goal at the Giants' four-yard line with 22 seconds left and one timeout. Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love — previously rushing for 63 yards on 14 carries (4.5 YPC) — was on the sidelines as Arizona opted for veteran running back Tyler Allgeier, who was on the field while Brissett threw three consecutive incompletions before a game-sealing pick-six.
There've been several talks of the town, but Love's absence on the biggest string of plays dominated social media following the game. Perhaps rightly so, as one of the Cardinals' more dynamic players was sidelined in crunch time.
This is what LaFleur had to say postgame:
"Well, we're just in our two-minute situation right there, so in our pass emphasis, it's obviously Tyler (Allgeier) being kind of that 'third-down back,' if you will. So they're heating us up pretty good. From that standpoint, it's more his role. Jeremiyah can obviously be out there and do it, but you want to segment, I guess you could say, a little bit. It wasn't like we were going to be using our back in the pass game, if you will. So it's more of a protection emphasis."
Arizona's first play was a play-action pass that fell incomplete to Michael Wilson. LaFleur says the Cardinals' second play was initially a run before it was checked to a pass, which also fell incomplete to  Wilson.
"Yeah, the second-down one was a run play. We just had a run alert with it because they went all out. So we could have ran it, but literally they would have gone all out, so it would have been a situation where you'd be praying that it worked, not just running it to run it," LaFleur said.
"That was the thought process on the second down. Again, you thought they probably would all out it, so we had the kind of the out route to Mike (wide receiver Michael Wilson) there that we feel good about."
A third-down incompletion to Trey McBride was followed by Brissett's third interception of the day, which was returned for a touchdown as time expired.
Arizona's performance in the red zone had been an underlying narrative around the Cardinals to start the season, as the offense has settled for field goals too much for their liking as opposed to punching it in for six.
Most believe Love's ability as a pass-catcher would have been beneficial to have on Arizona's final drive, as he's a better route-runner than Allgeier and could get open easier if the Giants indeed were wanting to send pressure like they were.
The rookie running back was spotted getting his ankle worked on during the game. It's noteworthy Love missed multiple weeks of the preseason with a high ankle sprain while he went down during the open portion of practice last week.
"I’ll have to see. I haven't talked to him yet in terms of that, but I know that they just kept saying he'll be up. So, we'll look at it a little bit more tomorrow, obviously," LaFleur said.

title: 3 Advanced Stats Reveal the Real Story of Cardinals' Week 4 Loss
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals suffered another frustrating loss in Week 4, falling to the New York Giants 36-24 at MetLife Stadium. After taking control early (14-3 lead), Arizona struggled to sustain its momentum and was held to just seven points in the second half.
"There is no script for this one," head coach Mike LaFleur said postgame.
"No loss is fun, all three losses that we've had over the last three weeks have been different. This one is going to sting."
Here are a few stats that stand out.
The New York Giants blitzed the Arizona Cardinals 53.8% of the time in Week 4. This was the highest blitz rate by a Giants defense since the start of the last season, per Next Gen Stats.
Against the blitz, Jacoby Brissett completed 6-of-18 passes for 55 yards. Overall, Brissett was pressured on more than half of his dropbacks Sunday (52.4%).
"They were heating us up pretty good," LaFleur said. "I'm going to put it on me in terms of having the right play design to get these guys open where we can play pitch and catch a little bit easier."
Arizona has struggled to limit explosive pass plays this season. Unfortunately, things did not improve against the Giants, as the Cardinals allowed five receptions of 20+ yards.
Malik Nabers, who was selected two picks after Marvin Harrison Jr. in the 2024 NFL Draft, was responsible for three of the five explosive pass plays (39,28,25).
Through four games, the Cardinals have allowed 14 passes of at least 20+ yards.
"We want explosives, and we want to limit explosives," coach LaFleur said postgame. "I got to look at the tape and see where some of the breakdowns occurred. We'll get it fixed and get it fixed fast."
The Cardinals' ground game was rolling early. After the first quarter, Arizona's running backs produced 81 yards on nine carries (9.0 YPC). To counter the rushing attack, the Giants decided to stack the box. Per Next Gen Stats, New York loaded the box with 8+ defenders 46.2% of the time. This was the third-highest stacked box percentage in Week 4 (Pending MNF).
"They just started loading it up. You could tell they had to talk about just playing a little bit harder," Mike LaFleur told J.P. Shadrick and A.Q. Shipley on the Cardinals Locker Room Show. "They loaded up, and when they do that, we obviously got to take advantage of it. And we just didn't."
Coach LaFleur believes there were "opportunities in the pass game" because there were so many defenders in the box.
"Obviously, I have to do a better job of putting these guys in positions to be successful to be able to attack that pressure in man (coverage) that they were giving us."

title: Cardinals Report Card: Grading Every Position After Week 4 Loss
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals are 1-3 after a frustrating loss in Week 4.
It was another matchup where the Cardinals had an opportunity to win in crunch time before falling flat.
Let's grade every position group A-F using C as an average:
We'll start with the good: Brissett tossed two touchdown passes and his trio of interceptions — to varying extents — weren't all on him. He was able to march the Cardinals down the field and put them in position to win the game.
With that said, the Cardinals didn't win the game, and Brissett's 55.2 passer rating was the worst he's had in years. Granted he's not exactly afforded time thanks to his offensive line, but Brissett's performance today wasn't anywhere close to a passing grade.
The Cardinals aren't making a quarterback change for Week 5, but if Brissett doesn't turn the tide quickly, it could be coming sooner rather than later.
The only thing holding this group back was not winning, which could have been the case had Arizona opted to hand the ball off on any of their four final plays when they were near the goal line.
The Cardinals' running back duo of Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier performed about as good as you could have asked, rushing for 105 yards on 22 carries (4.7 YPC) and a touchdown. Arizona got off to a 14-3 lead and for some reason abandoned the run until later in action.
When they did lean on the ground, both rushers performed extremely well. This will be one of the bigger regrets when Mike LaFleur reflects back on the game.
The Cardinals' array of pass-catchers by no means had a bad day. Marvin Harrison Jr. found the end zone for the first time this season while Arizona also had a surprise score from TE2 Elijah Higgins. Michael Wilson finished with 95 yards on seven receptions, too.
Yet none of the Cardinals' pass-catchers were able to make a play when the game was on the line, failing to either come down with tough receptions or create separation in any of Arizona's last four targeted passers (Harrison and Trey McBride were respectively open but that's a topic for another article).
McBride was limited to a mere checkdown option for Brissett (31 yards on seven catches). Harrison went quiet after his touchdown reception and Wilson had his number called twice in the final moments. The unit performed mostly well — they just couldn't find a way at the end.
Arizona's rushing attack looked pleasant early thanks to the holes paved by the Cardinals' offensive line. Yet that momentum went away, quickly, and the Cardinals were forced to deal with a heavy pass approach the rest of the way.
As a result, Brissett was blitzed on nearly 54% of his dropbacks with a pressure rate of 38.5%. Brissett was only officially sacked twice, but his 2.52 average seconds to throw time was among the fastest in the NFL this week.
As we established in our studs and duds , the right side of the offensive line particularly is a problem with Isaiah Adams and Elijah Wilkinson. Brissett wasn't running for his life every single play, though you would have liked to see much more from Arizona's unit.
A weak spot of the Cardinals' defense was one of their strong points today. Arizona allowed a mere 3.1 yards per carry with no touchdowns to the Giants on the ground with four tackles for a loss. New York's rushing attack was overall average.
In their pass rush, they tallied four quarterback hits and two sacks with Walter Nolen III coming alive along with a surprising sack from Darius Robinson. In the run, Roy Lopez was all over the place with six tackles.
A good step in the right direction.
It was really encouraging to see Josh Sweat make a splash on Sunday, reaching his first sack with multiple pressures while Zaven Collins — mostly known for the run — also brought Jameis Winston down today. We've been harping on this group all season to take a step up and help Arizona get to the quarterback, and that happened (at least to better extents) today.
The only thing stopping this grade from being a D grade is Mack Wilson Sr. forcing a fumble in the second half. Wilson was picked on in coverage, allowing two touchdowns through the air. Jack Gibbens, meanwhile, led the Cardinals in tackles with eight.
It was an overall mixed bag from this position, though the overall success allowed to the Giants' passing attack overshadows anything good that happened with the group.
Garrett Williams was all over the place and looked much healthier than he did last week. Denzel Burke came away with an interception. Without Will Johnson, expectations have to be tempered with this group. They did benefit from an improved pass rush, though Arizona's inability to limit Malik Nabers to any extent (6-112-1) dragged their overall performance down.
Budda Baker's performance really is carrying a ton of weight here, as the star defender undoubtedly had his best outing of 2026 with an interception and a pair of impressive pass breakups.
Fellow starter Andrew Wingard exited due to injury and was replaced by rookie Wydett Williams, who allowed several big plays in the passing game and even had a penalty (block in the back) on Baker's interception return. It was a very forgettable performance from Williams, which balances out Baker's strong performance.

title: The Good, Bad, and Ugly From Cardinals' Underwhelming Loss to Giants
full_text:
The honeymoon phase from Week 1 has officially ended. The Arizona Cardinals fall to 1-3, losing to the New York Giants, 36-24, on Sunday afternoon at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey.
No doubt, it was a sloppy game for both—the Cardinals and Giants combined for six turnovers throughout the afternoon. The final turnover was the most costly: a game-sealing pick-six on the goal line that secured New York's win.
Here is the good, the bad, and the ugly from Arizona’s Week 4 matchup:
If there is anything positive from this game, the Cardinals' opening script and second drive of the afternoon were impressive. Arizona's offensive line gave Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier the space to dart up for big gains on both drives. Allgeier's 22-yard touchdown run was the largest rush attempt of the game for either team.
Mavin Harrison Jr., the biggest story surrounding the Cardinals since the start of training camp, and now rumored to be shipped off at the trade deadline, got engaged early. Jacoby Brissett connected with Harrison Jr. for a 12-yard touchdown, his first of the season.
Against the San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks, Arizona's defense struggled to force turnover opportunities.  New York Giants quarterback Jameis Winston gave them plenty of opportunities, tossing two picks to Budda Baker and Denzel Burke.
The Cardinals' final two point-producing drives came off the interceptions - a field goal to close out the first half and a touchdown to open the second half.
In the fourth quarter, Mack Wilson Sr. forced the third New York turnover of the game, punching the ball out of Giants running back Najee Harris arms for a fumble.
It's a trend that's become a trait for the Cardinals' defense this year: the opposition's No. 1 receiver is going to have a career day. Giants receiver Malik Nabers set a season high with six receptions for 112 yards and scored his first touchdown of the season. New York used the "Kittle Experiment," targeting tight end Isaiah Likely 12 times for seven catches and 66 yards.
Nabers burned the Cardinals' secondary for three 20-plus-yard receptions. On third down, Arizona allowed Likely, Nabers, and Malachi Fields three 30-plus-yard explosive receptions. The longest third-down conversion came on Fields' 40-yard grab, converting 3rd-and-20 for New York.
After the Cardinals let the Giants convert the longest third down of the afternoon, the defense forced a critical third-and-out and held New York to a field-goal attempt. A holding call on Cardinals defensive tackle Dante Stills gave the Giants a fresh set of downs and the third-quarter lead after Harris scored a 2-yard rushing touchdown.
For now, Jacoby Brissett will be the Cardinals' starting quarterback, with head coach Mike LaFleur shutting down any post-game questions.
Still, Brissett did not have his best game, aside from an occasional throw to his favorite target, Michael Wilson, and two touchdown passes to open the game and the second half. Brissett's two second-quarter interceptions completely dampened the Cardinals' momentum that was built in the first 15 minutes.
On the Cardinals' final, potentially game-winning drive, Brissett went 5-for-11 in the air, and Arizona reached the goal line only because of a pass-interference call on New York.  Arizona was stopped on all four passing attempts at the goal line, capped by a game-sealing pick-six on the final play.
The Cardinals quarterback closed out his worst performance of the season since Week 2 against Seattle, going 21-35 for 166 yards, two touchdowns, and a single-game career-high three interceptions.

title: 14 Studs and Duds From Cardinals Heartbreaking Loss to Giants
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals have more questions than answers after their frustrating loss to the New York Giants in Week 4, one that went all the way down to the wire before the Cardinals crumbled with the game on the line.
Arizona drops to 1-3 after 60 minutes at MetLife Stadium — here's our weekly studs and duds:
Love's stat line was limited thanks to limited usage, but when he was on the field, Arizona was incredibly effective at moving the ball.
Love rushed 14 times for 63 yards, averaging 4.5 yards per carry. His role diminished after Arizona strayed away from the rushing attack and the Cardinals opted for Tyler Allgeier for pass protection late in the game.
Love's only reception was a massive loss on a screen pass for minus eight yards — though that was practically the only play Love was involved in that was negative.
He needs the ball more, no more ifs, ands or buts.
The Cardinals were forced to turn to Wydett Williams after Andrew Wingard went down due to injury and didn't return .
The gap between the two players couldn't be clearer.
Williams was responsible for multiple major lapses in coverage (one leading to a touchdown) and even a block in the back during an interception return, which yielded a penalty.
A very forgettable day for the rookie that will surely be a tough time in the film room tomorrow.
Nolen got off to a slow start this regular season, though Arizona's former first-round pick quickly found his footing in Week 4.
Nolen registered four tackles (2 TFL) and was involved in at least two sacks (though he only was credited for one).
Nolen holds serious potential to be a game-changer, and his presence along Arizona's line today in both rushing the passer and stopping the run was nothing short of impressive.
Look, Brissett wasn't completely at fault for Arizona's loss today. The two interceptions he threw early on were fluky while the game-ender was simply him needing to get the ball out.
That being said, Brissett was only strong in spurts today, and when the game was on the line, he failed to deliver.
His 4.7 average yards per completion is noticeably short while his 55.2 passer rating was the worst he's had in years.
Noise will continue to grow on his job security in relation to Carson Beck, and if a 21/35 for 166 YRD and 2 TD to 3 INT stat line is in the books consistently, it's only a matter of time before that comes to fruition.

title: NFL Official Caught Using Profanity Toward Cardinals Star Trey McBride in Moment Going Viral
full_text:
ARIZONA — It's not every day you see an NFL official going viral, especially for use of foul language.
Late in the Cardinals' comeback attempt against the Giants in Week 4, Trey McBride had some early contact from a Giants defender on a third-down pass attempt that wasn't called, prompting Arizona to bring on the punt team for fourth down.
McBride exchanged some words with the official nearest to him, and the tail end of their interaction was caught by CBS' broadcast cameras. The official, while we're not professional lip-readers, used some words that aren't quite safe for work.
"This kind of behavior from an official towards a player is unacceptable. Players are consistently held accountable when the roles are reversed. We expect the NFL to hold officials to the same standard," said NFLPA executive director JC Tretter.
Adam Schefter later added the NFL, "The NFL said it is reviewing the situation in which an official appears to use profanity at Cardinals TE Trey McBride."
Reaction from the Executive Director of the NFLPA: https://t.co/AjXj6zyxAq
Towards the end of the video you can see McBride point towards the camera, likely knowing the interaction was caught from cameras.
McBride had a relatively quiet day, catching just seven passes for 31 yards, far below the typically eye-popping numbers most have come to expect from the star tight end.
According to the league's official site , a first-time verbal offense against an official results in a fine over $33,500 while a second-time fine is just north of $67,000.
No information is available on anything regarding discipline towards officials for the same messaging.
Physical contact with an official results in a $41,907 fine for a first infraction.
The NFL will review the matter with strong evidence of what the official used against McBride.
How exactly the individual in question could be punished remains to be seen, as Arizona typically uses internal evaluations for their crews on a weekly basis.
There's been two prior instances where an official has been fined for confronting a player during a game.
Roy Ellison was fined one game check for an interactio with Jerry Hughes back in 2018 and previously was suspended for one game in 2013 after using profanity towards Trent Williams.

title: 4 Gut Reactions After Cardinals' Frustrating Loss to Giants
full_text:
After losing its previous two games to division rivals, the Arizona Cardinals traveled east to take on the New York Giants. In a game that went down to the wire, the Cardinals couldn't overcome turnovers and poor play in their 26-24 loss at MetLife Stadium.
Four gut reactions as the Cardinals drop to 1-3:
This was a hot-and-cold game. One moment the Cardinals looked like a dark-horse playoff team; the next, they looked like they could own the first overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. When the Cardinals looked great, the run game was a huge factor.
First-round rookie Jeremiyah Love had a very nice outing. Love totaled 63 yards and averaged 4.5 yards per carry on the day. While Love has been solid the first three weeks of the season, he showed special flashes in East Rutherford today.
However, it wasn't just Love who looked great against the Giants; free agent addition Tyler Allgeier also had a strong game — his best play coming on a 22-yard rushing touchdown. If Love and Allgeier keep progressing, the Cardinals could have one of the best duos in the NFL.
One unfortunate common theme for the Cardinals early in the season is their secondary not being a great unit. Coming into this game, Jameis Winston had not thrown a passing touchdown this season. In this game, he threw for 250 yards and three scores.
The Cardinals still do not have an answer for opposing teams’ number-one wideouts. In Week 2, Seattle Seahawks wideout Jaxon Smith-Njigba had an amazing day, and the same thing happened today with New York Giants wideout Malik Nabers.
Nabers had 112 yards on six catches and one touchdown. Now, yes, it is worth mentioning that stud cornerback Will Johnson is out for the season, so he did not play in this game. Still, there are schematic ways to prevent a number one wideout from having an amazing day.
However, it wasn't all bad. Star safety Budda Baker had an interception as well as a great pass breakup. Cornerback Denzel Burke also had an interception.
Still, the secondary has plenty to fix, and they need to do it fast, as the Cardinals face the methodical Detroit Lions offense next week.
The Cardinals’ offensive line is a huge mess. Two of Jacoby Brissett’s three interceptions came because the offensive line allowed pressure too quickly. Giants rookie linebacker/edge-rusher hybrid Arvell Reese was a problem for the Cardinals’ offensive line.
While Reese is talented, the Cardinals’ failure to find answers is concerning.
Of all the Cardinals’ issues, this could be the main reason the team has had such a disappointing season. While many fans aren’t happy with Brissett’s quarterback play today, you can only do so much about poor pass blocking.
All of these issues come down to one factor, and that is coaching. Sure, head coach Mike LaFleu r is still in his first year, but some of these coaching issues are inexcusable.
The Cardinals actually started out this game pretty well, as they were up 14-6 early. Both the running and passing offense looked good. However, LaFleur abandoned the rushing attack completely until Arizona found themselves behind.
The lack of rushes continued late in the game, where LaFleur opted for four consecutive passing plays with the game on the line. In a game where Arizona averaged 4.7 yards per carry, the lack of running is very interesting to say the least.
Overall, the Cardinals have a lot to fix in this young season so far.

title: Cardinals Shut Down QB Change: Brissett Stays, Beck Waits
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals aren't making a quarterback change after their Week 4 loss to the New York Giants, according to head coach Mike LaFleur.
"No," LaFleur said post-game before the question could even be finished during his press conference.
The Cardinals now drop to 1-3 on the season after being stalled near the goal line in the final moments of a very winnable game at MetLife Stadium. Starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett marched the Cardinals' offense down to the NYG 4 but was stalled on all four final plays, which ended with a pick-six.
In Arizona's 36-24 loss to New York, Brissett completed 21 of 35 passes for 166 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions. He finished with a passer rating of 55.2 — his lowest as a starting quarterback since 2022.
"There's no script for this one. No loss is fun. All three losses that we've had over the last three weeks have been different," LaFleur continued post-game.
"I like to think I keep it real with these guys, this one's going to sting. That's not gonna be the most fun ride home, and there's certainly things that I know I wish I would have done better, whether it be in the preparation phase or within that game.
"When we turn on the tape I'm sure it's going to be the same ... It might sting even tomorrow. But when they leave that building, like I say, I don't care if we're 4-0 [or] 0-4 or somewhere in between, which we are, we got to get right back to work on Wednesday because no one's gonna feel sorry for us."
The Cardinals have veteran Gardner Minshew and rookie Carson Beck behind Brissett. Each loss will only amplify Arizona's pressure to make a change at the position — particularly to play Beck, who was freshly drafted in the third round and will be a major variable in the Cardinals' offseason plans.
For now, however, Brissett remains under center for Arizona entering their Week 5 clash against the Detroit Lions.
"It's no magic words, but to turn the page. Let's get back to work, let's obviously correct it from the film, and then just get back to work. That's the only thing you can do," Brissett said when asked about moving forward.
The more losses pile up, the more pressure mounts on changes being made. LaFleur was quick to say no in New York, though noise will only grow if the Cardinals can't find the win column.

title: The Most Egregious Referee Call that Crushed the Cardinals in Week 4 Loss vs Giants
full_text:
One play doesn't decide a 60 minute football game, though the Arizona Cardinals were on the wrong side of a big call in their Week 4 loss to the New York Giants, which ultimately ended 36-24 in favor of the home team.
After stopping New York on third down late in the third quarter, the Cardinals and Giants brought out their respective field goal teams. Dominic Zvada booted home a field goal to cut Arizona's lead to 24-22 before a flag emerged on the field.
Cardinals defensive lineman Dante Stills was called for holding on the play, which gave New York a fresh set of downs.
Everybody from the broadcast booth to Mike LaFleur down on the sidelines was perplexed by the call, and just two plays later the Cardinals found themselves trailing after Jameis Winston threaded a touchdown pass to Theo Johnson.
The call, when looking at it, is ticky-tacky at absolute best. Stills clearly doesn't have a strong grasp on the Giants' offensive lineman and it wasn't close to egregious enough to potentially change the course of a game like it did.
Refs said this was a hold on Dante Stills 😭😭😭😭😭😭😭😭😭 pic.twitter.com/YmCTSpaoUn
Rather than being up by two, the Cardinals began the next possession trailing by three. A point-swing like that can change momentum in the snap of a finger, and it clearly did. The Cardinals were needing a touchdown to tie (and extra point to win) on their final drive instead of needing a field goal for a possible win.
Penalties have been a hot topic in the desert, as entering Week 4 the Cardinals were one of the most penalized teams in the league. Arizona cleaned their act up in New York with seven total penalties for 55 yards, though mistakes at inopportune times still killed the Cardinals down the stretch.
“You have to focus in on it. Like I told you guys two weeks ago, sometimes you speak it into existence. I don’t think we’ve done that. We know it needs to get done," LaFleur said during the week.
"We’re professionals — coaches and players and we’re in it with them, but that certainly is an aspect that has to get cleaned up because whether it was the pre-snap operation on that fourth drive or the holding on the first and second drive, it killed us."
The Cardinals now drop to 1-3 on the season. They'll get back to work in Week 5 against the Detroit Lions.

title: Falcons Reunion With Former LB Won’t Happen Against Saints, Injury Report
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons (1-2) will not face one of their defensive anchors from the previous three seasons when they face the New Orleans Saints (1-2) tonight .
Saints linebacker Kaden Elliss has been ruled out for the Week 4 NFC South rivalry game against his former team with a calf injury, a designation announced last Friday, Oct. 2, three days before the matchup.
Elliss spent the 2023 through 2025 seasons in Atlanta, accruing 380 tackles during his time there. He led the team in tackles during the 2024 and 2025 seasons.
This March, Elliss left the Falcons to rejoin the Saints, who drafted him in the seventh round out of Idaho in 2019. He inked a three-year, $33 million deal to return to New Orleans.
Elliss was a major part of the Saints’ plan to contain Falcons running back Bijan Robinson , who entered Week 4 leading the NFL with 467 scrimmage yards and fresh off a NFC Offensive Player of the Week performance in Atlanta’s 35-14 win over the Green Bay Packers .
Elliss’s inside knowledge of the Falcons and anchoring presence in the middle of the Saints’ defense would have been key against arguably the best running back in the NFL.
New Orleans will now likely look to reserve inside linebackers Danny Stutsman and Isaiah Stalbird to help fill in for Elliss’ absence.
Elliss isn't the only player for the Saints who will be missing on Monday night. New Orleans also ruled out edge rushers Carl Granderson and Anfernee Jennings.  Granderson has 11 tackles and a sack on the season, and Jennings has added seven tackles and a forced fumble.
Fellow linebacker Pete Werner is also listed as questionable for the game with a shoulder injury. Facing Robinson and the Falcons' running game down one linebacker is a daunting challenge on its own, but missing Elliss and Werner could cause big problems for the Saints defense.
The Falcons have linebacker troubles of their own, with Divine Deablo listed as questionable with a hamstring, which could open the door for rookie Harold Perkins Jr. to see more snaps. Perkins has seen time in passing situations, and with his speed, he could be an excellent answer to Saints quarterback Tyler Shough's ability to scramble.
All-time, Atlanta holds a 58-56 head-to-head record in 114 games dating back to the 1967 season.
Falcons versus Saints will kick off at 8:15 p.m. Eastern Time from Caesars Superdome on ESPN.
The game will honor 20 years of the Saints’ “Domecoming” when they returned to the Superdome after Hurricane Katrina.

title: Michael Penix Jr. Pours Gas on Falcons-Saints Rivalry Ahead of Monday Night Football
full_text:
Hate week is soon about to come to a head when the Atlanta Falcons (1-2) face their heated NFC South divisional rival, the New Orleans Saints (1-2) , on Monday Night Football.
And as fans banter on social media, Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix Jr. is getting into the fun before his team visits the Caesars Superdome for the Week 4 clash.
“It’s a nice dome,” Penix told reporters on Thursday, days ahead of the matchup. “That’s probably like the only nice thing I can say about them.”
The third-year NFL quarterback is set to make his first start in New Orleans.
In 2024, Penix sat behind Kirk Cousins in his rookie year as the Falcons and Saints split their semiannual divisional faceoff.
Last year, the rivals faced each other on the back half of the season, as Penix had already suffered his partially torn ACL injury. Cousins started the November 2025 and January 2026 games, and Atlanta swept the series.
Penix’s lone time he played in the Superdome was his final college football season. He threw for 430 yards and two touchdowns as the Washington Huskies defeated Texas 37-31 in the Sugar Bowl to advance to the College Football Playoff national championship game.
He expects his first NFL start in the Big Easy to draw a raucous crowd looking to send the Falcons back to the Peach State with a loss.
“It’s going to be real loud, and it’s going to be great, it’s going to be awesome,” Penix previewed visiting the Saints. “We’re going to go out there and accept the challenge and go out there and just compete our tails off to find a way to get a win. It’s definitely going to be rowdy.”
On Monday, the Saints will celebrate the “Domecoming,” marking 20 years since the team returned to the Superdome in September 2006, a year after Hurricane Katrina. They beat the Falcons 23-3.
When New Orleans honored 10 years of playing in the Superdome, Atlanta won 45-32 in the 2016 season.
“We want to go out and try to have the same results,” Penix said.
Penix enters the Saints game after going 18-for-25 for 256 passing yards, throwing a touchdown, and an interception while returning to the Falcons’ lineup . Atlanta beat the Green Bay Packers 35-14 on Sept. 24’s Thursday Night Football, moving the Falcons’ record to 8-3 in primetime games since 2024 .
Falcons-Saints kickoff at 8:15 p.m. on ESPN for Monday Night Football tonight. All-time, Atlanta owns the head-to-head series 58-56 in 114 meetings dating back to 1967.

title: FalconsSI Staff Split on Atlanta Falcons vs. New Orleans Saints Predictions
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons head into Monday Night Football with an opportunity to make an early statement in the NFC South when they travel to New Orleans to face the Saints. The winner of the game will move to 2-2 and keep pace with the Carolina Panthers, who got the win over
Atlanta enters the matchup with renewed confidence following the return of Michael Penix Jr. The Falcons offense will look to build on its Week 3 performance, while Bijan Robinson and the rushing attack could play a major role in controlling the game and keeping pressure off Penix.
The Saints will have the benefit of a raucous home crowd, particularly with New Orleans celebrating the 20-year anniversary of the Superdome’s reopening following Hurricane Katrina. Tyler Shough and the Saints will look to take advantage of the home field, but Atlanta’s defense will have an opportunity to make life difficult for the rookie quarterback.
With the NFC South implications, rivalry atmosphere, and primetime stage, the Falcons SI staff expects a competitive game in New Orleans.
There Can Be Only One: Gerald Thomas, III and Jerry Jones put their perfect 3-0 record on the line, but they have chosen different winners tonight. One of them is guaranteed to move to 4-0.
Falcons-Saints always bring good football. So expect this to be a good one. Atlanta comes into Monday Night Football with renewed energy and confidence after the return of Michael Penix Jr., but the Saints are also a well-improved team and have just fallen in close games so far this young NFL season.
Plus, they’ll have an energetic fanbase with the 20-year anniversary of the Superdome’s reopening after Hurricane Katrina. But feel-good stories don’t always lead to wins in this rivalry. Led by record-breaking tailback Bijan Robinson, the Falcons are one of the top teams in primetime football, and that means something. Expect Atlanta to escape New Orleans with a Monday Night Football victory to stay in early contention for the NFC South divisional race. Prediction: Falcons 25, Saints 21
After spotting the rest of the division two games via the Cooper Rush experience, the Falcons somehow find themselves playing for first place in the NFC South.
The Falcons offense rose from the dead like Lazarus last week, and I expect that to continue into this week. The Saints have a respectable defensive line and secondary, but I think they’re overmatched by the Falcons offensive line and receivers. But make no mistake, this is still a Bijan-first offense, and I think he’ll thrive again in this matchup.
The injured Falcons secondary doesn’t match up great against a talented Shough and the Saints receiving corps on paper. But if the Falcons d-line shows up like it did last week, it can neutralize that.
Ultimately, I expect this to be a very entertaining shootout. My gut tells me the Saints pull this one out in a game that’ll come down to the last possession.
Prediction: Saints 31, Falcons 27
The Atlanta Falcons will grind out a close victory over the New Orleans Saints. Bijan Robinson and the rushing attack will control the clock and take pressure off Michael Penix Jr., while Atlanta’s defense will make Tyler Shough uncomfortable and force New Orleans into difficult third-down situations. The Superdome crowd will make the game challenging, but the Falcons will make enough key defensive stops late to secure the win. Prediction: Falcons 20, Saints 17
The Atlanta Falcons showed us something in Week 3, and it all starts with that guy under center. Michael Penix Jr. elevated this entire team. They had life again, and I think that will carry over into Monday night.
Add in the injuries that the Saints are dealing with on defense, and I think this could be another strong performance for the Atlanta offense. Jeff Ulbrich has created a lot of pressure without sending a blitz, but that will be more important than ever with an athletic Tyler Shough who can maneuver in and out of the pocket. He won’t have Travis Etienne Jr., and that should help this Falcons defense pin their ears back a bit more.
They are walking into a hornet’s nest, but Bijan Robinson is the great equalizer. Falcons come out on top.
Prediction: Falcons 24, Saints 17
How good are the Saints? How good are the Falcons? Through three games, we still really don’t know. If the Falcons that played in Green Bay show up every week, they look like the best team in the division.
But teams will make adjustments to Michael Penix Jr. and offensive coordinator Tommy Rees, and we’ll see if they can adapt.
The Falcons’ play in the trenches on both sides of the ball looks like a steadying component that hopefully will keep the team from the low points that have tanked each of the last three seasons. I think the offensive and defensive lines make the difference in this game. Then there’s always this factor: Atlanta has Bijan Robinson, and the Saints don’t Prediction: Falcons 27, Saints 20

title: Jake Matthews Set to Make Atlanta Falcons History
full_text:
Jake Matthews will make history Sunday when the Atlanta Falcons offensive tackle makes his 200th career start against the New Orleans Saints.
Matthews will become just the fourth player in Falcons history to reach 200 or more career starts, joining an exclusive group that highlights his remarkable longevity with the franchise. He has spent his entire 13-year NFL career with Atlanta, becoming one of the longest-tenured players in team history.
Reaching 200 starts is an accomplishment Matthews admitted he did not fully appreciate until this week.
“To be honest, I wasn't fully aware,” Matthews said. “But pretty surreal.”
Matthews was quick to deflect the credit for his longevity, pointing instead to his ability to stay healthy and the people around him who have helped him throughout his career.
“I can't reiterate enough how much God has blessed me to have a body that can continue to do this and stay free from injury, and that's stuff I can't take credit for,” Matthews said. “Just very thankful to him and how good he's been to me.”
Matthews has missed only one game during his NFL career, a remarkable run that began with his rookie season in 2014. Coincidentally, his first career start came against New Orleans, giving Sunday's milestone another connection to the beginning of his career.
“I got hurt in that game,” Matthews said of his first start. “Man, feels like a lifetime.”
Matthews acknowledged how different he is from the player who took his first NFL snaps more than a decade ago.
“Completely different person,” he said. “It's pretty cool how far I've come and how long it's been here.”
The Saints have provided Matthews with another memorable moment in his career. Atlanta's 2016 matchup against New Orleans came during the Falcons' Super Bowl season, when the team put together one of the most prolific offenses in franchise history.
Now Matthews will return to New Orleans for his 200th career start.
“It's pretty surreal,” Matthews said. “Obviously going down there, playing that environment, it's always special. It's gonna be loud, it's gonna be challenging.”
While Matthews has continued to build his professional legacy, his family has become an increasingly important part of his life away from football.
Matthews revealed that he and his wife, Meggi, are expecting their third child. He credited her with playing a major role in his career.
“She’s been a huge part of the second half of my career,” Matthews said. “She sacrifices a lot for me to be out here.”
Matthews said the demands of raising a family have also changed his perspective off the field.
“I was pretty used to going home to do what I want whenever I want to do it,” Matthews said. “Now, it's, you gotta put other people in front of yourself.”
As Matthews prepares for this historic start, he is not putting a specific number on how many more games he wants to play.
“You keep chipping away, you make it through each week, and then you wake up one day, and it's like the 13th season, like 200 games. So, I keep that formula going.”
Matthews will add another chapter to that remarkable run as they face the Saints on Monday Night.

title: Surprise Free Agent Emerging as Key Piece of Falcons' Pass Rush
full_text:
For much of his NFL career, Atlanta Falcons defensive end Cam Thomas has had to wait for his opportunity.
Since entering the league as a third-round pick of the Arizona Cardinals in 2022, Thomas started just three games over his first four seasons. He bounced between Arizona, Kansas City, and Cleveland while largely filling a rotational role, recording eight sacks across 58 games before arriving in Atlanta.
Three games into his first season in Atlanta, Thomas has made the most of his opportunities.
Thomas has started all three games for the Falcons and has recorded seven tackles, 1.5 sacks, and a forced fumble. His production has increased each week, including a sack in Atlanta's Week 3 victory over the Green Bay Packers.
The opportunity was one of the primary reasons Thomas chose Atlanta after spending the previous two seasons with the Cleveland Browns.
“They offered me opportunity. And, you know, in this league, that's something that's very hard to pass up,” Thomas said.
Thomas has generated 12 total pressures through three games, including eight quarterback hits, two sacks, and two additional hurries. His 80.1 pass rush grade ranks ninth among qualified edge defenders.
The numbers represent a significant step forward for Thomas, who spent the previous two seasons with the Cleveland Browns.
Now, Thomas is showing what he can do with an expanded role.
“Just keep my head down,” Thomas said. “But on top of that, as I was talking about earlier, rushing as one. If all four of us are rushing as one, I think you can see all of us kind of benefiting off that. No independent contractors out there.”
Thomas has been part of a young Falcons defensive front that has quickly developed chemistry. Through three games, he has played 59 percent of Atlanta's defensive snaps, giving him a significantly larger role than he had during his previous two seasons in Cleveland.
The presence of Gervon Dexter Sr. has also helped create opportunities for Thomas and the rest of Atlanta's pass rush.
“Oh man, he's a monster,” Thomas said. “When he's taking care of the guards and the centers, you don't have to worry about the guard coming back. It's a huge deal.”
Thomas has also embraced the veteran presence of Za'Darius Smith, who he believes has brought another level of energy to the defensive room.
“I love Z. There's great energy from the day he got in the building,” Thomas said.
For Thomas, the early success is less about individual production and more about the collective performance of Atlanta's defensive front.
That has been the message since he arrived.
And after spending the majority of his career waiting for a chance to become a consistent starter, Thomas is finally getting the opportunity to show what he can do with one.

title: Falcons vs. Saints Odds, How to Watch, Injuries for NFL Week 4
full_text:
NEW ORLEANS – The Atlanta Falcons are back on the road for the second of three consecutive prime-time matchups. Awaiting them in Week 4 is their arch-rival in New Orleans on Monday night.
Michael Penix Jr. was the story last Thursday. His return from an ACL injury sparked a resurgent Falcons offense and helped the team secure its first win of the Kevin Stefanski era. Penix unlocked this unit's potential, and they will look to continue that success against the Saints in a crucial divisional matchup.
On the other end, New Orleans looks like an up-and-coming team, led by an exciting young quarterback in Tyler Shough, who is second in the league in passing coming into Week 4. His mobility and connection with Chris Olave will be a tough test for a solid Falcons defense that has been effective at generating pressure but has been hit through the air so far.
As always, this should be an exciting game.
The Falcons and Saints have produced one of the NFL’s most heated rivalries. The two franchises have met 114 times, and the all-time record sits at 58-56 in favor of Atlanta after their season sweep in 2025.
This game is always heated, but Monday night’s edition carries some added significance for the home team. New Orleans is 20 years removed from reopening the Superdome, when they welcomed the Falcons for a forgettable 23-3 beatdown highlighted by Steve Gleason’s blocked punt.
Atlanta got their revenge 10 years later with a 45-32 win in 2016, and they will look to do the same on Monday night. It will be a tough test for the Falcons, but here’s everything you need to know to watch their Week 4 matchup with the Saints.

title: Falcons Have Major Opportunity as NFC South Injuries Mount
full_text:
Injuries are mounting in the NFC South, and the Atlanta Falcons must capitalize on what is shaping up to be a tight division race this season.
Three weeks into the season, every team in the division has dealt with significant injuries. The Falcons have already dealt with their share, including Michael Penix Jr. missing the first two weeks and CB A.J. Terrell Jr. landing on injured reserve, but the latest wave could significantly affect the early jockeying for position.
Here's a look at the latest injury situations for Atlanta's NFC South opponents.
The Falcons’ Week 4 opponents are dealing with injuries on both sides of the ball, with several defensive contributors currently unavailable. Former Falcons linebacker Kaden Elliss is out for Monday night, as are edge rusher Carl Granderson and linebacker Anfernee Jennings, leaving the Saints without multiple pieces of their front seven.
Those losses up front could be especially problematic for a Saints defense that will have to face Bijan Robinson and the Falcons' rushing attack.
New Orleans also lost wide receiver Jordan Tyson (earlier this summer) and running back Travis Etienne Jr. to injured reserve, meaning Tyler Shough and Chris Olave will need to carry the Saints' offense for the next several weeks.
The Panthers are dealing with several significant losses in their secondary, with Mike Jackson and Jaycee Horn both landing on injured reserve. Slowing down some of the potent offenses on their schedule was already set to be difficult, but doing so without both starting corners will be especially tough.
The Panthers will have to find answers in their secondary quickly as the season moves forward.
On offense, Carolina is down a starting guard (Damien Lewis) and a depth wide receiver (Xavier Legette), while Jalen Coker also has nagging injuries that shouldn’t keep him out Sunday.
The biggest injury news in the division may come from Tampa Bay, where the 0-3 Buccaneers are staring down a lost season. Quarterback Baker Mayfield is out indefinitely with a thumb injury, leaving the Buccaneers without the heartbeat of their offense. In his place, Tampa will lean on a rookie undrafted free agent (Jalon Daniels) to carry its offense.
The Bucs will have to navigate that absence while also dealing with injuries on defense and at wide receiver – they are also without cornerback Benjamin Morrison and first-round edge rusher Rueben Bain Jr., while wide receiver Jalen McMillan is on injured reserve.
The Falcons are coming off a statement win over the Green Bay Packers in Week 3 and appear to be finding their identity on both sides of the ball. The offense is generating plenty of excitement with Penix's return, while Jeff Ulbrich's run defense has emerged as one of the team's biggest strengths.
Now they have to turn that momentum into wins.
The NFC South doesn't appear to have a team that will run away with the division, which means every advantage matters. Injuries are part of the NFL, and the Falcons will have to overcome their own, but when multiple division opponents are missing key players, Atlanta has to make those games count.
If the Falcons can continue playing complementary football and capitalize when opponents are shorthanded, they can put themselves in a strong position as the division race heats up.

title: Falcons Have Two Defensive Starters Questionable Ahead of Saints Matchup
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons have listed two defensive starters as questionable ahead of Monday night's matchup with the New Orleans Saints.
Inside linebacker Divine Deablo and defensive end Samson Ebukam are both dealing with hamstring injuries, leaving the Falcons with decisions to make regarding their defensive lineup. Neither player has been ruled out, but their availability will be worth monitoring leading up to kickoff.  Further complicating the depth chart at edge, the Falcons also added Yasir Abdullah as questionable due to illness.
Deablo has been limited throughout the week and remained limited during Friday's practice. He has started all three games for Atlanta this season and has played every defensive snap, making his potential absence particularly significant.
Through three games, Deablo has recorded 11 tackles, including five solo tackles, along with one pass defended.
If Deablo cannot play, Christian Harris is listed directly behind him on Atlanta's unofficial depth chart and would be a logical candidate to see an expanded role. Harris has appeared in two games this season and has recorded two tackles, both solo.
Harris brings considerable experience to the position. He started 12 games for the Houston Texans in 2023 and recorded 101 tackles, seven tackles for loss, two sacks, and seven passes defended that season. The Falcons could also increase the snaps for rookie Harold Perkins Jr.
Ebukam's situation comes with a more encouraging development.
The veteran defensive end missed Atlanta's Week 3 victory over the Green Bay Packers after suffering a hamstring injury the previous week. However, he returned to full participation Friday, marking the first time he has received that designation since the injury.
Ebukam has appeared in the first two games of the season, recording three tackles and half a sack.
If Ebukam cannot return Monday night, Atlanta can lean on its depth and rotate several players along the defensive front rather than relying on one player to replace his snaps. Bralen Trice has been elevated from the practice squad for two straight weeks. He's a natural addition this year.
Atlanta would need to make a decision on Trice after this week, needing to either sign him to the 53-man roster or release him because of maxing out his practice squad elevations.
Cameron Thomas has been a significant part of that rotation through the first three games. Thomas has played 118 defensive snaps, the most among Atlanta's defensive ends, while Za'Darius Smith has logged 77 snaps. Smith has also been one of the more prominent pieces of the Falcons' pass rush rotation.
The Falcons therefore have established options behind both questionable starters.
Atlanta has no players listed as doubtful or out on its final game status report, meaning both Deablo and Ebukam remain possibilities for Monday night's NFC South matchup.

title: Falcons CB C.J. Henderson Gets Bold Vote of Confidence From Jeff Ulbrich
full_text:
C.J. Henderson entered the NFL as a hyped cornerback out of the University of Florida, selected with the ninth overall pick in the 2020 NFL Draft by the Jacksonville Jaguars.
Six seasons and four teams later, Henderson is earning an opportunity to transform from what some would call a “bust” to now being a “late bloomer” in his second year with the Atlanta Falcons .
“When he got here, obviously, a very well-known past and history in this league,” Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich spoke to reporters about Henderson on Friday.
“To help him start to reinvent himself here brings me a ton of joy because he’s such an amazing young man. I’m excited for every opportunity he gets and show this league exactly who he is now today.”
With AJ Terrell Jr. on injured reserve , Henderson took over the lead primary cornerback duties in Atlanta’s 35-14 win over the Green Bay Packers .
The Thursday Night Football matchup saw the 6-foot-1, 205-pounder match up with Green Bay wide receiver duo Romeo Doubs and Christian Watson, and Henderson even defended tight end Tucker Kraft.
In a dominant defensive performance by the Falcons, Henderson finished the game with 12 targets, allowing five receptions for 52 yards. Henderson logged eight tackles, all solo, and defended three passes.
“To have him on this roster gives us so much security,” Ulbrich said of Henderson stepping in for Terrell. “Typically, a corner gets nicked or hurt, then the next guy comes in – they’re going to attack that guy, they’re going to target that guy. When CJ takes the field, I’m like ‘Please target him. Go at him. Good luck.’ It’s been a fun journey with CJ.”
Just like that, the sixth-year NFL veteran is now leading a Falcons cornerback room featuring Billy Bowman Jr. , rookie Avieon Terrell , and Mike Hughes .
Ulbrich holds Henderson in high regard.
“CJ is a tremendous luxury,” Ulbrich said. “In my opinion, he is a ‘one.’ He is a guy who would start on a lot of teams”
Next for Henderson is New Orleans Saints All-Pro receiver Chris Olave. He enters the Falcons-Saints NFC South rivalry Monday Night Football game with 27 receptions, 375 receptions, and a touchdown.
It will be a collective effort to contain the Saints’ star, Ulbrich says.
“He’s obviously a focal point of this offense,” Ulbrich said. “It’s going to take all of us – the rush, the coverage, the one-on-one matchup. I’d like to say we’ll have enough variants and answers to keep you guessing as far as how we’re covering him. What a great challenge for us. CJ, Mike, Billy – it’s not their job to cover him. It’s all of our job. And it’s on me too to get these guys in the right places and provide enough help and assistance to keep the offense guessing.”
Falcons (1-2) versus Saints (1-2) NFL Week 4 game kicks off at 8:15 p.m. on ESPN from the Caesars Superdome and will commemorate 20 years since New Orleans returned to the venue after Hurricane Katrina .
If Atlanta wins, it’ll jump to the sole No. 1 spot in the NFC South division as long as the Carolina Panthers lose to the Detroit Panthers.

title: Kyle Pitts Could Be Poised for Bigger Role in Falcons vs Saints
full_text:
Kyle Pitts has been one of the least involved players in the Atlanta Falcons offense through the first three games, but offensive coordinator Tommy Rees knows that needs to change.
Pitts enters Sunday’s matchup against the New Orleans Saints with just two receptions for 20 yards on six targets. His 8 percent target share is well below what would be expected from a player the Falcons signed to a new contract this offseason after he finished 2025 with 88 receptions for 928 yards and earned Second Team All-Pro honors.
Rees put the responsibility on himself Friday when asked about finding ways to get Pitts more involved.
“I need to do the best job I can to make sure Kyle can play,” he said.
Rees added that Pitts remains an important piece of what Atlanta wants to do offensively.
“We’re a better team when we can do that.”
It is a continuation of a message Rees has delivered throughout the early part of the season. The Falcons offensive coordinator acknowledged previously that Atlanta needed to find better ways to utilize Pitts, particularly after the tight end had only one catch through the first two games.
Now, the matchup with New Orleans presents another opportunity.
The Saints have allowed significant production to opposing tight ends through the first three games. Opposing tight ends have recorded 25 receptions for 250 yards and two touchdowns against New Orleans, with the Las Vegas Raiders accounting for 13 receptions, 148 yards and two touchdowns from the position last week.
The matchup is notable for Pitts because Atlanta does not necessarily need to force targets his way. The Saints have already demonstrated vulnerability against the position, creating an opportunity for the Falcons to incorporate Pitts naturally within the offense.
Pitts has continued to play a significant role in Atlanta’s offensive personnel, but his production has not reflected his presence on the field. Meanwhile, Bijan Robinson and Drake London have emerged as the primary focal points of the offense.
That has left Pitts waiting for his opportunities.
The Falcons have plenty of reasons to keep looking for ways to involve him. Pitts was one of the NFL’s most productive tight ends last season, finishing second at the position in receiving yards while ranking among the league leaders in yards after the catch.
Against New Orleans, the opportunity could be there.
For Rees, it will be about creating situations where Pitts can become part of the offense without forcing the ball to him.
After three quiet games, Atlanta will find out whether that approach can finally get Pitts going.

title: The Ravens Would Be Fools To Move Vega Ioane From Center Now. Don't Do It
full_text:
The Ravens need to leave Vega Ioane alone.
He is their starting center. He is their best option.
He needs to be given a real runway now to take to the role after being yanked around so much already. Figure out the guard situation, rotate the guards if you want – the Ravens love that fetish – once Ioane gets a little more cemented at center. But the center position is too important, the issues with the guards are acute enough already, and the last thing I would do is move Ioane now.
He had as much to do with them escaping with a 24-18 win over the lowly Titans at home on Sunday, snapping a four-game losing streak at M&T Bank Stadium, as anyone, on an ugy afternoon where injuries kept mounting including to maestro Lamar Jackson.
Titans defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons led Tennessee with 32 pass rush reps Sunday (seven more than any teammate), he got no free runs at the quarterback; he never even touched either quarterback (Jackson, who left with an ankle injury, or Snoop Huntley). Simmons had no pressures and no QB hits and no hurries . The NFL leader among all defensive tackles in sacks, pressures and tackles for a loss since the start of last season, coming in after collecting 10 tackles and a sack against the Eagles, leading all DTs in tackles and solo tackles, had just two solos on Sunday against that interior OL.
You couldn’t get me to move this kid for some journeyman now. No way.
The Titans started moving Simmons to the edge to hunt more favorable matchups before halftime, and get runs at left tackle Ronnie Stanley coming off a toe injury. They preferred their chances there. I’ve seen enough. Simmons had been held without a pressure in just one of his previous 31 full games since Week 3 of 2024 (it happened one other time in a game he played just 12 snaps).
I’m sold until or unless serious issues arise down the road. They found their guy, finally, after injuries to hope-and-prayer guys Danny Pinter and Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic coming off Achilles surgery.
“They found their center,” said one longtime NFL personnel executive who watched the Ravens closely. “At least for this year. You are 100 percent right. Leave him alone, let him keep snapping, he can get that solved for you. They just solved a problem … Don’t move him for the guy on the practice squad (center Andre James), and you could end up creating multiple problems.
“Now you have one problem: isolate the guard issue, and figure out who that guy is. You can experiment there. But a week ago it looked like they had three problems on the line. How they handled Simmons, that’s enough. I’m sold. You can figure the other stuff out. Run outside zone, play around with the run game.
“Center is a super important position for them - they drafted the last one in the first round (Tyler Linderbaum who left for Las Vegas as a free agent). They haven’t liked bigger, physical guys there, which is why they probably didn’t see this kid as a center. But the last thing I’m doing now is creating more uncertainty at center to look at a guy I signed off a practice squad last week because I lost three centers to injury.”
Do not overthink this. Don’t get too cute.
Simmons, while Jackson was still at QB, lined up basically over Stanley on his final five pass rush reps of the first half, including the sack where Jackson was injured. The only near pressure Simmons had in that first half came early in the game when he was lined up over right tackle. And it’s not like he was getting double teamed like crazy when he did take reps over the center or guards.
I don’t think anyone could have reasonably expected the interior pass protection to function this well , and far super to anything we’d seen the past two weeks.  Titans coach Robert Saleh probably should have blitzed more and brought linebackers to try to pierce the A Gap, but that’s not who he is (he blitzed 23.5% of the time. Tennessee had just seven pressures in the game and a pathetic 20.6% pressure rate.
Ioane was handed two very difficult assignments and where catastrophic issues were occurring in the A gap , now your biggest problem isn’t ever-collapsing pockets threatening your shoulda-been-three-time MVP quarterback in his walk season, it’s a 32-year-old running back looking like a 32-year old RB because the OL can’t open much up.
Okay, keep running pitch plays and get away from the under center runs that are going nowhere and yeah, seven rushing with Derrick Henry up the middle for six totals yards isn't ideal, but having the ability to gut teams downfield with Jackson to Flowers is the greatest super power this team has right now and it's not close. it is the super power.
They drafted Adam Randall to be a “Joker” offensive weapon for them and that running back could help with him eligible to come off IR. Justice Hill can get more carries. The more a five-man unit plays together more chemistry should develop. Going to a fourth center for the fifth game of the season, after a game-and-a-half without exchange issues and without the center flinching and without the A Gap being a mess on dropbacks is more than enough for me.

title: Ravens Defense Continued To Suffer In These 3 Key Areas In 24-18 Win Over Lowly Titans
full_text:
The Ravens defense had its moments on Sunday.
Book-ending the first half with takeaways and taking advantage of a novice quarterback on the road in Baltimore was a step in the right direction . They bowed up as a unit against the under-center runs that have been troubling them in a 24-18 win at M&T Bank Stadium, holding Tony Pollard to three yards per carry.
Nnamdi Madubuke, in just his second game back from neck surgery and just his second game in over a year since suffering the neck injury, made a critical stop on Pollard on a fourth-and-goal run and finished the day with three pressures, two quarterback hits and three hurries and led the team’s defensive linemen with 42 snaps played. But, alas there was also a lot that still needs to be corrected, and quickly, from a defense that still has far too much in common with the unit that struggled the last two years under former coordinator Zach Orr .
Rookie head coach Jesse Minter played a 3-4 front more than he had all year (33% in the first half when the Titans tried to establish the run), making necessary adjustments to win up front, but there are big questions being asked of his defense’s pass rush, its fourth-quarter mentality, and its ability to contain No. 1 receivers, suffering up front without top edge rusher Trey Hendrickson (finger surgery) and with their highest-paid corner, Marlon Humphrey, missing the second half with a calf injury.
“We’re chasing a much, much higher level for us,” Minter said after the game, perhaps summing it up best.
Maybe Hendrickson’s finger was a significant issue, but Baltimore’s pressure rate and potency impacting the QB peaked in Week 1 (before he was hurt), and Colts passer Daniel Jones did not look comfortable at all in his first game back from Achilles surgery. Sacks do matter at the end of games when you have to get off the field, and the lack of closers in the second half of games is a big part of why this second half defense remains so flawed even with a big lead.
The Ravens only mustered a pressure rate around 20% against a raw quarterback in Cam Ward, who struggled mightily against the blitz. Minter played it “conservatively” due to the big lead and injuries and other factors, and didn’t sell out to attack him (14% blitz rate) and settled for a lot of passes chucked out of bounds with moderate pressure.
They only hit Ward six times on 34 dropbacks, they mustered one sack, and now have a season sack rate below 5%; essentially what it was last year . They are generating pressure only around 32% of the time (23rd).
“We didn’t finish the way were capable of,” Minter said, later adding that “hopefully down the road that type of game is a four, five or six sack game.”
The Titans barely had the ball in the fourth quarter with Baltimore grinding out another six-minute drive on the ground. And everyone knew where the ball was going when Ward did throw – rookie Carnell Tate – and he still ran free and ran threw tackles and the Titans scored a touchdown and late two-point conversion to make it a one-score game at the end when it never shoulda been that close.
So now, for the season, the Ravens have been out-scored, 40-20, in the fourth quarter. That’s not nearly good enough, it will continue haunting them with the blown leads, and that differential ranks 29th in the NFL. They have allowed 414 yards in the final quarter, 29th overall and they are 30th in fourth-quarter points allowed.
A week after Kyle Hamilton called this defense “unacceptable” and put the onus on the players to improve, this unit still looks far more like a work in progress than anyone in The Castle was hoping when they made this coaching change .
It was no secret that Ward was not pushing the ball downfield at all and when he did it was always going to Tate. Maybe if Humphrey stays in the game he holds him down, but he was exposed by Chris Olave in Week 2 and several Cowboys receivers in Week 3. A few balls sailed over the head of free safety Malaki Starks and I continue to wonder if Hamilton, a hybrid defender, is going to find himself playing more in the deep end as the season plays on.
Tate catching nine of his 12 targets for 145 yards (and he dropped two other passes that could have been gains) is indicative of the state of this secondary and it’s continuing an ugly trend. Recall, the Colts deep threat, Alec Pierce, was coming back from surgery and was barely a decoy in Week 1. Since then, here’s what’s been going on against this group:
CeeDee Lamb : 7 catches on 8 targets, 112 yards
George Pickens : 7 catches on 11 targets, 82 yards
Olave : 8 catches on 10 targets, 86 yards, 1 TD
Those four receivers have combined for 21 first down receptions in three games. Two of those games were at home. The Titans were probably the worst pass game in the NFL entering this game, or certainly bottom three.
“It’s early in the season,” Madubuike said. “Everybody is trying to find their way, trying to find their identity.”
Perhaps, but these Ravens best find a new one, fast, on defense.

title: Lamar Jackson's Ankle Among Many Injury Concerns As Ravens Beat Titans, 24-18: Key Takeaways From Ugly Win
full_text:
The Ravens handled the Titans, as expected, in an ugly game, as expected, but lost Lamar Jackson to an ankle injury at the very end of the half that will color everything moving forward. And then a slew of injuries followed.
Jackson was listed as questionable to return at the half but his day was gone as the Ravens held a big lead (24-7), the field was slick, the Ravens were utilizing a makeshift offensive line – that held up remarkably well – and putting him back in this game under duress was never going to make sense. Jackson was limping on the sidelines and eventually went back to the locker room as the Ravens went on for a 24-18 win at M&T Bank Stadium that ended a four-game home losing streak.
Head coach Jesse Minter said after the game that he "we don’t know enough about it," yet to give a significant update on Jackson but added that there "were some talks" about him possibly re-entering the game, "so hopefully he's in a good spot."
That home losing funk was snapped due primarily to Jackson and receiver Zay Flowers (who was getting some medical attention as well very late in the game) putting together a ridiculously explosive half of football, but alas they have only played one full game together this season with Flowers dealing with a prior hamstring injury. The Ravens also lost top corner Marlon Humphrey to a calf injury, and blocking tight end Durham Smythe, who made an immediate impact as a pass protector and lead blocker, was immediately ruled out with an Achilles injury.
These were the key takeaways from a workmanlike victory in which the injury report could prove far more significant than the details of how this played out. (And the penalties were out of control again, too, with 13 for 131 yards in the game; the Ravens were tied for the NFL lead in offensive penalties through three weeks, and committed at least six penalties on that side of the ball for a fourth straight game). Oh, and young kicker Tyler Loop was true from 64 yards at the end of the half but missed from 40 yards when he could have put the game away.
"Oviously, it was unnaceptable," Minter said of the penaty parade.
Minter is going to be peppered about health questions this week. Again, hopefully, Jackson being out on the sidelines is hopefully some sort of positive sign.
The Ravens have been unable to keep a five-man unit together up front for any substantial period of time and guard Andrew Vorhees, thrust back into a starting role due to injuries, left early in the second half (foot) and did not return, with youngster Emery Jones taking over. Smythe was helping out considerably at the line of scrimmage and losing him for any period of time would be substantial.
Humphrey has been plagued by injuries in recent years and was having a difficult time in coverage. He carries the biggest cap hit of any corner in the NFL, and 10th-highest salary, and the Titans went after his replacement, veteran Chidobe Awuzie, when he left.
There was reason to worry about Jackson in pass protection with the Titans boasting dominant defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons against a makeshift offensive line that featured rookie guard Vega Ioane making his first career start at cente r, a new position for him. Left tackle Ronnie Stanley did return from a toe injury and Simmons was held in check and the line was doing an excellent job overall.
In fact, as the game went on Simmons ended up lined up more on the end, taking aim at the tackles, with Ioane thriving under serious duress and then having to play the second half with backup QB Snoop Huntley, who had never really snapped to before with all his work this week at the new position focused on getting in sync with Jackson.
Jackson was 15-for-20 for 222 yards and two touchdown passes at the time he left the game, and he has been in tremendous form all season despite the offensive line being a problem in the past two weeks.
Rookie coordinator Declan Doyle alertly attacked the perimeter in the run game, with the Titans more vulnerable there and Baltimore best running behind the tackles. The Titans bottled up Derrick Henry, which was not surprising under the circumstances, but this was about volume and intent.
The dynamo receiver got a little help from teammates with explosive plays, but he was still something of a one-man gang again. He came into this game with every catch this season (10 receptions on 12 targets through three weeks) going for a first down. That streak snapped but he was unstoppable with Jackson, nonetheless.
Flowers caught six of seven targets before the starting QB departed, for 119 yards and a touchdown. He fully extended for a ridiculous 52-yard catch down the sideline. He had a 19 yard catch-and-run for a TD. Four of his catches went for 11 yards or more and now 13 of his receptions have gone for that length on the season.
He was utilized out of the backfield again and in the slot and on the boundary.
Minter had to embrace curbing his predilection for flooding the field with defensive backs against arguable the most tepid downfield passing attack in the NFL. We’re talking a Titans team not averaging six yards per attempt but one that could play some bully ball in the under-center run game and they showed that power on an early touchdown drive.
The coach needed to change his spots and lean into more big bodies up front with Nnamdi Madubuike back from neck surgery and he did just that. The Ravens entered this game playing dime coverage (six defensive backs) over a third of the time (second-most in the NFL) and he rolled that coverage out just five times in the first half as Baltimore took a commanding lead, 24-7, at halftime.
Minter has been playing nickel or dime 90% of the time; that dropped to 65% in the first half with the Ravens leaning on a 3-4 front more than they had all season. And it worked. Titans feature back Tony Pollard had 13 runs for just 38 yards (2.9/carry), Tennessee was always behind the sticks and chasing the game the run game was effective dead.
Madubuike’s presence was massive with the game still very much in doubt, at a time when the Titans were commanding the ball on the ground and young QB Cam Ward was looking comfortable. Baltimore led just 14-7 at the time and the Titans had four cracks on the ground from goal-to-go, they leaned into under center looks and heavy personnel and Baltimore held up.
Madubuike made the stuff on fourth down, and it triggered a 98-yard scoring drive for the Ravens that basically put this game out of reach.
Trenton Simpson continues to look speedy and instinctive at linebacker and keeps showing up at the right place at the right time. Ward tried a shovel pass that never looked like a smart play call, the ball ended up right in Simpson’s gut and he clung to it and immediately flipped field position in this game on the first drive.
Baltimore finished that drive with a Henry touchdown plunge. And at the end of the half, with the Ravens about to get the ball to start the second half, Ward connected with rookie Carnell Tate for a big gain down the sidelines but Kyle Hamilton tracked him down from behind and punched the ball loose for a fumble the Ravens recovered.
That set up the long field goal to extend the lead before the half, and was about the last time the Ravens roster seemed in tact with the wave of injuries about to come.

title: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson Questionable To Return In Second Half With Ankle Injury
full_text:
The Ravens offense was executing at an MVP level, quarterback Lamar Jackson appeared as comfortable as ever Sunday afternoon at M&T Bank Stadium and his combination with Zay Flowers looked literally unstoppable. But his day ended far sooner than anyone would have expected.
Jackson was sacked very late in the first half, just before Tyer Loop’s 64-yard field goal put Baltimore up, 24-7 at the half, and left the game with an ankle injury. Jackson’s left ankle was rolled up on awkwardly and he was officially designated questionable to return but on a wet field, with a big lead, and with some questions on the Ravens offensive line it would be very surprising to see him return.
Veteran Snoop Huntley took over, emergency third-quarterback Joe Fagnano, an undrafted rookie out of UCONN, was now one injury away from making his NFL debut and the Ravens will have to turn their attention after this game to figuring out a plan for Jackson. Obviously, his health is paramount to anything they do this season, he is essentially in a walk year with his 2027 contract carrying an $85M cap hit, and he was playing superior football to start the season in rookie coordinator Declan Doyle’s offense.
Jackson was not running much Sunday, carving the Titans from the pocket, and did have a 28-yard scamper negated to just a seven-yard gain by penalty. Jackson stepped up into the pocket on the play where he was injured, avoiding pressure but getting clipped in the lower leg from behind.
The Ravens lost top corner Marlon Humphrey to a calf injury early in the second half, and he was quicky ruled out. And blocking tight end Durham Smythe, who quicky emerged as a vital cog in this offense, was quickly ruled out with an Achilles injury.
There was reason to worry about Jackson in pass protection with the Titans boasting dominant defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons against a makeshift offensive line that featured rookie guard Vega Ioane making his first career start at center , a new position for him. Left tackle Ronnie Stanley did return from a toe injury and Simmons was help in check and the line was doing an excellent job overall.
Jackson was 15-for-20 for 222 yards and two touchdown passes at the time he left the game, and he has been in tremendous form all season despite the offensive line being a problem in the past two weeks. Jackson is a two-time MVP who won the award under two offensive coordinators and he and Flowers have formed a ridiculous combination , with that receiver being moved around more by Doyle.
According to sideline reports from the CBS broadcast team, Jackson was limping and mostly imploring his teammattes in his absence. But he was not warming up or throwing himself on the sidelines.
