title: Ravens Three Keys to Victory vs. Titans
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens are heavy double-digit favorites to come out on top in their home matchup against the Tennessee in Week 4 of the 2026 regular season.
After squandering their first opportunity a couple of weeks ago, the team is still in search of its first regular-season home victory under new head coach Jesse Minter. With a win, they'll improve to 3-1 before hitting the road for their first primetime game against the Atlanta Falcons next week.
In this showdown between two teams clearly heading in two different directions under new leadership at the top, the Ravens can emerge victorious if they follow these keys.
As fun as it would be to watch five-time Pro Bowl running back Derrick Henry plow through the face of his former All Pro teammate between the tackles, with a reshuffled interior offensive line that features rookie Olaivavega Ioane
 making his first career start at center, the wiser move would be running out wide zone and off tackle.
Thankfully, that blocking scheme is the basis for the Ravens' rushing attack under new offensive line coach and run game coordinator Dwayn Leford. Getting the Titans' stout defensive front moving laterally instead of letting them tee off and try to shoot interior gaps down in and down out would be more advantageous when it comes to establishing the run and setting up the play-action passing game.
Since the Ravens will be without four-time Pro Bowl edge rusher Trey Hendrickson and are going up against second-year quarterback Cam Ward, who is making just his 21st career start, head coach and defensive play-caller Jesse Minter should be in his bag when it comes to dialing up packages to heat him up. While Ward can make some magic happen out of structure at times when he buys some time with his legs, the former first overall pick struggles mightily when trying to throw the ball under duress.
According to Next Gen Stats , he is only completing 32% of his passes when under pressure, as opposed to 74.6% when not, and his passer rating drops from 93 to 54.6. Keeping him guessing where potential pressure is coming from with simulated looks could lead to quick wins and unblocked opportunities to get home for sacks or at least force rushed throws. Expect to see All Pro safety Kyle Hamilton and other defensive backs hovering around the line of scrimmage early and often, and making the occasional play in the backfield.
The Ravens are on a mission to snap a four-game losing streak at their home stadium and finally send the fans who show up to support them back home on a high note for the first time since Week 12 of last season. Going up against an inferior opponent in the Titans, with one of the most inept offenses in the league and one of the stingiest defenses, this goal can be achieved by jumping out to a big lead early and setting the tone with how hard they play at the point of attack and in space on offense and defense.
That looks like flying to the ball and not missing tackles defensively and finishing plays with authority offensively, whether it's blocking to the echo of the whistle or fighting for extra yards without putting the ball in harm's way. Tennessee isn't built to mount a comeback from a double-digit point deficit and the Ravens are long overdue for a game in which they dominate from start to finish and don't let up or give their opponents a shred of hope that another late collapse on their part is a possibility.

title: Both Zay Flowers And Ronnie Stanley Playing For Ravens Sunday
full_text:
The Ravens have activated receiver Zay Flowers and left tackle Ronnie Stanley for Sunday’s game against the Titans, after both were listed as questionable for Week 4.
Both offensive stalwarts have been dealing with linger injury issues. Flowers aggravated his hamstring in training camp and it forced him out of Week 1 at halftime and kept him from playing in Week 2. Stanley tried to play through a painful toe injury in Week 2 and could noy finish the game and though he traveled with the team to Brazil in Week 3 he did not play against the Cowboys.
The Ravens already ruled out top free-agent signing, Trey Hendrickson ($30M/season) after getting a procedure to correct a finger/hand issue that had curtailed his impact the past two weeks after a great debut Weel 1 at Indianapolis. They placed two centers – Ethan Pocic and Jovaughn Gwyn – on Injured Reserve this weekend, which has prompted them to move rookie guard Vega Ioane to start at center in just his fourth NFL game.
Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano remains inactive as the third quarterback , able to play only in an emergency scenario. Veteran receiver and special teams ace Chris Moore (ankle) is inactive and defensive lineman Aeneas Peebles was a healthy scratch.
Flowers caught five of six balls thrown his way in Brazil, with gains of 22, 7, 14, 14, 27, and then the run. He has two plays of 49 yards or more against the Colts in Week 1. Baltimore has two distinct offenses at this point – with Flowers and without .
Ther Total Offensive Expected Points Added with Flowers: +25.59 . Their EPA without him on the field: -3.08 . Every reception he has this season is for a first down
The offensive line is a massive issue , giving up constant pressure in the interior and also perhaps having to operate without left tackle Ronnie Stanley (toe) for a while and now also marred by injuries at center . Cultivating a deep game with targets who are already deeply in sync with Jackson and who also do not possess the combination of twitch, talent, speed and inherent connection with this quarterback is going to be challenging.
The titans are winless but do boast one of the top defensive lines in the NFL, which could create issues for Baltimore up front. Having Stanley protecting the blindside and Flowers providing the potential for explosive plays is vital.

title: Four Ravens X-Factors For Clash vs. Titans
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens will continue the 2026 regular season back at home in M&T Bank Stadium, against the Tennessee Titans in Week 4, and the difference in the game could come down to how an individual player performs when it matters most or over the course of the game by capitalizing on their opportunities when presented with them.
With a win, the Ravens improve to 3-1 and could tie for the top of the AFC North division standings, but a loss would, at worst, tie them with either the already 2-2 Pittsburgh Steelers or the Cincinnati Bengals if they lose on Sunday.
Here are four players who could wind up tilting the scales in favor of the Ravens and first-year head coach Jesse Minter.
Since the Ravens will be without four-time Pro Bowl pass rusher Trey Hendrickson this week after he underwent minor surgery on his injured finger , Green is the next man up on the edge opposite Tavius Robinson. The second-year pro spent most of the summer being hyped up and projected to take a big leap this season after falling short of lofty expectations as a rookie. He has one sack and two quarterback hits through the first three weeks, and all of those came in the home opener in Week 2.
After playing less than 50% of the team's total defensive snaps in each game thus far, that figure will likely jump to just north of 60%, like Hendrickson was averaging. The Ravens will need Green to make the most of his expanded role if they intend to rattle second-year quarterback Cam Ward in Week 4 and maintain a semblance of a pass rush off the edge while Hendrickson is out of commission.
With both of their top two centers officially on injured reserve as of Saturday, the Ravens are set to start first-round rookie Olaivavega Ioane at the position for the first time in his fledgling professional career after starting the first three games at right guard. While this is not completely uncharted territory for the first-year pro, as he played a little center in college at Penn State and finished last week's thriller snapping the ball to Lamar Jackson, being asked to play all four quarters at an unfamiliar position is a different beast entirely. Having an experienced veteran guard like Simpson lined up next to him to help call out blitzers and either adjusting or relaying changes to the protection plan will go a long way toward easing the increased mental load that comes with Ioane's temporary position change. This line has struggled for quite some time.
The two-time Pro Bowler is another player in the defensive trenches who the Ravens are going to need to step up in Hendrickson's absence. For Madubuike, who just made his 2026 debut last week in Brazil, they need him to be the force multiplier who commands more attention from the opposing offense, so that it frees up more favorable opportunities and matchups for his other teammates to make plays.
When healthy, the eighth-year veteran is an elite disruptive force in his own right as one of the best interior pass rushers in the league. Against the Cowboys, he logged three total tackles, generated two pressures and Pro Football Focus gave him the highest grade of any Ravens defender, with an overall grade of 90.1. They'll need him to continue his return to form in this game against one of the better pass-protecting units when it comes to keeping their quarterback clean and not under constant duress.
The fourth-round rookie is coming off his first career multi-catch game in which he hauled in both of his targets for a career-high 23 receiving yards and his first career touchdown. He's already been used more as a blocker than many anticipated he would be, and now he could see his snaps in the offense increase even more as his role as a pass catcher expands. His ability to rack up yards after the catch and find the soft spots in zone coverage over the middle of the field was evident in last week's win and could be put on display in this game as well.

title: Five Pivotal Ravens Matchups to Watch vs. Titans
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens' Week 4 bout against the Tennessee Titans could ultimately be decided by battles between specific position groups or individual players outperforming their counterparts on the other side of the ball.
It'll take place back in Baltimore, where the Ravens haven't won a game since Nov. 23, 2025 , against the New York Jets before Thanksgiving. The Titans have returned home victorious from their last two trips to M&T Bank Stadium, dating back to their infamous 2019 Divisional Round upset.
If the Ravens prevail, they will improve to 3-1 and could be in a three-way tie for first in the AFC North standings, depending on how the Cincinnati Bengals fare at home against the Jacksonville Jaguars this week. Here are the five matchups that can either make or break this game.
Even before they lost their top two centers on the roster to long-term injuries within a handful of plays of each other, the Ravens were struggling to consistently hold up in pass protection. It was especially evident when opposing teams sent additional pressure through the A-gaps with blitzing off-ball linebackers.
The Ravens' reshuffled interior will feature first-rounder Olaivavega Ioane making his first career start at center after starting the first three games at right guard, which will be filled in by either a rotation or one of fourth-year pro Andrew Vorhees and second-year pro Emory Jones Jr. Those three, along with veteran left guard John Simpson, will have their hands full with the disruptive defensive tackle tandem of Pro Bowler Jeffery Simmons and John Franklin-Myers. Behind them is an up-and-coming young linebacker in rookie Anthony Hill Jr., who is the NFL's leading tackler through three weeks with 34. The second-rounder has reached double figures in total tackles in back-to-back games and will likely be aiming to do that and record his first career tackle for loss going up against a living legend like former Titans star running back Derrick Henry, who spearheads the Ravens' rushing attack.
The Ravens are going up against a young signal caller who can sling the ball around when kept clean or on the move, but struggles mightily when under pressure. With four-time Pro Bowl edge rusher Trey Hendrickson out for this game after undergoing finger surgery, head coach and defensive play-caller Jesse Minter could lean more on his three-time All Pro Swiss Army Knife to muddy up the pre- and post-snap picture for Ward.
Hamilton can wreak havoc on blitzes, even if he doesn't get home for a sack, and Minter can use the threat of him coming off the edge on simulated pressures to create favorable matchups for others to bring the heat off the opposite edge or up the middle. The Ravens could also look to use more of Hamilton's range in the backend to make some plays in coverage in traditional safety alignments, especially with some of the tackling struggles his fellow safeties have had as the last line of defense.
This matchup pits one of the league's most prolific offenses against one of its stingiest defenses. Baltimore's first-year play-caller has been the orchestrator of a unit that averages 30-plus points per game, hunts and hits on explosive plays at a high rate, both through the air and on the ground, and excels at putting second- and-third-level defenders in conflict.
Saleh is an experienced defensive playcaller whose unit ranks in the top 10 in fewest points allowed per game (19.7), yards per play allowed (4.9) and passing yards allowed per game (189). However, where they've been susceptible to giving up yards is on the ground, where they rank in the bottom 10 in yards allowed per game (126.3). On Sunday, the Titans will face not only their own former franchise legend in Henry, but also the best quarterback they've seen this year, with the best dual-threat at the position in NFL history lining up next to him in the backfield with Lamar Jackson. It's pretty clear which play-caller has the tougher test in this matchup.
Minter's unit ranks in the middle of the pack in run defense, almost by design since the Ravens are among the league leaders in deploying light boxes . They pretty much dare opposing teams to run the ball at a decent clip instead of trying to push the ball downfield through the air. While that strategy has somewhat worked at times through the first three weeks, when their opponents have committed to the run, the Ravens have been gashed and pushed around on the ground.
Last week in Brazil, the Cowboys went from one of the worst rushing teams to looking like one of the best, averaging nearly five yards per carry and moving the ball at will at times, but they didn't stick with it and got pass-happy in the wrong moments. Coming in with one of the most inept and least productive offensive units in the league, the Titans might feature their Pro Bowl running back and leading rusher more heavily in this game to take some pressure off Ward to have to carry them on that side of the ball.
When he's been on the field and healthy this year, the Ravens two-time Pro Bowler has been the most unstoppable and unguardable pass catcher in the league. Flowers leads the NFL with 9.0 yards per route this season, the highest mark in the first three weeks of a season in the Next Gen Stats era , with a minimum of routes. He leads the team with 234 receiving yards and is a big play waiting to happen anytime he touches the ball.
Since Doyle lines him up from all over, including the backfield at times, the responsibility of guarding him will be an all-hands-on-deck situation for the Titans corners, especially now that his so far removed from his hamstring injury that he wasn't even given a status designation on the final injury report.

title: Jesse Minter Needs To Rethink His Defensive Fronts, Now
full_text:
The Ravens may need to start recalibrating their approach to the line of scrimmage on defense.
Especially, the next three weeks. Starting Sunday against Tennessee.
This needs to be a get right spot for this defense before bigger challenges await with Joe Burrow and the Bengals and Trevor Lawrence and the Jaguars. If Jesse Minter’s defense is still hobbling around late in games and lacking bite , and if their issues all of sudden stopping the run continue into the middle of the season, we could have real problems on our hands.
But already, not even a full month into the season, rookie head coach Jesse Minter may have hit an existential crisis. His overriding defensive principle – using the least manpower as possible at the line of scrimmage to neutralize the run while deploying the most defensive backs as possible to take away deep balls – isn’t working nearly as well as it did with the Chargers. Small sample size to be sure, and perhaps getting Nnamdi Madubuike back into heavy rotation will change things dramatically, but Minter also might need to rethink some of his aspirational goals.
Baltimore’s top corner, at least in terms of compensation , Marlon Humphrey, is struggling, and already hybrid defender Kyle Hamilton is starting to sneak back 10 or 15 or 20 yards behind the line of scrimmage with more frequency to help free safety Malaki Starks, who has not had the immediate transformation many had expected . The average NFL team has faced 13 dropbacks by a quarterback against dime coverage; the Ravens have faced 61, most in the NFL, and it hasn’t exactly been stellar for the back end and it’s definitely creating issues up front.
The Titans do not even really try to push the ball downfield, young quarterback Cam Ward is averaging just about the lowest yards per attempt in the NFL (5.7 yards per pass!) and they don’t have a real deep game. But they are slamming the ball on the ground with under center runs by Tony Pollard the last two weeks at 5.4/carry – yeah, same as their passing game! – and that’s working out well for them and the Ravens are 30th in Run Defense Expected Points Added against under center runs , and 26th in success rate.
Yeah, that could be a problem.
Minter is playing nickel or dime defense 90% of the time , and only the Rams are playing a higher percentage of dime coverage (six defensive backs), and a Cowboys team that couldn’t run on anyone carved up Baltimore for 25 carries and 139 yards at 5.6/carry with a touchdown when they had at least five defensive backs on the field. Change could be coming as we discussed with former NFL defensive back and personnel exec Bucky Brooks on “The Daily Flock” this week.
“We're seeing more under center play, more old school tactics,” Brooks pointed out. “And so you now have a defense that is not quite built for what the league is doing as people are going back to running the football and doing three yards in a cloud of dust. And so the great thing about the league, I believe every team changes every quarter after three or four games.
“You’ve got to kind of switch up what you're doing because the league will quickly catch up to what you're doing. You’ve got to stay one step ahead of the curve. And so the great coaches, the great teams, they have the ability to adapt and adjust to what they have or what they're facing. And so how soon will it be before we see Jesse Minter make some changes and tweaks to best position themselves to be able to win games?”
Again, it’s early, and QBs Tyler Shough and Dak Prescott do like to chuck the ball all over the place, but Minter has already ramped up his blitz rate by about 50% from what he did with the Chargers in order to get pressure, and that’s really the only time they are getting pressure and top edge rusher, $30M-man Trey Hendrickson, is out with a finger injury .
Baltimore’s pass defense is just 16th in the NFL in opposer passer rating allowed, so it’s not like this is working incredibly well in the secondary. And the overall run defense looks pretty putrid, especially considering the Colts trailed big in Week 1 and didn’t really run and New Orleans can’t run and Dallas wasn’t running on anyone for years before Sunday.
The Ravens have an overall Rush D EPA of -2.12 (30th) and have already allowed five rushing touchdowns and are 25th in success rate (56.5%). Things better improve quickly, with Bijan Robinson, maybe the best back in the NFL, looming in Week 5. Defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver tried to frame the issue as one of minutia this week, but I’d be quite surprised if the Ravens don’t start playing more 3-4 and even 4-3 fronts with Madubuike back.
“I thought we started slowly,” Weaver said. “A couple of times, I thought our guys had more of a pass mentality up front, and they were able to get some push off the ball. One of the things particularly, and again, this is not an excuse, we do not live in that world. But when you have a couple of walkthrough practices, particularly up front, you have to make sure, early — really in warm-ups — that you're setting your pads and you're playing with low pad level.
“It's like human nature to play a little bit higher, and I thought early in that game in particular they came out and they were lower than us, and they were knocking us off the ball, which can't happen. We adjusted — there was about a four- or five-series stretch that we played better. We're just chasing consistency throughout, making sure we start fast, and we finish stronger.”

title: Three Ravens Who Will Have Breakout Games Sunday
full_text:
This could be a decidedly ugly football game between the Ravens and Titans on Sunday.
Tennessee would have it no other way . Given Baltimore’s issues winning at home (four straight losses) and putting lesser teams away, they may have no other choice. The perilous situation on the offensive line is begging Ravens rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle to attempt some workarounds and that should involve getting some more fringy contributors more involved.
This game could be closer and stickier than the line would suggest, and we expect Baltimore to be in survive and advance mode and for the staff to understand it’s going to take more than Lamar Jackson and Zay Flowers and Derrick Henry on offense to win, and that Kyle Hamilton is going to need other highly-paid veterans to step up on that defense even with All-Pro defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike back from neck surgery.
We expect these three lesser-discussed Ravens to play a very key role in Week 4.
His snaps have decreased each week (the reserve back got a heavy load bleeding the clock in Week 1’s blowout of the Colts), but that trend is over. With an already miserable offensive line now beset by injuries, volume in the run game is imperative . And, right now, shotgun runs are much more effective for Ravens RBs (6.0/carry) than under center runs (4.7/carry) and Hill shows up more in the spread stuff.
Oh and they need to attack the perimeter more and that pays to Hill and they better sell out to keep Lamar Jackson on his feet, and Hill is their best pass protecting back by a country mile and they might want to up the tempo at times and try to grind down this defensive line, and Hill is their two-minute back.
Hill has just three targets all season; we could see him surpassing that Sunday. He could run the ball upwards of 10 times on top of it. And, with a rethink of their short-yardage approach underway , he could even show up in the redzone in ways he normally might not. Would be silly not to lean into his skillset given the circumstances of this game.
Doesn’t catch many balls and doesn’t show up consistently, but he makes them count. Finished the season latching on to some deep balls and with Zay Flowers begging to be smothered in coverage at this point, we expect Jackson to target him on several deep shots. Maybe its not more than 50 yards gained on a defensive pass interference call on an underthrown ball – it all matters and this could be a slugfest.
We couldn’t be shocked if he caught a long TD pass on an under-center play action look on an early down. We like his chances, though Titans coach Robert Saleh isn’t one to blitz or take chances and he wants to keep a top on the offense.
He made some vital contributions against the Cowboys as fellow defensive tackle Nnamdi Madibuike played football for the first time in over a year. He read a shovel pass and blew up tight end Jake Ferguson and forced a critical turnover at a time Dallas was moving the ball up and down the field on this defense.
With Madubuike still working his way back, and Calais Campbell 40 years old and on a pitch count, and Minter not loving leaning into two-gap bodies to stop the run, a lot has been asked of Jones. Wouldn’t be surprised to see him show up in the backfield Sunday. He’s played 105 snaps, most of Ravens defensive linemen, and with $30M pass rusher Trey Hendrickson out for this game, getting more interior push up front would be huge.
He stands to benefit most from Madubuike coming back and already has four tackles for a loss and four pressures. Young Titans QB Cam Ward struggles against the blitz and can get rattled and we like Jones to do some damage in NASCAR packages .

title: CJ Gardner-Johnson Doubles Down on Foolish Comment After Bills' Loss to Patriots
full_text:
It's unwarranted and unnecessary , and it looks even worse when it isn't backed by actions.
For someone who has essentially made only  one noteworthy play in four weeks, Buffalo Bills ' safety Chauncey Gardner-Johnson should focus on his own performance rather than disrespecting the opponent without justification.
Following the Bills' mistake-filled Week 4 home loss to the New England Patriots, Gardner-Johnson chose to call out the little-known wide receiver that scored the game-winning touchdown .
With the Patriots facing a 3rd-and-5 from the Buffalo 23, Maye throw one up for Efton Chism, who made a spectacular one-handed catch in the end zone. Bills' second-round rookie cornerback Davison Igbinosun had solid coverage on the play, but it wasn't good enough to prevent the undrafted wide receiver from getting winning the rep.
Chism, who is in his second season with the Patriots, entered Sunday's game with only two prior receptions for -1 receiving yard this season.
Instead of moving onto the Los Angeles Rams, who will host the Bills in Week 5, Gardner-Johnson decided to fire a verbal cheap shot at Chism and the Patriots.
"An elevated guy made a helluva catch. Probably won’t happen to him again, respectfully. I say that with a lot of confidence because it’s like he didn’t put his confidence in his best player," said Gardner-Johnson in a locker-room media scrum.
Erroneously labeling Chism as a practice squad elevation, Gardner-Johnson was seemingly attempting to discredit the Patriots' 29-26 win as flukey.
"They ain’t do [expletive] better than us. We gotta play better. And they can mark that. We’ll be back, see them again at the end of the year. So, they better have that same energy," said Gardner-Johnson.
Naturally, Gardner-Johnson prefaced his comments by stating his intention to avoid "any bulletin board material." Unfortunately, the well-traveled safety hasn't shown that ability yet as a pro.
With Buffalo being the fifth different team that Gardner-Johnson has played for over the past four seasons, the Super Bowl LIX champion has made a habit of wearing out his welcome . Back during the preseason, rookie head coach Joe Brady called him out for inappropriately live streaming from the locker room.
In case his postgame comments weren't clear enough, Gardner-Johnson decided to reaffirm his opinion on his Instagram story .
Posting a slide that shows a black screen with text overlaid, the outspoken defensive back said, "I love IGB OVER DUDE ANYDAY." He punctuated the post with "#isaidwhatisaid," and underlined the text for emphasis.
Rather than simply show support for his teammate Igbinosun, Gardner-Johnson included "dude" in a presumed reference to Chism.
Maybe Gardner-Johnson should pay more attention to his subpar performance thus far, especially when it comes to tackling against the run. Not only is he the starting safety for the NFL's 27th-ranked pass defense, Gardner-Johnson has an 18.4 individual missed tackle percentage through four games.
If Gardner-Johnson is still on the Bills' roster when they visit the Patriots in Week 13, he better be ready to walk the walk.

title: Three High-Profile Bills' Players Most Responsible for Costly Week 4 Loss to Patriots
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills missed the chance to take an early-season stranglehold on the AFC East division, and there's plenty of blame to go around.
In a game with disappointments, which include a re-injury for wide receiver DJ Moore , sprinkled throughout, the most disappointing aspect of the 29-26 loss to the New England Patriots is the failure of Buffalo's big names to deliver.
While franchise quarterback Josh Allen is responsible for the inexcusable mistake that ultimately did in the Bills (3-1) on their final possession, he wasn't the only high-profile player to have a rough day against the Patriots (2-2). Veteran left tackle Dion Dawkins and second-year starting cornerback Maxwell Hairston made multiple costly errors in the Week 4 setback at Highmark Stadium.
It's been a shaky start to his Bills' career for the 2025 first-round draft pick.
After missing important parts of an underwhelming rookie season due to injury , Hairston has looked pedestrian at best as the starting cornerback opposite Christian Benford this season. With Benford out of the lineup in Week 4 due to injury, the Patriots consistently picked on Hairston throughout a humbling performance.
Hairston was routinely beaten by wide receiver Romeo Doubs, who isn't exactly AJ Brown. Doubs cleanly beat Hairston over the middle to catch a 14-yard pass in the end zone for the game's first touchdown.
On their opening second-half drive, the Patriots abused Hairston while marching downfield for a go-ahead touchdown. First, Hairston gave Doubs a massive cushion on a 4th-and-3 play. Running a sideline out pattern, the Patriots' receiver caught the ball, uncontested, seven yards past the marker.
Then, three snaps later, he committed a back-breaking penalty. The Bills sacked Maye on 3rd-and-goal from the 2-yard line, but Hairston was flagged for a late hold in the back of the end zone. Getting a fresh set of downs, the Patriots cashed in on a one-handed catch by Doubs against Hairston in man coverage on 2nd-and-goal.
Then, with the Bills needing a stop on 3rd-and-10 in order to get one last-chance possession, Hairston failed to close on Patriots' tight end Hunter Henry, allowing the receiver to run past the sticks after the catch.
It's Year 9 for Allen, but yet the five-time NFL MVP finalist could not stop himself from reverting to back to the immature decision-making he showed far too often during his early career.
While he seemed to ignore the quick, short game in exchange for waiting too long for routes to develop, Allen did not do an adequate job of taking what the defense was giving for much of the day.
His most egregious violation ultimately cost the Bills a victory with under 2:00 remaining. After marvelously avoiding an unblocked rusher, Allen declined to reset, and he, instead, abruptly threw a low percentage pass deep down the sideline to Josh Palmer in double coverage.
The risk was entirely uncalled for, especially considering the situation. Trailing by three points, the Bills, who were working with three timeouts, faced a 2nd-and-6 from their 40-yard line.
"Just a flood concept. They went man. [I] made a guy miss, threw one up. Just throw that one out of bounds, live another day," said Allen.
Simply put, the Bills need to cash in on that two-minute drive and beat their divisional rival, especially when the game is home. Their franchise quarterback failed to deliver , and now the road ahead gets a little tougher as a result.
Is time catching up to the 32-year-old Dawkins? It's certainly a fair question to ask, especially when considering his 2025 game film isn't particularly inspiring .
The Bills' franchise left tackle looked slow, sloppy and overpowered at times during Sunday's home loss. He lost an early one-on-one battle that allowed New England to record its lone sack of the game.
Subsequently, it was Dawkins who permitted the pressure on Allen, resulting in the wild, no-look throwaway from the goal line. With Allen dropping back on 1st-and-10 from the Bills' 11-yard line, Patriots' rookie pass rusher Gabe Jacas destroyed Dawkins by bulldozing him all the back toward the quarterback.
Dawkins was flagged for two penalties in the loss, too. He committed an offensive holding infraction on a 3rd-and-3 incompletion with the Patriots declining the penalty.
Then, he put the Bills in a tough spot during a red zone opportunity late in the second quarter. His illegal use of hands turned a 2nd-and-goal from the 6 into a 2nd-and-goal from the 16.

title: Four Reasons Bills Will Regret Falling to Patriots in AFC East Matchup
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills could have gotten off to a 4-0 start in back-to-back years for the first time since their 1990s Super Bowl era. Unfortunately, they’re now 3-1 , and they have no one to blame but themselves.
From Josh Allen’s puzzling fourth-quarter interception to allowing the New England Patriots to score a season-high 29 points, the Bills squandered a massive opportunity Sunday.
The AFC is as tight as ever, with teams like the Chiefs, Raiders, Ravens, Jaguars, and Browns all off to fast starts. So, falling to New England at home for the second straight year could haunt Buffalo in the future.
If the Bills had downed the Pats, they would have been 4-0. That would have dropped New England to 1-3 and, even more importantly, three games behind in the AFC East race.
Now, Buffalo only holds a one-game lead. But the loss also coincides with what may be its most treacherous slate of games on the year on the horizon.
The Bills' next four games are visits to both the Rams and Las Vegas, followed by a home tilt with Baltimore, their bye, and then a visit to the Vikings. All four of those teams have at least .500 records, with two of them remaining undefeated on the season (Kansas City and Minnesota).
Of course, losing to the Pats in Week 4 can be atoned for when Buffalo visits New England in December. But the team the Bills see then could look completely different come Week 13.
Some of New England’s best players did not suit up in the win over Buffalo. All-Pro CB Christian Gonzalez and DT Christian Barmore both missed the game due to injury, and WR1 A.J. Brown has been on injured reserve since suffering an ankle injury in Week 1.
That’s a trio of stars for the Pats who could have a major impact on the outcome of the next outing. They could also help take pressure off New England’s young star QB.
The most egregious piece of it all is that Maye looked like a viable NFL QB again. It seriously had gotten bad for him in this recent stretch — in the last seven games coming in, including the playoffs, the Pats' QB had turned the ball over 15 times, compared to seven total touchdowns.
While he was picked off against the Bills, he had his first three-touchdown pass game, and a game with a QBR above 90, since December 2025. He had season highs in both passing yards (269) and rushing yards (54).
Buffalo still has a strong shot at winning the AFC East, according to most sportsbooks, including Bet365 , Caesars Sportsbook , and FanDuel , which all tied for the shortest odds for the Bills at -250. But they have made it that much harder on themselves by losing to New England.

title: Two Winners & Three Losers From Bills' Inexcusable Week 4 Loss vs. Patriots
full_text:
Week 3 was an ugly win for the Buffalo Bills , as they held off the Los Angeles Chargers . Week 4 wound up being an ugly loss as they again played sloppily, but the New England Patriots took advantage .
Despite being short-staffed on defense, the Patriots made life tough on Josh Allen and the Buffalo offense. Even worse was the way the Bills' defense played. Drake Maye came into this game with one touchdown and six interceptions, but threw three touchdowns and one pick (and that interception wasn't his fault).
That all added up to a 29-26 win for the Patriots as they improved to 2-2 while Buffalo fell to 3-1. With the game behind us, let's see who stood out as winners and losers for the Bills.
Buffalo was trying to preserve a three-point lead in the third quarter, and they appeared to have shut the Patriots down on third-and-goal when the defensive line crashed on Maye. New England got a fresh set of downs, however, with Maxwell Hairston being flagged for holding. Making matters worse, Hairston was beaten for the touchdown on a fade pass to Doubs a couple of plays later, allowing New England to go up 21-17.
He had a mistake earlier in the drive as well, when he gave Doubs a massive cushion on a fourth-and-three play, allowing the Patriots to extend the drive.
Buffalo signed Dee Alford this offseason , looking for a defensive back capable of playing the slot. While he's done that job well, he made his first big play of the season for the Bills on Sunday.
With the game tied at 14 near the end of the half, Alford made a heads-up interception. Romeo Doubs had his hands on the ball, but as he was going to the ground, he rolled, and the ball popped up in the air. Alford ended up with the pick, setting up a field goal that gave them a narrow 17-14 lead at halftime.
This wasn't the ideal game from Josh Allen. He had trouble moving the ball consistently against a banged-up New England defense. He finished with 253 yards and a touchdown pass, and added another touchdown on the ground. Still, he had just four yards rushing and threw a crucial interception at the end of the game that allowed the Patriots to run out the clock. This was the second week in a row where Allen had some questionable decisions, and he needs to get right before they face the Los Angeles Rams next week on Monday Night Football.
With D.J. Moore again dealing with a shoulder injury, the Bills needed Keon Coleman to step up once again. He's continued his solid campaign, with his best catch coming early in the fourth quarter. Facing a critical third-and-six, Josh Allen threw a 50-50 ball to Coleman, who was covered by Kindle Vildor. The ball was batted in the air, and somehow, Coleman remained focused and snatched it out of the air.
How did Keon Coleman make this catch?? 😱 pic.twitter.com/cjEcjGJvGb
That 21-yard play put them in field goal range, and even though the drive stalled, the Bills cut the lead to 21-20, something they wouldn't have done if not for Coleman. As if that wasn't enough, Coleman also caught the go-ahead touchdown, catching a 34-yarder from Allen.
The numbers looked fine for Khalil Shakir, who had 82 yards on seven receptions. The problem is that he fumbled the ball away late in the first half. With the game tied at 14, Keon Coleman caught a 22-yard pass to move the ball into New England territory. On the very next play, Shakir had an eight-yard reception, but fumbled it away. That was one of two turnovers on the day and both were crucial in the loss.

title: DJ Moore Injury Update Confirms Buffalo Bills WR Aggravated Previous Issue
full_text:
For the second time this season, Buffalo Bills wide receiver DJ Moore exited a game early due to injury on Sunday in Week 4.
And, just like he did in Week 2, Moore exited because of a shoulder injury. The Bills wideout got banged-up in the third quarter and did not return to the game.
Now, ESPN's Adam Schefter reports that Moore has aggravated his AC joint sprain injury. However, Schefter adds that, as of right now, the injury is not believed to be serious.
"Bills WR D.J. Moore aggravated his shoulder injury during today’s loss to the Patriots, per source. It is not considered 'a long term issue as of right now,'" Schefter reported.
The key words there are "as of right now," which means Moore isn't out of the woods yet. Chances are testing tomorrow will tell the final story.
For now, this is certainly good news for Moore, who was able to play through the injury in Week 3 but was still dealing with the effects of it in Week 4, when he only logged limited practices before being removed from the injury report entirely.
While it appears he has avoided anything significant for now, we would have to assume his status for the Week 5 contest versus the Los Angeles Rams is in serious doubt.
What Moore does have working for him is the fact that the Bills will play on Monday night against the Los Angeles Rams, so he has an extra day to get right.
With the contest on Monday, the Bills will release their first injury report for Week 5 on Thursday afternoon.
Prior to his exit, Moore recorded just one catch for 11 yards and one carry for six yards. Through four games, Moore is up to 12 catches for 178 yards and two carries for five yards.
If Moore is forced to miss time, the Bills should be in OK shape.
We already know about reliable pass-catchers like Khalil Shakir, who recorded seven catches for 82 yards on Sunday, and Dalton Kincaid, who got off to a hot start before two quiet games in a row.
But 2024 second-round pick Keon Coleman has also proven to be reliable this season. Coleman, who once looked like he was on his way out in Buffalo, had another impressive game in Week 4, with Coleman tallying a team-high 116 yards on six catches, and he found pay dirt, also.
After being in a precarious spot at wide receiver last season, the Bills are in a much better spot in 2026 now that Coleman is stepping up.
Now, if only they could keep Moore healthy.

title: Bills Biggest Takeaways From Gut-Punch Week 4 Loss to Patriots
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills were looking for win No. 4 on the season and hoped to knock the New England Patriots down to 1-3 in the process. That's not what happened, however, as the Patriots went into Highmark Stadium looking like a completely different team than we've seen all season.
Drake Maye had three touchdown passes while adding 55 yards on the ground. Romeo Doubs made life miserable on Maxwell Hairston, scoring two of the Patriots' touchdowns.
Still, Buffalo fought back and took the lead late thanks to a touchdown catch from Keon Coleman. The Patriots answered with Efton Chism II scoring the game-winning touchdown pass while Josh Allen threw a pick on his final play, ending their hopes of a comeback. Let's take a look back at this game and see a few big takeaways from the Bills' first loss of the season.
The Patriots had just six points in Week 3, but topped that halfway through the first period. Drake Maye hit Romeo Doubs for a 14-yard touchdown pass to take a 7-0 lead. That capped off a 12-play, 97-yard drive, which was the first of the game for New England.
Their offense continued to find success, scoring in the second quarter on a one-yard rush from Rhamondre Stevenson. That drive covered 63 yards on just six plays as the New England offense took advantage of holes throughout the Buffalo defense.
As many issues as they've had, the Bills' defense has been very opportunistic. They had two turnovers in the first half. The first was when Ed Oliver and T.J. Sanders were credited with a half-sack each, which led to a fumble by Maye. There was also an unbelievable interception, which was when Dee Alford picked off a pass that was in the hands of Doubs, but he lost it as he was on the ground. Alford was able to haul it in and gave the Bills the ball in field goal range, allowing them to go into the half with a 17-14 lead.
The defense continued to have issues in the second half, including the frustrating fourth-quarter drive from New England that covered 73 yards on eight plays to give them a 29-26 lead with just under two minutes to play. They also couldn't force a punt after Allen's interception, but admittedly, they were put in a tough spot. In the end, this defense is pretty rough when they're not turning the ball over.
In this game, the Bills had issues in coverage at linebacker and in the secondary, but their depth at cornerback has become a major concern. They were without Christian Benford against the Patriots, and during the game, Dee Alford was injured. That led to Damar Hamlin moving to the nickel , which is less than ideal.
Entering this game, it was already clear that they needed help at cornerback . Seeing Alford go down in this one was just a reminder of what we already knew.
We all know Joe Brady can orchestrate an offense. He's had plenty of success doing so, but in Week 4, it was clear that he still has some room to grow.
The Patriots were short-handed with defensive tackle Christian Barmore and cornerback Christian Gonzalez both injured. Despite going against a short-handed New England defense, Brady couldn't get the offense rolling. James Cook had a rough outing, which included three-and-outs on two of their first three possessions.
The second half wasn't much better, with Buffalo managing just 16 yards on their first two possessions and having eight total offensive snaps in the third quarter. Cook got rolling in the fourth quarter, which opened up the offense, but Brady has to learn how to make adjustments more quickly, especially against a team that doesn't have two of their best defenders.
For the second time this season, the Bills had to replace DJ Moore , who was injured during the game. With him out, Keon Coleman was asked to step up, and that's exactly what he did.
Coleman finished with 116 yards and a touchdown on six receptions and was huge on two fourth-quarter scoring drives. First, he caught a third-down pass that was batted in the air to extend a drive that ended in a field goal. On the next drive, he hauled in a 34-yard touchdown pass to put Buffalo up 26-21.
It wasn't enough, but Coleman is turning the corner, which could be huge for this offense.

Kincaid is having a great start to the season, his showing last week notwithstanding. The fourth-year tight end has 14 catches, 263 yards and one touchdown in three contests.
Among tight ends, Kincaid leads the way in receiving yards.
Meanwhile, Moore has also been productive, with the Bills wide receiver reeling in 11 catches for 167 yards and a score, which came in Week 1. Making those numbers more impressive, the veteran wideout did not finish Week 2 due to injury.
With everything we know about the two Bills pass-catchers, here's our fantasy football start or sit advice for both, along with our take on if you should start the Bills' D/ST.
Moore entered last weekend questionable to play with a shoulder injury but was ultimately able to suit up. This week, Moore appears to be healthier after not carrying a designation into Sunday.
Even at less than 100% in Week 3, Moore was still productive, with the Bills' wideout reeling in six catches for 67 yards. Perhaps more importantly, he emerged from the contest unscathed.
In the two full games he has played in this season (he left Week 2 early due to injury), Moore is averaging 16.8 fantasy points per game, which places him at WR10 overall, according to Fantasy Pros , if you remove Week 2.
The Patriots have been a middle-of-the-road matchup against wide receivers this season, but what makes this matchup even more favorable is the fact that New England won't have its top cornerback, Christian Gonzalez, who has been ruled out .
Start Moore with total confidence in Week 4.
Kincaid came crashing back down to Earth last week after posting just two catches for 38 yards in what was his worst game of the season.
Things may not get any better this week, as Kincaid faces a New England defense ceding the fewest fantasy points per game to tight ends.
That said, Kincaid ranks as TE5 overall, even after his disappointing performance last week.
As an elite option at tight end, you're starting Kincaid in Week 4.
The Bills' D/ST enters Week 4 ranked as the No. 20 unit in the NFL. That is not good enough to make Buffalo's D/ST a weekly starting option, so it's all about the matchup.
The Patriots have been very giving to D/STs, with New England giving up the third-most fantasy points per game.
A lot of that has to do with the mess that Drake Maye is. The Pats' signal-caller has thrown a whopping six picks and has fumbled twice.
New England's offensive line hasn't been very good, either, with the unit surrendering nine sacks, which is especially concerning for the Patriots this week with a potent Bills pass-rush that has nine sacks, six of which have come from Greg Rousseau.
If you're streaming a defense this week, the Bills are a solid option.

title: 3 Surprise Standouts for Panthers in Thrilling Win vs. Lions in Week 4
full_text:
I don't think we need to spend much time figuring out who the stars were Sunday night. Bryce Young was great, Tetairoa McMillan had a monster game, and Chuba Hubbard finally got the kind of workload I've been asking for.
But those guys aren't really surprises. What stood out to me were some of the other guys Carolina had to depend on, especially with how beat up this roster is right now.
And funny enough, two of them were guys I was pretty worried about before the game.
When Damien Lewis was ruled out, Corey Bullock was one of the first guys I started thinking about. Detroit already had a defensive front I didn't love Carolina going against, and now the Panthers were doing it without their starting left guard.
It didn't exactly start great, either. Bullock got pushed back on an early sack, and I remember thinking this might become a problem pretty quickly. Then I really didn't notice him much after that, which for an offensive lineman is usually a pretty good thing.
Carolina ended up with 445 total yards, Hubbard ran for 122, and Young threw for 329. The Panthers did all of that with Bullock filling in for Lewis, and then they lost Monroe Freeling during the game, too.
Was Bullock perfect? No, and I'm not going to pretend he was. But I said before the game that if Sunday night ended and I barely noticed him, I'd probably consider that a pretty good night.
That's pretty much what happened.
I didn't exactly hide how worried I was about Will Lee III this week. I kept thinking Detroit was going to find the rookie and just keep going after him.
Can you blame me? Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson are both on injured reserve, Lee suddenly has a much bigger role, and now Jared Goff and that Detroit offense are coming to town for Sunday Night Football. That's a lot to ask from a rookie.
I'm not going to tell you Carolina's secondary shut Detroit down because it definitely didn't. Goff threw for 412 yards, and there were plenty of times when you could tell this was a secondary missing its two starting corners.
But when Carolina needed one more play to finally get out of there with a win, Lee was right in the middle of it. He and Lathan Ransom stopped Detroit short on fourth down, and that was finally it.
After I spent most of the week wondering how Lee was going to hold up, I have to give him credit. Detroit tested him, he had some rough moments, and he was still there at the end, making one of the biggest plays of the game.
Maybe I worried about him a little too much.
I almost put Lee and Lathan Ransom together because of that last play. The more I thought about it, though, I think Ransom deserves his own spot.
Detroit finished with 452 yards, and Goff threw it 52 times, so again, I'm not trying to turn this into something it wasn't. Carolina didn't dominate defensively. Honestly, there were a few times when I wasn't sure the Panthers were ever going to get Detroit off the field.
But they got the stop they absolutely had to have.
That's probably what I'll remember most about Ransom from this game. Nobody is going to look at the box score Monday morning and talk about his night the way they're going to talk about McMillan's 192 yards or Hubbard finally getting over 100.
And they shouldn't. Those guys were great, but somebody still had to finish the game, and Ransom helped do it.
I think that's what I liked most about this win. Carolina's best players played like its best players, but with all the injuries, that wasn't going to be enough by itself.
The Panthers needed guys like Bullock, Lee and Ransom to hold things together. None of them were perfect Sunday night, and I don't think they needed to be.
Just don't become the reason Carolina loses the game.
Instead, all three had something to do with why the Panthers won it.
For this team right now, I'll take that every time.

title: Panthers Fans Serenaded Bryce Young With MVP Chants. Are They Right?
full_text:
I definitely didn't have Panthers fans chanting “MVP” for Bryce Young on my list of things I expected to hear this season. But there they were Sunday night at Bank of America Stadium, and honestly, I kind of liked it.
Maybe it's too early. Actually, I know it's too early to start handing out awards after four games. But I also don't understand why that means we have to immediately dismiss what Young is doing.
He's been really good. And I don't mean good compared to what we've seen from him before, or good because expectations weren't exactly through the roof coming into the season. Young is playing really good football right now.
So when those chants started, I wasn't sitting there thinking Panthers fans had lost their minds. I was thinking maybe they're seeing the same thing the rest of us are starting to see.
I think that's where my opinion has changed the most.
After Young threw for 361 yards and three touchdowns against Chicago, there was an easy reason to question it. Carolina was getting blown out, so of course the Panthers were throwing the football all over the place. I understood that argument, and I probably made some version of it myself.
Then he went to Atlanta and threw three touchdowns without an interception in a 34-3 win. A week later in Cleveland, he threw for 291 yards amid a 51% pressure rate and had them driving for a chance to tie before a late turnover.
Then Detroit comes to Charlotte for Sunday Night Football, and Young does it again. At some point, I think we have to stop looking for reasons why it doesn't count. Four games isn't a season, but it's not nothing, either.
This is probably what the MVP chants made me think about more than anything.
It seems like every conversation we've had about Young since Carolina drafted him has come with something attached to it. He's too small. The offensive line isn't good enough. He doesn't have enough weapons. Carolina took the wrong quarterback. Maybe he'll eventually figure it out.
I'm kind of tired of doing that.
Why can't we just say Young looks like a really good quarterback right now? I don't think that's getting carried away anymore. Through four games, that's what he's looked like.
And Sunday night might have been the best part because he didn't have to do everything himself. Tetairoa McMillan went for 192 yards and two touchdowns, while Chuba Hubbard ran for 122 yards and a touchdown, after I spent most of the week begging Carolina to give him the football more.
Give your quarterback a running game and somebody who can make plays down the field, and suddenly everything looks a little easier. Maybe I'm making it too simple, but this looked a lot more like the offense I've been waiting to see.
I'm not putting Young at the top of an MVP ballot after four games. That's not what I'm saying, and I don't think that's really what Panthers fans were saying Sunday night, either.
They were watching their quarterback play well against a really good football team on national television. They were watching Carolina win a game not many people thought it would win. After what this fan base has watched for the last few years, I'm not going to tell them they shouldn't enjoy it.
But I also think there might be a little more to those chants than just fans having fun.
If Young has a bad game next week, I'm not suddenly throwing away what he's done through the first month. And I'm done saying, “Let's see him do it again,” every time he plays well because, well, he's doing it again.
That's the part I don't want to dismiss. Maybe Young cools off, or maybe we're having a completely different conversation a month from now. We'll deal with that if it happens.
Right now, I'm going to judge what I'm actually watching, and what I'm watching is a quarterback playing some of the best football in the league.

title: Grading Carolina Panthers QB Bryce Young in Primetime Win vs Lions
full_text:
The lights were bright at Bank of America Stadium as Sunday Night Football took place in Charlotte, where the Carolina Panthers faced the Detroit Lions. This was the Panthers' first SNF game in a decade, with the last one in 2016.
Carolina needed a big-time win after losing on the road to the Cleveland Browns in Week 3, and they got exactly that. The Panthers capitalized on a poor Detroit defense and secured a 32-26 win , moving to 2-2 heading into their bye week.
Primetime football is always a spectacle, and sometimes the lights can be too bright, but that wasn't the case for Panthers QB Bryce Young. In a clinical outing, Young continued his improved season with another stellar performance.
Young completed 29 of 41 passes for 329 yards, 2 touchdowns, and no turnovers. It doesn't get much better than that for a first SNF game ever. Now Young remains the league leader in passing through four weeks, and has all the momentum in the world.
Here are the best parts of Young's elite performance.
You can't discuss Young's performance without mentioning Carolina's WR1, Tetairoa McMillan .
The Panthers came into this game shorthanded on offense, missing two of their top three receivers, Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette. Coker led the team in receiving yards until last night. That said, Young leaned on his Offensive Rookie of the Year receiver in McMillan and it paid off.
Whether it was short throws that led to yards after the catch or deep touchdown passes down the right sideline, Young put the ball exactly where McMillan needed it, and McMillan had a career night because of it.
14 catches, 192 receiving yards, and 2 touchdowns, thats as elite as it can ever get for McMillan.
BRYCE YOUNG DART TO T-MAC pic.twitter.com/0FK89Ve7zg
Young made one of the better throws of his career to McMillan, rolling to his right and throwing a ball toward the right sideline that only McMillan could grab while dragging his feet inbounds.
Carolina's offensive line is beat up. By the end of the game, there were 4 preseason starters out of the lineup. Even so, Young's pocket presence, calmness, and maneuverability were exceptional.
Young started the game 12-12, and it was clear early on that he was as sharp as he'd ever been.
Watch every throw that Young made. Lions star pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson was right in his grill for most of them, and it didn't matter. Even when he knew hits were coming, Young didn't blink, and made elite throw after elite throw.
Panthers double Aidan Hutchinson and he spins his way to a quick pressure anyway pic.twitter.com/HLFitTKPdt
This is also a major sign of improvement because Young used to be awful under pressure, but now he's brushing off hits after completions down the middle of the field.
Just about everyone was picking against Carolina in the spot (including me), but Bryce Young did what great QBs do: exploit poor defenses and attack favorable matchups.
Young never held the ball for too long; it was either a quick throw or a scramble to get it out of bounds to avoid turnovers. After a stellar performance, Young has the most passing yards for a Panthers QB through the first four games of the season in franchise history.
As far as a first SNF game goes, Young couldn't have done better, and the Panthers beat what most view as a very good team because of his play.

title: Panthers May Have Beat the Lions, But These 7 Things Actually Matter
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers entered as slight home underdogs against the Detroit Lions . They made good on their first primetime opportunity of the year, something previous iterations of the Panthers have struggled with. What are the most meaningful takeaways, though?
The Panthers were without their top two cornerbacks, but this defense had a surprisingly decent performance despite the personnel deficiencies. Having Devin Lloyd back in the middle of the defense made a huge difference in the run and pass game. He was also pretty effective as a blitzer.
The Panthers struggled to get to Jared Goff all night. When they brought extra rushers, it worked out sometimes, but if they sent four, Goff usually had all day to pick on the backup cornerbacks. That's the sort of thing that can't happen after spending $30 million a year on a star pass rusher in free agency.
Last night was a glimpse of what the Panthers' offense can be when it's all working. Through three games, it was all aerial, with the ground game struggling. This time, both phases of the offense were impeccable, complementing each other well with a dynamic and nearly unstoppable RPO attack.
We wrote this last week, but the bye week can't get here soon enough because of all the injuries. Already missing a host of starters, Monroe Freeling left the game with a knee injury. Jaelan Phillips got hurt, too. Those are losses the Panthers frankly cannot afford at this point. Hopefully, they will all get healthy during the week off.
No Jalen Coker. No Xavier Legette. A bad offensive line that lost Monroe Freeling and inserted the player who yielded the most sacks in the NFL last year. No problem for Bryce Young, who started 11 for 11 and never really slowed down. He did pretty much whatever he wanted all night long.
We're willing to put an asterisk on this one because the Lions have good pass-catchers who were facing Will Lee III and Akayleb Evans, who had a really horrible game. Still, the amount of times the Lions were able to convert on long down-and-distances was concerning and still needs to be worked on.
You could tell how big this one was for Charlotte-area fans. They were loud all night, and it caused some problems for the Detroit offense at critical junctures. Despite coming in as home underdogs, Panthers fans did not let the Lions feel comfortable once.

title: 9 Winners and 9 Losers from Panthers' Exhilarating Victory Over Lions
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers hadn't been on Sunday Night Football in 10 years. Finally given another shot, they did not waste their shot. The Panthers' offense was electric, but which players stood out on their own, for better or worse?
The Carolina Panthers are doing what Kelvin Sheppard and the Lions' defense should be doing with two backup cornerbacks. Holding the Lions' offense to field goals. The true definition of coaching and maximizing players. What an embarrassing performance. Offense CAN'T settle…
The Detroit Lions are a brutal matchup without Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson. Yet, Ejiro Evero managed coordinating with one hand tied behind his back pretty well. His stunts worked well, and the zone actually helped mask some of the deficiencies in the secondary.
Pull the plug on Luke Fortner. He just continues to struggle against line games.
The Panthers can't run the ball up the middle (especially) , and they can't keep Bryce Young safe. At the center of that Venn diagram, unfortunately, has been Luke Fortner. Tonight was no different. He got abused by the Lions' defensive front once again, and it really cost Carolina. It's beyond time to see what Sam Hecht can do.
You’re taking a couple of backers with issues in coverage this year and putting them in a mental blender early in the game. These are fast, precise, intentional, RPO designs, and the execution is great https://t.co/7Ao7ad6ldq
It's clear what the Panthers planned to do on offense, and it worked. Brad Idzik had them spamming the RPO action to attack the linebackers. It was a phenomenal plan, and the calling from Idzik was really solid to help them execute the sort of offense they had to run in a game like this one. It also seemed like Idzik learned from some mistakes last week, which is huge.
It just hasn't been Robert Hunt's year. He has struggled at times and made mistakes you just wouldn't expect from a seasoned and quality veteran. His performance may be tied to some lingering issues from the multiple injuries he suffered last year, but the mental issues continue to stack up. Those are more concerning.
MVP chants for Bryce Young.
Concern that the injuries to pass-catchers or bad offensive line play would catch up to Bryce Young this week was overblown. He had it all working despite the Lions getting decent pressure on him and having to throw to John Metchie a whole lot more than anyone would've envisioned.
The Lions are finding Akayleb Evans.
Akayleb Evans probably deserves an asterisk here, but he did not have a good game. He's elevated to starting corner against the Lions, but still. It was not pretty, and some of his mistakes, like a blown coverage that allowed Detroit to score at the half, came at bad times. He did break up a touchdown pass right after the blown play, but it was still a rough overall outing.
Last week, the injuries to the other wide receivers meant that the Browns could double Tetairoa McMillan (or set Denzel Ward on him perpetually) and make anyone else beat them. This week, the Lions had no answers for McMillan despite him once again being the only real threat in the passing game.
The Panthers would've been toast without Ryan Fitzgerald last week. This was a new week, though, and Fitzgerald was pretty disappointing. He missed two extra points, and his made kicks were not all that inspiring, either.
Chuba bulldozes his way in 📺 NBC #DETvsCAR pic.twitter.com/bmmWJU1a2t
This is the Chuba Hubbard we have been waiting for. He finally broke through, as Jonathan Stewart told us he would . With the Panthers' rushing struggles, one would think the Detroit defense would've left a lot of defensive backs to help with their passing struggles and force Hubbard to beat them. It wouldn't have mattered, as Hubbard was exceptional, as was the passing attack.

title: 3 Bold Predictions for Panthers in Crucial Battle With Lions
full_text:
I'm not going to sit here and pretend I feel great about the Panthers' chances Sunday night. Detroit is really good, Carolina is beat up, and after three games, I still don't know which version of this team is going to show up.
Maybe that's why this feels like a good week for some bold predictions. I'm not talking about Tetairoa McMillan catching five passes or Aidan Hutchinson getting pressure on Bryce Young. We don't need a bold predictions article for that.
So I'm going a little further with these.
I feel like I've spent half the week asking Carolina to give Chuba Hubbard the ball more. At this point, I might as well stick with it and predict he finally gets his first 100-yard game of the season.
Hubbard has 184 rushing yards through three games, including 82 last week against Cleveland. That's not bad, but I still don't think Carolina has really leaned on him the way I expected coming into the season.
Maybe Sunday is finally the day. There's rain in the forecast, Detroit can get after the quarterback, and I really don't need to see Bryce Young drop back 48 times again after he was pressured on 51 percent of his dropbacks against Cleveland.
Just give Hubbard a chance to get going.
That's really all I'm asking. Don't give him eight or nine carries, fall behind by a touchdown and decide it's time to throw the ball every play. Stay with him for a while and see if he can make Detroit deal with the running game.
I'm going with 105 yards for Hubbard. And if Carolina does get that kind of night from him, it should make my second prediction a little easier.
I went back and forth on this one. Part of me looks at Carolina's offensive line, sees Aidan Hutchinson on the other side, and wonders why I'm doing this to myself.
But I keep coming back to how Young has played through three games. He's thrown for 939 yards and seven touchdowns, and outside of that interception at the end against Cleveland, I think he's played pretty well.
The bigger thing for me Sunday night is finishing drives. Carolina moved the ball against Cleveland and still ended up kicking four field goals. I like Ryan Fitzgerald, but if I'm seeing him every time Carolina crosses the 30-yard line against Detroit, this is probably going to be a long night.
So I'm going three touchdowns and no interceptions for Bryce. Is that asking a lot against this Detroit defense? Probably. But if Carolina is going to have a chance late in the fourth quarter, I think that's about the kind of game it's going to need from him.
And speaking of asking a lot, let's get to the one I'm probably going to regret the most.
I know what the secondary looks like right now. Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson are both on injured reserve, and Jared Goff comes into Charlotte with eight touchdown passes and hasn't thrown an interception.
So yeah, this makes perfect sense.
I don't even know who I'm picking to get it. Maybe Will Lee III makes me look stupid for worrying so much about him this week. Maybe Akayleb Evans gets one, or maybe somebody gets a hand on a pass and the ball just happens to fall Carolina's way.
I just have a feeling the Panthers get one. That's not exactly breaking down the All-22, I know, but these are predictions. Sometimes you just get a feeling about something.
Carolina could use one of those plays, too. With Horn and Jackson out, I'm not expecting this secondary to suddenly shut Goff and Amon-Ra St. Brown down for four quarters. At some point, somebody is probably going to have to make a play that changes a possession.
Now, if you're asking whether I really think all three of these happen, I'm not going that far. If they were all likely to happen, I probably couldn't call them bold predictions.
But I don't think any of them are ridiculous. Hubbard can run for 100 yards, Bryce has already thrown three touchdowns in a game this season, and eventually somebody is going to intercept Goff.
I'm just picking Sunday night for all three.
And if I'm sitting here after the game having gotten all three right, there's a pretty good chance we're talking about something I don't think many people are expecting right now.

title: Charlotte Weather Forecast: How Panthers Could Be Impacted vs. Lions
full_text:
Of course, there's rain in the forecast Sunday.
At this point, why wouldn't there be? Carolina is already missing both starting cornerbacks, the injuries on offense keep piling up, and one of the best teams in football is coming to Charlotte. Might as well add the weather to the list.
But when I actually looked at the forecast, it wasn't quite as bad as I expected. There's a chance of showers during the day, but that chance starts dropping around the 8:20 p.m. kickoff. Temperatures should be in the low-to-mid 60s, and wind shouldn't be much of an issue.
So no, we're probably not getting four quarters of football in a downpour. But if it rains most of the day and the field is still wet by kickoff, I'm starting to wonder if that's actually better for Carolina.
I know. I've talked about this enough already.
But Carolina has called pass plays on 67.9 percent of its snaps this season, the third-highest rate in the NFL. Bryce Young was pressured on 51 percent of his dropbacks against Cleveland, and somehow he still ended up throwing the ball 48 times.
I don't really understand that.
Now, if it's wet Sunday night, maybe this is finally the game where Carolina leans on Chuba Hubbard a little more. I'm not asking for 30 carries, and I'm definitely not saying you completely change the offense because it rained six hours earlier.
I just don't need to see Young throwing it 48 times again. Give Hubbard the ball, see if he can get something going, and maybe make Detroit deal with a game that's a little slower than it wants.
Because if this turns into Goff throwing for 350 yards and Carolina trying to keep up, I don't like the Panthers' chances.
This is probably where I changed my mind about the weather.
Normally, I'd want perfect conditions. But Carolina is about to face Jared Goff and Amon-Ra St. Brown without Jaycee Horn or Mike Jackson. Will Lee III and Akayleb Evans are going to be asked to do a lot more than anybody expected a couple of weeks ago.
So would I mind a wet field slowing everybody down a little?
Obviously, Carolina's receivers have to deal with it, too. Tetairoa McMillan isn't suddenly running around on a dry field while everybody else is slipping. But Detroit has the better offense and the healthier team, so anything that makes this game a little less normal probably helps Carolina more than it hurts.
At least that's how I'm looking at it.
This is the part I'd worry about.
If the field is wet, somebody is probably going to slip. A pass might get away from a quarterback. Maybe the ball hits the ground when it normally wouldn't.
That's fine. Just don't be the team that turns one of those plays into seven points for the other side.
Carolina has enough problems trying to beat Detroit without handing the Lions a short field because somebody couldn't hold onto the football. If the conditions aren't great, I'm perfectly fine with Bryce taking the easy throw or Carolina handing it to Hubbard instead of trying to force something.
It doesn't have to look good.
I don't know if the rain is going to stick around long enough to matter Sunday night. The forecast right now says there's a pretty good chance it won't.
But I'm also not sitting here hoping for perfect weather anymore. Perfect weather means Goff gets to throw the ball around against a secondary missing its two starting corners, and I'm not sure that's the game Carolina wants.
Give me a wet field. Give me Hubbard getting a few more carries. Give me one of those weird games where nobody really gets comfortable, and it's still close going into the fourth quarter.
Would I take that right now?

title: Lions' Wobbly Defense Has Tall Order on Sunday Night vs. Panthers
full_text:
There should be plenty of points put on the scoreboard at Bank of America Stadium this evening as the 2-1 Detroit Lions visit the 1-2 Carolina Panthers. Both teams have had few problems finding the end zone this season.
Dan Campbell’s club is expected to come away with a victory against a Panthers’ defensive unit that will be minus starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson. On the other side of the ball, quarterback Bryce Young will likely be without the club’s top pass-catcher this season in underrated Jalen Coker.
Nine of NFL.com’s finest minds are the focal point of the site’s bold predictions for Week 4. As it turns out, two of the writers pointed to Carolina’s prime time clash with Campbell’s squad. Keegan Abdoo dished out some intriguing information in regards to Panthers’ pass-catchers and the Lions’ secondary.
“Jalen Coker (6’3”), Tetairoa McMillan (6’5”) and Darren Waller (6’6”) each score a touchdown on Sunday Night Football,” explained the Next Gen Stats Analyst . “ The Lions do not have a single defensive back standing over six feet tall on their active roster. In fact, this is the third-largest average height advantage for an offense’s wide receivers and tight ends against an opposing secondary in a matchup over the last decade (plus-5.3 inches).”
Meanwhile, colleague Chad Reuter echoed Abdoo’s sentiments when it came to two of those performers reaching the end zone. “Panthers tight end Darren Waller and wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan each catch a touchdown pass from Bryce Young on Sunday night against the favored Lions, who have already allowed nine passing scores this season…”
The improved Panthers’ offense—with coordinator Brad Idzik calling the plays—entered Week 4 as the seventh-ranked offense in terms of total yards per game (392.7). The key has been an aerial game that ranks first in the league in terms of yards per outing (295.7 average). Young has thrown for 939 yards and seven scores, with only two interceptions.
Even without Coker, keep in mind that two of the other four wide receivers on Carolina’s active roster are over six foot tall in Brycen Tremayne (6’4”) and Ja’Seem Reed (6’2”)— the latter recently activated from the practice squad. Besides Waller, Carolina’s tight end room also includes Tommy Tremble (6’4”), Mitchell Evans (6’5”), Ja’Tavion Sanders (6’4”), and Feleipe Franks (6’6”).
It’s also worth noting that entering this week’s action in the league, no team had allowed more passing yards per game than the Men from Motown. And as for those aforementioned nine aerial scores mentioned by Reuter, the Lions have given up exactly three touchdown passes in each of their three outings.
It’s safe to say that this clash has all the makings of a Sunday night barnburner in Charlotte.

title: 5 Key Things to Know About Lions vs. Panthers in Week 4
full_text:
A season ago, the Carolina Panthers finished 8-9 and wound up winning the NFC South for the first time since 2015. Meanwhile, the Detroit Lions’ 9-8 resume was good enough for last place in the NFC North.
In 2026, Dave Canales’s club is off to a 1-2 start with losses to the Chicago Bears and Cleveland Browns. In between, the Panthers rolled the Falcons in Atlanta, 34-3, in Week 2.
Dan Campbell’s club has won two if its first three contests, and has scored exactly 31 points in each of their first three outings. Only the Buffalo Bills (101) and San Francisco 49ers (98) have totaled more points that Detroit (93), which has also given up a league-high 31.7 points per game.
Canales’s team is extremely banged up, especially at wide receiver and at cornerback. Can the host Panthers keep pace with one of the premier offenses in the league on Sunday night?
There’s not a lot of backstory when it comes to this series due to the fact the Panthers’ first season in the league was 1995, as well as the fact that these clubs are obviously in two different divisions.
This will mark just the 13th meeting between two teams that first met in 1999. Still, Carolina has won eight of the previous 12 encounters, although the Panthers fell at Ford Field, 42-24, back in 2023 the last time the clubs met.
What’s particularly interesting is that while Detroit came away with a 24-9 victory at Charlotte in ’99 in the teams’ first encounter, the Lions have lost six consecutive road games in this series dating back to 2002. The last clash between the club at Bank of America Stadium came in Week 16 of 2022, a 37-23 Panthers’ victory in which Carolina gained a team-record 570 total yards of offense.
Detroit’s defense is giving up the second-most total yards per game in the league (416.7). However, the Lions’ pass rush has managed to total 12 sacks—led by two-time Pro Bowler Aidan Hutchinson (3.5). The Panthers will be minus left guard Damien Lewis. Rookie right tackle Monroe Freeling faces a big challenge.
Carolina has the NFL’s top-ranked passing game, averaging 295.7 yards per contest. Quarterback Bryce Young has already thrown seven TD passes, compared to a pair of picks. However, the ground game is averaging only 97.0 yards per game. The team has run the ball fewer than 25 times in all three contests.
Jahmyr Gibbs takes it into the end zone himself 💪 @NYJvsDET on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/yad3HrCqGu
He entered Week 4 ranked fourth in the NFL in rushing yards (307), second in the league in total yards from scrimmage (463) and tied for the NFL lead with six TDs. Running back Jahmyr Gibbs has scored half (6) of Detroit’s dozen offensive trips to the end zone this season, just ahead of Amon-Ra St. Brown (5).
Minus starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson, Lions’ quarterback Jared Goff could be primed for a human being. Along with St. Brown, there’s wideout Jameson Williams, and tight end Sam LaPorta. Keep a close eye on Panthers’ cornerbacks Akayleb Evans, Chau Smith-Wade, and rookie Will Lee III.
