title: Bears Look Far From Solving Running Game Issues at Close Quarters
full_text:
The coaching never ends, even in easy victories
The Bears' running game churned up the New York Jets defensive front — a defense that had been ranked seventh in average ground yards allowed at 87.3 yards a game going into the 23-12 Chicago win .
Kyle Monangai gained 146 yards and the ball control was downright montonous. Their own defensive players were getting antsy standing on the sidelines.
"It was boring. I got bored," joked Bears linebacker Devin Bush.
Not everything was seamless, though.
"There's still a lot of things we need to clean up," coach Ben Johnson said.
Jets' defense comes away with a 4th and goal stop! NYJvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/aSBLWuml0t
Heading into this week at Green Bay, Monangai's thumb injury becomes a concern but there are two other issues regarding whether they can play as effectively as they want on the ground.
The first is their goal-line or short-yardage attack, particularly on runs. It failed miserably early in the game and even had one failure late, and this had been a problem earlier this year agains the Vikings. They converted only once Sunday on their first eight chances facing 3 yards or less for touchdown or first down. A few series later, they were at 2-for-10. Monangai exploded into the end zone on fourth-and-goal from the 1. Replay overturned a few TDs in the early sequence.
"Yeah it's frustrating but, like, it's next-play mentality," Monangai said. "You know, were coming up short in those moments. We've got to have it. We know we got to do better, don't leave it into the hands of the referee. That's just stuff to improve on.
Kyle Monangai should be the #Bears ' goal line back, IMO D'Andre Swift isn't terrible in short yardage, but Monangai is stronger with a lower center of gravity
"We're going to watch that on film and make sure it doesn't happen next week."
The Bears might lead the NFL in rushing but are 5-for-8 on fourth-and-2 or less this season, 6-for-10 on fourth-and-3 or less. They went 2-for-5 on third-and-1 against the Jets, are 7-for-11 on the year in that situation, and are really bad in third-and-3 at 1-for-7. They're only 11-for-22 on third-and-3 or less.
"Obviously, we’ve got to get better in the red zone," Johnson said. "It's been really three weeks in a row that we've left points out there. So that'll be a major emphasis for us going forward, as well as the turnovers. We can't have those on offense."
Who attempts to do this will be the real question going forward. On Sunday, D'Andre Swift came out of the game and didn't return. He had fumbled earlier in the game for the second time this season and it set up a Jets field goal. Swift had a knee injury early in the week and sat out practice but had been cleared by the game.
Johnson was asked if the knee had been a reason for Swift coming out.
“No, nothing like that," he said.
Ben Johnson on if D’Andre Swift was Benched due to Injury: “No, nothing like that.” Fumble was costly. pic.twitter.com/0VpD94cnxa
Apparently it's performance-based, although it worked another way and that was Monangai was tearing up the Jets with his power running so they wanted to go to him.
"But he ran super, super hard," Johnson said. "Roschon (Johnson) came in, ran super hard as well. We really like that room and where they're at right now.
"And then, of course, you combine that with our bigs up front and the tight ends, the way that they block. It's fun to watch them go to work.”
Just not in near the goal line or in short-yardage situations.
Through 4 weeks, the Bears lead the NFL in red zone scoring attempts per game (4.8). But, they rank 30th in red zone scoring percentage. They score a TD just 42.11% of the time. Chicago is 3-1, but this area needs to get fixed, NOW. Doesn't matter who the QB is.
This needs to be corrected going forward or they'll be passing more and more on short-yardage situations, like the Bears did five times needing 3 or less Sunday. When a team must do that, they eventually lose the identity as a powerful running team with the ability to dictate to defenses.
The secoind issue is Monangai's injured thumb and whether they'll even be able to keep the same group together and try to overcome this problem. He felt like it wouldn't be a problem afterward.
As for Swift, do they bench him and go with Monangai if healthy moving forward? It seems unlikely since it was only the second fumble.
Two Kyle Monangai TDs! NYJvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Z2mrZUc1IP

title: Was D'Andre Swift Benched? What Ben Johnson Said About Bears RB's Week 4 Disappearance
full_text:
While the Chicago Bears had a strong day overall in the Week 4 win over the New York Jets, D'Andre Swift did not.
Swift carried the rock 15 times for 58 yards, which is less than four yards per carry, and he was stuffed on multiple goal-line chances.
But those weren't even the worse things to happen to Swift, as he inexplicably fumbled in the third quarter , which helped set the struggling Jets up for a field goal a handful of plays later.
After Swift lost the football, we didn't see him for the rest of the game. Meanwhile, Kyle Monangai ran wild over Gang Green.
After the win, when asked if Swift was out of the game because of injury, Johnson said that was not the case.
“No, nothing like that," Johnson said.
So, if Swift wasn't sitting for the final quarter and a half because of injury, that would mean he was indeed benched, and it's hard to argue with the logic behind that decision.
Not only was Swift's fumble inexcusable and costly, Monangai was also running a lot better than his backfield mate .
The second-year running back cooked the Jets for 146 yards and two scores on 30 carries. It was a much-needed showing for the Bears' rushing attack, which had struggled the last two games.
Monangai was also able to do what Swift couldn't, which was convert goal-line carries into touchdowns.
Swift had two chances on the first drive, but after being credited with a touchdown on two separate occasions, reviews overturned those scores and the Bears ultimately turned it over on downs.
On the very next drive, the Bears found themselves in the same situation and Monangai got stuffed once before he broke the plain.
"You gotta get the ball across the goal line," Monangai said after the game, according to Gabby Hajduk of ChicagoBears.com . "It really shouldn't have taken me that many plays... [but] I'm gonna scrap for every yard I can."
The Bears should be using Monangai at the goal line exclusively, as his power running style is a much better fit for those situations than Swift's.
After Swift's fumble in the third quarter, it was all Monangai after that, and he made the most of his opportunities, as he helped put the Jets away for good by allowing Chicago to control the clock.
"He ran hard, really hard," head coach Ben Johnson said of the former seventh-round pick. "He found some creases, turned on the gas, and threw a really good stiff arm out there.
"When you see a guy running like that, as a play caller you just want to keep feeding him. It elevates everybody blocking for him and gives the whole unit a spark, which we really needed."
For Swift's sake, we would like to say Johnson didn't put him back in simply because of how well Monangai was running, but given the fact Johnson didn't just come out and flatly say that, it's obvious the fumble was behind Swift's absence.

title: Ben Johnson Confirms Caleb Williams' Week 5 Status Ahead of Bears vs. Packers
full_text:
It didn't take long for Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson to make a decision about the Week 5 status of quarterback Caleb Williams.
On Monday, Johnson was a guest on ESPN Chicago and revealed that it will be Tyson Bagent starting for the Bears in the contest against the Green Bay Packers.
That, of course, means the Bears do not plan on having Williams ready to play by the time Sunday rolls around.
"Tyson Bagent will start for the Bears in Week 5 against the Green Bay Packers, coach Ben Johnson said on his weekly radio hit at ESPN-1000," The Chicago Tribune's Sean Hammond relayed.
"Tyson will be the guy. We'll go from there. We're in good shape," Johnson said .
This is not entirely surprising, as Williams is dealing with a Grade 2 hamstring strain that is expected to sideline him three to four weeks. So, he could be out next week, also.
What is surprising is the fact that Johnson announced this as quickly as he did after keeping things so close to the vest last week.
Johnson never officially announced the starting quarterback for Chicago ahead of Week 4, although reports surfaced saying it would be Bagent over Case Keenum, who started in Week 3.
Johnson even went as far as to troll the media for reporting the Bears' decision by officially starting Keenum , who played one single snap under center before giving way to Bagent.
Because Keenum got that snap to start the game, he was officially given not only the start, but the win, also.
"I got all these memos saying that Tyson was starting before I ever made an announcement, so I wanted to get Case out there first time," Johnson stated . "It was like his ceremonial first pitch out there. Handing off the torch."
"Good for him," Johnson said of Keenum after he was told that the 38-year-old, not Bagent, would get credited with the win. "I think the team gets credited for the win."
Bagent's first start under center was mostly a success . He went on to complete 25-of-34 passes for 268 yards, but he did not throw a touchdown and recorded one interception.
He wasn't exactly better than Keenum was in Week 3, but it was close enough that there isn't much of a conversation to have about who will start against the Packers.
"Tyson (Bagent) has earned the right to be our No. 2 quarterback. I have a lot of confidence in him," Johnson said after the game, according to The Score's Chris Emma .
While this does appear to be official confirmation that Williams is not going to play, do not rule out the possibility that this is some gamesmanship from Johnson. He could very well be trolling us once again, so be ready for anything.

title: Bears Set to End 20-Year Streak at Lambeau Field in Week 5 vs Packers
full_text:
A hot start to the 2026 NFL season has the Chicago Bears in uncharted waters. After a dominant Week 4 victory over the New York Jets , the Bears are heading into next week as -2.5 road favorites per FanDuel against the Green Bay Packers for the first time in 20 years. The last time the Bears were favored to win at Lambeau Field was Week 1 of the 2006 season, according to Brendan Sugrue of The Bears Wire.
The Bears actually started Sunday as a slight road underdog, according to CHGO's Adam Hoge , but the NFL world appears to be buying up all the Bears stock they can. Meanwhile, a narrow win over the hapless Tampa Bay Buccaneers has the Packers looking like a pretender. Remarkably, the Bears are favored despite the fact that we still don't know whether Caleb Williams will be ready to play next week.
The Chicago Bears entered the 2026 NFL season with only one mission: prove that last year wasn’t a fluke. Whether that means just making the playoffs as a Wild Card team or winning the Super Bowl, they just need to prove that their 2025 awakening on offense was a new normal and not a flash in the pan.
Through one quarter of the season, that’s exactly what the Bears have done. They’re 3-1 after Week 4, one game behind the Vikings for first place in the NFC North. Indeed, the Vikings handed the Bears their only loss so far, but that came in monsoon-like conditions at Soldier Field and Caleb Williams’ hamstring injury prevented what should have been a go-ahead touchdown late in the fourth quarter. Their other three games have all been impressive, and they're averaging 36 points per game in those wins.
Everything is coming up roses for the Bears, but the same cannot be said for the Packers. In fact, things could not be going much worse. They're still without Micah Parsons, and now they've likely lost star linebacker Edgerrin Cooper to a season-ending injury. As for the offense, running back Josh Jacobs remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List, which means he isn't playing, right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele is done for the year after rupturing his patellar tendon, and Jordan Love looks lost.
At 2-2 on the season, the Packers just look like a team in complete disarray. Not even their two wins were impressive, as one was an overtime nailbiter against the New York Jets and the other was the aforementioned win over Tampa Bay, who was starting an undrafted free agent rookie quarterback in place of the injured Baker Mayfield.
The most historic rivalry in the NFL has been flipped on its head over the last year and a half. Since losing 14 of their last 17 matchups, the Bears have now beat the Packers twice in a row, including their miraculous Wild Card win in January. They'll be looking to make it three in a row next Sunday, a feat the Bears have also not accomplished since that 2006 Super Bowl season.
Yes, for the first time since before Brett Favre first donned a green-and-yellow jersey, it seems that the Bears are clearly a better team than the Packers, and not just for this season. Even looking at the next five years, I don't think there's any coach or general manager who would take the Packers over the Bears, and there's one reason for that: after decades of incompetence, the Bears finally got the right head coach and quarterback.
Enjoy this new feeling, Bears fans. This is what having a well-run NFL team looks like. And to Packers fans, maybe seek out the Bears fans in your lives for tips on how to cope with a rudderless franchise.
Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER.

title: Ben Johnson Leaves No Doubt About Bears' Week 5 QB Decision Between Tyson Bagent, Case Keenum
full_text:
The Chicago Bears will enter Week 5 with some uncertainty at the quarterback position.
But that's only because we don't know the status of quarterback Caleb Williams, who has missed the last two games with a hamstring injury.
Williams was initially given a three-to-four week timeline because of his Grade 2 hamstring strain, and with Williams not practicing at all last week, it looks like he's headed for another absence.
If that turns out to be the case, head coach Ben Johnson made it quite clear who is going to be under center in Week 5.
"Tyson (Bagent) has earned the right to be our No. 2 quarterback. I have a lot of confidence in him," Johnson said after Sunday's victory, per The Score's Chris Emma .
As far as his review of how Bagent played on Sunday, when he led the Bears to a 23-12 win over the New York Jets, Johnson was pleased with what he saw.
"I thought he played really well today, efficient with the football," he added. "I thought he did a great job with the operation."
Johnson has always expressed a ton of confidence in Bagent, even as far back as February, when Johnson said he believes Bagent is one of the 32-best signal-callers in the NFL .
"I'm of the mind the mindset he's probably one of the best 32 (QBs) in the NFL. His preseason tape over the past few years has probably confirmed that in my opinion," he said.
Johnson made those comments while trade rumors were swirling around his quarterback. That's another aspect of Bagent playing: he could improve his stock to the point where the Bears can flip Bagent for a solid return down the road.
But, for now, he's QB1 until Williams returns.
Bagent completed 25-of-34 passes for 268 yards, but he didn't find the end zone and threw one pick. He might not have been as impressive as Keenum was in Week 3, but Bagent was very close and clearly did enough to earn the right to keep the job .
"It meant a lot. I thought the guys rallied behind me. I felt extreme faith from the coaches towards me," Bagent said. "Shout out to the defense. They shut them out completely on third down."
There were no doubt a few bad passes from Bagent, but his accuracy was sharp overall . The Bears should feel good about starting him next week if necessary, although Chicago should leave things open just in case Bagent struggles.
The shoutout to the defense was well-deserved, as the unit has now put together three impressive performances in a row , with two of those coming in the two games Chicago's backup quarterbacks have started.
The Bears knew everyone needed to step up with Williams out, and for the most part the entire roster has answered the bell.

title: Bears QB ID Game Shouldn't Be Necessary After Tyson Bagent's Effort
full_text:
Tyson Bagent's first action since 2023 didn't go quite as well as Case Keenum's did.
It went well enough, though. The 23-12 victory in a game nowhere as close as the score indicated had plenty of running and ball control but also a second straight strong passing day by a backup QB to injured Caleb Williams.
The only thing that went poorly was the first Jets interception since Aaron Glenn became coach, and the fact one media member couldn't come up with the name of John Denver's "Take Me Home, Country Roads."
“It was unbelievable," Bagent said of his start. "I'm just from a small town in West Virginia. Shout out to Martinsburg, West Virginia. Don't ask me questions like this. I already told you I will start crying, so don't do this again. But it's extremely humbling, it's an amazing experience. I really can't thank enough people. I'm only here because of those that were around me growing up, and those who are around me today."
They were playing the song over the Soldier Field loudspeaker as Bagent headed for the locker room with a 25-for-34 effort and 268 yards.
Bagent to Rome on 3rd down (ruled down by contact) pic.twitter.com/iWsimrxwSS
"Almost Heaven, West Virginia, Blue Ridge Mountains, Shenandoah River..."
"So, it meant the world to be able to hear a song like that and it's really a full circle moment," he said. "I grew up a huge West Virginia fan, really supported (Jets QB) Geno Smith throughout his years, and thought he did an outstanding job during his time at West Virginia.
"So just really a cool full circle moment, and a nice birthday present for my dad (Travis, the arm wrestler). Happy 50th birthday to the Beast. So, it's just a great weekend.”
Bagent learned he'd start very early in the week after a call at home from Case Keenum and enjoyed how they had refused to reveal to the media who the starter would be.
“Yeah, well, I was getting worked on at my house," Bagent said. "My body work person was at my house. We were getting work in on Tuesday, or no, this was Wednesday morning. And Case kind of hit me like, ‘hey man, what time are you getting in here today?’ I said, ‘I'm going to get in there at around 11, would you like me to get there sooner?’ He said, ‘yes, I would like you to get there sooner.’
"So, I told my guy to leave, and I left the house, went to the facility, got in there, and he was telling me how appreciative he was of me throughout his week preparing for his start, and I really did more of the same. He's a top-two friend, teammate, that I've ever had, and he's definitely not (No.) 2. So, I can't say enough about Case Keenum and what he means to me, what he means to really my family. I love his family. He was very vital and helpful throughout the week. But his delivery, he was just telling me that he really hopes and prays that I'm able to have a night kind of like he did on Monday and that I will and that week is going to be this week because you're starting. So, he kind of hit me with that at the end and I just gave him a big hug. I told him how much he meant to me, and then just business is business going forward.”
This snag by Rome. 👀 Perfect placement by Tyson Bagent. #DaBears #Bears pic.twitter.com/2ZiUTTBcFO
Bagent took full responsibility for the interception. Actually, it was four interceptions. The Jets picked off three more that were called back by obvious penalties. The other Bears turnover was D'Andre Swift coughing up the ball near the sidelines for a fumble.
The interception on a throw to Colston Loveland was tough for him to see.
“Yeah, 100% unacceptable on my end," Bagent said. "You have to continue to just be super clean, play in and play out. I had the crossing route to Loveland, really just have to put it out in front of him, or if I don't like it, find my check down.
Tyson Bagent showed you what he is. He can play in this league, but he’s purely a backup. There’s things he does well, but has notable limitations. Nothing more. You don’t want to rely on him for more than a game or two. And that’s ok.
"But thought that we had two turnovers today, have to be a lot cleaner in that department going forward. But yeah, 100% my fault on that, and have to be better going forward.”
What Bagent did really well was get Rome Odunze and Loveland extensively involved for the first time this season. Odunze had six catches for 94 yards, including a 37-yarder when he went to the post. Loveland made six catches for 57 yards.
For a change, they looked away from overworked Kalif Raymond, who had just two catches for 6 yards.
Ben Johnson and the Bears have won now with two different undrafted free agent quarterbacks two weeks in a row. This proves he doesn’t need Caleb Williams. Completion Percentage: Case Keenum vs. Eagles: 70.6% Tyson Bagent vs. Jets: 73.5% Time to throw (PFF): Case Keenum vs.… pic.twitter.com/KQYKFdPm6i
When finished, Bagent's place as the backup to Williams was seconded by Ben Johnson just in case anyone wondered who would start next week.
"Tyson's earned the right to be our No. 2 quarterback," Johnson said. "I have a lot of confidence in him, thought he played really well today.
"Efficient with the football. Obviously, he had the one pick, left the ball a little bit behind where he'd like to go with it, but other than that I thought he had a great job with the operation.”
So Tyson Bagent should have been picked off four times today. #DaBears #Bears

title: Bears Week 4 Stock Report: Kyle Monangai and Rome Odunze Lead 8 Surging, D'Andre Swift Falls
full_text:
The Chicago Bears improved to 3-1 on the season in Week 4 after beating the New York Jets in convincing fashion on Sunday.
The score wasn't especially jaw-dropping, but if you watched every snap you know the Bears were in full control for the entire contest, and it would have been quite the blowout if the Bears managed to convert more than just 2-of-7 red-zone attempts.
Outside of the finishing problem, Chicago's offense played well, and the defense was even better.
Now, a look at who is rising and who is falling in our Week 4 stock report that features Kyle Monangai and Devin Bush for good reasons, and D'Andre Swift for bad.
After the Bears' rushing attack struggled for the most part in the last two games, Monangai provided a jolt with his 30 carries for 146 yards and two touchdowns.
Monangai also ran through the wall D'Andre Swift couldn't at the goal line to score a few touchdowns. Monangai should easily be the primary goal-line back moving forward, and he might start taking more work away from Swift entirely.
One thing to monitor: head coach Ben Johnson revealed that Monangai has a thumb injury , so eyes on the injury report.
Swift has not been very good since Week 1. He carried the ball 15 times for 58 yards in Week 4, which is less than four yards per carry, and he could get into the end zone on multiple goal-line totes.
Making matters worse, Swift had an egregious fumble that got him benched. Johnson said that wasn't the case, but Swift didn't play the rest of the game after he coughed up the football, so what should we call it?
Whatever the case may be, Swift needs to get himself back on track or else he might be in an even 50/50 split with Monangai moving forward, or worse. That extension isn't looking too hot right now.
There were definitely some throws Bagent would like back, but he had a strong showing overall.
Bagent ran the offense well, and the vast majority of his throws were accurate and on time. There was never a sense that this game was too big for him and he was in over his head.
Bagent did throw a pick, and there was another that was called back due to injury. But there were also several accurate throws during the contest. His lack of a touchdown isn't ideal, but the Bears did a lot of running in that area.
Not everyone will agree, but we thought he did more than enough to be the clear starter going into Week 5. From there, all bets are off, though, and that should be the approach in every game that Caleb Williams misses from here on out.
The only life the Jets showed on offense was a 58-yard touchdown pass from Geno Smith to Isaiah Williams.
And guess who gave up that: Tyrique Stevenson, who surrendered 96 of the Jets' 119 passing yards on the afternoon, per Pro Football Focus .
The inconsistency we've seen out of the fourth-year corner was exactly what Dennis Allen pointed to during the offseason as something he badly needs to correct. He hasn't done that.
This was a bad week to let that happen, too, as Kyler Gordon looks like he might return in Week 5 and if Gordon returns to his job in the slot, that will push Malik Muhammad to the boundary and Stevenson to the bench.
It was clear things were headed in that direction in Week 3, though, as Stevenson was relegated to just four snaps while Muhammad played outside and Cam Lewis played in the slot.
With Lewis hurt in Week 4, Stevenson got another opportunity to show he deserves his job back and failed miserably.
Odunze has been woefully disappointing this season and things hit a fever pitch in Week 3 when he dropped a lob pass from Case Keenum that should have went for six.
Odunze showed he's better than that with six catches for 94 yards, both team-highs, in Week 4. He also reeled in a few impressive grabs, including a one-hander and another in which he took a massive hit yet held onto the football.
Motivated Dayo is turning into dominant Dayo.
Odeyingbo has been the most pleasant surprise this season and he continued that on Sunday with another sack, pressure, tackle for loss and pass defensed.
In three contests, he has three sacks and 12 pressures. Those numbers are more than he had in eight games last season, and Odeyingbo has tied his 2024 sacks total already
Odeyingbo's resurgence is a massive development for Chicago's defense.
Booker led the way with two pressures and a sack for the Bears, and he added one run stop, one tackle for loss and two QB hits.
Booker hasn't been as good as Odeyingbo, but he has been good enough as a complementary piece to a Bears pass-rush that has played better than expected this season.
Bush was exactly the do-it-all linebacker the Bears wanted when they acquired him this past offseason.
Bush was tied for the second-most tackles on the team with four, with one of those going for a loss, and he notched a sack and three run stops.
It was easily Bush's best game as a Bear.
Dennis Allen has taken a lot of flak for past defensive struggles, but there is nothing bad to say about him in recent weeks.
That's because the Bears have rebounded nicely after a terrible Week 1 showing. Chicago gave up just 157 yards of offense in Week 3, and 12 points.
The run defense was stout, the coverage was excellent and the pass-rush is getting pressure, both with and without blitzing, and that has been the story for three straight games now.
Over the past three weeks, the Bears have given up just 28 points combined, nine less than they surrendered in Week 1. We give the Bears' defensive coordinator grief when the defense struggles, so it's only fair to praise him when the unit plays at a high level.
And, there's even more optimism for this unit with guys like Kyler Gordon, Shemar Turner and Noah Sewell possibly set to return from the PUP list this week.
Caleb Williams, Case Keenum, Tyson Bagent, it just doesn't matter. Ben Johnson is going to run his offense all the same, and he's going to have success doing it.
Not everything was perfect on Sunday, but the Bears were a few failed goal-line and red-zone opportunities away from totally destroying the Jets.
That 23-12 score doesn't do justice just how much Chicago dominated on both sides of the ball.
Johnson is a special coach, plain and simple, and the Bears are in fantastic hands with him, and hopefully for a long time to come.

title: Chicago Bears Report Card in 23-12 Win Over Jets: Perfection Draws Closer
full_text:
No greater an example existed of how far the Bears have come as a franchise than the simple fact they went without punting Sunday for the first time since 2014.
It isn't so much the fact they didn't punt, but what happened and why when it last happened and what happened and why on Sunday in the Bears' 23-12 domination of the New York Jets.
On Sunday it happened because they had the ball for so long, an NFL season high total of 42:45, the most since the Bears had 44:53 in a 1997 win at Miami. They never gave up the ball to punt while possessing it and moving into scoring range.
Yet, when they didn't punt last time in 2014 under Marc Trestman, they were totally outclassed by the Green Bay Packers 38-14 and they didn't punt because they either turned it over or failed on attempts to go for it on fourth down all game. The worst thing about that game was the Packers didn't punt either. The Bears were so bad on defense that they never forced a punt.
“You guys know what next week is, enough said” Next Sunday can’t get here quick enough 😤 pic.twitter.com/S4wwttXId8
They truly have become grown into an offense now with a purpose and it hasn't mattered who played quarterback. Their head coach directs the show and they do what he dictates.
It works also because their defense has played three straight strong games after struggling in a season-opening blowout win.
After 89 plays, their most since 1999, the Bears look like a team capable of repeating for a division title even though the oddsmaker say they're No. 3 in the NFC North.
Breaking 🚨 Many #Bears players are reportedly “pissed, confused, frustrated, and enraged” that Ben Johnson is starting Tyson Bagent over Case Keenum. Would could see this decision backfire. pic.twitter.com/y43Ouv6Jk9
Even so, Ben Johnson isn't afraid to look for perfection and their inability to score at the goal line on the first drive stood out.
"It's been really three weeks in a row that we've left points out there," Johnson said. "So that'll be a major emphasis for us going forward, as well as the (two) turnovers. We can't have those on offense."
Here are Sundays' grades for a team unafraid of striving for perfection even without its on-field leader available.
Bookmark this tweet. The Bears will lose Sunday to the Jets if Bagent starts. Ben Johnson will get annoyed all week after being questioned about it, and he will then pivot to Keenum starting next Sunday against the Packers and they’ll lose again😂😂😂 Caleb will be back Week 6. https://t.co/ueK6RyvxEn
The 232 yards overall on the ground and 146 by Kyle Monangai are nice totals, though the team total isn't even close to what they gained against the Panthers in the opener. The impressive number associated with their running game is 54 rushing attempts. When a team runs 54 times, they mean business. This is a number from the Walter Payton/Roland Harper era. They pounded the Jets over and over in the second half. Their best drive was the final one when they owned it the game's final 9:16, 12 runs. Their 34 first downs resulted largely from the run game and it was their most since 1991. The only flaw in this performance was D'Andre Swift badly fumbling it away for the second time in a home game. They pulled him from the game and it had nothing to do with an injury, according to Johnson. If Monangai runs any harder he's going to hurt someone.
Not many are running it better than Kyle Monangai today 😤 NYJvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/aOzQXt1CM5
The floaty interception Tyson Bagent threw when he should have led Colston Montgomery gave the Jets three points and it was their only real mistake, although they had a few other scares. Three other interceptions got wiped out by penalty but on two of those there was no way Bagent did not know a flag had been thrown. He was definitely taking a shot on a freebie on an offsides and on another play a hold was out in the open and flagged immediately on the side of a field where Bagent was looking before throwing the interception. Rome Odunze, Colston Montgomery and Luther Burden III all got involved extensively for the first time this season. One 8-yard sack when Bagent is not quite as mobile as Caleb Williams says the pass blocking got its part done, as well.
Bears fans told me this dogshit ass WR who cant create separation, can't get YAC, drops everything and wasnt even good in college was going to "break out" this year lmao Rome Odunze sucks man pic.twitter.com/wT55TuQ7Bw
A 4.2-yard average isn't spectacular but the Bears bowed up on the running downs when it really counted and as they took control on offense the Jets had to turn away from the run. The Bears allowed a season-low 59 yards rushing. Devin Bush and T.J. Edwards filled the running gaps and the only real damage being done against the rush defense came straight up the middle on first downs.
For the first time since 2018, the #Bears defense has held opponents under 250 total yards in THREE straight games. 🔥 Dennis Allen’s defense is absolutely ROLLING right now. 🐻⬇️ #DaBears pic.twitter.com/5kvyDRVJx5
The only thing they didn't do was take it away but who needed a takeaway when the defense was allowing no first downs on seven third-down attempts, the first time they allowed no third-down conversions since 1991. They managed to prevent any downfield damage by Geno Smith until Tyrique Stevenson committed the one flaw by getting beat deep. Stevenson might have only been playing because Cam Lewis has a hip injury. Dayo Odeyingbo even had his second sack of the season and both Devin Bush and Austin Booker showed up in the sack column, as well. The Bears allowed only 118 passing yards, fewest since ... well ... the last time they played against Smith in 2025 (117).
Tyrique Stevenson gotta have this one lol pic.twitter.com/nOK89PsyfJ
Zavion Thomas' kick returns need work as he's not heading straight upfield the way he should. The return teams were responsible for two of the four flags walked off against the Bears on the day. It was refreshing when three short field goals were made by the Bears without a near block or block occurring. It helped having Joe Thuney line up on the outside on the line of scrimmage instead of rookie Sam Roush.  The Bears' coverage teams allowed three kick returns at a 25.7-yard average and they had one really effective way to limit punt returns by Isaiah Williams. They just didn't punt.
Another penalty by Roush. Just keep him off the field, he can't do anything right! #DaBears
Johnson didn't hide from the possibility of a trap game coming off Monday night and with the Packers up this week. He discussed it with the team to make sure they were aware not to come in flat. Dennis Allen is dialing it up now. Every pressure or coverage he orders is coming up right. He's like a craps shooter on a roll. Johnson's game plan knew exactly how to hit Aaron Glenn's defense on the ground, as it should because they were colleagues on the same team.
The penalty number might have been the second most impressive number. They had a season-low four and were entirely sharp despite having a short work week, playing with their third QB in three weeks, and facing a team that easily could have triggered a letdown. Johnson has them moving fast and in the right direction. The most impressive number: 14:15 of possession time in the fourth quarter. You don't allow many comebacks when the other team doesn't have the ball.
If you get these guys, I am sorry. Been a brutal listen so far Bears-Jets pic.twitter.com/anIQLuNDet

title: Bears' Ascending 'No-Name Defense' Set to Get Even Better With Reinforcements Coming
full_text:
Don't look now, but the Chicago Bears might have themselves a good defense this season.
After a terrible start to the season in the shootout against the Carolina Panthers in Week 1, the Bears have now seen their defense put together three straight fantastic performances.
The unit's latest came in Week 4 on Sunday, when Chicago gave up just 157 yards of total offense to the New York Jets in the 23-12 win. There really was no facet in which the Bears' defense did not thrive.
After the game, head coach Ben Johnson couldn't say enough good things about his "no-name defense," which he says isn't "super flashy," yet is getting the job done.
"You could almost call them the no-name defense at this point," he said. "Nobody's super flashy all over the place, yet they're playing really good football as a collective 11. They're unselfish, sound in their assignments, and just want to do right by their buddy."
"When your eyes are right and alignment is proper, you play good defense. Our physical style of play showed up across all three phases today," Johnson added.
Over their last three games, the Bears have given up just 28 points, which is nine less than they gave up in Week 1.
How's that for a turnaround?
The Bears are playing this well on defense lately and the unit isn't even at full strength right now.
Lest we forget, Cam Lewis didn't even play this week , and three players on the PUP list, slot cornerback Kyler Gordon, defensive lineman Shemar Turner and linebacker Noah Sewell are all on the cusp of returning.
Gordon, Sewell and Turner are all eligible to come back this week, and there appears to be at least a decent chance that happens, as Gordon logged three full practices last week and Turner and Sewell managed to turn in a full session on Friday.
The return to be most excited about is Gordon's. The slot corner is one of the better ones in the NFL when he's healthy and playing at his best.
The Bears could put him back into that role upon his return, and that would allow Malik Muhammad to move to the outside, where he was initially slated to play before he was pushed into the slot role with Gordon's injury. Muhammad has been the Bears best cornerback this season by a country mile.
That will lessen the reliance on Tyrique Stevenson, who appeared to get benched in Week 3 after playing just four snaps while the Bears deployed Muhammad on the boundary opposite Jaylon Johnson.
Stevenson was pushed back to the outside role in Week 4 after Lewis was ruled out because of his hip injury, which sent Muhammad back into the slot.
Of course, we mentioned Johnson without noting that the veteran has not played well this season, so Stevenson could potentially push him for a starting job if Johnson doesn't rebound.
As great as everything looks for Dennis Allen's unit right now, the potential is there for Chicago's defense to be even better moving forward.

title: Did Tyson Bagent do Enough to Keep the Bears' QB2 Job Over Case Keenum?
full_text:
Tyson Bagent guided the Bears to another win on Sunday, a dominant Week 4 victory over the New York Jets , but in a cruel twist of irony, he won't get the official credit for the win. Instead, that honor goes to Case Keenum. Head coach Ben Johnson gave Keenum the first snap over Bagent , which means he will be listed as the starting quarterback.
As frustrating as that may (or may not) be for Bagent, it points to an intense debate now raging through the NFL media and Bears fans: did Bagent do enough today to keep Keenum from stealing his role as the backup quarterback? The sample size is small, one game apiece, but with Caleb Williams' hamstring injury likely sidelining him for at least one more week, the Bears must determine who gives them the best chance to beat the Green Bay Packers in Week 5.
That said, let's take a brief bird's-eye view of the last two games and determine which quarterback deserves the QB2 role going forward.
First things first: Case Keenum's role in the Bears' upset Week 3 win over the Philadelphia Eagles was the kind of performance you see in the movies. He completed 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards and two touchdowns with zero turnovers. He deserved his moment in the spotlight. But a careful look under the hood of those numbers belied a game that could have been a catastrophe.
If you think Bagent doesn't put enough zip on his passes, you would be mortified to see some of the pass attempts Keenum made on Monday Night Football. His intended targets frequently had to turn around and slow down to catch the ball, and D'Andre Swift bailed Keenum out on a short third-dow pass attempt that nearly hit the turf in the first quarter.
We also need to talk about the close calls. Several passes that were broken up by Philly's defensive backs could have very easily been intercepted instead, and at least one of them could have been carried back for a touchdown. Keenum also fumbled early in the fourth quarter, before the Bears put the game out of reach, and was fortunate to see the ball bounce straight back up into his arms.
Yes, Keenum played a great game and deserves to remember his performance fondly for the rest of his life. But when it comes to deciding who to start in the next game, we can't get caught up in only the highlights.
Did Tyson Bagent have his struggles on Sunday afternoon? Absolutely, yes. Did he play as poorly as many angry Bears fans on social media appear to believe? Not even close. Just look at the numbers: 25 of 34 passes for 268 yards plus an interception. He didn't have any touchdowns, but that's because Kyle Monangai was an absolute beast and racked up two red zone touchdowns. He finished with a 77.2 QBR per ESPN , which is 3.1 points better than Keenum.
Did Bagent play an easier defense than Keenum did? Some will say that, but the numbers don't back it up. The New York Jets gave up the second fewest yards per game through three weeks, trailing only the defending Super Bowl champions; the Eagles came in at 12th in this stat. They also gave up the 11th fewest points per game in three weeks, five spots better than the Eagles.
At tomorrow's film review, Bagent is definitely going to be kicking himself on a few plays. But the fact is that he played a good game, and he did his fair share of work to lead the Bears to victory.
For the Bears fans who wanted to see Keenum again on Sunday and believe that Bagent played his way to the bench, I would advise you to prepare to be disappointed again next week. Head coach Ben Johnson has been very clear about how highly he thinks of Tyson Bagent, and nothing that transpired today would be enough to shake his confidence in the 26-year-old quarterback. He made a couple of bad throws, but he also made some truly impressive plays that Keenum might not have pulled off.
Keenum had his moment, and what a moment it was. But, to quote Johnson, there was a reason why Tyson Bagent ended training camp as the Bears No. 2 quarterback. If the Bears decide to rest Caleb Williams another week, and with a 3-1 record they absolutely should not feel any rush to get him back on the field, then Bagent is almost certainly going to get his first start in the historic Bears-Packers rivalry.

title: Zac Taylor Updates Injuries to Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins After Bengals’ Loss
full_text:
Injuries are back in the spotlight this week for Cincinnati. Bengals head coach Zac Taylor met with the media on Monday afternoon after watching all the tape from yesterday. Tape that tested all of Cincinnati's pass-catching depth.
The team basically has two wide receivers healthy right now after Tee Higgins (groin) and Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) couldn't finish the 22-17 loss.
Taylor gave the latest update on both talents. Chase is still in concussion protocol and likely will be for most of, if not the entire week. Higgins is "day-to-day" according to Taylor. The veteran head coach left the door open for Higgins to play this week against Miami.
On the Bengals' final drive, Mike Gesicki had to start taking on outside receiver duties because Cincinnati was so undermanned at that position. Only Mitchell Tinsley and Dohnte Meyers are healthy enough to play wide receiver on the active roster.
Expect Ke'Shawn Williams to get a ton of run in practice this week, and Cincinnati may have to sign another WR off the street just to make sure they have enough healthy bodies against the Dolphins this Sunday.
Even with all the receiver injuries, Cincinnati still passed 54 times for 428 yards in a very unbalanced offense. They ran it just 15 times for 23 yards, one of the lowest rushing totals in team history.
"We don't want to rush for 23 yards. We don't want to go (just) 15 carries. That's not what we want to be about. I thought we did a good job adjusting to how we had to play the game as the game unfolded," Taylor said on Sunday. "You can call 30 runs, but when you feel like sometimes you're only going to get two yards a carry — now you're second-and-eight, third-and-seven — and that's not a fun way to play the game.
"You're not admitting defeat — that's the way the game went for us in the second half, and we had to play that style of game. It doesn't mean that next game we can't run the ball 40 times, but I'm not going to look at it and say, 'Man, we should have called 15 more runs.' If it wasn't effective and you feel it, and you feel like you've got a really good rhythm in the pass game — let's just keep attacking in the pass game, and that's where it went."
Cincinnati has Tuesday off before getting back to practice on Wednesday.

title: Bengals Rushing Performance in Loss to Jaguars Was So Historically Bad It Belongs in a Museum
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals turned in a historically inept rushing performance Sunday afternoon against the Jacksonville Jaguars, amassing just 23 yards on 15 carries in a 22-17 loss.
It not only was the lowest yardage production in the Zac Taylor era, it was the third lowest in franchise history.
The only two totals that were lower were 4 yards on 16 attempts in a 37-0 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in 2000 (leading to head coach Bruce Coslet quitting the next day), and 14 yards on 16 carries in a 13-10 win at Pittsburgh in Week 16 to clinch a playoff berth.
The 15 rushing attempts Sunday were tied for the sixth fewest in the Taylor era.
And the 1.53-yard average was the second lowest of the Taylor era and fifth lowest in franchise history.
If you take away Joe Burrow’s scrambles and sneak for a touchdown, Bengals running backs Chase Brown and Samaje Perine combined for 17 yards on 12 carries.
"The run game definitely wasn’t there today," Brown said. "We’ve been taking a lot of pride in making that better and being better in that area. We’ll be able to watch the tape and learn from it and be better next week. But unfortunately, we just weren’t efficient in the areas that we could choose.”
Taylor echoed Brown's disappointment and explained why he gave up on calling runs against the Jaguars.
“We don’t want to rush for 23 yards. We don’t want to go 15 carries,” Taylor said after Sunday’s loss. “That’s not what we want to be about. I thought we did a good job adjusting to how we had to play the game as the game unfolded. You can call 30 runs, but when you feel like sometimes you’re only going to get 2 yards a carry — now you’re second-and-eight, third-and-seven — and that’s not a fun way to play the game.
“You’re not admitting defeat — that’s the way the game went for us in the second half, and we had to play that style of game,” he continued. “It doesn’t mean that next game we can’t run the ball 40 times, but I’m not going to look at it and say, ‘Man, we should have called 15 more runs.’ If it wasn’t effective and you feel it, and you feel like you’ve got a really good rhythm in the pass game — let’s just keep attacking in the pass game, and that’s where it went.”
Through four games, the Bengals have 83 rushing attempts. That ranks 30th in the league and will drop to 31st when the New Orleans Saints have their fourth attempt tonight against the Atlanta Falcons.
Of the 12 teams with the fewest rushing attempts in 2025, only one – the Steelers – made the playoffs.
In 2024, only one of the bottom 14 made it (Houston Texans).
In 2023, only one of the bottom nine (Kansas City Chiefs).
Balance is critical to success.
Since 2000, there have been 106 coaches who lasted at least 48 games (roughly three seasons).
Taylor ranks 100th in rushing attempts per game with 23.8.
His career win-loss record is 54-65-1.
The only coaches who ran the ball less were (career win-loss record):
Jim Caldwell, 23.3 (62-50)
Robert Saleh, 22.9 (20-40)
Ken Whisenhunt, 22.6 (48-71)
Rod Marinelli, 20.4 (10-38)

title: Tee Higgins Leads All Bengals in Pro Football Focus Grading From Jaguars Loss, Tight Ends Struggling
full_text:
The Bengals fell to Jacksonville 22-17 on Sunday in a penalty-filled contest where Cincinnati's offense fell flat. Pro Football Focus graded it all across 70-plus plays of action for both sides.
Starting on offense, Cincinnati got another great game from Tee Higgins, who led all Bengals with an 89.9 overall grade. Four other Bengals chalked up 70-plus grades on offense: Joe Burrow (83.3), guard Dalton Risner (75.2), wide receiver Dohnte Meyers (73), left tackle Orlando Brown Jr. (70.4).
At the bottom, the tight ends continue dragging down the offense as three of the bottom six grades came from that position. They weren't the worst, though, as guard Dylan Fairchild (47.9) checked in with the third-worst team grade overall on offense or defense. He had a rough day with three penalties mixed in.
The rest of the bottom six went in this order: Tight end Tanner Hudson (51.7), TE Erick All (51.8), center Ted Karras (52.6), running back Samaje Perine (53.2), and TE Drew Sample (57.5).
On defense, the Bengals highs were lower and the lows even lower despite holding the Jaguars to just 22 points. Defensive tackle Jonathan Allen (80.6) led all Bengals defenders with his strong grade. Four other Bengals defenders had grades of 70 or higher: defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence (76.4), defensive end Cedric Johnson (75.6), linebacker Barrett Carter (74.7), and safety Jordan Battle (70.7).
Among high-snap players, DJ Turner II (40.9) had his worst game of the season and had the lowest grade of any Bengal. Oren Burks (27.8) was worse, but he only suited up for 11 snaps. The rest of the sub-55 grades went in this order: Defensive end Cashius Howell (41.5), defensive tackle T.J. Slaton (50.9), defensive end Myles Murphy (52.2), safety Russ Yeast (52.3), and linebacker Demetrius Knight Jr. (52.4).
Cincinnati is licking its wounds and hoping to get a lot of names healthier over the coming days. They face one of the worst teams in the NFL this Sunday as Miami awaits, but it's a road game in Florida early in the season. Some of these numbers will have to get better and stay as strong to get back above .500 this week.

title: Three Overreactions From Bengals' 22-17 Loss to Jaguars
full_text:
After losing to the Jaguars and falling to .500 on the season, it feels as though any momentum the Bengals had after a 2-0 start has completely stalled.
There are many overreactions after the teams Week 4 loss, however there are some that could hold more weight than others.
Here are three overreactions following the Bengals painful loss to the Jaguars.
It is safe to say that many completely lost faith in Zac Taylor and his ability to lead the Bengals to the promised land after Sunday's week 4 loss. Taylor is one of the longest tenured head coaches in the league currently behind only names such as Andy Reid, Sean McVay, and Kyle Shanahan.
Unlike those names though, Taylor is the only one with a losing record of 59-66-1. The others also have multiple Super Bowl appearances throughout their respective tenures, where Taylor's only appearance happened in 2021.
Another large reaction following Sunday's loss is that the team must trade for another playmaker, whether it be on offense or defense. Jordan Battle in particular struggled heavily against the Jaguars and has shown little to no progress in a contract year. After injuries to both Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, there have been calls to acquire a name such as Marvin Harrison Jr. from the Cardinals.
Of the players available for the Bengals to acquire, Harrison makes the most sense as he has failed to make an impact in Arizona due to poor quarterback play. He would immediately give Joe Burrow another weapon on offense, and set the Bengals offense up with a dynamic receiver trio they have missed ever since Tyler Boyd left town.
Joe Burrow completed over 70% of his passes for 428 yards and a touchdown on Sunday. Those impressive stats however do not tell the full story as Burrow tossed two crucial interceptions that ended up as the difference in the game.
This has caused some to question whether or not Burrow is the same quarterback he has been throughout his career as turnovers have occurred much more often than they used to. Last season after returning from injury, Burrow tossed a costly pick-six that ultimately ended any remaining hope to the Bengals playoff aspirations. This season he has now found himself involved in two different errors that cost the team possible victories both last week, and now recently during Sunday's loss to Jacksonville.
With this recent string of mistakes, Burrow's performance's are now going to be a key storyline to monitor going forward until we see him regain his past excellence.

title: Winners and Losers from Bengals Loss Against Jaguars
full_text:
The Bengals could not overcome their own miscues and fell to 2-2 on the season after the team's 22-17 loss to the Jaguars.
Here are three winners and four losers from Sundays loss at Paycor.
After Ja'Marr Chase left the game, Higgins took matters into his hands to lead the Bengals receiving core with 11 catches for 157 yards off 16 targets. Unfortunately Higgins did not finish the game as he left late in the fourth quarter with a possible groin injury.
With both Higgins and Chase now dealing with injuries, the Bengals receiving core is extremely thin.
In a game where the defense forced an early three and out and the crowd hit otherworldly levels of loud, Zac Taylor played conservatively on the offense's first possession. On 4th & 1 at midfield with the offense finding momentum early in the drive, Taylor opted to try and draw the Jaguars offsides. The Jags defense stayed disciplined, Taylor accepted a delay of game penalty and punted on 4th & 6.
This is a game where Taylor should have been as aggressive as possible out of the gate to make a statement that this team recovered from last week's loss.
What an emergence from Dohnte Meyers today. Meyers finished with 7 catches for 82 yards including a diving first down grab on a 3rd & 16 and impressive contested grab on the final drive of the game.
Mitchell Tinsley made a couple impressive plays in his Bengals return as well with his best being a 29-yard sideline toe-tap catch on the final drive. Both Meyers and Tinsley are in line for big roles on the offense, especially if both Chase and Higgins miss time.
A Myles Murphy sack setup the Jaguars offense for a 3rd & 18 and put the defense in position to force Jacksonville's offense off the field on consecutive drives early. Battle however had an inexcusable missed tackle on Jaguars tight end Brenton Strange that allowed him to convert for a first down extending the drive for a field goal later.
On what ended up as the game-winning score for Jacksonville, Battle took a poor angle against running back Chris Rodriguez on a 25-yard touchdown run. His play from this game warrants questions as to whether or not Kyle Dugger should start over him when he returns from injury.
Hill had pressure on him entering Sunday to perform well in the slot and matchup against Parker Washington for the Jaguars. Needless to say he did just that as Washington ended the day with only three targets, and one catch for seven yards.
Burrow and the offense failed to get into the endzone on what could have been the game-winning drive after failing to convert on 4th & 10. That is not why Burrow is a loser from this game though as he tossed a bad interception in the red-zone on a drive where the Bengals could have gained a lead early in the 4th quarter.
Failing to establish any positivity in the run game forced the Bengals offense into being as one-dimensional as possible. Chase Brown and Samaje Perine both accounted for only 12 total carries and 17 yards on the day, with Burrow scrambling three times for six yards.
In the past the offense has managed to cover up a poor run game because of playmakers like Chase and Higgins at receiver. Now with both battling injuries and possibly missing time, it has to emerge as a key component to the offense, something that feels like a pipe dream following this performance.
The Bengals travel to Miami next week to take on the struggling Dolphins, and are attempting to enter their Week 6 bye 3-2.

title: Mike Gesicki Takes Blame for Missed Chance on Possible Game-Winning TD From Joe Burrow
full_text:
Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow got the look he wanted and made the throw he needed to squelch – if not drive a stake through the heart of – any debate about his clutch gene.
Trailing by five with 1:44 to go, Burrow walked into a huddle that was missing wide receivers Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, who were felled by a concussion and adductor injury, respectively.
But Burrow needed just three plays to take the Bengals from their own 17-yard line to the Jacksonville 21.
The first pass went to a player who was on a different team seven days ago.
The second went to a guy who was playing out of position and learning his new responsibilities by having coaches draw and diagram plays for him during the timeouts.
And the third pass landed in the hands of a receiver who was playing in a different league in a different country this time last year.
Burrow and the Bengals were on the cusp of a game-winning drive with no Chase or Higgins.
On second and 10, Burrow – who had already thrown one red-zone interception in the fourth quarter – had what he thought would be a touchdown pass nearly turn into another interception when tight end Mike Gesicki, who was playing Higgins’ role as outside receiver, made a wrong turn.
“We just had a little miscommunication there,” Burrow said. “A little miscommunication.”
Gesicki admitted that communication breakdown was on his end.
“It was a play that because of personnel stuff, normally that's, that's Tee running that,” he said. “So when I went in, I moved to Tee’s spot. I felt the corner heavy inside. I’m supposed to cross his face. I didn’t.
“I learned that (play) on the sideline,” he added. “There’s no excuse for it. I was just trying to make a play. It is what it is.”
Gesicki and Burrow had already hooked up once for a score on a 15-yard pass with to cap the opening drive of the second half, drawing the Bengals within 13-10.
Burrow was expecting Gesicki to cross in front of Jacksonville cornerback Travis Hunter, and if he had, he likely would have hit him just outside of the 5-yard line with a chance to take the ball into the end zone for the go-ahead score.
Instead, Gesicki went vertical and Hunter nearly got his hands on the ball.
“Whether we’ve got two receivers (left), I trust those guys to go make plays,” head coach Zac Taylor said. “Joe obviously trusted them. He gave them some balls on some one-on-one tight coverage situations where he trusted them.
“Mike G’s playing outside receiver at points,” Taylor added. “These guys just wanted to go win the game. They're doing whatever it takes to win.”
If Gesicki makes a right-hand turn, as the play called for, the conversation about the Bengals – and especially Burrow – is drastically different.
Imagine leading a game-winning drive in the final 100 seconds with two of the best receivers in the game unavailable, not to mention the absence of any semblance of a run game.
Instead, the narrative grows and the championship hype slows.
At least outside the building.
“I’ll go to battle with him every day if that’s what we’re going to get,” Taylor said of Burrow’s performance. “The communication during the game – just how he played in the pocket, the throws he saw, the plays he made, the plays guys made for him and the protection.
“I thought he fought hard in the pocket,” Taylor continued. “Losing Tee and Ja’Marr … I thought out guys handled it really well. To say that I’m concerned? In no way, shape or form am I concerned.”

title: 'This Isn't Armageddon' - Joe Burrow Not Panicking After Bengals Offense Falls Flat Against Jaguars
full_text:
Joe Burrow had another great outing on Sunday ... in a loss. Cincinnati's most important player tallied two total touchdowns and 428 passing yards in the 22-17 loss to Jacksonville .
He did it with only three healthy wide receivers for much of the game and a losing streak mounting, but he's staying even-keeled entering what should be the easiest stretch of the season against Miami, Baltimore, Tennessee and Atlanta coming up across the next four-game chunk.
Cincinnati can't keep losing one-score games along the way.
"We had our opportunities in the last two weeks, but certainly this isn't Armageddon or anything. We're still in a great spot and feel really good about our team," Burow said. "Come back to practice next week, get better, and that's what the NFL is all about. You can't ride the roller coaster from week to week. You're going to win some, you're going to lose some. Obviously, you want to win every single one. You're going to fight like hell to make it happen, but we're not going to ride that roller coaster."
Cincinnati was short all those pass catchers and his offense still only ran it 15 times for 23 rushing yards, one of the worst running days of the Burrow era.
He had to toss it 54 times to tighten the slack.
"It's just like we would have if anybody else was in there," Burrow continued. "Those guys made plays. I've said that this is the deepest room that we've had. Thank God we got Mitch (Tinsley) back this week. He really came in and played great and made some big-time plays for us. Obviously, Dohnte (Meyers) did too. Mike (Gesicki) is going to be Mike. He's going to find the spots and be creative in his routes. And Tanner (Hudson) went in there and did a good job as well.
"So we got so many pass catchers we feel really good about. I think they really did step up today. I don't know how many yards we had, but it felt like we were completing the pass and moving the chains."
Luckily, none of Cincinnati's injuries seem like long-term issues, with most concussions knocking players out for one game, maybe two max depending on the severity. Chase shouldn't be out long.
Both sides of the pass defense equation will be back to full strength soon, and Burrow may need to dig a little deep for wins to keep pace in the process.

title: 'There's No Excuse' - Zac Taylor, Bengals Won't Blame Key Factor For 2-2 Start
full_text:
Cincinnati isn't dropping injury excuses after the 22-17 loss to Jacksonville. The Bengals fell to 2-2 on the season and are in last place in the AFC North with the result.
They only had three healthy receivers by the end of the game and may have to go sign another one off the street this week, with Ja'Marr Chase going through a concussion he suffered early in the loss.
Zac Taylor knows his team was close again to beating a good team, but one thing or another led to their demise. Injuries weren't the only issue, as they had a bunch on defense as well, but that unit played very well.
"Well, Ja'Marr's a big part of the plan, but again, they could have lost one of their better players, and they got to adjust. So I don't want that to be the story," Taylor said. "That's what this league's about: winning or losing, and so there's no excuse, try to go out there and win. We came up a half yard short or whatever it was. It's probably the way the guys put us in position to potentially win the game. We just came up a little short, but we got playmakers on this team.
"So whether we got two receivers in a game, I trust those guys to make plays. Joe (Burrow) obviously trusted them. He gave them some balls and some one-on-one type coverage situations where he trusted them. Mike G(esicki) is playing outside receiver at points. Like these guys just they just wanted to go in the game. They're doing whatever it takes to win."
Cincinnati has its easiest game of the whole season in Week 5 when it travels to face the winless Miami Dolphins, but they have to get right in the coming days and start stacking wins as part of arguably the most competitive division in the NFL this season.
The one-score, clutch moments need to be more sound for a roster that is banged up.
"It's disappointing that we came up short because we had our opportunities and we didn't fully take advantage of them until now we're two and two. We got to own that and bounce back next week," Taylor said.
Cincinnati travels to face Miami next week at 1 p.m. ET.

title: Instant Takeaways: Joe Burrow's Rally Falls Short, Bengals Lose to Jaguars 22-17
full_text:
The Bengals had a chance to establish themselves as one of the AFC's top teams, instead they fell back to the pack.
Joe Burrow and the Bengals fell to the Jaguars 22-17 on Sunday at Paycor Stadium.
Burrow led the Bengals downfield for what would've been the go-ahead touchdown with 50 seconds left, but Chase Brown was tackled one yard short of the first down to end it. Burrow completed his first three passes on the drive and got the ball quickly downfield. The drive stalled in the red zone.
Cincinnati appeared to be on their way to taking a lead at the start of the fourth quarter, but that didn't happen.
Burrow threw an interception to Foyesade Oluokun on the second play of the fourth quarter with the Bengals just 10 yards away from the end zone. The defense held the Jaguars to a punt, but that was Cincinnati's chance to climb out of a 13-3 hole that they were in earlier in the game.
Here are our instant takeaways from the loss:
The Bengals were lifeless for most of this game. The crowd wasn't engaged because they didn't have much to cheer for. Cincinnati stayed within striking distance, pulling within 13-10 early in the third quarter, but untimely turnovers, penalties and mistakes got in the way.
Cincinnati falls to 2-2 on the season and have more questions than answers after Sunday.
Burrow completed 39-of-54 passes for 428 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. He was hit on the first interception while throwing and it came up short. Jourdan Lewis made the easy interception. The second one felt like a backbreaker.
The Bengals were just 10 yards away from tying the game and likely taking their first lead. Instead, Jacksonville got the ball with the lead.
Outside of the turnovers, which are impossible to overlook, Burrow played well. He hung tough in the pocket and delivered the ball with accuracy for most of the game.
Ja'Marr Chase caught three passes for 27 yards before being knocked out of the game by Ventrell Miller. The Jaguars linebacker hit Chase with Jarrian Jones already making the tackle. Jones grabbed Chase's facemask and was twisting him down. Miller came in late and delivered the hit on Chase.
Chase was officially declared out with a concussion at the start of the third quarter.
Ja’Marr Cause took a monster hit here. He walked off under his own power and is in the blue tent pic.twitter.com/e8AE28VpgG
Tee Higgins led the way on offense, finishing with 11 catches for 157 yards. He suffered what appeared to be a leg or groin injury late in the game while catching a ball on the sideline, but return to action a few plays later.
Mike Gesicki had one catch for 15 yards and a touchdown. Dohnte Meyers caught six passes (seven targets) for 67 yards.
The run game was awful. Chase Brown had nine yards on eight carries. Samaje Perine had seven yards on three attempts and Burrow had six yards on three carries and a touchdown.
Brown did have 10 catches for 62 yards, but the Bengals' run game was non-existent.
The defense was shorthanded on Sunday, playing without safeties Bryan Cook and Kyle Dugger. They were also without starting nickel Jalen Davis.
Overall, they held up well enough, but couldn't get off the field late in the game to give Burrow and the offense a chance at the win. They did hold up following Burrow's ugly fourth quarter interception and got the ball back to the offense with less than two minutes left in regulation.
Missed tackles are still a major issue for this defense. Jordan Battle led the way in that department, which included a missed open field tackle on 3rd-and-18 early in the first quarter.
The Bengals travel to Miami to play the Dolphins on Sunday, Oct. 11 at 1 p.m. ET.

title: These 3 Trades Could Set Browns Up For Deep Playoff Run This Season
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are atop the AFC North standings.
Sitting with a 3-1 record through the 2026 season's first four games, the Browns look like a well-rounded, high-upside young team.
However, while there are plenty of talented pieces already on the roster, there are still moves the front office could make to polish this team as the year continues to tick on.
Here are three moves the Browns could make to round out the roster ahead of the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline:
Marvin Harrison Jr's time in Arizona should come to a close at some point this season.
Stuck behind a loaded offense headlined by tight end Trey McBride, who already has 46 targets, 242 yards and two touchdowns to begin the year, Harrison Jr.'s future as a Cardinal has a dark cloud over it. In comparison, he has just 13 targets, 85 yards and one touchdown.
In 2024 and 2025, he combined for 1,493 and 12 scores. His best season, by far, was his rookie campaign. However, it seems like he may not be able to replicate such efforts unless he joins a new squad.
And the Browns could be that destination.
If the Browns' front office decides to move on from wideout Jerry Jeudy, they could make a move for Harrison Jr.
Bringing the 6-foot-3, 220-pound, 24-year-old back to the Buckeye State could be a perfect way to save his career. Marrison Jr. would also get a chance to work with a young offense, with wideouts Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion balancing out his game.
The Browns are also building up a strong future, and adding Harrison Jr. to that now could make him a staple for years to come.
The Commanders aren't in a good position.
After losing starting quarterback Jayden Daniels to an injury early in the season, the team sits at a measly 1-3 record. They've only scored 88 points and have given up 122.
Payne, a one-time Pro Bowler, hasn't been able to generate much productivity in the backfield to begin the year, especially with such a lackluster defense around him. He has eight tackles, zero for a loss, three quarterback hits and 12 pressures.
As long as he keeps up the pressure, eventually the numbers will grow.
But doing so in Washington is going to be difficult.
With the Browns looking to establish a No. 2 next to Mason Graham, and potentially take his spot for the next few weeks due to an injury suffered in the Thursday night victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers , Payne fits the mold.
The 29-year-old is searching for a long-term extension, and Cleveland could be the team to offer him one to be a staple on an already strong defense moving forward.
If the Commanders do make some moves to reset at the deadline, dealing Payne to Cleveland for a few picks could end up on their plate.
Even if the Browns don't bring in a body to fill his void, Jeudy is likely on his way ou t by the time the deadline hits.
The front office has shown that they have younger, more impressionable wideouts, with rookies JC Concepcion and Denzel Boston already taking a good chunk of targets offensively. Even outside of those two, tight end Harold Fannin Jr., the entire running back room and even Isaiah Bond have seen increased opportunities through the first four weeks.
And Jeudy sits with just eight targets, five catches and 62 yards.
At 27 years old, he has plenty of time to continue growing, but it seems that he doesn't fit the Browns' future plans. The rookies and second-years have taken his opportunities.
In order to get the most out of the Browns this season, and give a bigger workload to guys the team are trying to develop, trading away Jeudy gives the Browns the best opportunity to move forward.
He may not be worth too much, especially now, but freeing up his cap hit will also help big-time.

title: Browns Insider Ends Conversation Surrounding a Shedeur Sanders Trade
full_text:
The Browns are first in the division and they get 10 days to recover for the upcoming game against the New York Jets, but that is not the main conversation in Cleveland.
Rumors have begun to swirl that the Browns were open to trading backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders ahead of the trade deadline on November 10.
Sanders was initially believed to be named the starting quarterback as early as Week 3, but Deshaun Watson has played too well and the season has shifted to competing this year.
As Watson has stabilized the quarterback position, the Browns could attempt to trade Sanders to get additional draft capital and allow him to play for a quarterback-needy team.
Dillon Gabriel is scheduled to come off the injured reserve list soon and the Browns will need to trim the position group down to three. Gabriel has been praised for his understanding of offense and if Sanders be traded, then he would step in as the backup.
However, Browns’ insider Daryl Ruiter says that Sanders is staying in the orange and brown . Todd Monken has liked Sanders’ development in his offense and the position still remains an uncertainty in the future. Although Watson has played well and the team is winning, he has had struggles with injuries in his career. Watson has not played a full season in a Browns’ uniform.
Sanders is one play away from entering the game and taking over the offense.
The front office owes it to the coaching staff and players to win as many games as possible this season after their first-place start .
If Watson goes down with an injury or his performance declines, Sanders provides the team with the best chance to win. He was in a quarterback competition with Watson in the preseason and has been on the sidelines for the first four weeks. Gabriel was not considered to be the starter at any point in the offseason.
Watson is not contractually obligated to be on the Browns roster next year and Sanders is on a cheap rookie contract. The Browns are winning themselves out of a draft position to be able to land a top guy in college.
The roster is showing that they are ready to compete and the team needs a capable starter for next season. Sanders provides the best option at quarterback next season should Watson not return and they cannot draft a replacement.
As quarterbacks get injured during the season, teams will contact other teams about their backups. The league saw J.J. McCarthy get traded to the New York Giants for a fifth-round pick. McCarthy was a top-ten pick when he was drafted and Sanders was plucked in the fifth round.
The compensation the Browns would get for Sanders will not be worth it as the pick would be in a very late round and they no longer need to rely on those draft picks to contribute to the team.
Sanders has handled his backup role with grace and should the Browns need to rely on him, there should not be much of a drop-off.
The Browns are winning now and moving on from Sanders would hurt the team more than help their future.

title: What the Browns Need To Do To Stay Atop the AFC North Standings Moving Forward
full_text:
Ever since the AFC North was created back in 2002, the Cleveland Browns have never won the division.
In fact, the last division win they had was almost 40 years ago in 1989.
After the week four victory against the Pittsburgh Steelers, the Browns sat in sole possession of first place in the AFC North.
Here are some things the Browns will need to do for the remainder of the season if they want to rewrite history:
Who are the 2026 Cleveland Browns?
Right now, they are a young team with a first-year head coach. Yet somehow they are winning games.
If the Browns can nail down who they are and what it means to be a Cleveland Brown, they can run with that juice for the rest of this season.
The main example of the last time the Browns truly had a culture and identity was in 2018 when former Brown Jarvis Landry gave that iconic speech in an offseason meeting.
Last time the #Browns were featured on Hard Knocks included this viral moment from Jarvis Landry: pic.twitter.com/0GVVSnFCR5 https://t.co/bXAOV89xww
At times this season, we have seen the Browns pull off some incredible plays and scoring drives. In the same breath, we have also seen some moments of pretty ugly football.
The AFC North is by no means an easy division to win. Some people around the league even consider it the toughest division based off of how tough each team plays.
If the Browns want to claim the title of division champs, they need to find ways to get themselves out of offensive slumps
Head Coach Todd Monken needs to string his guys together throughout the game and motivate them to find new ways to be successful.
In the first four games, the Browns have 43 penalties for 297 penalty yards.
Averaging over 10 penalties per game is a recipe for failure, especially when they get to those hard-fought, close divisional games.
Additionally, there have been other moments where the offensive line lets a defender scream through gaps untouched, the defense gets beat deep, and special teams makes errors like turning the ball over on a kickoff.
Good football teams don't make the simple mistakes. If they do, they find ways to climb themselves out of the hole.
The last thing, and maybe most important thing the Browns need to do is to not give up no matter what.
In years past, Cleveland has been known to get themselves in a bad spot in games. From there, you could clearly see from the couch at home that the guys had lost hope and given up that week.
This falls on the shoulders of Monken. No matter what, you can't give up. Not with a quarter left, two minutes left, or even 10 seconds.
You have to play a full 60 minutes of football.
There's nothing more Browns fans want than seeing the team do well.
If the Browns can string together some wins, beat the AFC North rivals, and finish the season on a high note then maybe a division win is in the books
Regardless, hopefully Browns fans enjoyed the time the team sat in first place during the 2026 season.
