title: Why the Browns Need to Cut Ties With This Quarterback Before the Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are 3-1 and winning, but success has only made their quarterback dilemma more complicated.
Deshaun Watson has led the team on three straight game-winning drives and Shedeur Sanders has served as his backup. The Browns were thought to use the season to build for the future, but the future is now and the team is ready to win.
Dillon Gabriel is eligible to come off the injured reserve list and the front office has to make a decision in the quarterback room. Gabriel last played in the preseason against the New England Patriots, and threw for 186 yards with three touchdowns.
Although it was against backups and players that did not make a roster, he did look like the best quarterback in the preseason games. After the game, Gabriel was surprisingly placed on the injured reserve , making him ineligible for the team’s first four regular-season games.
It was believed that should Watson have lost the first two games, then he would have been benched for Sanders. He has earned the starting quarterback role and will keep playing as long as they are winning.
Sanders has had four weeks learning how to get through preparation under Todd Monken.
Sanders could be a trade candidate, but the NFL has shown that there has been little interest in the high-profile backup.
The New York Giants traded for J.J. McCarthy rather than checking in on Sanders. The rest of the other teams passed on him for four rounds in last year’s draft.
Gabriel should be the odd man out. It would be unwise to use three roster spots on quarterbacks, especially because Gabriel does not bring a high chance of becoming a star in the league.
The Browns have also used talented rookie Taylen Green as their emergency quarterback and his ability has too much upside to part ways in his rookie year.
They cannot afford to keep four quarterbacks on the roster going forward as it would take a roster spot away from another position on the team.
Although the Browns thought they bought enough time to evaluate and allow the play on the field to dictate the quarterback situation, the surprise start to the season changed everything. The Browns are winning, and that is all that matters.
When Gabriel comes off the injured reserve list, cutting him is the move to keep the momentum rolling.
And if not, Cleveland better be prepared to make some other sort of move to justify the roster spot.

title: Harold Fannin Jr. Reveals the Work Behind the Browns’ Late-Game Execution
full_text:
Harold Fannin Jr. described the Browns’ 27–24 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers as a statement for a team that had to overcome obstacles and execute in a tense finish .
Cleveland’s tight end had three catches for 27 yards and a touchdown, and his postgame comments pointed to the preparation behind the offense’s work.
“I mean, obviously, feeling good. Beat all the obstacles. We’re juiced up, we’re pumped. I don’t know, just excited, proud of the guys, played their tails off. It was good to see all our hard work come out,” Fannin said.
The second-year tight end was asked what was working suddenly between him and quarterback Deshaun Watson.
“You know, it’s simple: practice. Talking through things…Deshaun (Watson), got me the ball; I just went out there and caught it.”
The Browns had trouble getting the offense going at times , and Fannin said the team needed to be more efficient and stay on schedule.
“Just got a little bit off schedule. We just gotta, as you said, first downs, be more efficient.”
That efficiency mattered late, when Cleveland’s offense took the field for its final drive. Fannin said the players did not need an extended conversation before heading out. They had prepared for these types of situations during training camp.
“I mean, not much for there to be said. We knew what time it was. You know, obviously throughout camp, we did situational. We already knew what the moment was; we just gotta go out there and do it.”
Fannin also celebrated kicker Andre Szmyt, who connected on a career-long 56-yard field goal. The kick helped secure the victory, and Fannin said he appreciated the pressure that comes with Szmyt’s job.
“Words can even explain it, man. I’m proud of him, you know. People don’t even think about all the stress that goes into it. But every time, he goes out there and does his job. I’m very proud of him, I love him, man, and [I'm] excited to see him do something that great.”
Asked how the Browns will handle the inevitable outside noise, Fannin returned to the same theme of preparation and steady work.
“Just keep coming to work every day ready to work, and you know, don’t settle. Just keep coming to practice and keep working hard.”
The Browns will look to improve their record to 4-1 when they travel to MetLife Stadium next Sunday to face the New York Jets. Kickoff is scheduled for 1:00 p.m. ET.

title: Browns Went from Disaster to 3-1 as Todd Monken Reveals what Fueled the Turnaround
full_text:
Todd Monken didn’t pretend he saw the Browns’ 3-1 start coming.
“I’m human,” Monken said. “If you said that’s the way we’d start the season after the way we’ve worked, I would’ve said you’re nuts . And if you said we’d be 3-1 after that first game, I’d say you’re nuts, but that’s a credit to our players because all they do is just work. They didn’t blink. That week after was a little chippy, and that was a good thing. They were not happy with the way we played, and sometimes, that’s good.”
That frustration gave Monken something to build on. The Browns weren’t happy with their performance against Jacksonville , and their response showed him how much the work mattered to them.
Cleveland has since found ways to finish close games . Monken noted that the Browns have been on the winning side of three one-score games, while emphasizing that their work is far from finished.
“We’re nowhere near where we want to be or where we’re going to be, but we’ve got the right guys and the right mindset every single day to attack it, which gives you a chance,” he said.
The victory over Pittsburgh offered another example of how Cleveland has handled adversity.
The Browns endured a lengthy opening drive, 14 penalties and multiple turnovers. Denzel Ward’s interception helped change the momentum, giving Cleveland an opportunity to get its offense going.
Monken knows how dangerous it is to leave an experienced quarterback like Aaron Rodgers within striking distance. Even when the Browns built a lead, Pittsburgh kept forcing them to respond.
“But you’re right, the resiliency of our team to keep fighting and to not blink, that’s the bottom, don’t flinch,” Monken said.
He traced that lesson back to his days as a graduate assistant under Lou Holtz at Notre Dame. Nearly four decades later, it still applies.
“Absolutely don’t flinch, and our guys have not flinched,” Monken said.
Still, surviving mistakes doesn’t mean accepting them. Cleveland’s penalties remain a concern, particularly the infractions that happen before the snap.
“And especially the pre-snap penalties, that’s something we control, that’s got nothing to do with them, it’s got everything to do with us,” Monken said.
Monken said he hasn’t deliberately made “believe” the team’s rallying cry . He has emphasized trusting the process, playing physically, giving effort and staying connected.
The belief has developed as players and coaches have watched that work produce results.
“So, when you watch the guys work as hard as they work and connect like they connect with each other, there’s going to be a growing belief in what they’re going to show on tape, every time you take the field,” Monken said.
The coaching staff has had to respond, too. Monken said the Jacksonville game reinforced the need to be aggressive defensively and continue adjusting the scheme.
“We’re always under construction,” he said.
At 3-1, the Browns have given themselves a promising start. Monken’s confidence comes from the way his players return to work, even with plenty left to fix.
“I just think our guys believe in the staff, and the staff believes in them, but then you’ve got to go out there and do it.”

title: The Good, the Bad, the Ugly From Browns Win Over Steelers on TNF
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns moved to 3-1 after beating the Pittsburgh Steelers 27-24 in a memorable Thursday Night Football showdown.
Here are a few moments from the game that stood out in both good and bad ways:
Watson resembled his former Houston self in several moments, especially in the first half and again at the end of the fourth quarter. He led the Browns on a game-winning drive that ended with a field goal by Andre Szmyt.
The 31-year-old quarterback completed 24 of 33 passes for 268 yards, with one touchdown, one interception and one lost fumble. Watson needs to address his turnover issues, since both turnovers occurred in the second half and kept the Steelers in the game.
One of the main reasons why the Browns came out with a win was getting Aaron Rodgers on the ground. The Browns recorded five sacks, with five players each getting one. Maliek Collins, Mike Hall, Sam Williams, Isaiah McGuire and Adin Huntington.
The Browns' defensive line quickly pressured Rodgers, and even when they didn't sack him, they still applied enough pressure to force incomplete passes.
It's hard to find negatives when the Browns beat the Steelers, but the biggest concern is the injury that defensive tackle Mason Graham sustained in the first half. Graham has been the best defensive player heading into the Week 4 matchup against the Steelers, with four sacks this season. Unfortunately, he will miss time due to the injury.
The good news is that Graham did not suffer a season -ending injury. The Browns reported on Friday that he has an MCL sprain and an ankle sprain, and he will be week-to-week as he recovers.
It's brutal to see Graham miss time, as he looked like one of the best defensive tackles in the NFL so early in his second NFL season.
The Browns are finding a way to win games, even though they can't always avoid penalties. Cleveland had 14 accepted penalties against them on Thursday, and that doesn't even count a few penalties the Steelers declined. One play in the first quarter saw three penalties on the Browns' defense.
Cleveland needs to address its penalty issues, as it may start to catch up to the Browns. Penalties almost cost the Browns in the last two weeks, and while they didn't lose, it will become a problem soon if they aren't careful.

title: Viral Cowboys-Texans Photos Show How Dangerously Close Dallas Came To Brutal Loss
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys were close to losing once again in the Week 4 game against the Houston Texans, but you might not be aware exactly how close that loss was.
The Cowboys got off to a putrid start to the game, climbed back into it and took a lead in the fourth quarter, lost that lead with just over two minutes remaining in the game, and then recovered it with just 40 seconds left on the clock.
But, of course, things can never be even remotely easy for Dallas. The Texans drove up to midfield and put themselves in position to throw up one last prayer that, thankfully for the Cowboys, fell incomplete.
One glaring mistake on the play was that Malik Hooker didn't bat the ball down when he had an opportunity to do so, and that almost proved to be disastrous.
Based on a photo making the rounds on social media, it's quite clear the Cowboys just barely averted disaster, as Texans wide receiver Jaylin Noel was maybe a toe and certainly a fingertip length away from breaking the Cowboys' hearts.
Jaylin Noel likely had his foot out of bounds, but this is a testament to how precarious these Hail Mary situations can be when the ball isn't batted down immediately. https://t.co/qIFoocGD78 pic.twitter.com/vyui09FMAv
Here's yet another angle before that which showed just how close the Texans were to pulling off a miraculous victory.
. @HoustonChron photo from @coomerchron of the final Hail-Mary play. Didn't realize it was that close. pic.twitter.com/BGw26nP1Jr
Had the Cowboys lost like that, it would have been time to just pack up shop and call it a season.
That would have been two brutally devastating losses in a row for the Cowboys after the last-second debacle that was the Week 3 loss to the Baltimore Ravens, when the Lamar Jackson hit Zay Flowers for a long completion with just one second left, which allowed Tyler Loop to kick the game-winner.
Losing on a Hail Mary to the Texans would have been even worse, but would anyone really be surprised with the way this season has gone thus far? Hard to say we would have been.
The Cowboys' defense is still not playing good enough , as evidenced by the 30 points it allowed on Sunday.
Granted, things got better as the game progressed after Dallas' unit was getting torn to shreds by Houston's passing attack early on, but the Texans still managed to throw for nearly 350 yards and the defense completely folded on Houston's nine-play, 87-yard drive that put the Texans ahead again with 2:23 left.
Thankfully, Dallas' offense was able to bail the defense out, but as we saw in the photos above, the defense nearly wrecked that.
If there was one positive to take away from the defensive effort in Week 4, it's that Dallas' unit completely shut Houston's rushing attack down to the tune of 19 carries for 62 yards, with David Montgomery gaining just 24 of those yards on 10 carries.
However, we even have to be skeptical of that, as the Texans weren't running the ball effectively going into the game.
Long story short: Dallas' defensive showing on Sunday did nothing to quell our fears about the unit.

title: Joey Porter Jr.'s Comments About Cowboys Debut Will No Doubt Frustrate Steelers
full_text:
Before his trade from the Pittsburgh Steelers to the Dallas Cowboys last week, there was no shortage of controversy surrounding cornerback Joey Porter Jr.
Porter sat out training camp on the PUP list with a supposed back injury. He was activated before the cutdown deadline , but he did not play over the first three games, at least in part because of, again, a supposed back injury.
However, upon being traded to the Cowboys , that back injury was miraculously gone, as Porter wasn't even on the injury report for Dallas this past week. He was, however, on Pittsburgh's before being traded .
In all seriousness, it's quite clear at this point that Porter's back injury was not the cause of his absence over Pittsburgh's first three games and the inability to get a contract extension was.
After his Cowboys debut on Sunday , Porter said it "took a lot" to get ready to play on Sunday after he only had days to prepare following the trade.
But Porter was extra motivated to get ready to go because, as he says, he wanted "to be out there with my guys."
“It took a lot,” Porter said, according to Joseph Hoyt of The Dallas Morning News . “But I’m a dog at the end of the day. And I want to be out there with my guys, so I had to prove why they got me here, and I felt like I did that today.”
The Steelers and their fans are not going to enjoy reading that. After all, clearly Porter was much more motivated to "be out there with my guys" in Dallas than he was in Pittsburgh.
What will be even more frustrating for the Steelers and their fans to hear is the fact that Porter is going to play for the Cowboys for the rest of this season without a new contract , something he obviously wasn't willing to do in Pittsburgh.
“Bet on myself. You got to always have that at the end of the day, and that’s what I’m doing,” Porter said in the lead up to Week 4.
The Steelers were certainly in no position to trade Porter. He was a big piece of their defense and Pittsburgh does not have an in-house solution to replace a No. 1 cornerback.
But Porter really left the Steelers no choice, as they didn't want to pay him what he wanted and he just wasn't going to play for them without a new contract.
“Definitely. It was a hard process," Porter said of contract talks. "A lot of ups and downs. Definitely felt disrespected. Definitely felt undervalued. But that’s old news now.”
As a result of everything that has transpired, from Porter's holdout to his comments since joining the Cowboys, he will no doubt be public enemy No. 1 in Pittsburgh for a long time to come.
And his dad, former Steelers linebacker Joey Porter Sr., isn't exactly endearing himself to his old fan base, either, as Porter blames the Steelers and not his son for how things ended.
When it comes to Porter's performance in his Cowboys debut, he did exactly what Dallas acquired him to do. Porter completely shut down one side of the field, as he was only targeted once and did not allow a completion in 19 coverage snaps, five of which came against Houston's No. 1 recevier, Nico Collins.

title: Cowboys Report Card in 34-30 Win Over Texans: Dallas Still Not Good Enough Despite Victory
full_text:
It certainly wasn't pretty, but the Dallas Cowboys still managed to escape Reliant Stadium with a win over the Houston Texans on Sunday afternoon to get back to .500.
Things were not looking promising early on, as Dallas stumbled out of the gate on both sides of the ball. However, the Cowboys showed some resiliency in the second half and avoided what would've been a disastrous 1-3 record.
Now, let's dive into the details and check out the grades we gave to Dallas in all facets on offense and defense.
Dallas' passing attack struggled mightily in the first half.
Dak wasn't particularly sharp, and the offensive line did not hold up its end of the bargain over the first two quarters, as Prescott was under pressure regularly and took way too many hits .
The Texans finished with three sacks and 26 pressures in all, per Pro Football Focus .
Prescott and Co. turned it around big time in the second half and things were much different, which allowed Dallas to overcome its two-score deficit and win the game on a late fourth-quarter drive.
CeeDee Lamb's performance was legendary, and George Pickens had two very big catches, also.
Javonte Williams punching it in three times saved this one. Otherwise, the Cowboys would have gotten a failing grade.
Williams barely averaged three yards per run as the offensive line once again struggled to open up lanes for him to run through. It was a far cry from what we saw last week.
Unfortunately, it wasn't a far cry from what we've seen all season. The Cowboys have now failed to successfully run the football in three of four games. Hopefully things improve when Tyler Smith returns, which could be this week.
C.J. Stroud could have knit a sweater in the pocket in the first half, as the pass-rush was non-existent and, of course, that allowed him to pick apart Dallas' suspect secondary and zone defense. Stroud ultimately finished with 347 passing yards and two touchdowns.
The Cowboys did show some life against the pass in the second half. The coverage was a bit better, a few drives not withstanding, and there was more pressure and even a few sacks, with Rashan Gary recording one, which was his first since Week 8 of last year.
One of those drives was the one that allowed the Texans to take the lead back late before the offense saved the day, so the pass defense proved unreliable in a big spot.
Joey Porter Jr. did his job shutting down one side of the field in his 19 coverage snaps, but DaRon Bland was a total liability once again.
Cobie Durant can't return soon enough, and Shavon Revel needs more snaps over Bland, also.
A good showing from the run defense?! What timeline are we in?
The Texans averaged less than four yards per carry, and David Montgomery barely broke two yards per tote.
However, we're not sure how much of this was a good game from the run defense and how much was the Texans simply not being able to block adequately for the run, as Houston was terrible on the ground going into this game.
Nevertheless, the numbers were positive and that's all we can ask for at this point from Dallas' usually putrid unit.
The Cowboys failed to convert on two field goals, with one of them getting blocked and Brandon Aubrey simply missing the other. Dallas allowed 106 kick return yards on four attempts to Jaylin Noel, with one of those going for 53 yards.
KaVontae Turpin had a few impressive returns himself, with one kick return going for 48 yards, which helped set up a touchdown drive. Bryant Anger also ripped off almost 59 yards per punt and dropped two inside the 20.
Even still, that wasn't enough to overshadow what was another bad day overall on special teams for the Cowboys.
Sorry, there are no more moral victories for a coaching staff that has struggled all season long.
Christian Parker still has no answers for how to slow down teams through the air, and Brian Schottenheimer's play-calling continues to be more of a hinderance than a positive for the offense. Dallas' coaching staff can't even get things figured out on special teams.
This is just not a well-coached team right now,  and that's even more glaring with the Cowboys' talent deficiencies in all three phases.

title: Cowboys Must Pursue Chargers Trade Candidate Identified By Adam Schefter
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys emerged from their Week 4 game against the Houston Texans with a win , and we saw a better performance from the pass-rush.
After sorely lacking over the first three games with just two sacks, the Cowboys had that many in Week 4, and the team had 20 pressures in total, according to Pro Football Focus .
But the fact that we're even remotely excited about a two-sack effort shows just how low the bar is in Dallas. The bottom line is the Cowboys need to be exploring any and all avenues to get better in that area between now and the trade deadline.
ESPN's Adam Schefter discussed some players he views as trade candidates and among them was Los Angeles Chargers edge rusher, Khalil Mack.
"Last year of his contract on a team that is not winning," Schefter said of Mack. "The Chargers need to turn it around to keep him. If not, they'll be getting calls about his availability."
Hard to argue with the logic there.
The Chargers are a total mess right now at 0-4 and their chances of making the playoffs are the slimmest of slim. Only one team has ever made the postseason after an 0-4 start and that was the 1992 San Diego Chargers.
Mack has already contemplated retirement before, so chances are that's a real possibility after this season. Knowing that, Mack will likely want to be moved to a team that gives him a chance to win should Los Angeles continue to stink.
With the respect the Chargers have for him, and with the team's desire to get something for Mack before he possibly retires and leaves the Chargers with nothing to show for it, Los Angeles will probably oblige.
Plenty, even at 35 years old.
The future Hall of Famer has notched three sacks through four games this season, which is one fewer than the Cowboys have combined. His 13 pressures rank 15th among edge rushers.
Mack was very good last season, also, with the nine-time Pro Bowler notching 5.5 sacks in just 12 games.
So, not only does Mack have something left in the tank, he might have more in his tank than anyone else in the Cowboys' edge rushers group.
Since we've already established trading for Mack is a no-brainer for the Cowboys, it all comes down to cost, even though we're pretty sure Jerry Jones will stop at nothing to improve this defense.
We would estimate Mack will cost a fourth-rounder and maybe a late-round selection. We would usually say he's worth more, but considering there is a chance he'll only be a half-season rental given his retirement odds, that's what we're going with.
We could see Los Angeles fetching a third-rounder, but only in a deal in which they send the other team back a Day 3 pick.
With Jerry seemingly all-in this season, we could definitely see the Cowboys springing for either one of those types of deals at the deadline.

title: Cowboys Breakout Star Just Shut Down Two of NFL’s Best Pass Rushers
full_text:
While preparing to face the Houston Texans this past week, the Dallas Cowboys had one primary area of concern. Houston boasts an elite defensive line led by Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter.
Both pass rushers are capable of taking over a game and can ruin a drive in a single snap. While they both made plays on Sunday, neither was able to stop the Cowboys from putting up 34 points . As a team, they generated pressure and Dak Prescott was sacked three times, although he lost just 11 combined yards.
One of the reasons the defensive line wasn’t as impactful as Houston hoped for was the performance of Tyler Guyton. The third-year left tackle had some highs and lows throughout his first two seasons in the NFL, but has been a breakout star in 2026 .
On Sunday, he spent most of the day lined up across from Hunter and as Patrik Walker shares, Guyton was dominant . He faced Hunter 32 times, going one-on-one 87.5 percent of the time. Hunter managed just two pressures and didn’t sack Prescott once while facing Guyton.
He didn’t see Anderson as much, but was still able to hold his own when matched up with the All-Pro defensive end. Guyton faced Anderson eight times and had no help on any matchup. He surrendered one pressure, but Anderson didn’t record a sack against Guyton.
There were another 12 snaps where Guyton faced different members of the Houston defense and he was just as impressive there, giving up zero pressures and zero sacks.
Both Anderson and Hunter had a half-sack in this game and Anderson came dangerously close to forcing a huge turnover. None of that happened when they were lined up against Guyton.
As much praise as the Dallas offensive line deserves for holding up against the Texans, they’re about to get even better.
All-Pro left guard Tyler Smith has been out for the first four weeks of the season after having thumb surgery. He’s eligible to return from IR now that he’s sat out four games, and there’s a chance he could play Thursday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Even if he’s not ready due to the short week, Smith’s return is near and that will put another stud next to Guyton, which will be another boost for this already explosive offense.

title: Good & Not So Good From Cowboys' Hard-Fought Week 4 Win Over Texans
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys had to dig deep on Sunday afternoon, but thanks to the team's resilience, Dallas was able to erase the memory of last week's heartbreaking loss in Brazil . In Week 4, the team came through with a bounce-back effort to get back into the win column.
It wasn't easy, but Dak Prescott and the Cowboys' offense showed up in a big way and were able to come through in the clutch.
Now, Dallas needs to prepare for a quick turnaround as they return to action on Thursday Night Football, but first, let's take a look back on some of the standout performances from Week 4.
From CeeDee Lamb's standout performance to Joey Porter Jr. making a statement in his Cowboys debut, there was a lot for Dallas fans to be excited about.
Joey Porter Jr. wasted no time showing Cowboys fans why the team aggressively pursued him. In 24 snaps, Porter was targeted just one time and allowed zero catches.
While the Cowboys' secondary has been putrid throughout the past two years, Porter is giving fans a reason to believe that things can turn around.
"Special teams is so vexing... but Turpin had his best return game of the year!" @Boys_Vox weighs in on the Cowboys' special teams performance on Sunday vs. the Texans on the postgame show with @ZachWolchuk and @BryanBroaddus pic.twitter.com/BDpK5cAuvQ
One of the common themes throughout the game was Cowboys fans coming together to rip special teams coordinator Nick Sorensen. While KaVontae Turpin turned up this week, Sorensen continues to be a weak spot on the coaching staff.
It looks like Tyler Guyton has finally begun to turn the corner in his career, and as long as he can stay healthy, he is putting together an incredible season. The stats from Sunday speak for themselves.
👀 🔬 Tyler Guyton in #Cowboys vs Texans: vs. Danielle Hunter - 32 snaps, 2 pressures, 0 sacks, 28 1v1 reps (87.5%), 4.45s Time to Pressure vs. Will Anderson Jr. - 8 snaps, 1 pressure, 0 sacks, 8 1v1 reps (100%), 2.8s TTP remainder - 12 snaps, 0 pressures, 0 sacks holy …… pic.twitter.com/3Mfd3ihJr6
It's hard to believe that Guyton was competing for his starting job during training camp.
The Texans offense bullied Bland on Sunday afternoon. Bland was targeted four times and gave up four receptions for 83 yards and a touchdown.
Daron Bland didn’t stand a chance there. Tough https://t.co/kaN00FxzDB
He has become a liability in coverage, and is going to need to up his game if the defense is going to have a breakthrough and begin to turn things around.
Lamb is leading the league in receiving yards through four weeks, and his 498 yards in those games is the most through four weeks in Cowboys history.
Lamb hauled in 17 catches for 189 yards and one touchdown. He becomes the first player in NFL history to have 10 catches and 150+ yards in three straight games. As an added bonus, Lamb had more receiving yards than the division rival Eagles had in total offense (172).
The Cowboys' defense has enough issues that the offense needs to be firing on all cylinders every drive. Unfortunately, the offense sputtered on third downs throughout the game, going just 5-of-14 on third-down conversions.
Dallas will need to do a better job extending drives moving forward, but for now, they can be happy that the team was able to overcome the issue to come away with the win.

title: Cowboys WR CeeDee Lamb Defends Brian Schottenheimer Amid Hot Seat Speculation
full_text:
Dallas Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb had one of the best games of his career in Sunday's 34-30 win over the Houston Texans.
In one of the most impressive individual performances ever by a Cowboys wide receiver, Lamb finished with a career-high 17 catches for 189 yards and touchdown, which included the game-winning score with 40 seconds left to give Dallas its first lead of the afternoon.
But after the game, Lamb made sure to direct focus elsewhere and send a strong message toward Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer, who faced notable scrutiny following Week 3's late-game collapse in a loss to the Baltimore Ravens.
While speaking with reporters after the game, Lamb expressed his confidence in Schottenheimer by using an interesting choice of words.
"I want Schotty to know that I got his back. I'm with him," Lamb said of Schottenheimer, per Nick Harris of the Fort Worth-Star Telegram. "I'm one of his strongest soldiers. It's just going to battle with each other. Once you have that confidence and know who you're going to battle with, just shoot your gun. And I feel like we shot it today. No pun intended."
That's quite a statement from Lamb, who has been working with Schottenheimer since 2023 when he was promoted to offensive coordinator after one year with Dallas as a coaching analyst the season prior.
Lamb leads the NFL in receiving yards (498) as the league heads into the Monday Night Football slate to close out Week 4. If can string together performances like he had Sunday, it will likely lead to more wins for Dallas and less negativity surrounding Schottenheimer moving forward.
Entering Brazil with a 1-1 record and a woeful Week 1 loss to the New York Giants already under their belt, the Cowboys needed to come away with a win over the Ravens.
It appeared as if Dallas was a shoe-in to emerge victorious after getting down to the Ravens two-yard with a chance at the game-sealing touchdown. Instead, the Cowboys lost a 34-31 heartbreaker after a wild finish.
As a result, Schottenheimer faced major criticism for multiple reasons. His offense was unable to punch in the go-ahead score, which was low-lighted by what he admitted was a predetermined coaching decision that tasked Dak Prescott with throwing the ball away despite having George Pickens wide open at the front pylon clear as day.
This also included how he and the coaching staff handled the ensuing kickoff and final offensive play that allowed the Ravens to get into game-winning field goal after having just seven seconds of clock to do so.
Schottenheimer's seat likely got a bit warm after the way that game ended but he and the Cowboys turned things around in Week 4 against Houston.
Schottenheimer, Lamb and the Cowboys will aim to build on Sunday's win as they head into a short week before hosting the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Thursday Night Football.

title: Joey Porter Sr. Takes Shot at Steelers While Celebrating Joey Porter Jr.'s Cowboys Debut
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys' Week 4 game against the Houston Texans was also the debut of Joey Porter Jr., who was playing his first game with the team, and the his first game of the season.
Porter didn't play over the first three games of the 2026 season because he was supposedly hurt , but at this point we know he didn't play because he was seeking a new contract.
However, apparently his dad, Steelers great Joey Porter Sr. does not blame his son at all for what transpired. Instead, Porter Sr. blames the Steelers for the contract standoff with his son.
We know that because Porter Sr. recorded a video while attending his son's first game with Dallas, and in the video he accuses the Steelers of trying to "take me away from football."
"Forgot what it's like walking through a hostile environment on game day," Porter Sr. said as he navigated Reliant Stadium, the home of Dallas' Week 4 opponent, the Texans.
"(The Steelers) tried to take me away from football for four weeks," Porter added. "I forgot what it feel like. I forgot how intense it gets. It feel like I'm back at home. Walking into a hostile environment. Football is back."
"They held us down for three weeks, they couldn't hold us down no longer. Football is back. Love Sundays."
Porter didn't go to games while his son was locked in a contract standoff with the Steelers, so that's what he means when he says the Steelers "tried to take me away from football."
Porter Sr. obviously blames the Steelers for that standoff that led to Porter Jr. not playing.
The source of that feeling likely comes from the fact that Porter Sr. believes Pittsburgh didn't offer a good enough contract otherwise Porter Jr. would have been playing.
What was that offer, you ask? Well, ESPN's Ian Rapoport reported that the Steelers' offer reached $28 million annually, which would rank seventh among cornerbacks .
Was that a fair offer? That's really up for debate and depends upon how you view Porter Jr. Clearly, his father thinks he's worth more than that.
Speaking of Porter Jr.'s debut , the former second-round pick had a good one. He played 24 snaps in total, with 19 of those coming in coverage. Porter was only targeted once and did not allow a reception on that target, per Next Gen Stats .
Porter was matched up against Houston's top wideout, Nico Collins, a total of five times but nothing was thrown at Porter.
Christian Parker called Porter Jr. a "boundary eraser" and we saw every bit of that quality on Sunday. Porter Jr. erased an entire side of the field with the Texans having no interest in throwing at him and instead opting to go after DaRon Bland.
Now, the Cowboys just have to figure out a better option than Bland for a side that figures to be very active moving forward if Porter is able to keep doing what he did in Week 4.
Hopefully that option will be Cobie Bryant when he returns, as he has been Dallas' best cornerback. Even Shavon Revel would be welcomed. But it just can't be Bland, who continues to be a massive liability.

title: Cowboys Offense Reaching Historic Numbers That Could End NFC Championship Drought
full_text:
After last week's crushing loss to the Baltimore Ravens , Dak Prescott questioned whether or not the Dallas Cowboys offense deserved the self-proclaimed title of "Greatest Offense There Is."
"Frustrated. Frustrated as hell. Excuse me. Embarrassed," Prescott said. "We call ourselves best offense, you know, GOTI, and we get down in the one-yard line and don't put it in. Yeah, it just sucks. Not a lot of words or full explanation of it."
These strong words from the Cowboys quarterback and newly-crowed franchise leader in passing touchdowns couldn't be ignored, but he helped turned things around in Week 4. And in the process, that "GOTI" label might just have some merit back.
The Cowboys got a much-needed 34-30 win over the Houston Texans at NRG Stadium on Sunday, doing so in comeback fashion behind a career day from wide receiver CeeDee Lamb , who caught the game-winning touchdown from Prescott with 40 seconds left. Their dominant connection now has Dallas on pace with some of the best NFL offenses of the past 25 years, and could signal that the franchise's long-running drought of an NFC Championship appearance has a chance ending.
Following the win over Houston, the Cowboys offense has 3.39 points per drive across the first four this year.
This ranks No. 5 among all NFL offenses through the first four games of a season since 2000, as pointed out by The Ringer's Anthony Dabbundo.
This 3.39 points per drive total would rank No. 1 since 2000 if it's sustained over the course of an entire season. Obviously that's easier said than done, but it goes to show what Dallas has done through four games this year.
The other four teams alongside Dallas in the 1-6 range of this category all made the NFC Championship. No. 1 - 2020 Green Bay Packers (3.67) No. 2 - 2024 Washington Commanders (3.56) No. 3 - 2021 Kansas City Chiefs (3.53) No. 4 - 2007 New England Patriots (3.53) No. 5 - 2026 Dallas Cowboys (3.39) No. 6 - 2018 Kansas City Chiefs (3.29)
The Cowboys last made the NFC Championship during the 1995 season, when they won the Super Bowl. Since then, it's either been an exit in the Wild Card, Divisional Round, or missing the playoffs altogether.
These early offensive numbers could be even better if not for three missed field goals by Cowboys kicker Brandon Aubrey, who got one blocked last week against Baltimore before the Texans blocked another on Sunday. He then missed a 64-yard field goal at the end of the first half against Houston.
On top of that, the Cowboys' offense has had its share of early inconsistencies. They have failed to capitalize on some major opportunities, most notably in the loss to Baltimore and the New York Giants along with Sunday's win over the Texans.
The fact they are still on such a historic pace speaks volumes of this unit's ceiling once everything can truly come together.
Dallas will have a chance to build momentum with a quick turnaround on Thursday Night Football against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 5.

title: How Joey Porter Jr. Fared in First Game With Cowboys Since Trade From Steelers
full_text:
Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. made both his season and Dallas Cowboys debut on Sunday in the win over the Houston Texans.
Porter had sat out the first three games with a supposed back injury that magically healed up when he arrived in Dallas after being traded by the Pittsburgh Steelers.
Despite having just days between the trade and the Week 4 game against the Houston Texans on Sunday, Porter, who was not on the Cowboys' injury report, was ready to roll against Houston, albeit on limited snaps .
Porter played 24 of a possible 52 defensive snaps in his debut, and according to Next Gen Stats , he was targeted once in 19 coverage snaps and did not permit a completion.
Porter was matched up against Houston's No. 1 wide receiver, Nico Collins, five times and was not targeted.
As far as the rest of the box score goes, Porter did not record a stat, as he finished without a tackle in the contest.
It was very clear the Texans had no intention of challenging the 24-year-old cornerback throughout the game, which just goes to show how much respect teams have for him.
While it's impressive to see how little the Texans challenged Porter, that also meant Houston went after Dallas' other cornerbacks instead, which didn't end well.
DaRon Bland was tied for the most targets on the team with six, and he gave up five receptions for 104 yards, with those marks ranking tied for the most and the most on the team.
Reddy Stewart, who played in the slot with Caleb Downs operating mostly at safety thanks to injuries at the position, gave up three catches on four targets for 48 yards. All three of those catches came on one drive.
Dallas' other cornerbacks, Shavon Revel and Ameer Speed, were not targeted at all. Revel played just seven snaps, though, and Speed played 23.
The good news is, the Cowboys will have to rely on those guys less and less as Porter builds up his snap count.
Dallas needs to be less dependent on Bland, whose job should be in serious danger after yet another disappointing performance on Sunday.
Once Cobie Durant comes back from injury , he should be the one starting across from Porter, although that may not be possible because the Cowboys might need him in the slot with Caleb Downs at safety because of injuries at the position.
Putting all of that aside for now, Porter's first game with Dallas was a success, as he completely shut down one side of the field, just how the Cowboys wanted him to.
And Dallas will hope he can play a full allotment of snaps in Week 5, when the Cowboys will take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Thursday night.

title: Broncos’ Pat Surtain II Injury Update Could Have Been Far Worse
full_text:
The Denver Broncos have dodged not one , but two major bullets following Sunday's costly loss to the San Francisco 49ers.
The Ringer's Tom Pelissero reported Sunday that Broncos cornerback Patrick Surtain II, who left the Week 4 game with an apparent non-contact injury, "avoided any worst-case scenario" and his Achilles' tendon remains "intact."
Further testing revealed an ankle injury for Surtain, who's classified as "week-to-week" and is expected to miss only a short period of time, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Monday .
Surtain was having a solid game prior to being assisted off the field, recording four combined tackles including two solo stops while helping limit San Francisco's passing attack.
The perennial All-Pro defender was among multiple players to suffer injuries amid the 24-14 defeat in the Bay Area; Denver also lost wide receiver Pat Bryant to an ankle injury and fellow starting cornerback Riley Moss to a rib injury.
Predictably, head coach Sean Payton offered little by way of an official update.
"Of course today and throughout the week, really we’ll stay away from any updates," Payton told the media on Monday. "Guys were all in today getting work and rehabbing. We’ll make sure we go through the process well, and then we’ll have a report Wednesday."
The Broncos stay on the road to face the 0-4 Los Angeles Chargers in Week 5.
The Broncos' schedule doesn't get any easier after Week 5, with matchups against the Seattle Seahawks, Arizona Cardinals, Kansas City Chiefs, and Carolina Panthers yet to come over the next month — all teams with viable passing games.
Much will hinge on the status of Moss, who may or may not play through his rib issue. If he does, he'll be locked in as the club's No. 1 corner, with Jahdae Barron or Kris Abrams-Draine starting opposite him and Ja'Quan McMillian holding down his familiar slot role.
If Moss cannot go in Week 5, Barron and Abrams-Draine will be the top two CBs. In that instance, it's likely Denver would comb the market for help at the position, as they have only Brent Austin on the practice squad.
“Relative to their play yesterday, I thought they came in and did a real good job. It was good to see," Payton said of Barron and Abrams-Draine on Monday. "I think it’s a position we have depth at, and those guys both kind of got thrown into the fire and I thought they handled it well.”

title: Insider Provides Key Pat Bryant Injury Update—What It Means
full_text:
Exhale, Denver Broncos fans. Second-year wide receiver Pat Bryant will only miss "a few weeks" with an ankle sprain.
ESPN 's Adam Schefter broke the news Monday morning, reporting that Bryant suffered an ankle sprain in the Broncos' 24-14 loss to the San Francisco 49ers .
Broncos WR Pat Bryant sprained his ankle during Sunday’s loss at San Francisco, and now is expected to miss “a few weeks” per source. pic.twitter.com/uwZA3UYou2
We're still awaiting an update on cornerbacks Patrick Surtain II and Riley Moss, who exited Sunday's game at Levi's Stadium with a lower leg and rib injury, respectively.
As for Bryant, "a few weeks" could mean two or three, or it could mean four-plus. If the Broncos expect it to be at least four games, they'll place him on short-term injured reserve.
Hopefully, it doesn't come to that, but even if it does, that would put Bryant back on the field somewhere around Week 9 and beyond. He'd still be back in time to contribute to the Broncos' stretch run, even if it's an IR designation first.
Bryant's injury occured on a 30-yard catch-and-run that helped set up a Wil Lutz field goal. Bryant finished the day with three receptions on three targets for 47 yards.
Beyond the running backs, Bryant and Jaylen Waddle have been the Broncos' passing attack. Courtland Sutton and Evan Engram have been disappearing acts thus far, while RJ Harvey caught as many passes against the 49ers as Bryant, Waddle, Sutton, and Engram combined.
How much of Bo Nix's checkdown obsession was game-plan oriented or quarterback-driven we don't know, but it became so predictable that even fans watching the game knew what was coming on a down-to-down basis.
Outside of Week 2, the Broncos' passing game has been anemic and frustrating to watch. We're mystified by this failure to launch, and it's hard to see it suddenly improving with Bryant being gone for the next few games.
A third-round pick out of Illinois last year, Bryant had an impressive rookie showing. He started off a bit slow, but as the season wore on, he slowly began to eat into Troy Franklin's snaps.
Bryant was on the cusp of doing great things when he suffered a brutal concussion in Week 16 that hospitalized him. He was back in time for the Broncos' playoff run, but another concussion, followed by a hamstring injury in the AFC championship game, sidelined him for most of it.
Entering Year 2, Bryant had one heck of a training camp, easily earned the No. 3 receiver spot behind Sutton and Waddle. Bryant was a big reason for both of Denver's wins this season, so he will be missed.
Fortunately, the Broncos still have Franklin, who's very experienced for a third-year player, and Marvin Mims Jr. is healthy again. That gives the Broncos a four-deep receiver rotation, plus Lil'Jordan Humphrey is on the practice squad.
If Bryant ends up on short-term IR, expect Humphrey to promoted back to the active roster. We'll hopefully learn more about Bryant's outlook soon.

title: Broncos Player Grades: Plenty of Blame to Go Around in Loss to 49ers
full_text:
Try as they might, the Denver Broncos couldn't pull off another comeback win against the San Francisco 49ers, falling 24-14 .
The Broncos played it close and tough until late in the game, trailing 14-17, before 49ers tight end George Kittle sealed it with a massive 56-yard catch-and-run to paydirt.
Denver's performance had some good showings and a few bad ones. This week's grades will highlight the best and worst.
Hopefully, Bryant's lower-leg injury isn’t long-term, though early indications aren't promising. He once showed off his elusiveness with a big catch-and-run to set the Broncos up in good field position, though that was the play that hurt him.
Bryant was also doing well as a blocker, and his overall ability as a big riser would be missed if he were out for multiple weeks.
It feels weird to write up Singleton as the best defender in a game, but he had a great game against the 49ers. He had a few negative plays, but he flew downhill against the run and played a big role in the Broncos' overall success in containing Christian McCaffrey, especially with multiple defensive linemen having issues.
Denver limited Singleton's exposure in coverage by changing his role, and I can't help but wonder whether that could’ve been the difference in his play.
Look, a 5.3 average depth of target, which is below the league average, and 5.1 yards per attempt is not good. Nix couldn't push the ball, and while it wasn’t all his fault, he shoulders a fair amount of the blame.
Nix worked off reads quickly when pressure wasn’t even threatening, and moved into pressure, making poor decisions and off-target passes. He looked spooked out there, and his averages reflect it.
Patrick Surtain II | CB | Grade: 81.6
Surtain also exited this game early with an injury , but hopefully it isn’t severe. He's a difference-maker; when he left, the 49ers adjusted what they were doing when he was on the field. Denver didn’t miss him too much on the field because Surtain's replacement played well, but it was a small sample size. Hopefully, the star corner is back soon.
Jahdae Barron | CB | Grade: 80.5
Barron has been questionable on the field since his rookie season, but in his limited action against the 49ers, filling in for Surtain, he played well . He was tough against the run and played well in coverage, including some tight, consistent coverage. This was the first time Barron has looked like a legitimate starting-caliber corner.
Zach Allen | DL | Grade: 78.9
If you factor in his special teams play, Allen would be the defensive MVP thanks to his blocked field goal. He's had a monster season, filling up stat sheets with his best all-around campaign so far. If Allen can keep this level of play up, he could push for the NFL's best defensive lineman.
Quinn Meinerz | OG | Grade: 68.4
The Broncos' blocking was questionable, but aside from a handful of plays, Meinerz played a great game. He blocked well in both the run and pass game and sustained blocks to make it easier on the ball carrier.
Jaylen Waddle | WR | Grade: 65.3
Waddle's touchdown came off an excellent play design that gave him the opening, but the route left little room for error. He ran it perfectly. There were some questionable effort plays and a bad drop, but Waddle was mostly a positive impact for the Broncos.
Garett Bolles | OT | Grade: 58.9
Bolles had a rough day with penalties, but his play was sound. He had some miscues in the run game with the looks the 49ers gave the Broncos, but he handled it about as well as he could, given the O-line's other issues with blocking.
Que Robinson | OLB | Grade: 30.2
Robinson is explosive, but he needs to get stronger for the NFL. The 49ers were able to shut down his explosiveness, and he didn’t have an answer for it because he doesn't have the strength to add non-explosive moves to change things up.
Ja’Quan McMillian | CB | Grade: 32.4
If this were the 2010s, McMillian could have a 10-plus-year career as a nickel corner, but as offenses shift to bigger slot players, his lack of size and athleticism can be exploited. With him being in the final year of his deal before becoming an unrestricted free agent, his market will be interesting to watch.
Jonah Elliss | OLB | Grade: 38.7
Elliss is almost the polar opposite of Robinson. Elliss doesn’t have that explosiveness in his game; the strength and technique are there, but he isn’t that initial threat, and it changes how blockers handle him. The lack of explosiveness with Elliss was exploited by the 49ers.
Evan Engram | TE | Grade: 39.1
Engram isn’t cutting it as a receiver; he still seems to have chemistry issues with Nix, and his blocking remains a liability. Denver took a shot on Engram to improve its tight end room and got burned. The 49ers, like the rest of the NFL, no longer fear Engram, and how they played him proves it.
Luke Wattenberg | C | Grade: 41.4
One has to wonder whether Denver regrets the Wattenberg extension that locks him in through the 2027 season. He had a few games last year where he looked like a legit top-five center, but outside of that, he's been bottom-10. To start this year, he looks unplayable, but the Broncos are forced to play him because of his contract.
J.K. Dobbins | RB | Grade: 43.5
Dobbins's lack of explosiveness, combined with terrible vision, led to a pitiful game against the 49ers. He had 40 yards on 11 carries — with a long of nine yards — meaning 10 runs for 31 yards. He added a pair of catches for 12 yards, but he's supposed to be the force in the running game, and he only compounded bad blocking with terrible vision and slow-moving feet.

title: Sean Payton Responds to Dre Greenlaw Confrontation After Broncos-49ers
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw played like a man possessed against the Denver Broncos.
It's like Greenlaw had a chip on his shoulder, but I can't imagine why. In all seriousness, we know why he was uniquely motivated to go against the Broncos: he was released after one season in Denver.
In the 49ers' 24-14 win over the Broncos , Greenlaw finished with a team-high 12 tackles (seven solo) and was often seen pointing toward head coach Sean Payton and the Denver sideline. After the game, Greenlaw was a bit fired up, as he intercepted Payton at midfield and was kind of pulled away by his fellow linebacker Fred Warner.
According to Greenlaw, he told Payton, "Get the f--k off the field," per Eric Branch of the San Francisco Chronicle .
Dre Greenlaw needed Fred Warner to pull him away from Sean Payton at midfield (footy via @Romi_Bean ) pic.twitter.com/Ni8aFW6ra8
Payton seemed unperturbed by Greenlaw's antics. At the post-game podium, Payton had nothing but good things to say about Greenlaw, which has been his message when asked about the veteran linebacker at every turn since Denver released him this past spring.
"No. Listen, when I say this —and I said this to [49ers head coach] Kyle [Shanahan] afterwards—I think the world of him," Payton said of Greenlaw post-game. "Really love everything about him. He plays with that emotion, and so all good."
Payton's remarks echoed what he said when asked about Greenlaw on Friday. Clearly, Payton laments the unfortunate way that injuries hamstrung Greenlaw's one season with the Broncos and ended his tenure two seasons early.
“He’s such a passionate player. [I’m] a huge fan, and it’s why we signed him," Payton said of Greenlaw on Friday. "He got nicked up, and the injury bug was something that he was fighting, but just that process of getting to know him and him being here, I feel like we’re better for it. He’s exactly what you’re looking for in a football player, not any position-specific, but it’s all football.”
Dre Greenlaw talking shit to Sean Payton on the sideline after that tackling Harvey near the broncos sideline pic.twitter.com/H3qlfBxI7z
For his part, Greenlaw was asked whether his first tackle against the Broncos released a little tension, given that he turned and pointed to Payton on the sideline.
"Uh, I mean, nah," Greenlaw said. "I just pointed at him."
When asked whether there was any "chatter" with his former Broncos teammates during the game, Greenlaw dismissed that notion, too, claiming that "it's all love and respect."
"All them players, I love all the players," Greenlaw said. "Every single person that's on that field over there. I mean, sure, there's a couple of them that weren't there last year; they got the talk, but, I mean, everybody else that I was with out there last year, for the most part, they know how I play the game, so it's all love and respect."
However, in a one-on-one with Branch, Greenlaw admitted that his unique energy against the Broncos  was motivated by Payton's "disrespect." Greenlaw resented that his agents informed him of the Broncos' release, and not Payton.
"The disrespect," Greenlaw said via the Chronicle . "He couldn't be man to man and call my phone and say, 'We're going to cut you.'"
The Broncos signed Greenlaw to a three-year deal worth $35 million in the spring of 2025. The Broncos knew he was an injury risk, given his history with the 49ers, but they loved his makeup so much that they were willing to roll the dice.
That's Payton for you. He looked past the obvious downside risk because he was such a fan of Greenlaw.
Alas, it kind of blew up in Payton's face because Greenlaw suffered an offseason quad injury, which haunted him throughout the summer and preseason. He ended up starting the 2025 regular season on injured reserve.
In his first game as a Bronco, Greenlaw was activated ahead of Week 7's tilt against the New York Giants, which Denver stormed back to win thanks to a 33-point fourth quarter. After the game, Greenlaw's run-in with an official led to a one-game suspension . He was accused of verbally threatening a ref.
Between his injuries and suspension, Greenlaw only appeared in eight games with the Broncos, with seven starts. He finished with 45 tackles, a sack, and a forced fumble.
There were rumblings during the season that Greenlaw struggled to pick up Vance Joseph's defense. We later learned how true that was, as the Broncos released him in March, and he went on to talk publicly about how difficult the system was, saying he " just wasn't happy " in Denver.
Greenlaw landed on his feet, reuniting with the 49ers. He seems to have picked up right where he left off in San Francisco.
It's a disappointment that the Greenlaw experiment didn't pan out. Payton clearly regrets it — not the signing of Greenlaw, but how the Broncos were unable to make it work and will the injury bug to avoid him.
Payton refused to say one bad word about Greenlaw. And to Greenlaw's credit, he too would not say anything bad about his former head coach or team.
And that, as they say, is that.

title: Broncos' Biggest Winners & Losers in 24-14 Loss to 49ers
full_text:
The Denver Broncos turned in their usual slow start on Sunday, putting just three first-half points on the board against the San Francisco 49ers.
Absent this time around, though, was the full-team fourth-quarter performance. Bo Nix and the Broncos' offense made the beginnings of a comeback, narrowing the deficit to just three points, but the defense couldn't close this time around.
The 49ers prevailed 24-14.
As the Broncos drop to 2-2 on the season, they now face two games within the next 11 days, which isn't great given the injuries suddenly piling up. There's plenty of time yet to look ahead to next week's matchup...
We're still sifting through the aftermath of this disappointing showing by the Broncos. Let's break down the Broncos' biggest winners and losers from Week 4.
Mims returned from the foot injury that cost him the preceding two games and found a way to make an impact. Alas, it was a negative impact.
In a game with zero margin for error, the Broncos hung tough and may have truly had a chance to win it had Mims not fumbled in the third quarter. It wasn't a muffed punt, though the fumble did occur on the return, but as Mims was getting leg-tackled, he stretched out with the arm carrying the ball, and when it came into contact with the ground, he lost control.
I thought the ground can't cause a fumble, but the play was reviewed and upheld. The 49ers capitalized on the short field, marching down for their first touchdown of the game on the massive momentum swing.
Suffice it to say, the Broncos never recovered. Beyond the fumble, Mims looked out of sync with the offense, which can be forgiven considering his lack of time on task since training camp. He has missed a ton of time, and it showed at Levi's Stadium.
Harvey led the Broncos with a whopping 10 receptions for 68 yards. He also carried seven times for 25 yards.
Against a stingy, swarming 49ers defense that missed few tackles, Harvey did force a handful of misses. He was the only thing keeping the Broncos' enemic offense going.
On the surface, a glance at the box score suggests that Nix turned in a good, efficient game. Oh, how the box score can deceive.
Nix completed 25-of-42 passes for 214 yards and a touchdown. However, 14 of his completions were checkdowns to the running backs, with Harvey leading the way.
Not every pass that went to Harvey or a running back was a checkdown; some of them were obviously designed, but it allowed the 49ers to crowd the line of scrimmage and patrol the boundary to great, lasting success. The Broncos didn't challenge the 49ers beyond the sticks, and it led to a frustratingly impotent offensive showing.
When Nix did look beyond five yards, he was generally off-target on his throws. I don't blame his receivers and tight ends for being out of sync with him, though, considering the long stretches they went without usage in the passing game.
Nix has to be better than he was in Santa Clara. For that matter, he has to be better than he's been through the first four games of this season. Those fans awaiting a big Year-3 leap from Nix have been woefully disappointed thus far.
With Patrick Surtain II exiting with a concerning lower-leg injury , the onus fell on Barron. The second-year cornerback stepped up and answered the bell, finishing with three tackles and a pass breakup.
We're still waiting to hear what the prognosis is on Surtain, but in his opportunity to step up, Barron did just that. The 2025 first-round pick didn't exactly save the day, but he held his own, helping to limit the 49ers' previously red-hot offense until their final possession, which featured a big George Kittle touchdown catch-and-run spurred by several missed tackles and a zero blitz.
Then Riley Moss exited with a rib injury, which put Kris Abrams-Draine on the field with Barron and nickel cornerback Ja'Quan McMillian. Abrams-Draine didn't fare as well as Barron did, but he should be considered a Week 4 winner, too, simply because his playing time appears set to increase.
Webb's play-calling has not been good this season. Then again, the player execution hasn't been acceptable either, but Webb's game planning for the 49ers left much to be desired.
The Broncos opened the game with a signature three-and-out, fueled by Webb's decision to call three straight passing plays. He stayed relatively committed to the rushing attack throughout the game, but the execution by the offensive line was poor.
That's not Webb's fault, but when the 49ers' defense swarmed the Broncos' offensive line, refusing to give up more than 3.5 yards per run, he had no counterpunch. The 49ers were able to crowd the line of scrimmage and shade coverage to the boundary, and so long as you tackle well, that's a recipe for success for a Webb offense.
Sean Payton's fingers have to be twitching to take back the play-calling sheet about right now. The problem is, he has to give Webb the opportunity to learn from his mistakes if he expects him to grow from these early games.
The question is, for how much longer can the Broncos afford Webb's trial-and-error education?
Bolles was penalized three times in this game. They were drive killers.
As a blocker, Bolles has been good, though not up to his usual snuff. He's been penalized way too many times this season. Three in one game?
That hearkens back to the 'Garett Holds' era. Not good.

title: 3 Disheartening Takeaways From Broncos' 24-14 Loss to 49ers
full_text:
The Denver Broncos started on solid footing in their 24-14 loss to the San Francisco 49ers . Denver even went into halftime tied 3-3.
Against a tough 49ers team on the road, though, the margin for error was always going to be slim. Sure enough, the tide didn't turn until a Marvin Mims Jr. fumble in the second half.
Unfortunately, the Broncos didn’t leave Levi's Stadium unscathed, with three key players getting hurt — including cornerback Patrick Surtain II, who exited the game with a lower-leg injury . This will be something to watch with two games coming in 11 days.
What did we learn from the Broncos' second loss of the season? Here are my key takeaways from this game.
If anything is going to hold the Broncos back this year, it will be their run-game inefficiency on both sides of the ball . Offensively, the Broncos can’t get a run game going — not even a boom-or-bust level rushing attack.
Denver's interior offensive line is inconsistent at best and is getting no push. Even All-Pro right guard Quinn Meinerz is struggling, though not as much as left guard Ben Powers and center Luke Wattenberg.
The Broncos' tackles, especially Mike McGlinchey, and the tight-end blocking also remain significant problems for this offense. Now, the issues aren't only on the offensive line, as the running backs' vision has been terrible.
J.K. Dobbins looks like Javonte Williams, running into contact when there is an open lane, and RJ Harvey still seemingly can't see defenders because he runs right into their arms. The play designs are actually fine. If the Broncos could execute the blocking, we’d probably see a solid run game.
The Broncos showed some offensive improvements in the fourth quarter after sticking with the run game, wearing down the 49ers' defense, but it was ultimately too little, too late. The Broncos absolutely have to get the run game going earlier.
The Broncos have to get to the bottom of why the run-game execution is so poor.
As for the defense, the Broncos had some big moments against the 49ers, including some huge short-yardage stops, but their consistency issues remain. Late in the game, the 49ers found a way to run the ball at will.
The Broncos lack mass on the defensive line, and the players who normally thrive against the run have been playing poorly, which has a trickle-down effect on the rest of the defense.
By now, every football fan should know about the 49ers' electrical substation, or at least the memes and jokes stemming from it. Well, the substation curse seemingly hit the Broncos hard in this one, as well as the 49ers, with multiple key players suffering injuries that took them out of the game.
Denver lost Surtain to a non-contact ankle injury. Shortly after Surtain exited, fellow cornerback Riley Moss was lost to a rib injury in the first half, so the Broncos had to play the whole second half with their fourth and fifth corners.
Wide receiver Pat Bryant was carted off after a big catch-and-run in the second half. Over the past few years, Denver has had relatively good luck with injuries, but these are three key players, with two of them making up one of the best starting cornerback duos in the NFL.
Hopefully, these injuries aren’t long-term, especially with Surtain and Moss. Kris Abrams-Draine and Jahdae Barron are solid depth, but neither has shown enough to be a full-time starter for multiple weeks.
With Bryant, at least the Broncos have good depth, including Troy Franklin and Lil’Jordan Humphrey, the latter of whom is on the practice squad. Denver can rotate them in to fill the void Bryant leaves, though it'll be hard to replicate his reliability if he misses extended time.
We know that Nix can push the ball downfield and look for big plays, but against the 49ers, the Broncos were more than happy to play the short passing game. Sure, the 49ers pressured at times and forced the short throws, but Nix was quick to dump it off to Harvey or Dobbins out of the backfield — like that was the plan.
When you face an explosive offense, such as the 49ers, you have to find a way to generate your own big plays, and the Broncos were unable to manage it. Before the fourth quarter, the Broncos had just two explosives on about 45 offensive plays, compared to six on about 50 plays for the 49ers.
In the fourth quarter, the 49ers had two explosive plays on 15 non-kneel-down plays, while Denver had zero on 18 offensive plays.
Averaging 5.1 yards per attempt isn’t going to get it done, as again Nix lived the check-down life with his backs. Not to take away from the effort of the running backs; they did a lot with with very little.
But 14 of Nix's 25 completions going to running backs makes it even harder to walk out of Levi's Stadium with a win. Maybe it's on the game plan and coaches, but Nix has to be held accountable here, as he has always shown to be more aggressive as a game unfolds, almost to a fault, only for him to be so passive in this one.
This is an issue because when Denver needed big, explosive plays, there was a clear disconnect between Nix and his receivers, and his ball placement was consistently off. It's about getting into a rhyth.
Honestly, Denver played a solid game, but offensive complacency ultimately cost them. That and the same ol' too-little, too-late problem.

title: Broncos’ Pat Surtain II Suffers Scary Non-Contact Injury vs. 49ers | Watch
full_text:
Deep in the second quarter of Sunday's game between the Denver Broncos and San Francisco 49ers , Pro Bowl cornerback Patrick Surtain II went down with an injury to his lower right leg.
It was a non-contact injury that happened far away from the ball.
Non-contact injury for Pat Surtain. A closer look pic.twitter.com/p0Pmy0qXRv
With how hot it is at Levi's Stadium , it makes me wonder if the temperatures had anything to do with this injury. Temperatures are in the mid-90s, making it already one of the hottest games in Broncos history.
Surtain was down for a minute, again, with trainers examining his lower right leg. He was able to stand on his own, though, before walking slowly to the locker room with his arms around the shoulders of two Broncos trainers for support.
People are concerned that it could be an Achilles injury because it was non-contact. But it's too early to say. I would take encouragement from the fact that Surtain was allowed to stand on his own and the Broncos opted not to cart him off.
If the trainers were worried it was an Achilles tear, they would not have let him get to his feet and they would have called for the cart, in all likelihood.
Coming out of the half, Broncos head coach Sean Payton told CBS ' Melanie Collins, "Right now, he's out to start the second half. I don't have a final update. We'll be without him until we hear otherwise.
While we await any updates on Surtain, the injury vaults Jahdae Barron back into the mix. When Surtain missed three games last season with a pec injury, the Broncos moved Riley Moss to his spot as the left-side boundary cornerback, with Barron stepping into Moss's right side.
Ja'Quan McMillian will stay at his spot in the nickel. Kris Abrams-Draine could also factor in, depending on whether the Broncos want Barron to split his snaps like last year.
One big difference between now and then? Barron was a rookie last year. Ostensibly, the coaches should trust him far more to step in as the fourth guy on the cornerback depth chart, and do his job.
It's a tough break for the Broncos. But here's to hoping that it isn't too serious for Surtain.
As a pro, Surtain has only missed five games to injury since being drafted in the first round back in 2021.
At the time of this writing, the Broncos are tied with the 49ers 3-3 at the half.
After the game, Payton said it's too early to know anything about Surtain's injury. Broncos cornerback Riley Moss and wide receiver Pat Bryant also exited the game never to return, and here's what Payton said afterward.
Well, I’m not going to give you any report on the injuries because I don’t know," Payton said from the podium. "But I would say it probably impacts the defense when both your corners are down coming into the second half, and then with Pat [Bryant]. So nothing right now. I just asked the same question coming off the field to both, so I appreciate it."
As soon as we know anything, we'll pass it on to you, our readers.

full_text:
The Denver Broncos are in Santa Clara, California, for their Week 4 tilt against the San Francisco 49ers . The weather could be a big factor, with temperatures in the mid-90s .
With about 90 minutes to go until kickoff, the Broncos and 49ers have released their inactives list for Week 4. Let's examine.

Ehlinger goes down as a healthy scratch officially, but he'll dress as the Broncos' emergency quarterback. Then there's the injured Dondrea Tillman, who's nursing a hamstring, and three rookie draft picks.
Casey, Bentley, and Onyedim are still waiting to dress for their first game as a pro. Onyedim has been the only defensive lineman yet to dress for a game, but that's how Sean Payton typically handles rookies.
Sai'vion Jones and Que Robinson dealt with such rookie vagaries last year. It's Onyedim's turn as a rookie, but the Broncos will have no qualms with playing him if there's a genuine need. Right now, though, there isn't one, with Jones and Jordan Jackson healthy.

title: 5 Bold Predictions for How Broncos Can Take Down 49ers
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers have been the NFL's best team through three weeks, and it isn't all that close. The Denver Broncos have to face them on Sunday.
To add to the difficulty, the Broncos won't have home-field advantage, and they'll be playing in potentially record temperatures at Levi's Stadium. That puts the onus on a few players to deliver elite performances and puts pressure on the team to play its best overall this season.
This week's bold predictions factor all of this in. Nailing these would all but guarantee a win. Let's dive in.
Denver ranks 11th in overall explosive play rate on offense, 20th in rushing, and eighth in passing, while the 49ers' defense ranks first overall, first in rushing, and third in passing for the lowest explosive play rate allowed.
It is difficult to find explosives against the 49ers, but the Broncos manage to produce eight, with three runs over 10 yards and five passing plays over 20. J.K. Dobbins and Jaylen Waddle need to step up in this one.
There is growing concern about the Broncos' run game because their blocking has been an issue across the board.
The Broncos need to find a way to build a reliable run game. Despite the 49ers' strong run defense, the Broncos run the ball efficiently, averaging at least five yards per rush, with Dobbins and RJ Harvey leading the way.
There may not be a better overall playmaker in the NFL than McCaffrey, given what he can do as a runner and receiver. That said, he has yet to break 120 scrimmage yards this season, with a single game over 100, but the Broncos have had serious issues handling running backs.
The McCaffrey threat will draw attention his way, but the Broncos will be ready for it. Denver emerges with its best day handing a running back so far this season.
Few teams can shut down McCaffrey and Kittle in the same game, and these two bold predictions see the Broncos do just that.
In the last two games, Kittle has 174 receiving yards, with 82 yards last week, 80 yards the game before that, and only 12 in Week 1. Given what Denver allowed the Los Angeles Rams' tight ends to do, and the attention McCaffrey needs, Kittle could have a big game.
But not this time. The Broncos hold Kittle to under 50 yards.
The 49ers' special teams units have been decent, while the Broncos' units have been great. Denver has an opening here to make some big plays on special teams.
With Marvin Mims Jr. back on the field, Denver manages to bust off a return for a touchdown, adding a defensive touchdown to total 14 points. This helps bridge the gap for the Broncos' offense, allowing them to keep up with the 49ers.

title: Several Broncos on Brink of Major Milestones vs. 49ers
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are focused on advancing to 3-1 this week as they travel to take on the San Francisco 49ers .
With the Kansas City Chiefs and Las Vegas Raiders both getting off to a 3-0 start, the Broncos can't afford to drop to 2-2 this week — especially given Denver's schedule through Week 8. Meanwhile, the 49ers are also undefeated, though they've yet to really face an opponent quite like the Broncos, and that includes the Los Angeles Rams, who were jet-lagged in their season-opening game down in Australia.
The Broncos lead the all-time series vs. the 49ers 8-7, but they're 3-5 on the road. Denver would much prefer to leave the greater Bay Area 9-7 all-time against the 49ers than 8-8.
Suffice it to say, winning at Levi's Stadium is the Broncos' top priority, but several individuals have milestones or records on the table this week. Let's highlight what to watch for on Sunday.
Payton needs one win to fully overtake Chuck Knox for the 12th-most regular-season wins among head coaches in NFL history. Payton tied Knox last week in the Broncos' 30-26 win over the Rams.
Payton currently has 186 career wins in the regular season. He can officially scoot past Knox, and set his sights on Dan Reeves at at No. 11 (190 wins) with a victory over the 49ers.
With 123 passing yards, Nix would tie Kyle Orton for the seventh-most passing yards in team history. Last week, Nix joined the late Craig Morton and Jay Cutler as the quarterback with the fifth-most games with multiple passing scores in Broncos history.
Nix gets the chance to continue moving up the Broncos' all-time record books with even a subpar passing performance vs. San Francisco.
Sutton needs just one reception ot tie McCaffrey for the fifth-most catches in Broncos history. Once he passes McCaffrey, the next guy is Lionel Taylor, who sits at No. 4 all-time with 543 career receptions.
From there, it's the holy triumvirate of Broncos pass catchers in the top 3 spots: Rod Smith (849 receptions), Shannon Sharpe (675), and the late, great Demaryius Thomas (665). Sutton currently has 461 career receptions.
If Adkins catches a touchdown pass against the 49ers, he'd become the first undrafted tight end in team history to notch a receiving score in three straight games. He had one in Week 2 against the Jacksonville Jaguars and another last week against the Rams.
Adkins has been seeing the field a lot as new Broncos offensive coordinator Davis Webb implements his multi-tight end vision.
Allen needs just one sack to become the first Broncos defensive lineman since Derek Wolfe (2016) to notch 4.0 sacks within the first four games of a season. Allen has been off to a rip-roaring start, especially as an interior pass rusher.
He leads the Broncos with three sacks thus far. Here's to hoping he makes it four in San Francisco, and does what no one else has this season, and sacks Brock Purdy.
You read that right; Purdy is yet to be sacked this season.
Since we're talking sacks, Bonitto needs just two QB takedowns to reach 40 sacks for his career and become the seventh player in Broncos history to reach that milestone. Von Miller leads the franchise with 110.5 career sacks.
Bonitto is still a ways off from joining Miller's lofty status, but becoming one of the elite seven to reach 40 career sacks in a Broncos uniform will be special. Going against 49ers left tackle Trent Williams won't be easy, but nothing lasting or worth while ever is.
If Lutz makes his first extra point attempt on Sunday, he'll tie Tyler Bass for the second-longest point-after streak since 2015. Lutz has nailed 103 consecutive extra-point tries, and he's looking to extend it even further.
Alas, Lutz missed a field goal last week, but that's its own thing. The streak pertains to extra points.
