title: Everything Jacksonville Jaguars Have to Fear About Cincinnati Bengals in Week 4
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars have a chance to prove themselves in a big way in Week 4, but to do so they will have to clear a few hurdles.
With the Jaguars set to kick off against the Cincinnati Bengals in a key road battle, the Jaguars can show that they are amongst the AFC's elite with a win. With a loss, they drop to 2-2 before back-to-back games overseas in London.
The Jaguars have their won fair share of advantages entering Week 4, but what are the biggest reasons to worry when it comes to the Bengals' matchup? We break it down below.
The Bengals have an elite wide receiver duo that has done plenty of damage against the Jaguars in the past. Ja'Marr Chase is a future Hall of Famer, while Tee Higgins would be a No. 1 receiver on almost any other offense in the NFL. Jacksonville had issues stopping a volume-heavy No. 1 threat in Jaylen Waddle in Week 2, and this challenge will be even tougher. The Jaguars have the talent to matchup with Chase, but it will take an entire team effort from a banged-up cornerback room.
Chase has 25 receptions and over 300 receiving yards with two touchdowns in his last two games against the Jaguars. What he has done in eight quarters is as good as many players would hope to do over the course of a full-season. Meanwhile, Higgins was a bigger impact against the Jaguars in last year's battle (three catches for 56 yards, one touchdown) than he was in the last matchup in 2023. Higgins did not play in the 2021 game, where Chase caught six passes for 77 yards as a rookie.
If there is one type of quarterback the Jaguars have struggled against in their few losses during the Liam Coen era, it is the quarterback who is willing to play the quick game and be a point guard from the first snap to the last snap. Quarterbacks who, for lack of a better term, accept the dink-and-dunk method have had success against the Jaguars over the last 20 regular-season games. Joe Burrow and the Bengals' offense love to live in that world, and they have won a lot of games and put up a lot of points doing so over the years.
The Jaguars' worst defensive game this season (Week 2 vs. Denver) was the quickest time to throw (2.75 seconds) and lowest air yards per attempt (9.4) of any quarterback facing the Jaguars this year, and it resulted in Bo Nix having a +0.26 EPA/DB -- the only positive EPA/DB performance against the Jaguars this season.
This trend goes back to last year, too. The quick game hurt the Jaguars in losses to Jake Browning, Davis Mills and Matther Stafford, while it also helped Geno Smith have his best performance of the entire season. The Jaguars have not yet figured out how to stop the quick-game, and that is not a great position entering a matchup with Burrow.
Dexter Lawrence gets the most attention when it comes to the Bengals' defensive line, and for good reason. He is a true blue-chipper who has changed the Bengals' entire defensive front, which means the Jaguars will have to gear up for a new challenge along the interior defensive line. But the Bengals have talent outside of Lawrence, too, namely with new edge rushers Cashius Howell and Boye Mafe, who have combined for 28 pressures over the first three weeks. Add in Jonathan Allen and there are a ton of new faces to this front who have already made a difference.
The Jaguars have a lot of faith in their offensive line, and rookie left guard Emmanuel Pregnon has shown a ton of ability over the first three starts of his career. But it will take a team effort to slow down a talented Bengals' front this week, and the Bengals' defensive line is much closer to the Denver Broncos' than the New England Patriots'. This is a real challenge, and the Jaguars will have to make sure they do not let their front tank their passing game like they let Denver do.

title: Three Things That Mattered in Chiefs' 30-27 Win Over Raiders
full_text:
For the fourth week in a row, the Kansas City Chiefs secured a victory to open the 2026 season. For the third week in a row, it was far from the prettiest of triumphs.
Still, the only thing that matters in the NFL is whether you won or lost. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes, head coach Andy Reid and company ensured a positive outcome against the Las Vegas Raiders, finishing with 30 points to the host team's 27. Several developments stood out, both good and bad , which creates an interesting dynamic as Kansas City heads into the bye week.
With that in mind, here are three of the top things that mattered from Sunday's game.
When the Chiefs first signed Kenneth Walker to a hefty multi-year contract during the offseason, some (including this writer) believed the team would have to give him a heck of a workload in order for him to be worth it. Now that the dust has settled on the running back market and four games have been played, it's safe to say the reigning Super Bowl MVP has lived up to the hype and then some.
Walker delivered yet another classic performance on Sunday afternoon and evening, toting the ball 22 times for 177 yards (eight yards per carry) and a pair of touchdowns. A whopping 152 of those yards and both scores arrived in the second half. Ahead of Monday Night Football , he's currently leading the sport in yards and yards per attempt while also holding a staggering lead on missed tackles forced with 43 (Detroit Lions star Jahmyr Gibbs is second with 28).
The prized free agent pickup joined Jim Brown and O.J. Simpson as the only players ever with two or more 170-plus-yard rushing performances in the first four games of a season. He's elusive, explosive, consistent and is a perfect fit given the tweaks made by the coaching staff .
Right when everyone thought Walker couldn't endear himself to his teammates and fans enough, he found a way to do just that in Week 4.
Yes, Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins attempted 52 passes. He was bound to rack up some volume. Not only that, but Las Vegas mustered only 2.8 yards per carry on the ground. On the other hand, allowing a 38-year-old to pick apart your defense to the tune of 365 yards and a pair of touchdowns and letting the home team hold the ball for 35:42 of game time is iffy at best. Twenty-seven points later, it was a somewhat alarming showing for the Chiefs' defense again.
According to RBSDM , Cousins averaged 0.25 EPA per play overall and the Raiders owned a 61% success rate on early-down passes. The Chiefs' linebackers got absolutely picked apart by the home club's tight ends, Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer. Removing Week 1's throttling of the Denver Broncos , Kansas City's defense is now 20th in EPA/play and 17th in success rate surrendered. It isn't like the Raiders, Miami Dolphins or Indianapolis Colts are unstoppable on offense.
Coordinator Steve Spagnuolo's defense got to Cousins for hits plenty of times and ranked 14th in pressure rate ( via TruMedia ), although coming away with no sacks for another week is concerning. It isn't time to panic given the youth and sample size this group is dealing with, but we're firmly in wait-and-see mode here.
With left tackle Josh Simmons nursing a back injury and left guard Kingsley Suamataia benched , the Chiefs were already behind the proverbial eight-ball as a passing offense. Once wide receiver Rashee Rice left the game in the first quarter with a hamstring injury , things got even worse. Luckily for them, Tyquan Thornton rose to the occasion and had the best game of his career, but the outing ended prematurely due to a gruesome ankle injury of his own in the final frame.
Losing someone with 11 catches, 219 yards and a pair of touchdowns in four games is far from the end of the world, to be fair, but it's the timing and nature of Thornton's impact that make this loss significant.
The former second-round NFL Draft selection is a chunk-play savant, averaging 23.1 yards per reception in 2025 and 19.9 at the time of his injury. In Weeks 1-4, 53.3% of the plays directed to him went for a first down or touchdown. KC tried him four times on third down on Sunday, with two being immensely successful.
Thornton's rapport with Mahomes seems to be second to only tight end Travis Kelce, and his ability to routinely outplay the bar set for him (+18.4% catch rate over expected this year) adds electricity to an aerial attack that needs it.
No one knows at this moment when or whether Thornton, who suffered a dislocation, will return in 2026. Perhaps the replacement solution is giving rookie Cyrus Allen more playing time or reuniting with old friend Tyreek Hill , but something's got to give so Kansas City doesn't regress in a major way — especially while Simmons is still on the shelf.

title: Tyquan Thornton’s Injury May Make Tyreek Hill Reunion With Chiefs Inevitable
full_text:
While the Kansas City Chiefs topped the Las Vegas Raiders 30-27 yesterday, they lost a budding star in the process. Wide receiver Tyquan Thornton, who was in the midst of a career-high 111-yard, two-touchdown performance, suffered a gruesome injury late in the fourth quarter that will presumably knock him out for the rest of the campaign.
Concerns about the wide receiving corps had already risen after WR1 Rashee Rice exited the contest on the second drive with a hamstring strain. Now, Andy Reid's squad might be short two of its top three wideouts when it returns from the bye in Week 6. All of these factors combined make a Tyreek Hill reunion in Kansas City impossible to ignore. Unsurprisingly, more reports linking Hill and his former team have surfaced since the final whistle sounded last night.
ESPN insider Adam Schefter revealed this morning that Hill's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, is looking to negotiate a contract for the 32-year-old speedster. A deal could reportedly be signed in the "next few days," which is a pretty significant development in the situation.
Developing: Tyreek Hill’s agent Drew Rosenhaus said he plans to begin negotiating a deal for his veteran wide receiver with multiple teams today. One of those teams is the Chiefs, who have maintained contact with Hill. “I would anticipate Tyreek  potentially signing with a team… pic.twitter.com/RBn7ju28Ku
Hill is coming off a horrific injury of his own, as he dislocated his knee and tore multiple ligaments four games into the year with the Miami Dolphins in 2025. He spent the offseason recovering and is nearing full health — whatever that might entail — entering his 11th year in the pros.
"Cheetah" spent six years in Kansas City and reeled in 6,630 yards and 56 touchdowns with the franchise during his tenure. He helped the team win Super Bowl LIV against the 49ers and was Patrick Mahomes' favorite downfield target until he was traded to Miami in the 2022 offseason. It's no coincidence that all the smoke connecting Hill to the Chiefs has re-emerged with the wide receiver room's status looking grim. ESPN's Nate Taylor wrote in an article yesterday that Hill was targeting a November return — The Athletic's Michael Silver echoed that same sentiment — but Schefter's latest report suggests a signing might be more imminent than initially believed. There's also a world where Hill signs with the Chiefs soon but spends multiple weeks ramping back up to game speed.
I expect the Chiefs to have strong interest in a Tyreek Hill reunion when the free agent receiver is healthy enough to play. He's believed to be targeting a November return. Players I talked to in the locker room (Mahomes, Kelce, Chris Jones & others) are all for it. @TheAthletic
Even if Rice does not miss any time, general manager Brett Veach has to act sooner rather than later to add another target to the passing attack. It's upsetting that it had to come at the expense of a player who was developing into a fan favorite, but the Chiefs no longer have to create an open roster space for Hill if they place Thornton on season-ending IR.
The important caveat to note is that we don't know what Hill will look like in game action. He is aging rapidly and dealing with an injury that many thought could end his career at the time. The Chiefs can't realistically expect him to return to his elite form right away.
Regardless, a Chiefs reunion with Hill was already likely before yesterday's string of injuries. Now, it simply seems inevitable before it becomes official sometime this week.

title: Biggest Winners and Losers From Chiefs' Win Over the Las Vegas Raiders
full_text:
The biggest Raiders-Chiefs game in quite some time lived up to the billing. Six lead changes, several big-play swings, and a finish that required every bit of Kansas City's blood pressure to rise.
In the end, the Chiefs defeated a longtime division rival on their home turf to move to 4-0 and took sole possession of first place not just in the AFC West, but in the entire AFC.
It wasn’t perfect, and it was tense, but it was a win, and the Chiefs head into their bye week unbeaten. Here is a full breakdown of the biggest winners and losers from Sunday afternoon in Las Vegas.
What else is there to say at this point? Kenneth Walker leads the NFL in rushing with 537 yards through four games, 116 more than the next closest back. Sunday was perhaps his best performance yet, and the biggest splash came at the perfect time.
On a first-and-10 in the fourth quarter, he found an opening immediately and took it 76 yards to swing the game wide open, setting up Tyquan Thornton's second touchdown of the afternoon and giving the Chiefs a lead they would not relinquish.
His fourth-quarter production didn't stop there, though. He added two more touchdowns in the fourth quarter, one from two yards out and one from 22, to put the game away. Even without the long run, Walker still topped 100 yards. He finished with 177 yards on 22 carries, and the Chiefs do not win this game without him, once again.
The Chiefs did not record a sack for the third straight week, which remains a legitimate concern. But 18 pressures, according to PFF, and 10 quarterback hits on Kirk Cousins was progress, and nobody showed up bigger along the defensive line than defensive end George Karlaftis.
He accounted for six of those hits, and none was bigger than the last one. On the Chiefs' final defensive snap, his hit on Cousins caused an errant throw that undrafted rookie Xavier Nwankpa hauled in, allowing Kansas City to end the game in victory formation.
Karlaftis finished with eight pressures, double his output from any game through the first three weeks. When the defense needed a play to close it out, he delivered it as he did all afternoon.
The penalty gaffes will still drive Chiefs Kingdom crazy, but the unit made two plays that directly changed the game's outcome. The first came immediately after Walker's opening fourth-quarter score.
As Dareke Young was being tackled on the ensuing kickoff return, linebacker Jeffrey Bassa punched the ball clean out of his hands for fellow linebacker Jack Cochrane to recover at the Raiders' 22. Walker needed one play to run it in for his second touchdown and push the lead to 30-19.
The second ensued after a Raiders touchdown and a Chiefs three-and-out, when punter Matt Araiza booted a 52-yarder that Xavier Nwankpa downed at the one-yard line, forcing Las Vegas to go 99 yards to tie or win. Araiza placed all five of his punts inside the 20 on the afternoon.
Wide receiver Nikko Remigio also contributed a 27-yard punt return into Raiders territory in the third quarter, and Araiza picked up 12 yards on a fake punt for a first down, though neither led to a score. It was the unit’s best performance of the season.
Wide receiver Tyquan Thornton would have been just below Walker in the winners column if not for how his afternoon ended. After setting a career high with five catches for 111 yards and two touchdowns, including a 42-yarder and a 55-yarder that got the deep ball going for Kansas City, he suffered a dislocated ankle late in the game .
Doctors put the ankle back in place Sunday afternoon, and he flew back with the team, but he will miss significant time, and a season-ending injury is presumably not out of the question.
It is a particularly cruel twist of timing. Rashee Rice exited earlier with a hamstring injury, and Thornton stepped up in his absence as the team's most reliable passing-game threat, though Xavier Worthy had by far his best game of the season. Thornton’s emergence was starting to feel like a real development for this offense. For now, that will have to wait.
Exploiting the middle of the field against this Chiefs defense was always going to be the Raiders' game plan, and Las Vegas executed it well. The numbers were ugly.
Slot corners, linebackers, and safeties were targeted 34 times, allowing 26 catches for 301 yards, according to PFF. L'Jarius Sneed allowed nine catches on 11 targets for 88 yards, extending a troubling trend in coverage. Linebacker Nick Bolton was not far behind, allowing seven catches on eight targets for 79 yards.
Tight end Brock Bowers lived up to the billing with six catches for 86 yards and a touchdown, but he was not the only problem. Las Vegas had six pass catchers finish with 32 yards or more. Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo will need to find answers in the middle of the field during the bye week.
Given the final result and their personnel, you will walk away feeling acceptable about the offensive line's performance. But acceptable is a relative term when you look at the details.
Mahomes took eight hits, three of them from Maxx Crosby. Right tackle Jaylon Moore allowed a team-high four pressures, and Mahomes finished 15-for-30 for 225 yards, two touchdowns, and zero interceptions, his least efficient outing of the season, though he still averaged 7.5 yards per attempt.
To be fair, the Chiefs were without both Josh Simmons and Kingsley Suamataia (coach's decision) , and they allowed just two sacks against an extremely talented defensive end unit. The passing game got the job done when it needed to. But the offensive line needs reinforcements, and the bye week could not have come at a better time for this group to regroup.

title: Andy Reid Remains Tight-Lipped on Kingsley Suamataia’s Unexpected Chiefs Benching
full_text:
In the Kansas City Chiefs' 30-27 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders, a key piece on the offensive line was nowhere to be found. Kingsley Suamataia relinquished his starting left guard role to veteran Mike Caliendo for the entirety of the action.
During the contest, ESPN's Nate Taylor revealed that Suamataia's absence was a "coaching decision." He hadn't been listed on the injury report all week, making it clear that it was due to something behind the scenes. There were questions about whether Suamataia was out for personal reasons or being disciplined by the coaching staff. In his postgame press conference , Andy Reid didn't necessarily give reporters much to run with, addressing the situation before anyone could even ask.
"As far as the Kingsley thing goes, before you guys ask, that's between Kingsley and I," Reid said. "But we'll figure it out down the road. We'll be better as a team for it, and Kingsley will be better for it."
The decision to start Mike Caliendo over Kingsley Suamataia is a coaching decision, not injury related, per Chiefs. Caliendo is still lined up in the huddle for the first snap of the second quarter.
The 2024 second-round pick out of BYU had played all 201 offensive snaps at left guard prior to today. Instead, Caliendo received the nod at guard opposite Trey Smith on the right side.
Without speculating too much, it does sound like the decision was made based on something Suamataia did, potentially breaking a team rule or standard. Then again, it's evident that we're not going to get much information beyond Reid's comments.
Patrick Mahomes also addressed the situation after the game and acknowledged the importance of Suamataia. Then again, the Chiefs' signal-caller made it known that he had plenty of confidence in his replacement today. "Kingsley knows how important he is to the team," Mahomes said. "Like coach said, he'll keep it between him and Kingsley. But at the end of the day, we have a guy like Mike Caliendo who's played in a lot of big games and had a lot of reps. He stepped right in and did a great job against a really good defensive line. I have a ton of trust in him, and then we'll get Kingsley back in the fold here soon."
Suamataia is a tackle-turned-guard who excelled at his new position in 2025 , starting all 17 games there. It remains to be seen whether this coaching decision will extend beyond this week or if it will just be a one-time benching to teach him a lesson.
Overall, the offensive line wasn't particularly clean tonight. Mahomes was sacked twice on the afternoon, but the Raiders were in Kansas City's backfield on many occasions. Obviously, the best version of this Chiefs roster includes Suamataia at left guard. We should find out more about his status for Week 6 against the Los Angeles Chargers after the bye.

title: Andy Reid Provides Update on Tyquan Thornton After Gruesome Ankle Injury
full_text:
While the Kansas City Chiefs did enough to secure a road win against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, it didn't come without multiple key players going down. Unfortunately for head coach Andy Reid's crew, both of the noteworthy injuries from the game arrived at the wide receiver spot.
An afternoon that already saw Rashee Rice exit with a hamstring ailment got even worse when Tyquan Thornton's heroic effort got cut short in the early evening. The club's Sunday receiving leader sustained an ugly-looking ankle injury at the end of a 55-yard reception in the fourth quarter.
It was a critical third-down grab from Thornton, which paved the way for a touchdown by running back Kenneth Walker to close out the drive. The former second-round pick attempted to stand up and continue celebrating the catch, then realized he was injured due to his leg getting caught in a tackle by Raiders safety Treydan Stukes.
As expected, Thornton's day was done with less than four minutes left in the game. He left the field on the back of a cart while wearing an air cast on his left leg. Keep scrolling if you're squeamish.
Won’t show the full thing because it’s a difficult watch, but Tyquan Thornton tried to get up and then realized his ankle is pointing in the wrong direction. This sucks. pic.twitter.com/UeTHvR4wyb
Speaking to the media following Sunday's 30-27 narrow victory , Reid addressed the Thornton injury and provided an early update on his rising star wideout's status.
"Tyquan Thornton's ankle, that doesn't look good," Reid said. "He's going to fly back with us and we'll get further evaluation later here."
At the time of his injury, Thornton had set career-high marks for receiving yards (111) and touchdowns (two) in a game. The former New England Patriot and second-year Chief sits at 11 receptions for 219 yards and those two scores in 2026, just a season removed from a breakout 2025 that resulted in 19 snags, 438 yards and three touchdowns in 14 games.
Although it isn't clear how long Thornton will miss at this juncture, Reid knows Kansas City will have a void left both on and off the field.
#Chiefs WR Tyquan Thornton suffered a dislocated ankle that was put back into place by doctors earlier today. He did make the plane with the team. Thornton will have a full evaluation in the morning, along with a second opinion. Out indefinitely, but in good spirits. pic.twitter.com/DBvRHI3jeJ
"That's a rough one when you see your teammate [get hurt], especially a guy like Tyquan," Reid said. "Great father, great husband and all that. Just his attitude. You guys deal with him, you know. His attitude's unbelievable. He's great for the team and kind of a leader for that group in there. For that to happen — especially with the year he's having, he's having a phenomenal year to this point — and a great play to boot on top of that. It's a tough one to see for all the guys."
Behind Thornton, third-year man Xavier Worthy led the wide receiver room in Week 4 with four catches for 70 yards. Other options in the room include Rice (when healthy), Jalen Royals, Nikko Remigio and rookie Cyrus Allen .

title: 10 Instant Observations From the Chiefs’ Thrilling Rivalry Win Over Raiders
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs entered Raider week with some extra excitement surrounding the matchup, as both teams came in with undefeated records. While Las Vegas made a late push and kept things close throughout the afternoon, KC's defense tightened up and was able to triumph over its biggest rival 30-27.
This was a back-and-forth contest and one of the most entertaining games of the entire NFL season. It resulted in a victory for the Chiefs, even if they took a few blows along the way. Here are 10 instant observations from today's thriller in Vegas.
As soon as this penalty was called, I knew I'd have to find a way to work it into this article. It didn't end up being significant, but Nikko Remigio was flagged for an invalid fair catch signal on a punt return, setting the Chiefs back five yards in the third quarter.
The penalty has only been called four times since the 2018 campaign, and it could be the last time we see one all year. This was definitely a judgment call, as Remigio didn't fully wave his arm in the air, but it was still pretty funny to see such an unusual penalty called in a live game.
The Chiefs had scored on each of their first three opening drives this season (two touchdowns, one field goal). However, the offense began the day with a turnover on downs after Khyiris Tonga and Kenneth Walker III were stuffed up the middle on consecutive plays.
It only took Vegas four plays on its opening possession to get onto the board and kick off the scoring. Surely, this is a trend that Eric Bieniemy will want to erase moving forward.
Rookie wideout Cyrus Allen, the darling of training camp , received his first NFL target early in the contest today.
Of course, his appearance on the field came at the expense of two other receivers who will be mentioned later in the article, but we'll see if his workload gradually increases as the coaching staff has suggested .
Right before kickoff, it was revealed that left guard Kingsley Suamataia would not be starting as he usually does. Instead, veteran Mike Caliendo received the nod in his place.
Suamataia's benching was a coaching decision, as he was completely absent from the injury report all week. Whether it was for a disciplinary punishment or personal reasons remains to be seen. Regardless, Caliendo was beaten badly a few times today, and Las Vegas' relentless pressure made it clear that Kansas City could have used Suamataia in the trenches.
A Selfish, Stupid, and Petty Decision for Andy Reid to put a half a billion dollars worth of Patrick Mahomes coming off of a Torn ACL behind a turnstile in Mike Caliendo at LG because of a personal matter with Kingsley Suamataia. Coaching Malpractice. pic.twitter.com/F4JLvA1Hl5
After a three-and-out to open the afternoon, the Chiefs were forced to send out their punting unit. However, they noticed that Vegas had sent several players deep into coverage, which opened the door for a tremendous trick play by Matt Araiza.
FAKE PUNT ALERT 🚨 @KCvsLV on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/kzaqwL8CMM
Kansas City's punter fooled everyone in Allegiant Stadium by sprinting toward the right hash and successfully converting a fourth-and-nine to keep the drive alive. He was already leading the NFL in yards per punt heading into the contest and downed the Raiders at the one-yard line in the final minutej, but Araiza just pulled off perhaps the best highlight of his career on a non-kicking play.
While Patrick Mahomes had to roll out of the pocket several times today to evade pressure and hit the grass on several occasions, Kirk Cousins had all the time in the world under center. For the third consecutive game, the Chiefs' defensive line failed to record a sack. Kansas City has now gone more than 180 minutes of football without bringing down an opposing quarterback. The 38-year-old Cousins isn't exactly a spring chicken, either. No Chiefs player logged a QB hit until there was less than a minute left in the first half.
Chris Jones has expressed frustration with the media's criticism of the defensive line. Although Steve Spagnuolo got a little more creative with his personnel in the second half, there have to be tangible results at some point. When you consider that Daniel Jones and Malik Willis — the last two quarterbacks Kansas City faced — were sacked a combined four times today alone, it makes you wonder why this pass rush can't get into the backfield.
I took offense to the unnecessary roughness call on Nohl Williams in the second quarter. He made an exceptional play and met the receiver immediately after he made contact with the ball. What else was he supposed to do in that situation?
Jalen Nailor Gets Decked By Nohl Williams After A Hospital Ball From Kirk Cousins 😭 That Was A Dangerous Throw. pic.twitter.com/KLpEgQyOUI
It stinks that Jalen Nailor had to get hurt in the process, but if Williams had sagged off and not tried to make a play on the ball, he would have been gifting Nailor a free touchdown had he come down with it. And as for calling him a "defenseless receiver," the only person who deserves criticism for that is Kirk Cousins, who put him in that position in the first place.
Thankfully for Kansas City, it didn't matter too much in the end, as the defense stood tall in the red zone. However, the penalty turned what would have been a 45-yard field goal attempt into a chip shot.
When it looked like the offense had no juice, running back Kenneth Walker flipped the momentum in an instant. On the final play of the third quarter, he broke off a 77-yard run, the longest of his young Chiefs tenure and his entire NFL career.
Kansas City was trailing by three at the time, but Mahomes found Tyquan Thornton for his second touchdown of the day on second-and-goal to give the Chiefs the lead. This was shaping up to be an "off day" for Walker's standards until he single-handedly helped change the outcome with one explosive burst.
Kenneth Walker III breaks a 77-yard run pic.twitter.com/BXqfVBaR84
Walker wound up scoring two touchdowns in fewer than 30 seconds after he ran it in to give the Chiefs a 23-19 lead, then found paydirt again after the Raiders fumbled the kickoff. He finished the day with an unbelievable season-high 177 yards on the ground.
Now sitting at 537 rushing yards on the year, Walker is the clear favorite to win the rushing title and could even make a case for AFC Offensive Player of the Year. He's been one of the most dynamic weapons in the NFL and has quickly become a must-watch player.
If there's one thing Klint Kubiak's squad proved today, it's that they can put up a fight with anyone. I came away thoroughly impressed by this perceived inferior Raiders roster matching up with Kansas City physically and athletically all day.
A lot of the questions surrounding Las Vegas through its first few weeks were about the level of competition it had faced. However, this Chiefs group is a true Super Bowl contender, and the Raiders just held their own for an hour of game time. I'm not necessarily saying that the Raiders will be competing for the division by the end of the season, but it wouldn't surprise me if they finish above .500 and remain in the mix for a Wild Card spot.
On his first catch of the day, Rashee Rice came up lame trying to make a defender miss in the open field. He darted to the sideline and did not return due to a hamstring injury .
Rashee Rice hurt it was non contact pic.twitter.com/PGgn1ashNM
Concerns about the receiver room already existed after Rice went down, but an even more significant blow came with three minutes left in the fourth quarter when Tyquan Thornton suffered what appeared to be a broken ankle on a 55-yard catch. That reception turned out to be the game-winning play for the Chiefs, but it was a bittersweet feeling afterward.
Tyquan Thornton went down after this play pic.twitter.com/oRrUsDxfQ7 https://t.co/mZ6TjUmnI1
Thornton had suddenly emerged as one of Mahomes' favorite targets, but he's almost certainly played his final game of…

title: Chiefs WR Rashee Rice Exits Week 4 Game vs. Raiders With Injury
full_text:
UPDATE: Rice has been downgraded to doubtful, per the Chiefs .
The original story, in its entirety, continues below.
The Kansas City Chiefs rolled into Sunday's showdown against the Las Vegas Raiders with a healthy receiver room, but that didn't last long. On just the second offensive series of the game, No. 1 target Rashee Rice appeared to suffer an injury.
On a first-and-10 pass from quarterback Patrick Mahomes, Rice gained seven yards but quickly came up gimpy and was grabbing at his left leg. He quickly exited for the sideline and remained there for the rest of the possession, which ended with a touchdown.
The Chiefs have confirmed a hamstring injury for Rice, deeming him questionable to return. He went to the locker room around the start of the second quarter.
Rashee Rice pulled up after a catch and exited the game with an apparent leg injury pic.twitter.com/VXDskpMIHR
With Kansas City near the goal line near the conclusion of the series, sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson provided a quick update on Rice's status.
"You mentioned about Rashee Rice, Wolfson said. "He has been standing on the sideline talking to head athletic trainer Rick Burkholder. He doesn't seem to want to go in the locker room. He's trying to stretch out that leg. No official report. It looks like he wants to get back in, but they maybe wait until after this drive to bring him into the locker room."
A former second-round pick, Rice entered Week 4 with 13 catches for 190 yards and a touchdown across Weeks 1-3. After a quiet 2026 debut that saw him record just a pair of snags for 19 yards, he combined for 11 catches on 15 targets for 171 yards over the next two contests. He came alive in last weekend's showing against the Miami Dolphins, drawing the praise of head coach Andy Reid.
“Yeah, it was good to see him get a couple catches in there that were physical, good, strong catches," Reid said. "He's so good with the ball after he gets it and so physical that he adds another dimension to that. He's almost like having a running back at a wide receiver spot where when he gets it, he's going to bring it and that's always good.”
According to SumerSports , Rice leads the Chiefs' wideout room with an 18.68% target share. He's an integral part of the offense, serving as a volume funnel for Mahomes and taking some pressure off Xavier Worthy and Tyquan Thornton to perform.
Rice played catch-up during training camp after returning from offseason knee surgery. He also spent time in jail following a probation violation, although he's clearly been able to get closer to his 2024 and 2025 self prior to Sunday's injury.

title: Complete Chiefs Inactives for Week 4 vs. Raiders: Who's In, Who's Out?
full_text:
In the blink of an eye, the Kansas City Chiefs will be almost a quarter of the way through the 2026 NFL regular season. Sunday's Week 4 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders has significant AFC West implications , too, as both teams enter the clash at 3-0 on the year.
As is always the case at this point in the campaign, neither team is 100% healthy. Kansas City is still without one of its top starters, whereas Las Vegas rolled into the weekend expecting to miss one of its first-string linemen as well. Those absences, paired with other game-day calls on who will and will not suit up, add some intrigue to a contest that's already loaded with storylines .
With that in mind, here's who's inactive for Kansas City and Las Vegas in Sunday's matchup.
Chiefs inactive list vs. Raiders in Week 4: LT Josh Simmons QB Garrett Nussmeier  (3rd QB) TE Jared Wiley OT Diego Pounds DE Jack Pyburn CB Jadon Canady Chiefs elevated LB Cole Christiansen from the practice squad for today's game.
Just like Weeks 1-3, there aren't many surprises here. The most notable name is left tackle Josh Simmons, who's been nursing a back injury for well over a month now. This week, head coach Andy Reid provided some more details on the issue and said it's a bulging disc . Simmons hasn't practiced since August; it remains to be seen whether he'll make his 2026 debut in Week 6 following the Chiefs' bye.
In better news, safety Chamarri Conner is active for the first time this season. He sat out the team's first three games with a knee ailment but was a full participant in this week's practices. The defense's leading snap-getter from 2025 figures to eventually replace Jaden Hicks as a starter alongside offseason pickup Alohi Gilman in the secondary.
On Saturday, Kansas City announced that linebacker Cole Christiansen was activated from the practice squad via standard elevation. That maxes out his allotted total of three elevations for the regular season, meaning he'll head back to the practice squad following Sunday's game. If he's to be promoted again, it'd either have to be a signing to the 53-man roster or a postseason activation when limits reset.
Inactives for #KCvsLV pic.twitter.com/G5crDAJZMH
On the Raiders' Friday injury report, quarterback Aiden O'Connell (non-injury-related/personal) was deemed questionable for Week 4 after not practicing all week. Offensive lineman Jackson Powers-Johnson also missed the week of work following a groin injury sustained in last week's win over the New Orleans Saints. He was ruled out prior to the weekend.
Elsewhere, tight end Brock Bowers was a limited participant in Friday's practice due to knee injury management but didn't carry a designation. He was added to the Las Vegas injury report on Sunday morning with an illness, although initial reporting signaled that the club fully anticipated him being good to go for Week 4. That's held consistent leading into game time.

title: Chiefs vs. Raiders: NFL Week 4 Preview, Score Predictions
full_text:
Who would've anticipated the Chiefs and Raiders playing for the top seed in the division in Week 4? Regardless of who called that shot, it's the reality sitting in front of both franchises on Sunday.
Behind a lava-hot start from quarterback Kirk Cousins and some of the best defending Las Vegas has seen in years, the Raiders have fared like a force to be reckoned with under new head coach Klint Kubiak. Andy Reid's Kansas City squad, meanwhile, keeps chugging along but still has some things to sort out before being an unquestioned Super Bowl-caliber group again.
How might Sunday's game unfold? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 4 of the regular season.
Joshua Brisco: Even with a bit of skepticism regarding how "for real" the Raiders may be, their strengths line up well with many of the Chiefs' biggest questions. The Raiders' trio of edge rushers (Maxx Crosby, Kwity Paye and Malcolm Koonce) will have a chance to stress-test both Kahlil Benson and Jaylon Moore while Patrick Mahomes tries to keep the passing game on track.
I have total faith in the Chiefs' boundary corners, but tight end Brock Bowers can line up anywhere on the field, giving Las Vegas a chance to hunt for favorable matchups. Kansas City's pass rush is improved, but Kirk Cousins can get rid of the ball quickly, similarly to how Daniel Jones stayed clean in Week 2.
All in all, I think the Chiefs are the better team, but the Raiders have some key places to search for advantages. I'll ride with the better overall squad in a close game.
Jordan Foote: There's no love lost between these AFC West rivals, but the Chiefs have made it known this week that they believe their foes are a worthy opponent. Whether it's head coach Andy Reid tipping his cap to Vegas or quarterback Patrick Mahomes doing the same to Crosby , the respect level is there.
I'm just not sure it means anything on the field. While the Raiders' offense has played some low-mistake football and the defense is forcing plenty of turnovers, not all of this seems sustainable. That isn't to say the home crowd and some self-inflicted errors on the Chiefs' behalf couldn't swing this one in the other direction, but the better team should win.
I'll roll with the Chiefs here in a one-score victory that sends folks into the bye week still not completely sold on the offense or defense, although still feeling well enough given the circumstances of a road triumph over an undefeated intradivision club.
Joshua Schulman: Everything is clicking for Klint Kubiak’s group through the first trio of games. It leads the NFL in turnover margin and has not allowed a point in the fourth quarter all season. Then again, 38-year-old Kirk Cousins is bound to come back to Earth at some point, and the Raiders haven’t encountered a weapon as dynamic as Kenneth Walker yet.
This 3-0 start from Vegas has been a fun story, but it’s time for it to come to an end… right? In the words of the legendary Lee Corso, not so fast, my friend!
Brock Bowers will single-handedly pick apart KC’s second level, and Ashton Jeanty is bound for a big evening against an underperforming Chiefs defensive line. Steve Spagnuolo’s defense simply hasn’t passed the eye test for me so far, and I think this week is when it finally gets exposed. Kansas City will have a better record this season when it’s all said and done, but I’m picking LV to hand Andy Reid’s squad its first defeat of 2026.
Tyler Brown: This could be foolish, but this one feels like a grind from start to finish. The Raiders aren't the pushover Miami was supposed to be, and Cousins is playing well enough to keep Las Vegas in it. Bowers will get his, and the Chiefs' defense will not have all the answers.
Steve Spagnuolo has shown enough in his career to know how to limit a team's top weapon just enough when the moment calls for it, and Kansas City's offense should do enough on the other side to keep the Raiders from ever feeling comfortable.
The key is whether Andy Reid can establish the run game early and take the pressure off both tackles and the passing game. If Walker gets going and the play-action opens up the way it did against Miami, Mahomes should have enough answers to stay a step ahead of Rob Leonard's defense all afternoon.
The Raiders will make it interesting, and Chiefs Kingdom may be holding their breath late, but Kansas City has too many weapons and too much experience in close games to let this one slip away.

title: 3 Winners and 5 Losers After Chargers' Flop vs. Seahawks
full_text:
The Chargers walked out of Seattle still searching for their first win after a 30-23 loss. A disastrous opening half put them in a major hole, and while the offense showed enough fight to make the final minutes interesting, the early mistakes ultimately proved too costly.
There were still some encouraging individual performances, but several players and position groups left the afternoon with plenty to improve on.
Cameron Dicker once again provided reliable production when his team needed it. He went 3-for-3 on field goals and converted both extra-point attempts, accounting for all 11 of his points.
With several drives failing to reach the end zone, getting points whenever possible was important. Dicker gave his team that consistency and avoided adding another problem to an afternoon already filled with them.
Omarion Hampton did not get an enormous number of touches, but he made his opportunities count. The rookie carried the ball nine times for 45 yards and scored the team’s opening touchdown.
His five yards per carry suggested there was room for the running game to make an impact if given a larger role. Hampton also caught both passes thrown his way, showing that he can contribute outside of the backfield.
Finding more ways to involve Hampton should be a priority going forward.
Tuli Tuipulotu was one of the few defensive players consistently making things happen. He recorded six tackles, half a sack, a forced fumble and the first interception of his NFL career.
The interception was particularly important because it gave the offense another chance to generate momentum. Even with Seattle finding success early, Tuipulotu continued creating disruption near the line of scrimmage.
THE CHARGERS DEFENSE GET IT RIGHT BACK!! ⚡️ @LACvsSEA on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/d17s4Ng7cL
Justin Herbert had an afternoon he would probably like to forget. He threw for 189 yards and a touchdown, but two interceptions and a lost fumble played a major role in the outcome.
The slow start was particularly damaging. Herbert entered halftime with only 36 passing yards, leaving the offense struggling to keep pace while Seattle built its advantage.
There was a different version of Herbert in the fourth quarter, when he helped spark a late comeback attempt. By then, however, the turnovers had already created too much ground to make up.
Some of the best and worst from Justin Herbert today from the end zone angle pic.twitter.com/BXFWsHvfMF
Derius Davis made one of the game’s most costly errors when he muffed a punt. Seattle capitalized immediately, turning the short field into a touchdown.
Mistakes like that become even more damaging when an offense is already struggling to put together productive drives. Davis finished with just one catch for six yards, meaning there was little offensive production elsewhere to make up for the turnover.
Protection was a major issue throughout the afternoon. Herbert was sacked four times, and the constant pressure prevented the offense from developing any consistent rhythm. The most damaging moment came toward the end of the game, when a strip-sack wiped out one of the final opportunities to complete the comeback.
The offense showed considerably more life after halftime, but it is difficult to sustain that momentum when the quarterback is constantly under pressure.
Ladd McConkey was barely involved in the passing game. He received only two targets and finished without a catch.
That lack of involvement stands out, especially considering how important McConkey is to the passing attack. Playing from behind should have created even more opportunities for one of the team’s primary receiving threats. Seattle deserves credit for its defensive performance, but finding ways to get McConkey involved has to be a priority.
The opening two quarters were the biggest overall disappointment. The offense managed just six points before halftime and repeatedly struggled to stay ahead of the chains.
By the time the team found its rhythm, Seattle had already built a 20-6 advantage. Four turnovers made the comeback even more difficult.
The second half offered a glimpse of what this group can accomplish when everything starts clicking. The problem is that waiting until the game is nearly out of reach leaves almost no room for another mistake.
FINAL: #SEAHAWKS 30, CHARGERS 23

title: Should the Los Angeles Chargers Fire Mike McDaniel?
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers were within striking range of winning a Super Bowl during the 2026 NFL season, at least according to many media personalities and outlets. This hype for the Bolts majorly stemmed from the fact that Justin Herbert, one of the league's best quarterbacks, is now finally paired with an offensive coordinator who can elevate him, rather than weigh him down.
That offensive coordinator was Mike McDaniel, the former 49ers offensive coordinator and former Miami Dolphins head coach. After being fired in Miami for reasons other than his offense, it made perfect sense for all sides to have McDaniel come in for a year and revitalize his name and abilities as an NFL coach. The Chargers in their Super Bowl window (at least, as thought by the fanbase and front office) will have a one-year rental of one of the league's premier play callers.
Instead, the Chargers are now 0-4 with the fourth-worst offense in the entire NFL (by points per game; stats courtesy of teamrankings.com ). They are behind the likes of the New York Giants, New York Jets, Cleveland Browns, Atlanta Falcons, etc. McDaniel seems aware of these shortcomings , yet he still finds himself here.
Beyond points per game, McDaniel's Chargers rank 22nd in passing yards, 25th in passing touchdowns, T-2nd in turnovers given, 21st in yards per game, T-21st in third-down conversion rate and sixth-worst QB sack percentage. McDaniel's run game fares slightly better with the ninth-best rushing yards per game ranking.
Beyond the rankings and statistics, some of the anecdotal things seen from the viewpoint of fans could give reason for the seat to get even warmer for the former Dolphins head coach.
1. Predictability : McDaniel often gives tells about where a run play is going by personnel. If Omarion Hampton is in, it's going inside the tackles. If Keaton Mitchell is in, it is going outside . While it is not 100% this way, it is noticeable enough for defenses to constantly make plays in the backfield against a team with an already struggling offensive line.
2. Outside runs to the short side of the field: At least to my knowledge, it is extremely important to know where the ball is placed on the field, whether it is the hashes or the middle section of the field. This allows you to either open up plays or remove plays that you can call, depending on where the ball is. McDaniel often runs plays that need more room (like tosses or sweeps) to the short side of the field, yielding less ability for the ball carrier to have space to make plays.
3. Simply being "too cute": As much as I would like to be complimented on McDaniel's appearance in this section, this is about his poor play calling and his job security with the Chargers. McDaniel has run 68.4% of plays in motion, only behind the Miami Dolphins and San Francisco 49ers  ( stat courtesy of SharpFootballAnalysis ), both of which were previous teams that McDaniel coached for. While pre-snap motion can cause conflict for defenses, it can also allow for the offense to make more mistakes and find zero rhythm, with the team constantly having to wait or time up motions correctly for them to work effectively. The Chargers as a team rank fourth-worst in penalties, with the majority of the issues stemming from the offense.
So, with the Chargers losing and not scoring nearly enough points , what is the verdict? The truth is that the verdict is already out, and McDaniel will not be fired, even with his very poor first month in Los Angeles.
Jim Harbaugh was asked after the Seattle Seahawks' loss if McDaniel's job was on the line. He responded with : "No, his job is not in jeopardy. He's a skilled coach and we're going to keep growing."
This essentially ends the debate over what will happen. However, the debate over what should happen should continue until the "mastermind" proves himself to be such in the 2026 NFL season.

title: The Morning-After Thunder: Chargers Show Signs of Life, Too Little Too Late, Now 0-4
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers dragged a banged-up roster to Lumen Field in Seattle to try to find themselves and pull their season from the darkness enveloping them. They fell further down the dark hole against the Seahawks in the first half but now head home with signs of life and at a confusing point moving forward.
Quarterback Justin Herbert continues to look lost and the worst he's looked in his NFL career. Herbert threw a terrible interception on the first play from scrimmage. and another later in the second quarter that was worse than the first.
The defense, for the second week in a row, came for a fist fight against the defending Super Bowl champions. The offense and special teams put them into indefensible positions all game. Seattle's first touchdown came off the defense shutting down Sam Darnold and the Seahawks deep in their own territory and on the ensuing punt, the ball bounced off of returner Derius Davis' chest and the Seahawks recovered the ball just outside of the 20-yard line. Seattle scored on the next play.
Los Angeles' defense appeared to react all game with pure exasperation when the offense or special teams left them in terrible positions. After the muffed punt and interceptions, the defense seemed to put up little fight immediately after and the Seahawks scored almost instantly. Outside of those moments, the defense went to absolute war to try to keep the game within reach.
For the second week in a row, the Chargers offense couldn't move the ball with any level of consistency and finished the first half with less than 100 yards of total offense. Justin Herbert had a big scramble near the end of the half to get the Chargers within field goal range to get to six points to cut the lead to 20-6.
The Seahawks opened up the second half with a touchdown drive and the Chargers looked helpless, until they didn't. Justin Herbert unlocked something in the second half, he took started scrambling around and simply engaged playmaker mode and started running around instead of staying locked into the offense and playbook.
The offensive line started to drop left and right, literally. Right tackle Joe Alt went down with a neck injury, left guard Trevor Penning went down with a head injury, their replacements were rookies Travis Burke and Logan Taylor. Herbert ended up taking a nasty lower-leg hit from Seahawks edge rusher Demarcus Lawrence which resulted in a 15-yard roughing penalty and several plays later he took another massive hit courtesy of defensive lineman Derrick Hall, which appeared to hurt the same ribs he cracked a few years back. The hit did draw another 15-yard roughing call. Trey Lance warmed up but Herbert was not coming out.
The offense suddenly had life. Kimani Vidal scored on an angry run nearly stating with his play that he was sick and tired of this and was not going to be denied. The Chargers offense went down and scored on their next drive, this time capping off the drive with an Omarion Hampton angry run. Left tackle Rashawn Slater was injured and exited the play before the score, the Chargers were out of reserve offensive lineman.
Hampton's score came behind rookie lineman Logan Taylor swapped from left guard where he originally replaced Trevor Penning, over to left tackle, Jake Slaughter shifted to left guard, undrafted rookie Jacob Spomer took over at center, Cole Strange held down the right guard spot and rookie Travis Burke stayed at right tackle for this play.
oh my o pic.twitter.com/t90ObcuqhJ
The Chargers eventually got the ball back, down by ten. Herber and the offense faced a tough fourth and down deep near their own endzone and Herbert escaped the pocket and made a merculean throw deep and wide receive Quentin Johnston leaped from the ashes of ruin and made a spectacular catch to keep the drive, and team alive. They quickly marched down the field, got close enough and made the smart decision to kick a field goal before the two-minute warning.
OMG, Q!!! pic.twitter.com/jCRsnZMPft
The defense showed up one final time and locked down the Seahawks and got the ball back to the offense with just under two minutes left in the game. The offensive line, almost entirely backups, could not hold up for the final drive and Justin Hebert was strip sacked to end the game.
Following an uninspired first half that looked like it could have gotten out of hand, the Chargers found some life. It seemed to be driven by Herbert, he finally showed fight and a willingness to sacrifice himself to try to get back in the game no matter what.
This game could have easily shifted to a 2023 style Thursday night meltdown against the Raiders, but the team put their feet down and fought back. They didn't give up, but they are still 0-4.
The odds now for this season to be anything but a failure are near zero, so now what? They aren't giving up but they are severely injured, but it looks like their next opponents, the Denver Broncos are too.

title: Chargers Stock Report: Three Players Rising and Two Falling After Week 4
full_text:
Now that the Los Angeles Chargers have found themselves 0-4 and likely completely out of playoff contention, it is important to see what the future of this franchise is, especially considering the possibility of major moves across the coaching staff coming soon.
On a player scale, who are some guys rising and falling after the Chargers' somewhat impressive (considering what we have seen) performance against the Super Bowl champions of last year, the Seattle Seahawks?
Oronde Gadsden II has been placed on riser and faller lists before, being both a "riser" and a "faller" after his seemingly up-and-down 2026 NFL season. For this week, he finds himself as a riser, being a more reliable target in the passing game, gathering five catches for 36 yards, including a juggling fourth-down conversion late in the game.
To be truthful, it is tiring putting Derius Davis on these lists as a faller or whatever negative category the article calls for. However, he continues to disappoint and make this Chargers team worse. He had a better day as a kick returner with 32 yards per return, but a muffed punt turnover marked his day as a failure.
Tre Harris is finally getting more and more involved in this weak Chargers offense. He has been a reliable target who can take some of the load off of Justin Herbert and Ladd McConkey. He recorded another good week, tallying a team-high 60 yards on three receptions. He was the only wide receiver with a reception until Quentin Johnston had his 44-yard reception deep in the fourth quarter.
Cole Strange has been a terrible starter for the Chargers, even going back into the preseason. He has not shown anything as a run blocker or as a pass blocker. While PFF grades are becoming more and more unreliable, it is worth noting that at halftime, Strange had a 0.0 pass-blocking grade. For what it's worth, Trevor Penning had a 4.9 grade, making Strange not alone as an underperforming offensive lineman.
Chargers halftime @PFF pass blocking grades vs Seahawks pic.twitter.com/0fIQP5PClG
All we can really say is "poor Khalil Mack ," as he is having a very strong season, even in his mid-30s. He deserves to be on a team better than the Los Angeles Chargers. That said, his day against a strong Seattle offensive tackle duo had him recording a sack, a tied team-high six tackles, while wreaking havoc in the backfield as one of the Bolts' only capable run defenders.

title: Chargers vs. Seahawks predictions, injuries and concerns
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are in now-or-never mode during the Week 4 encounter with the Seattle Seahawks.
Both the Chargers and Seahawks have some major injury concerns following them into the game. But it’s Jim Harbaugh’s Chargers risking an 0-4 mark while the Mike McDaniel-Justin Herbert pairing flops .
Here’s a look at things from the Seahawks’ point of view, courtesy of Seahawks on SI’s Jeremy Brener.
Seahawks on SI: I wouldn't say "big" concerns, but there might be some small ones. It's Seattle's first loss in 12 games dating back to last season, so it's definitely a shock to the system. However, watching the game, they fell to a team by two points in a rainy weather game on the east coast with a quarterback coming off of an injury who still nearly threw for 400 yards. They certainly could have put together a worse performance.
Charbonnet is still on the PUP List, so he's out for Week 4. A return in Week 5 or 6 isn't out of the question. His return to practice this week is a step in the right direction.
The Seahawks have a healthy squad this week for the Chargers game, but Jadarian Price (chest) missed Thursday's practice after limited participation on Wednesday, so that's something to monitor.
There's been some trouble at right guard with Anthony Bradford's injury. He went to IR after missing Week 2. Christian Haynes and rookie Beau Stephens have been holding the fort down, but it's a spot that can be exposed by the Chargers defensive line that could really change the game.
The run game. It performed well in the first two weeks, which led to wins. It dropped off a cliff in Week 3 and it cost them. The Seahawks want to be a smash mouth running offense, but the personnel makes it difficult. Price's fumbling issues in the last two weeks, Charbonnet's injury and inconsistency in snaps for Emanuel Wilson and George Holani have disrupted the rhythm in that part of the offense.
I think this game is low-scoring, but Jaxon Smith-Njigba plays for the Seahawks, so I've got them winning. He's picking up where he left off last year by leading the league in receptions, yards and touchdowns. I think he scores another one or two as the Seahawks win 23-13.

title: Fantasy Football Start or Sit: Can Ladd McConkey, Omarion Hampton Produce vs. Seahawks?
full_text:
In the last three weeks the Los Angeles Chargers' playmakers have had many inconsistent performances. The Bolts have a difficult matchup ahead against the Seattle Seahawks, which makes this a tricky week for fantasy managers.
Some of these might be bold , however this game feels a bit different for me. I believe they will turn it around in all aspects of the game. With that being said, here are three Chargers worth putting into your lineup and three who could be better left on the bench.
Hampton is still the Chargers running back I would trust most because of the opportunity he receives. Even with Seattle presenting a difficult matchup, his ability to contribute on the ground gives him a chance to put together a useful fantasy day. He is worth keeping in starting lineups, especially for managers who need a running back with a solid workload.
fantasy managers take note pic.twitter.com/6atkzV9XvH
McConkey would normally be an easy player to consider, but his health makes this a much tougher decision. He is dealing with a foot injury heading into the game, and the Seahawks are not an ideal defense to test with a banged-up receiver. If you have another dependable option available, I would stay away from McConkey this week.
Herbert has not had the start to the season fantasy managers were hoping for, but this could be an opportunity for him to turn things around. The Chargers need their passing game to find some consistency, and Herbert remains the player most capable of creating something when the offense gets stuck. I would still give him a chance in most leagues because it’s only a matter of time until he produces an elite performance.
Mitchell has shown flashes, but there simply isn’t enough consistency in his role to make him an appealing fantasy option this week. Hampton remains the primary back, and Seattle’s defense makes the Chargers backfield even harder to predict. He is almost a touchdown or bust type of player. Unless your roster is extremely thin, Mitchell belongs on the bench.
Harris is the kind of player who could make a fantasy lineup worthwhile with just a few big plays. The Chargers need another receiver to emerge alongside their top options, and Harris has the talent to take advantage if opportunities come his way. He is more of a flex play than a must-start, but I like his upside enough to put him in lineups this week.
Johnston is another Chargers receiver who is difficult to trust against Seattle. His fantasy value depends heavily on whether he can turn limited opportunities into significant plays, and that’s a risky proposition against a defense that can make life difficult for opposing passing games. I would look for a safer option at receiver or flex this week.

title: Is Ladd McConkey Playing Today? Chargers vs. Seahawks Updates for Week 4
full_text:
Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Ladd McConkey continues to be a staple of the injury report ahead of his team’s Week 4 game against the Seattle Seahawks .
McConkey has had multiple nagging injuries through three games, which have played a part in the super-underwhelming Mike McDaniel-Justin Herbert offense for the winless Chargers.
That’s to say nothing, of course, for the fantasy football players who invested in McConkey early and probably have similar records to those Chargers right now.

Ladd McConkey’s injury is a disaster for the Chargers. If he’s on the field, there’s a chance it helps with the spacing of McDaniel’s offense because defenses need to respect him.

title: Chargers Confidence Meter: Will LA Get Their First Win of the Season?
full_text:
It is getting to the point where the Los Angeles Chargers have to stop talking about what they should be and actually show it on the field.
The Bolts come into Seattle winless , and there is obviously plenty of reason for fans to be frustrated. This team has had opportunities in every game, but somehow they keep finding ways to let them slip away. The offense has been the biggest concern, and through three games, they simply have not looked like the team many expected them to be coming into the season.
But this is where my confidence meter starts to move a little bit.
I am not going into this game thinking they are guaranteed to win. Honestly, that would be ridiculous. Seattle is 2–1, they are playing at home, and they have one of the better defenses this team has faced so far. The Seahawks are also coming off a loss, which means they are going to be looking to respond in front of their home crowd.
Still, there are reasons to believe this team can make this interesting.
The biggest thing I want to see is Justin Herbert playing like Justin Herbert. He has not been terrible, but the offense has not given him enough opportunities to consistently get into a rhythm. At some point, this team has to let its quarterback take control of the game instead of constantly playing from behind.
The defense is another reason I am not completely out of this group. Against Buffalo last week, the defense forced five turnovers and still lost. That is incredibly frustrating, but it also shows that this unit is capable of creating opportunities. The problem is that the offense has to actually turn those opportunities into points. And that might be the entire game right there. If they can protect the football, avoid giving Seattle easy possessions and finally string together some offensive drives, I think this game can be much closer than people expect. Seattle is favored for a reason, but the Seahawks are not unbeatable. They just lost a 33–31 game to Washington last week after turning the ball over three times.
For me, this is less about expecting the Bolts to suddenly become a Super Bowl contender and more about wanting to see some fight. An 0–4 start would put this team in a really uncomfortable position. A win in Seattle would completely changes the conversation going into Week five.
I believe they can win this game. I just need to see them prove they can finish one.

title: Monday Morning Rambling: Rams Finally Flip the Script in Win Over Eagles
full_text:
Over the last two years, the Los Angeles Rams haven’t just lost games. They’ve found ways to lose in the most gut-wrenching fashion possible . It hasn’t been often that the Rams have lost ‘normally’.
In their first loss of the 2025 season, the Rams fell to the Philadelphia Eagles after not one, but two potential game-winning field goals were blocked. In Week 5, the Rams lost to the 49ers, getting stopped on 4th-and-1 from the 11-yard line in overtime.
How the Eagles' game-ending field goal block on Joshua Karty sounded on Rams radio pic.twitter.com/ZYymbHtcyb
While the Rams didn’t lose again until Week 13 to the Carolina Panthers, Matthew Stafford fumbled with the offense in field-goal range to tie the game late.
Everybody remembers what happened in Week 16 when the Rams blew a 16-point lead to the Seattle Seahawks with the help of a controversial two-point conversion to lose in overtime. When they tried to lose in a normal fashion, they still managed to come back from 21-0 against the Atlanta Falcons to lose on a field goal in the final 30 seconds.
Zach Charbonnet with one of the craziest two-point conversions ever 😳 pic.twitter.com/cVxpndsudN
In the NFC Championship Game, the Rams got stopped on fourth-and-4 from the six when trying to take the lead in the final five minutes. That was after fighting back from 11 points down because of a muffed punt.
Fast forward to this year, and the Rams lost last week to the Denver Broncos after leading 16-0 at the half and then coming up on the wrong end of a defensive pass interference penalty.
Josh Wallace called for DPI against Pat Bryant pic.twitter.com/8QJQNT46Lg
It’s been special teams gaffes, controversial officiating decisions, untimely turnovers and a plethora of other issues. However, when the Rams have lost over the last two years, they’ve tested the sanity and emotional breaking point of fans.
On Sunday against the Eagles, the Rams looked to be dead in the water . They trailed 20-10 and had shown no signs of being able to move down the field to score. While Nick Sirianni got criticized for his decision to go for it from the two-yard line, could you blame him? The Eagles got stopped, but Matthew Stafford and the Rams’ offense faced a 98-yard field in front of them. In their previous five drives combined, the Rams had only picked up 75 yards.
With 8:17 left in the fourth quarter, the Rams had a 3.2 percent win probability according to Next Gen Stats. Even when the Rams took over with 7:26 left in the game, they only had a 5.1 percent win probability according to ESPN Stats and Info.
It was looking to be a box score anomaly. At that point, the Rams were set to become the first team since the 1997 Chicago Bears to lose while holding their opponent to at least 0-for-12 on third down. Teams were previously 2-23 when going at least 0-for-12 on third down and had lost 23 straight. The Rams had significantly outgained the Eagles. Through three quarters, the Rams had 247 yards to the Eagles’ 119.
Stafford hadn’t played well up to that point . In fact, the only quarterback to win a game with 50 or more passing attempts, 300 passing yards, two interceptions and zero touchdowns was Jameis Winston back in 2018. Up until Sunday, quarterbacks were 1-27 with that stat line.
Much like he had in the Super Bowl, head coach Sean McVay gathered his offense to remind them what was at stake and not to lose belief. There may have only been eight minutes left, but the game was far from over.
The thing with Stafford is that he can play poorly for 3.5 quarters, but more often than not, he plays his best football in that final half of the fourth quarter. That was the case on Sunday. On the Rams’ two scoring drives in the fourth quarter, Stafford was 12-for-15 for 140 yards. When Kyren Williams broke three tackles to put the Rams up 24-20 and give the Rams their first lead of the game, McVay’s speech had worked, and a switch had flipped for the Rams’ offense.
When Kam Curl batted down Jalen Hurts’ pass on fourth down, it was as if a huge weight was lifted off the Rams’ shoulders. For all the times that the Rams had lost in the most gut-wrenching ways possible, they had finally come out on the other end of one. It was the most improbable win since McVay took over as the Rams’ head coach, and it was also one that this team desperately needed.
Over the past two years, I’ve been one of Kyren Williams’ biggest critics. That’s not to say I haven’t been appreciative of his value to the Rams’ offense. At the same time, I have questioned whether or not he should be the bell cow in the backfield. The Rams do not beat the Eagles without Williams. It certainly didn’t look like Todd Gurley, but Williams had a Gurley-esque stat line. His touchdown run to put the Rams ahead in the fourth quarter was iconic and will go down as one of the best plays of the season.
Kyren Williams POWERS IT IN FOR THE LEAD!! @LARvsPHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/LW85llHviL
Much like with Williams, the Rams don’t win without the defense. They were consistently put in bad spots in the first half and didn’t let that faze them. In the second half, the Eagles picked up a total of four first downs and didn’t have a single first down in the third quarter. If the defense even allows one touchdown in the second half, the Rams don’t have a chance to come back. They kept fighting and the offense finally rewarded them at the end.
For as consistent as Harrison Mevis has been inside of 45 yards, in today’s NFL, you have to have a kicker you can trust to at least have a chance of making a long field goal. Mevis missed from 48 yards on Sunday, and the Rams opted not to kick from 56 after Jake Elliott made from that distance earlier in the game. Mevis then had a kickoff go out of bounds. Alex Bachman replaced Xavier Smith, but he didn’t look to be the answer either. The Rams need to bring in some competition like they did for Josh Karty last year.
Can I split the game ball or give out two and also give one to the Rams defense? If I only have one game ball, it has to go to Kyren Williams. Again, the Rams do not win the game without him. With Terrance Ferguson hurt, the Rams needed a third option in the passing game to step up. That player was Williams who became the first Rams running back since Todd Gurley in 2018 to record 10 receptions in a game. ​​​​ ​Williams is the first player this season to record at least 10 receptions and at least 10 carries in a single game. Only Christian McCaffrey and Jahmyr Gibbs have accomplished the feat since 2024.
For the first time in franchise history, the Rams held a team to at least 0-for-12 on third down. It’s only the third time that they’ve held a team to at least 0-for-10 on third down. The last time they did it was in Sean McVay’s first game as the Rams’ head coach in 2017 against the Indianapolis Colts. It’s also the first time a defense has held an opponent to at least 0-for-12 on third down since the Los Angeles Chargers held the Denver Broncos to that mark in 2023. What the Rams did against the Eagles, even if they were short-handed, was special.
There’s no doubt Sunday’s win against the Eagles was important for the Rams. The Rams are set to play the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football in Week 5, and outside of last week, they were looking like the best team in the NFL. They turned the ball over five times and managed to beat the Chargers. Despite not playing as well, they could have still beaten the New England Patriots on Sunday.
Instead of being 1-3 and staring at a potential 1-4 start, the Rams are 2-2 and will be no worse than 2-3 when they face the Arizona Cardinals in Week 6. Given how the Bills have played over the last two weeks, this game at least feels more winnable than it did a few weeks ago, especially at SoFi Stadium. The Rams will have to play much better than they did against the Eagles, but in the final two drives, it finally looked like something clicked with the offense.
