title: 10 Takeaways From Rams’ Comeback Win Over Eagles
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams got a win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday, coming back from 10 points in the fourth quarter. When all was said and done, the Rams won 24-20 and improved to 2-2. While the final eight minutes were impressive, the first 52 weren’t pretty. The Rams looked to be on their way to another loss against the Eagles. There was a lot to like in this game and the Rams winning certainly allows for positive vibes. However, there is a lot to clean up if the Rams are going to hit their ceiling. Here are 10 takeaways from the Rams’ win over the Eagles.
We might need to have a conversation about Matthew Stafford and his start to the 2026 season. There was always going to be some regression to the mean after his MVP season. It's as if his level completely flipped. For the first time in his career, Stafford has thrown an interception in all four games to start the season. He was directly responsible for 10 of the Eagles’ 20 first-half points. He missed Davante Adams open on another deep ball.
The thing about Stafford is that he can play poorly for three quarters and then perform well in the final quarter when it matters most. On the final two drives, he was 12-for-15 for 140 yards and nearly flawless. Still, the first three-plus quarters need to be talked about as well. If the Rams are going to hit their ceiling, they need a much better version of Stafford. Stafford became the first quarterback since Jameis Winston in 2018 to win a game while having more than 50 pass attempts, throwing for more than 300 yards, and having two interceptions with zero touchdowns. Prior to Sunday, teams were 1-27 in such games.
It feels like we talk about special teams every single week and it absolutely shouldn’t be that way. The Rams allowed a 41-yard punt return that set up the Eagles to score a touchdown. Prior to the big return, Alex Bachman set up the Rams’ offense deep in their own territory. Additionally, Harrison Mevis missed a 48-yard field goal and had a kickoff go out of bounds.
It’s hard to blame the coordinator right now given how bad the unit was last year. While they moved on from Xavier Smith last week, that can’t be the end of the changes. Late in the game, the Rams passed up a 56-yard field goal and instead decided to go for it on 4th-and-8. It’s worth asking how much the Rams trust him outside of 45 yards. Alex Bachman was a band-aid, but he’s not the solution. More changes need to happen.
In the first half, the Rams’ defense gave up 20 points. However, on 17 of those points, the defense was put in a bad position. Given how stagnant the offense was for most of the game, the Rams do not come back in this game without the defense performing the way it did.
Yes, the Eagles were short-handed on offense without DeVonta Smith and Saquon Barkley for much of the game. At the same time, the defense held the Eagles to 172 yards of total offense. Jalen Hurts had 93 yards passing. It’s the fewest passing yards the Rams have allowed since 2018 when Sam Bradford threw for 90 yards with the Arizona Cardinals. The defense also held the Eagles to 0-for-12 on third down. It’s the first time in franchise history that the Rams have accomplished that. If the defense allows a touchdown on 4th-and-goal from the two-yard line in the fourth quarter, the game is over.
The Rams were happy to have Puka Nacua back in action after he missed the last two games with a hip/groin injury. For the most part, Nacua looked like himself. He had nine receptions for 125 yards and had a rushing touchdown. He played with the same physicality that many are used to seeing. When the Rams’ offense was working, it was typically tied in with Nacua getting involved. On three of the Rams’ four scoring drives, Nacua had at least one reception for 15 yards and on two of them he had at least one reception for more than 25 yards.
Welcome back, Puka Nacua pic.twitter.com/N7g4I1JmA8
Without Terrance Ferguson and Colby Parkinson in this game, the Rams had to go back to utilizing more 11 personnel and three-wide-receiver sets. The Rams used 11 personnel at an 87 percent rate, which is their highest rate in a game since Week 5 of 2025. However, for as much as the Rams may not have had the personnel to operate out of 13 personnel, it’s fair to wonder if they have the personnel to operate out of 11 personnel.
Outside of Davante Adams and Puka Nacua, Rams wide receivers caught three passes on six targets and none had more than 10 yards receiving. The Rams simply can’t rely on Jordan Whittington, Konata Mumpfield, and Tutu Atwell to get open consistently. Both of Stafford’s interceptions came when targeting Mumpfield and Whittington. Stafford was unsettled for most of the game, and some of that is likely because the receiving options were limited. As much as some continue to deny it, the Rams need a third wide receiver .
When the Rams needed a player to rely on in the second half, it was Kyren Williams who stepped up and delivered. After averaging 3.4 yards per carry in the first half, Williams had nine carries for 56 yards in the second half. On both touchdown drives in the fourth quarter, Williams was the one to punch it in the end zone. His seven-yard touchdown run, breaking three tackles on his way to score was especially impressive.
Williams may not be Todd Gurley, but he had a Gurley-esque stat line against the Eagles. He became the first Rams running back since Gurley in 2018 to record at least 10 receptions in a game,, coincidentally also against the Eagles. Williams is the fourth Rams running back in the last 65 years with 80+ rushing yards, 10+ receptions, and 60+ receiving yards, joining Gurley II, Steven Jackson, and Robert Delpino. Williams stepped up in a big way on Sunday.
For as much as the defense deserves credit, Chris Shula also deserves his flowers. Shula has been criticized heavily at times this season , despite the Rams’ defense being one of the better units in the NFL since Week 1. The Rams were without key starters in Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald, and Jaylen Watson on defense and still managed a dominant performance.
Shula blitzed Hurts at a 60.6 percent rate, which is the highest blitz rate since he took over as defensive coordinator. On those blitzes, the Rams had a 65 percent pressure rate and allowed just five completions on 16 passes. Shula called a blitz on every third down except the last one. Without Watson, the Rams still played man coverage on 40 percent of their snaps.
The only thing consistent about the Rams right now is how inconsistent they are. Too often, they hurt themselves with self-inflicted wounds. In the first quarter, with the offense in the red zone, Davis Allen got called for a holding penalty that stalled the drive. There were obviously the turnovers from Stafford and special teams errors that essentially handed the Eagles free points.
In the second half, the Rams had a sequence in which a 23-yard run from Williams got moved back 15 yards because of a penalty on the bench. Two plays later, Nacua caught a pass for 24 yards, but it was called back because of offensive pass interference. In the fourth quarter after the Eagles turned it over on downs, Williams had a seven-yard run that was taken away because Nacua was called for an illegal blindside block. These are mistakes that we aren’t used to from a McVay-coached team and they are mistakes that good teams don’t make.
There’s no debating that the Rams’ win against the Eagles wasn’t pretty and they won’t get any style points. At the same time, it feels like a turning point and a win that this team desperately needed. For much of the game, it felt like the Rams were going to lose a game that they probably should have won with a cleaner game. When they faced a 98-yard field with around 7:26 left, they looked as good as done.
However, the Rams fought back and scored a touchdown on each of their final two drives. The Rams were staring 1-3 directly in the face and decided what type of team they were going to be.…

title: Rams Winners and Losers: Kyren Williams, Defense Save the Day in Comeback Win
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams won in dramatic fashion on Sunday as they beat the Philadelphia Eagles, 24-20, coming back from 10 points in the fourth quarter. To say the least, it was an inconsistent performance. For much of the game, the Rams were beating themselves and continued giving a short-handed Eagles team opportunities. Let’s look at this week’s winners and losers.
While Kyren Williams may not be the perfect running back, he’s the perfect running back for the Rams. Needing a third option in the passing game, the Rams relied on Williams and he delivered. Williams had 18 carries for 80 yards and added 10 receptions. He became the first Rams running back since Todd Gurley in 2018 to have at least 10 receptions in a game. Williams played a key role in the Rams’ comeback, scoring both touchdowns in the fourth quarter. On the game-winning touchdown, he broke three tackles before finding the end zone from seven yards out.
Without Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett, there was a lot of pressure on the defense and Byron Young to produce. The defense got consistent pressure on Jalen Hurts and on the final drive, Young sacked Hurts twice and forced a fumble. He finished with five pressures and three quarterback hits. If there was any doubt that Young can be a No. 1 pass rusher, he showed that he can be that on Sunday.
There are two parts of Matthew Stafford’s performance. There are the first three quarters of the game, when he appeared unsettled and threw two interceptions. Then there’s the final two drives when Stafford went 12-for-15 for 140 yards. He’s the first quarterback since Jameis Winston in 2018 to win a game with over 50 pass attempts, more than 300 passing yards, at least two interceptions and no touchdown passes and win. Teams were previously 1-27. At the end of the day, the Rams need Stafford to be better.
Over the last two weeks, the Rams have been without wide receiver Puka Nacua as he dealt with a groin injury. In his return, Nacua looked like his old self as he finished with nine receptions for 125 yards. When the offense was at its best, it was usually when Nacua got involved. He also had a touchdown run on a jet sweep. At the very least, it was good to see Nacua back.
Let’s be clear, the Rams don’t even have an opportunity to come back if it’s not for the defense. The defense was put in bad positions throughout the entire first half. However, they didn’t let that get to them. They completely shut out the Eagles in the second half. The Rams defense held the Eagles to 0-for-12 on third down and 1-for-16 on third- and-fourth down conversions combined. Their fourth-down stop at the two-yard line in the fourth quarter saved the game. Chris Shula blitzed Hurts at a 60.6 percent rate, allowing just five completions on 16 pass attempts. While this group has earned some criticism, it deserves a lot of credit for their performance on Sunday.
It’s another week in the NFL, which means we are here to talk about the Rams’ special teams. It’s clear more changes are needed. Xavier Smith wasn’t the answer on the punt return unit , but neither is Alex Bachman. Harrison Mevis is solid inside of 45 yards, but in today’s NFL, being inconsistent outside of that is a liability. Mevis also had a kickoff go out of bounds. Last week was a start, but more changes are clearly needed.
An argument can be made that the Rams saved their season with their comeback win against the Eagles.Had they lost, the Rams would have been sitting at 1-3 with a game against the Buffalo Bills on deck next week. Another loss would have dropped them to 1-4. At 2-2, the Rams are in a much better spot. Even if they lose to the Bills, it’s possible that the Rams get to 7-3 at their bye week.
On Sunday, the Rams were without Terrance Ferguson, forcing them to operate out of 11 personnel and three wide receiver sets.Outside of Nacua and Adams, the Rams struggled to find other options in the passing game. Tutu Atwell, Jordan Whittington, and Konata Mumpfield combined for four receptions on six targets. None of them had over 10 yards receiving. Tight end Davis Allen also had zero receptions on two targets. This is one area where the Rams could use some help.

title: Rams Overcome Their Demons in Dramatic Comeback Win Over Eagles
full_text:
Two years ago, Los Angeles Rams running back Kyren Williams left Lincoln Financial Field distraught after his fumble changed the game and led to a Philadelphia Eagles win in the 2024 NFC Divisional Round. Last year, the Rams blew a 26-7 lead and lost on the final play after Joshua Karty’s kick was blocked and returned for a touchdown.
On Sunday, the Rams faced all of their demons at The Linc and came back to beat the Eagles, 24-20. Behind Kyren Williams and the defense, the Rams came back from a 10-point fourth-quarter deficit to win.
For much of the afternoon, the Rams couldn’t seem to get out of their own way. Despite facing a short-handed Eagles team without wide receiver DeVonta Smith and Saquon Barkley, who left in the first quarter, the Rams kept giving them opportunities.
Much like last year, on the team’s opening drive quarterback Matthew Stafford threw an interception over the head of Konata Mumpfield. Stafford has thrown an interception in all four weeks to start the season, which is the first time he's done that in his career. While the defense got a stop, the Eagles settled for a field goal. In the second quarter, it was special teams rearing its ugly head.
New punt returner Alex Bachman set the Rams up with bad field position. After the offense went three-and-out, Britain Covey returned the punt 41 yards and into the red zone. Two plays later, Jalen Hurts found Darius Cooper for a touchdown.
While the Rams’ offense had gone three-and-out on consecutive drives, they answered the Eagles’ score with a touchdown of their own. Making his return, wide receiver Puka Nacua took a jet sweep from two yards out and found the end zone.
Puka Nacua walks in for the TD! @LARvsPHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/wtqqYlOwhW
With three timeouts remaining, the Rams still had a chance to tie the game going into halftime. The defense did its part to get a stop, but two plays later, Stafford threw his second interception of the day. Again, the Eagles capitalized and Hurts found Cooper in the back of the end zone.
The Rams went into the half trailing 20-10. However, they didn’t have to travel more than 40 yards on any of their scoring drives. Sunday’s game was setting up to be a box score anomaly. In the first half, the Eagles went 0-for-6 on third down, but had found a way to score 20 points and lead by 10.
Time and time again, when the Rams tried to get back in the game in the third quarter, it was one step forward and two steps back for the offense. After the defense forced a three-and-out, the offense drove into field goal range. However, Harrison Mevis missed the 48-yard attempt wide left.
On the next drive, Williams picked up 23 yards, but a 15-yard penalty made it only an eight-yard gain. Puka Nacua caught a pass for 24 yards, but an offensive pass interference penalty wiped it out, and the Rams eventually had to punt. When the Rams turned the ball over on downs after the defense stopped an Eagles tush push, the game seemed over. The only thing consistent about the Rams up to that point was how often they committed self-inflicted errors.
For much of the game, the offense appeared disjointed. With the injuries to Terrance Ferguson and Colby Parkinson, the offense had to resort to more 11 personnel and three wide receiver sets. The Rams operated out of 11 personnel at an 88.2 percent rate. The Rams had previously used 11 personnel on 56 percent of their offensive snaps this season.
Facing Vic Fangio’s defense on the other side, Matthew Stafford was just 12-for-21 with two interceptions and a 33.9 quarterback rating in the first half. Through three quarters, he was 19-for-34 for 168 yards.
While the defense allowed 20 first-half points, most of it was because they had been put in bad positions. In the second half, they kept the Rams in the game. The Eagles finished with only 172 yards of total offense and averaged 3.9 yards per play. Chris Shula was aggressive on third down, consistently blitzing Hurts and forcing throwaways. The Eagles finished 0-for-12 on third down in the game and 1-for-4 on fourth down.
After the defense stopped the Eagles at the two-yard line on fourth down, leaving the offense 98 yards from the other end zone, a comeback still didn’t seem possible. However, Stafford found Nacua for nine yards to give the offense some pace and then 32 yards to put the Rams at around midfield.
When the Rams couldn’t find answers in the passing game or lean on their quarterback, they turned to Kyren Williams. Williams finished with 16 carries for 80 yards and added 10 catches for 67 yards. With the Rams needing a touchdown, Williams caught two passes to set the Rams up at the one-yard line and then punched it in himself.
The defense forced another three-and-out and the offense took over at its own 21-yard line and 2:55 to play. Despite just needing a field goal to tie, there’s no doubt the Rams preferred to win in regulation and not go to overtime.
Stafford hit Nacua on back-to-back plays and then again for 12 yards to put the Rams in the red zone at the Eagles’ 19-yard line with 1:37 to play. Facing a 3rd-and-2, Stafford handed it off to Williams who picked up the first down. Another handoff to Williams forced the Eagles to use their final timeout.
On 2nd-and-goal from the seven, Williams got the ball again and shook three Eagles defenders, fighting his way into the end zone to give the Rams their first lead of the game. After looking as good as done 10 minutes earlier and losing a fourth-quarter lead on that same field a year prior, the Rams led 24-20.
Kyren Williams POWERS IT IN FOR THE LEAD!! @LARvsPHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/LW85llHviL
As it had all game, the defense pressured Hurts and Byron Young sacked him twice, forcing a fumble on the second. When Hurts’ pass on 4th-and-25 hit the ground, the Rams’ comeback was complete.
There were times throughout the game when the Rams didn’t deserve to win. Issues that have haunted them all season continued to creep up. Special teams errors once again nearly cost them the game. The Rams made more mistakes than a winning team should and they found a way to gut out a win in Philadelphia. The result certainly can’t mask the things that need to be cleaned up, and there are a lot of them, but this was a much-needed win nonetheless.
That’s a character-building win that the Rams needed. After they turned it over on downs in the fourth quarter, the Rams faced 98 yards with 7:26 to play while needing two scores. They looked done. However, tthe defense kept the Rams in the game, playing lights out in the second half, and the offense didn’t give up. When the offense needed it most, it delivered. To see how much the Rams needed this game,look no further than McVay’s celebration after Young’s sack on the final drive.
Coach McVay is HYPED 🔥 pic.twitter.com/oRF5GqYvuy
The Rams will now return to SoFi and be back in primetime next Monday night against the Buffalo Bills. It’s a Bills team that has looked unstoppable but just lost to the New England Patriots on Sunday. At 2-2, the Rams are still in a good spot. There’s no doubt that the Rams need to be better, but they’ve managed to keep the season alive as they get healthy.

title: Sunday Morning Rams Notebook: New Details Emerge on Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald Injuries
full_text:
Injuries have been a common theme throughout the first month of the season for the Los Angeles Rams. Following their Week 1 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, Myles Garrett was placed on injured reserve. Additionally, wide receiver Puka Nacua injured his hip and missed the next two games. On Sunday, Aaron Donald hurt his back and is set to miss Sunday’s game against the Philadelphia Eagles.
There are a lot of questions when it comes to the injuries to those three players. However, we got some clarity this week with Nacua set to return. Still, Donald’s injury popped out of nowhere and there is still no clear timeline on Garrett. Let’s get into this week’s Rams game day notebook.
Aaron Donald was a surprise addition to the injury report this week with what the team described as a back injury. The team didn’t seem too concerned when discussing it, but Donald didn’t practice this week and will miss Sunday’s game against the Eagles. NFL Media’s Ian Rapaport shed some light on Donald’s injury on Friday.
“My understanding is it is a relatively minor back injury for Aaron Donald,” said Rapoport. “I wouldn’t call it precautionary because it’s a real thing, but really what the team wants to do is sit him out now with the hopes of healing this for the long term.”
From The Insiders on @nflnetwork : #Rams DT Aaron Donald is out on Sunday with a minor back injury. pic.twitter.com/xQTWJFNtUr
Rapoport added that Donald is protected in his contract. While some players don’t get paid if they are on the 46-man roster, Donald will still get his $660k game check as his is tied to the 53-man roster rather than the 46-man roster.
The Rams understand that it's more important to have Donald available and healthy in December and January than October. Still, Donald will be a player to watch next week as the Rams get ready to host Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills at SoFi Stadium.
Following Bubba Ventrone’s press conference on Thursday, there was a lot of criticism of how the Rams were handling their special teams. Ventrone had noted that the team wasn’t considering a change at punt returner, despite Xavier Smith struggling.
While there was so much focus on Ventrone’s first comment, many missed when he also called Smith inconsistent and said that he needed to improve in areas, specifically when tracking the ball. The next morning, Smith was cut.
At the very least, it’s a sign that the Rams acknowledged that a change was needed on the special teams unit, and they may not be done. Ventrone also noted that Ethan Evans has been inconsistent and they need more consistency from the punter.
“We need to get more consistency from the punter,” said Ventrone. “Ethan can do a better job being able to elevate the ball and match hang times and distance at a greater rate. We have to do a better job in his position.”
The Rams do have Jack Bouwmeester on the practice squad if needed, but Evans’ seat might be getting a little warm.If Ventrone doesn’t start to see some improvement and consistency, don’t be surprised if there’s a change.
For the past two weeks, the Rams have been without edge rusher Myles Garrett. However, with two games gone, there are just two more weeks until Garrett is eligible to return and have his 21-day practice window opened.
Last week, it was reported by Rapoport that Garrett had been given a six-week timeline for his return as he recovers from knee surgery. McVay hasn’t placed a timeline on Garrett’s return, but did comment on his rehab this week.
“He physically looks good,” said McVay. “It's been great having him in and out of a lot of the different meetings while he's attacking his rehab. He’s making good progress, but as far as a specific timeline, not ready to be able to give you guys that.”
While Rapoport reported a six-week timeline for Garrett, The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones added on Saturday that the six-week timeline would be a worst-case scenario. According to Jones, the team remains hopeful that he can return in Week 6 against the Arizona Cardinals, but a second source believes that Garrett could return the following week against the Las Vegas Raiders.
There were a couple of different conspiracies floating around with Puka Nacua missing the last two games with a hip/groin injury. There was some belief that Nacua had been quietly suspended by the NFL, which is why his injury came on so suddenly and he missed exactly two games. Additionally, There was some thought that Nacua was being extremely cautious because of his contract situation.
Both theories are unequivocally false. McVay addressed the rumors this week on ESPNLA and said, “Yeah, it’s not true…He’s been working, chomping at the bit to get back out there with his teammates this week.”
As far as the NFL quietly suspending Nacua, that wasn’t the case either. Earlier this offseason, there was some speculation that Nacua could be suspended by the NFL following an incident in which he allegedly bit a woman’s shoulder on New Year’s Eve. The civil case got pushed to 2028 and the NFL hasn’t intervened.
According to Jones, a highly placed source said that if the league wanted to punish Nacua, it would do so publicly. Jones also reported that Nacua has had to overcome the mental hurdle of his injury, which is complicated by his physical style of play and the risk of re-injury. Nacua practiced this week and seems to be good to go moving forward for the time being.
Nacua said this week at practice that he had been struggling with some change-of-direction stuff and that his hip area wasn’t feeling great and was causing some pain. However, Nacua noted that he felt good several times.
“The ability to put my foot in the ground. It feels good to do that and working through it,” said Nacua. “I've been working through it like getting acceleration, change of direction.”
Nacua was officially listed as a limited participant in practice on Thursday and then practiced fully on Friday. He doesn’t have an injury designation, so it’s safe to assume that he feels like he’s in a good spot.

title: Rams Make Two Roster Moves Ahead of Week 4 vs. Eagles (And What They Mean)
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams have promoted two players from the practice squad to the active roster ahead of Sunday’s game against the Philadelphia Eagles. On Saturday, the Rams promoted cornerback Cam Lampkin and edge rusher Darryl Peterson III to the active roster.
LA Rams Roster Moves: • Activated, from Practice Squad (Standard Elevation) CB Cam Lampkin, OLB Darryl Peterson III pic.twitter.com/hZfiHq7EmB
Lampkin was a standout during training camp and the preseason, but was part of the team’s final roster cuts. He carried a strong training camp into the preseason where he had a few timely pass breakups. He was one of nine players with at least six tackles and one sack in a game.
It’s not too surprising that the Rams are looking to add cornerback depth ahead of Sunday. The Rams are set to be without cornerback Jaylen Watson in Week 4 as he deals with a dislocated shoulder. Watson left last week’s game in the second half and did not return.
The Rams will likely primarily rely on Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes against the Eagles, but Lampkin will at least provide them with some depth at the position if needed.Lampkin has the ability to move between outside cornerback and inside to the slot.
In addition to Lampkin, the Rams also opted to promote Peterson to the active roster. Peterson was signed as an undrafted free agent this offseason. He played well in the final preseason game against the Chargers, recording three pressures and two sacks while also forcing a fumble.
While the Rams do have some depth on the edge with Wesley Bailey already on the active roster, Josaiah Stewart was a late addition to the injury report this week with a groin injury. Stewart didn’t practice on Friday and was officially listed as questionable for Sunday.
Peterson getting promoted to the active roster ahead of Sunday’s game against the Eagles doesn’t necessarily mean that Stewart is trending toward being out. However, he will provide depth on the edge if Stewart’s injury were to get worse.
With both Wesley Bailey and Darryl Peterson III on the roster for Week 4, it’s a testament to the number of injuries the Rams have dealt with early this season, especially on the edge. Myles Garrett was placed on injured reserve after Week 1, and now Stewart is also managing an injury.
The Rams entered the season with impressive depth on defense, but that depth is already being tested. Elevating Lampkin and Peterson gives the Rams some necessary insurance at two positions that have been hit by injuries. Having that depth could be important in a game that the Rams need to win.

title: 5 Keys to a Rams Victory Against Eagles in Crucial Week 4 Matchup
full_text:
Heading into the season, some may have thought that the Los Angeles Rams and Philadelphia Eagles would be heading into their Week 4 matchup undefeated and playoff implications would be on the line. Instead, both teams are dealing with injuries and lacking an overall identity. Last week, the Rams fell to 1-2 after losing to the Denver Broncos, and the Eagles lost to a Chicago Bears team led by Case Keenum.
Both the Rams and Eagles are in need of a quality win in a desperate way. With the Buffalo Bills on the schedule, a loss on Sunday could result in the Rams falling to 1-4. The Rams need to get back to 2-2 as they await the return of Myles Garrett. Here are five keys to victory for the Rams as they head into Sunday’s game against the Eagles.
Since 2022, Jalen Hurts has been the best quarterback on throws of 25-plus yards. He has the most touchdowns and completions on such passes. So far this season, the Eagles' offense lacks an identity and Hurts’ deep ball is all they have. DeVonta Smith has been a big part of that and he’s set to be out on Sunday. Still, the Eagles have Dontayvion Wicks who has looked good. Against the Tennessee Titans in Week 2, Wicks had key plays on five big conversions, including catches on two 3rd-and-12 situations.
Without Smith, the Eagles don’t have a lot of options in the passing game and the Rams’ secondary can’t bail them out by allowing big plays over the top. It wouldn’t be surprising if the Eagles test Emmanuel Forbes and Joshua Wallace as the Rams will be without Jaylen Watson. This is where the Rams’ cornerbacks need to step up.
While Hurts is throwing over the middle more this season, it’s still not something he’s comfortable with. He’d much rather attack the perimeter. This season, he has 12.9 total EPA on middle-of-the-field throws on 12 attempts.
Without Smith, it’s going to be hard for the Eagles to attack the outside. They drafted Makai Lemon, but he’s much better over the middle and in the slot. He’s also struggled in the first three weeks. If the Rams can take away the perimeter, they may be able to force Hurts into some mistakes or have a similar start to last year where they forced three consecutive three-and-outs.
Jalen Hurts’ passing chart looks night and day different compared to last week. Outliers: • Heavily favored right side • Lack of middle field success • Too many screens Hurts/Mannion had 8 days to prepare for a below average Bears defense and this is the product they bring. https://t.co/MsGHt5dYdz pic.twitter.com/HQJQGI11un
Last year, the Rams did well containing Saquon Barkley. Barkley averaged just 2.6 yards per attempt. This is the key to stopping the Eagles’ offense. If the Rams can find success on early downs and force the Eagles into 3rd-and-5 and 3rd-and-6 situations, it forces the Eagles to become a passing team, which they don’t want to be.
Barkley has just a 36.4 percent rushing success rate on early downs. If the Rams can get the Eagles into those third-and-long situations, they can unleash the pass rush and blitz Hurts. Hurts ranks 19th against the blitz this season with a -0.08 EPA per dropback.
This is a game where the Rams really would have benefitted from having Terrance Ferguson available . Jihaad Campbell has struggled in coverage and the Eagles are without Zack Baun. Additionally, Cooper DeJean has taken a step back and the Eagles’ safeties as a whole have struggled.
Still, while the Rams may not be able to work their tight ends down the seam without Ferguson, they should still be able to get Puka Nacua involved over the middle. Nacua returning should give the Rams’ offense a major boost in the passing game and will provide more options for Stafford. The Rams have used Nacua more on the outside in the last two years, but this might be a game where using him in the slot is a benefit.
Last season, the Rams arguably lost to the Eagles because of special teams. While Josh Karty made four field goals in the game, his final two attempts were blocked, both of which would have essentially won the game. His second blocked field goal was for the win, but it was returned the other way for a touchdown.
The Rams made a major change on special teams on Friday morning when they cut wide receiver and punt returner Xavier Smith . However, it was just a start, as the Rams still have other issues to figure out. Last week’s comeback by the Broncos was started because of special teams errors. The Rams need to be sharp on special teams on Sunday.

title: Rams vs. Eagles: Position-by-Position Breakdown Ahead of Week 4
full_text:
Over the past two years, the Los Angeles Rams and Philadelphia Eagles have played some of the more entertaining games in the NFL. The Rams nearly beat the Eagles in the 2024 NFC Divisional Round and then should have won last year’s Week 3 matchup. On Sunday, the Rams will be back in Philadelphia for a third straight time . Let’s take a look at how the Rams match up with the Eagles before the game.
There’s no question that the Rams have the advantage at quarterback in this matchup. Jalen Hurts has shown moments of being a top-12 quarterback. However, he struggles to throw over the middle and access certain areas of the field. That limits what the Eagles can do offensively. Stafford hasn’t played like the reigning MVP up to this point, but he’s been better than Hurts. Advantage: Rams
Jalen Hurts’ passing chart looks night and day different compared to last week. Outliers: • Heavily favored right side • Lack of middle field success • Too many screens Hurts/Mannion had 8 days to prepare for a below average Bears defense and this is the product they bring. https://t.co/MsGHt5dYdz pic.twitter.com/HQJQGI11un
When it comes to Kyren Williams and Saquon Barkley, there is a clear winner. Barkley is clearly the better running back because of his explosiveness and how he can take an offense to the next level. Behind Barkley, the Eagles have Tank Bigsby while the Rams are working with Blake Corum. That’s not a fair comparison either. The Eagles may have the higher ceiling because of Barkley, but the Rams have the better 1-2 duo. Advantage: Even
For the first time in two weeks, the Rams are going to have Puka Nacua back . Additionally, Davante Adams is playing like he’s still in his prime. Going into Sunday, the Eagles will be without DeVonta Smith and relying on rookie Makai Lemon. The Rams have the clear advantage here. Advantage: Rams
Both teams are managing injuries at tight end. The Rams just put Terrance Ferguson on injured reserve and Colby Parkinson didn’t practice all week. Meanwhile, Dallas Goedert is out for the Eagles, and they’re relying on Zach Ertz. Even with the injuries, the Rams’ depth with Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen, and Max Klare gives them the edge. Advantage: Rams
Over the past several years, the Eagles have been considered to have one of the best offensive lines in the NFL, and that is likely still the case. However, they are without Landon Dickerson right now, as he’s on injured reserve. The Rams’ offensive line hasn’t played at the same level that it did last season through three games. Advantage: Eagles
Pass block grades in true pass sets only You'll never guess who comes in last here pic.twitter.com/6ChM4tRjpl
As the Rams head into this game, they are set to be without Aaron Donald . Donald picked up a back injury and will miss Sunday’s game. The Rams are already without Myles Garrett as he’s on injured reserve. Normally, the Rams would have the slight edge here, but with the injuries, it is very close. The Eagles have done well building their defensive line as well. This one is even. Advantage: Even
It’s another week of football, which means it’s another week where the Rams don’t have the edge at linebacker. Nate Landman has struggled to start the year and needs to be better. Advantage: Eagles
Due to the injury to Jaylen Watson, the Eagles are probably better at cornerback with Quinyon Mitchell, Riq Woolen, and Cooper DeJean. However, the Rams have the clear edge at safety and the better overall cornerback in Trent McDuffie. Advantage: Even
In last year’s game, the Eagles won because of special teams. Had the Rams been able to make either of their two potential game-winning field goals, they would have won the game. The Rams made changes on special teams this week, cutting Xavier Smith , but they still have issues to fix. Advantage: Eagles
There's almost no debate that Sean McVay is a better head coach than Nick Sirianni. However, Sirianni is 4-0 against McVay. Vic Fangio is also a better defensive coordinator than Chris Shula while Nate Sheelhaase and Sean Mannion are first-year offensive coordinators. The Rams should have the edge here, but it's fair to call it even. Advantage: Even

title: Rams Players Detail Three Biggest Challenges Against Eagles
full_text:
As the Los Angeles Rams prepare to play the Philadelphia Eagles this week, quarterback Matthew Stafford and Davante Adams detailed some of the challenges they’ll face during the game . Over the past two years, the Eagles have been one of the better teams in the NFC. While they have struggled the last two weeks, losing to the Chicago Bears on Monday night, they return home to play the Rams. Following a loss to the Denver Broncos in Week 3, the Rams will look to play focused for 60 minutes and get back to .500.
During the week, Stafford and Adams talked about some of the challenges that the Eagles present, especially defensively.
While Sunday’s game will be between the Rams and Eagles, many will also be watching the c hess match between head coach Sean McVay and defensive coordinator Vic Fangio . McVay and Fangio changed the course of the NFL back in 2018. With McVay’s offense looking unstoppable, it was Fangio’s quarters defense and the 6-1 front that shut down the Rams’ offense.
Over the past two years, McVay and Fangio have gone head to head when the Rams and Eagles have played. Fangio has gotten the better of McVay in all three meetings. The Rams have averaged 20.5 points per game over their last four matchups with the Eagles, which is the fewest points per game by the Rams against any opponent they’ve faced since 2023.
However, Matthew Stafford also has a long history against Fangio, as they went against each other in the NFC North from 2015-18. During that time, Stafford was the quarterback for the Detroit Lions and Fangio was the defensive coordinator of the Chicago Bears. Stafford was 5-3 against Fangio when he was the defensive coordinator with the Bears.
“I have a ton of respect for him. Like I said, he mixes fronts and coverages as well as anybody,” said Stafford this week. “He does a great job of coaching those guys so that they're always winning to their leverage, playing the way they're supposed to play. He gives the quarterback a lot to think about, a lot of things to figure out and adjust to. It's always a big challenge.”
Since 2024, Stafford has a 0.02 EPA per pass against the Eagles compared to a 0.14 EPA per pass against the rest of the league. His efficiency against the Eagles over that period has been significantly worse than his efficiency against the rest of the league. Stafford threw for 196 yards with two touchdowns and an interception last season against the Eagles.
A big reason for this is the Eagles’ ability to generate a pass rush. Stafford has been sacked on 8.7 percent of his dropbacks against the Eagles, which is more than double his 4.2 percent sack rate against other teams.
Over the past two weeks, Davante Adams has been playing like he’s still in his prime. He had back-to-back 100-yard games for the first time since 2024. For the most part, he and Stafford have been on the same page.
Last season against the Eagles, Adams had three receptions for 56 yards and a touchdown. However, he was held to just two catches for 12 yards against cornerback Quinyon Mitchell . The Eagles’ secondary has struggled to start the year, but it’s still a group with a lot of talent. Despite the early-season struggles, the Rams aren’t going to be taking them lightly.
“I know there have been some talks about the secondary and safeties, but it's the NFL. These guys all can play and go out there and make plays on any given day,” said Adams. “Humility is one play away if you know you're sleeping on somebody. We don't take anybody lightly at the end of the day. We know Cooper [DeJean] is obviously a really good player as well so we have to go out there and account for everybody.”
With Nacua returning, it will be interesting to see how involved Adams still is in the offense. He’ll certainly still get targets, but his 26.7 percent share has also ranked inside the top 15 among wide receivers. Sunday against the Eagles’ secondary will be a good test.
Despite the talent on the Eagles’ defense, they haven’t lived up to expectations this year. Case Keenum had 247 yards and two touchdowns last week as the Bears beat the Eagles. The Eagles rank 23rd in defensive EPA per play and 20th in overall defensive success rate. However, the Rams will be prepared for their best.
“Like I said earlier, they're always a tough out,” Stafford said. “They play extremely physical up front, a penetrating style of defensive line, especially this year. They're doing a great job of hiding and mixing coverages. They're as good as anybody in the league at doing that kind of stuff. We just got to go out there and play within ourselves, execute, play physical and find a way to win.”
After losing to the Eagles in the way that the Rams have the last two years, there’s no doubt they’ll be focused and ready for this one. As mentioned, Stafford has struggled to handle the pressure that the Eagles can create defensively. While they have struggled defensively, the Eagles are still generating a quarterback pressure rate of 39.2 percent, which is the ninth-highest in the NFL.
If the Rams are going to win this game, they’ll need Stafford to be sharp and for the offensive line to keep him upright.

title: 3 Key Matchups That Could Decide Rams vs. Eagles in Week 4
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are set to take on the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 4 in what will be a must-win game. Entering Week 4, the Rams sit at 1-2 following a disappointing loss last week to the Denver Broncos. Over the past few seasons, the Rams are 0-4 against the Eagles and are in need of a win with the Buffalo Bills on the schedule next week. Both teams are managing injuries and will be looking to bounce back after losing in Week 3. Here are three matchups that could decide the game between the Rams and Eagles.
The Eagles are going to be without their top option in the passing game in DeVonta Smith on Sunday, leaving them with rookie Makai Lemon. Lemon hasn’t been very good this season as he has just seven receptions for 38 yards. His 0.42 yards per route run ranks 91st out of 92 qualifying wide receivers. Lemon simply hasn’t been a fit in the Eagles’ offense with Jalen Hurts.
However, with Smith out, the Eagles may have no choice but to get Lemon involved. If that’s the case, most of Lemon’s snaps will come from the slot, and that’s where the Rams will line up Quentin Lake. If Lake can eliminate Lemon, it’s going to be very difficult for Jalen Hurts and the Eagles’ passing game to get anything going.
For the first time in two weeks, the Rams are set to have Puka Nacua back on the field for Sunday’s game against the Eagles. It’s possible the Eagles put Quinyon Mitchell on Nacua. However, last season, Mitchell lined up against Davante Adams. Adams had just two catches for 12 yards against Mitchell and the Eagles may take that route once again.
If that’s the case, it would set up a former NFC West showdown on the other side between Nacua and Riq Woolen. Nacua had two catches for 55 yards and a touchdown against Woolen last year in the NFC Championship Game.The Eagles have some talent in the secondary, even if the unit hasn’t lived up to expectations. The Rams will need Nacua back at 100 percent, especially with the injuries at tight end .
Kevin Dotson has struggled to start the season as he’s allowed 11 pressures in three games. That’s tied for the third-most in the NFL among guards this season. His 29.7 pass-blocking grade via PFF also ranks 57th out of 58 guards. Dotson is an important part of the Rams’ offensive line, and they need him to play better.
Dotson will have a big challenge this week against Jalen Carter. However, Carter also hasn’t played well to start the year. Carter was held without a pressure for the first time in his career last week against the Chicago Bears. The Rams need to keep Matthew Stafford upright, and that starts in the middle of the offensive line with Dotson.

title: Assessing Kirk Cousins' Performance in Raiders Loss Against Chiefs
full_text:
For anyone still not fully sold on the Las Vegas Raiders, Sunday should have been enough to prove that they are legit.
Yes, the Raiders fell to the Kansas City Chiefs 30-27, but they pushed Patrick Mahomes and Co. to the brink. After four weeks, this contest was the first true test Las Vegas faced, and despite the result, it showed this team can contend for a playoff spot . Quarterback Kirk Cousins also faced questions about his standing as a starter. The 38-year-old signal caller has also proved doubters wrong. Here's an assessment of his Week 4 performance.
The Raiders played at a controlled, steady pace in the first half and took a 13-10 lead into halftime. However, the second half told a completely different story, with two lead changes in the fourth quarter after both teams combined for zero points in the third quarter. That forced Las Vegas into a pass-heavy script.
It's reflected in Cousins' output, as he completed 31-of-52 pass attempts for 365 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception. That's a 59.6 completion rate which isn't the best, but the 15-year veteran made a handful of impressive plays, considering he's not the most agile quarterback.
With over 50 pass attempts, the pass-catching contributions were spread out. Once again, the Raiders' rushing attack left much to be desired, with Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington Jr. combined for 76 yards on 24 carries (3.1 yards per attempt).
Kansas City has been susceptible to tight ends in recent memory, and head coach Klint Kubiak clearly recognized that, deploying multiple tight ends on the field at the same time. Mayer was peppered with targets underneath, setting the pace for the passing attack in the first half. Bowers had four catches of 16+ yards. The third-year tight end led the team with 11 targets. Mayer finished second with 10 targets.
The Raiders' offense has been firing on all cylinders through four weeks, and Cousins has fit seamlessly into Kubiak's system. In Week 5, Las Vegas faces the New England Patriots in one of next week's most interesting matchups.
Across four games, Cousins has accumulated 1,026 passing yards, 11 touchdowns, and four interceptions, while completing 64.6 percent of his passes.

title: Grading Every Raiders' Position Group After Week 4 vs. Chiefs
full_text:
The Las Vegas and Kansas City Chiefs both entered their Week 4 matchup undefeated. By any measure, for the Raiders, the matchup represented the most critical game the team has played in years. With 13 games remaining, it was not critical in terms of the record.
Sunday's matchup between the two teams was the most important game the Raiders have played in a while, for reasons the scoreboard at Allegiant Stadium didn't reflect. Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes had been nothing short of flawless against the Raiders over the past decade.
Below are the grades for every position group on the Raiders' roster following their Week 4 loss.
Overall, it is hard to find many flaws in Kirk Cousins' performance. Cousins threw two touchdowns, and his lone interception came at the end of the game. Las Vegas' offense has things to work on, but Cousins is not one of them.
Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty is far from healthy, but Las Vegas needs him on the field. With the Bye Week not arriving until late in the season, the Raiders may soon need to consider giving Jeanty practices or even a game or two off. Unfortunately, that is not likely.
Las Vegas may also want to start using Dylan Laube on offense and potentially elevate a running back from the practice squad to mix things up and give Jeanty a few extra plays off, after also using Mike Washington. Las Vegas' issues on the ground are multifaceted.
Connor Heyward made several plays that were quietly big. He seems to do so weekly.
When it works, it works, but Sunday showed the downsides of the Raiders' approach to building their wide receiver group. Already missing wide receiver Jack Bech, the Raiders also lost Jalen Nailor to a possible concussion on Sunday.
Losing Nailor made an already thin group even thinner. They will likely keep adding to the position with small signings throughout the rest of this season, but they must add multiple wide receivers next offseason. Objectively, the group did the best it could with what it had.
Despite missing their starting right guard, Las Vegas' offensive line allowed no sacks. With Cousins throwing the ball 52 times, the offensive line deserves credit. However, the Raiders' ground game still couldn't get going.
Part of it is because of Jeanty's health, as there were times when the line created running lanes that a healthy Jeanty would have sped through. However, the unit has performed too well in pass protection for Las Vegas' struggles on the ground not to be partially the unit's fault.
Yardage-wise, Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer were Las Vegas' top two pass-catchers. The Raiders' tight ends saved the day in multiple ways.
The defense held the Chiefs scoreless for the entire third quarter. The unit allowed running back Kenneth Walker to break for a big gain on the quarter's final play, changing the game's trajectory.
However, Las Vegas' defensive line and the defense as a whole did their part. No defense in the league can hold the Chiefs to 13 points through three quarters while getting little run support from their teammates on offense. The Raiders' defense was bound to break at some point.
Las Vegas' linebackers played well, and the mistakes they made were mostly a testament to a good scheme and solid play-calling by the Chiefs.
The Raiders' inexperience in the defensive backfield showed up repeatedly between their safeties and cornerbacks, but Treydan Stukes and Jeremy Chinn played well overall.
AJ Cole averaged almost 50 yards per punt on his three punts.
Matt Gay remains a force for the Raiders. He has made at least one critical field goal in each game this season. Sunday was more of the same.
Also, the Raiders should have taken the points. It wasn't as if they simply passed on a makeable field goal attempt. Gay made a field goal; the Chiefs were penalized on it. Instead of keeping the points that were already on the board, Las Vegas literally took points off their own score.
Taking points that were already on the board off, while already up by three against Mahomes, is not the same as passing on a makeable field goal. If Las Vegas took those points, the score would have been tied late in the fourth, with Gay possibly lining up for another makeable field goal to win.
For the second week in a row, Las Vegas fumbled a kickoff return. For the second consecutive week, that fumble immediately led to a touchdown for their opponent. This time, it essentially cost them the game.
Las Vegas still put up a fight late, but Dareke Young's fumble was the last of a laundry list of Raiders mistakes on Sunday. Laube had a nice return late, helping keep the Raiders within striking distance.
It is not all on Malik Benson, but the Raiders' punt returns have been unproductive this season.

title: Latest Kubiak Statement Proves Raiders Are Officially Back
full_text:
Who could have seen this coming from the 2026 Las Vegas Raiders?
Sure, the Raiders may have lost to the Kansas City Chiefs at home on Sunday, dropping to 3-1 on the year. However, there's a much bigger story than a simple win or loss: this Raiders team is different, and it starts with the head coach.
Early in his tenure, Klint Kubiak looks like an absolute home-run hire for Las Vegas. Regarded as one of the top young offensive minds in the NFL, Kubiak is putting that on display through his first handful of games at the helm for Las Vegas.
On Sunday, the Raiders were playing with house money. They faced a Kansas City Chiefs squad led by the best quarterback in the NFL, Patrick Mahomes, and overall, a team that is certainly more talented than the Raiders.
It wasn't so much about winning or losing this game as it was about giving Raider Nation a sense of hope going forward. The Raiders fought and nearly pulled off a comeback effort. This franchise desperately needed some bravado; Kubiak is providing that.
His latest statement proves that Las Vegas has its swagger back. Heading into the halftime locker room with a 13-10 lead over Kansas City, what Kubiak told CBS on his way into the locker room says everything Raider Nation needs to know.
"Got to be better, but you know what? We're winning. We're going to win the game."
Win or not, this from Klint Kubiak at halftime was brilliant:  "Gotta be better, but you know what? We're winning. We're gonna win the game."
Ultimately, the Raiders didn't emerge victorious, but it's important to look at the bigger picture here. Las Vegas fought and remained in the contest for the majority of the way, even when they were kicked in the teeth late. Kubiak has brought a fire back to this organization, and it's showing on the field.
There were questionable calls in this game, and it's perfectly okay to be upset about a loss in a game that the Raiders had a chance to win. Maybe the Raiders should've taken those points, and Kubiak acknowledged that after the game.
"And obviously, there's a point there where I took three points off the board, and we were going to be aggressive going into the game. I don't regret it. I regret not getting it."
However, what Kubiak has done is establish a new culture in Las Vegas, and one that is leading to winning football. At the end of the day, the Raiders are still 3-1 and are likely to greatly surpass most expectations put on them before the season started.
John Madden famously advised, "Never take points off the board." He strongly believed that if a penalty occurred on a successful field goal or extra point, coaches should accept the points rather than take them back to chase a touchdown. #Discuss
This team is young and talented, with a stud head coach leading the way. That simple halftime statement from Kubiak showed that these Raiders are building something special.

title: Raiders vs. Chiefs: Winners & Losers From Las Vegas
full_text:
LAS VEGAS, Nev.—The Las Vegas Raiders (3-1) fell to the perennial AFC West powers, the Kansas City Chiefs (4-0), 30-27 on Sunday.
Despite the first loss of the season for the Silver and Black, reasonable fans know that the 3-1 start, and battling an exceptional Chiefs team in the midst of a rebuild, is a great start.
Despite the loss, the Raiders have plenty to build on, and here are the biggest winners and losers.
Chiefs coach and, in my opinion, the best coach in the NFL, Andy Reid, praised the Silver and Black.
“My hat goes off to the Raiders and the job which they've done there. Listen, they're a good football team, and we knew it coming in. We figured it'd take four quarters of good, hard football. It is the Raiders. It is an AFC rival, and there's a ton of tradition there. They're building it here, and with that competition, it increases it even more. So, my hat goes off to them.”
"Gotta be better, but you know what? We're winning. We're gonna win the game." - @Raiders coach Klint Kubiak to @tracywolfson at halftime 👀 pic.twitter.com/87ESYVPBiC
Exiting the field at halftime, he did the usual coach interview on CBS. He didn’t just shock the nation; he stunned it when he boldly declared, "Gotta be better, but you know what? We're winning. We're gonna win the game."
John Madden famously advised, "Never take points off the board." He strongly believed that if a penalty occurred on a successful field goal or extra point, coaches should accept the points rather than take them back to chase a touchdown. #Discuss
You may question his decision to take points off the board; that is a fair debate (I agree with him), but he has single-handedly infused this team with fight, vigor, and bravado that would have made Al Davis proud. It's been a long time since this team had it, and Kubiak rightfully put it out there for the nation. This Raiders' rebuild is solidly planted on toughness.
It is one of many reasons his guys love him. He believes in them, and they in him.
Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker III won a Super Bowl with Kubiak, is friends with him, and Kubiak specifically recognized him in his opening press conference. He loves his former coach and praised his skill set afterward.
"He's doing great. I didn't get to talk to him or anything but obviously he's a great coach. I was there with him last year, and I know how he is. He always keeps everybody detailed and hold everybody accountable. So, he's a great coach, and he's going to continuously do well."
He did make a controversial call that goes against everything the legendary John Madden said you should never do: “Take points off the board.”
After a successful field goal, the Chiefs were penalized, and Kubiak elected to take the points off the board and go for it on fourth down.
He addressed it, saying, “…obviously, there's a point there where I took three points off the board, and we were going to be aggressive going into the game. I don't regret it. I regret not getting it.“
I am not going to act critical of Kubiak because the risk failed. I thought it was the right thing to do, and I would have done it too. The Raiders have overachieved, and Kubiak wanted and needed his team to see, tangibly, the faith he has in them.
The one thing everyone can agree was a first-year-coach mistake was that, at the end of the game, Kirk Cousins was rushed because Kubiak delayed getting the play in. Once again, in true Kubiak fashion, he took it head-on.
“I didn't get the play call in fast enough to the quarterback. Total missed opportunity. So, I blew it."
Ashton Jeanty loves his coach and the aggressive nature he leads with: "We love that from him, and that just shows the confidence he has in us as players and as a team. So, we just got to continue to get better and make those plays."
Reid wasn’t shy about what Kubiak is doing; he is a fan of the Raiders' first-year head man.
“Klint's [Kubiak] done a nice job. Like I mentioned earlier, he's holding the guys accountable for what he wants to get done. You can see that in their discipline of play. They haven't had a lot of turnovers, haven't had a lot of penalties on either side. They're trying to do what he's asking them to do, he's demanding it and it shows."
While not perfect, no one is, he was truly exceptional last night, and the Raiders would not have had a chance had he not been at the helm.
Cousins was 31/52 for 365 yards, threw two touchdown passes, threw one interception, and finished with a QB rating of 86.
All that despite not having a WR1, TE Brock Bowers essentially being taken out of the game plan by the Chiefs' superstar DC, and Jalen Nailor going out with a concussion. Kubiak wasn’t surprised by his veteran leader.
"Yeah, that's who he is. That's who he is. He played really good football tonight. That's why we brought him here."
Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes and Cousins are friends, and he had high praise for his leadership of the Silver and Black.
“When Kirk [Cousins] is dealing like that, man, it's hard to stop. He knows the entire offense, and he gets the ball out of his hand to his playmakers, and they got a guy like Brock Bowers out there making plays. That's a really good football team. It was a good win for us, but we have to keep building and keep getting better, and I'm sure they'll do the same."
Cousins had no time to praise his performance. “Every game is so important in this league, and so anytime you feel like you left one that you could have had, it hurts a lot. But all we can do now is respond and get back to work and be hard on ourselves tomorrow and get ready for New England.”
He continues to shine for the Raiders. Tonight, the offense settled for too many field goals, but that isn’t his fault. He once again kept the Raiders in the game and looked like an All-Pro. He was an outstanding 4/4 on field goals.
He said of his performance, "Any day you can go out there and make your kicks. Alex [Ward] and AJ [Cole] did a great job getting opportunities, and they were awesome with snaps and holds. Big guys up front were awesome for protection. Gave me a clean pocket to kick from, and you try and stack one kick after the next."
"And anytime you can go out there and help your team, that's the most important thing for me. Just going out there and getting those guys to believe in me that I can go out there and get points on the board for our team."
While disappointed in his offense settling for so many FGs, Cousins is thrilled to have the sure-thing kicker Gay.
"Yeah, he's been outstanding. We've put him in some tough spots with the lengths of his kicks, but he keeps responding. In this league, you really need it. It makes a major difference, and so many of these games and the bigger games, seem to come down to kicks. There's so much football up ahead, and we'll rely on him quite a bit in the weeks to come."
The aforementioned future Hall of Fame QB Patrick Mahomes raved about the Raiders' improved defense under Rob Leonard.
"That's a good football team. Defensively, they got a lot of veteran guys that came over to add into the talent they had, the D-line, the linebackers, and then the secondary, all were playing together, and really getting us off the field a lot of the time. We had some explosive plays there, especially towards the end that really helped us, but that's a really good football team.”
nothing but love after the whistle ❤️ @KCvsLV on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/j2d4FXQj8K
The Raiders superstar forced the Chiefs to do everything they could to avoid him, and even then they had to poke, prod, and hold, and that much attention opened up opportunities for multiple other players. Mahomes wasn't silent, however, about what he means to the Silver and Black.
"He's going to go hard the entire time. He's a great player, great competitor. He's tackling, he's getting the hits and stuff like that, but I'm going to hop back up. He helped me back up just like I would try to help him back up if I saw him in that position. It's a ton of…

title: Key Moments, Decisions in Raiders' Week 4 Loss to Chiefs
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders entered their Week 4 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs with nothing to lose. Anything less than a blowout loss would have made Sunday's matchup between the two teams just another regular-season game confirming the gap between them.
Since becoming the Chiefs' starter, Patrick Mahomes has always had the Raiders' number. Over the years, Mahomes, Andy Reid, and the Chiefs have made themselves at home at Allegiant Stadium. Reid entered Sunday with a chance to become the winningest NFL head coach at Allegiant.
Las Vegas won the toss and deferred to the second half. Deferring until the second half works best for both the Raiders' offense and defense, especially against someone like Patrick Mahomes. Handing Mahomes the ball first in the second half puts a lot of pressure on defenses.
Deferring also takes pressure off the Raiders' offense on their first drive. Not scoring points on their first drive and giving the ball to the opposing team first in the second half is all but the worst-case scenario for most teams, but especially for Las Vegas against Mahomes.
The Raiders' defense held the Chiefs to a three-and-out on their first drive. However, after a Chiefs penalty on the punt, Las Vegas accepted the penalty, forcing Kansas City to punt again. Kansas City converted a fake punt, giving Mahomes another first down.
Three plays later, Kansas City faced another fourth-and-short near midfield. This time, they faced a fourth-and-one. Mahomes and the Chiefs' offense took the field, but their fourth-down run was stopped by Las Vegas' defense, setting them up with great field position.
This has been the Raiders' story this season. Las Vegas' first three games witnessed what they can be when they play sound football. Week 4 was everything it was expected to be. Both teams had their moments that made the game a competitive, hard-fought outing.
The first half had a pace that favored Las Vegas, with a low-scoring game that moved quickly as both teams ran plays that kept the clock running. The Raiders ran a stellar two-minute drill that put them in position to connect on a 48-yard field goal as time expired in the first half.
Las Vegas entered the second half up 13-10. As in the season's first three games, the Raiders' offense failed to score. However, the drive became a turning point: Las Vegas' offense scored, kicking a short field goal.
However, a penalty was called on the Chiefs' defense, making it fourth-and-two. With a three-point lead, deep in the Chiefs' territory and their defense playing well to that point, Kubiak chose to be aggressive. Instead of taking the points, Las Vegas sent their offense back on the field.
The Chiefs stopped the Raiders on fourth down. It was the closest Las Vegas' offense would get to scoring for the rest of the quarter. The third quarter was mostly back-and-forth, with neither team scoring. The single biggest play of the quarter, and arguably the game, came at the end of the third.
After keeping Walker from breaking off big runs the entire game, Walker finally broke a long run on the final play of the third quarter. Walker's 76-yard run in the third quarter flipped the field, making way for an easy touchdown for the Chiefs at the start of the fourth quarter.
For the fourth straight week, the Raiders had a strong fourth quarter. Running back Dylan Laube returned a punt 50 yards, which helped make up for his fumble against the New Orleans Saints last week. His return also helped Las Vegas score a field goal a few plays later.
The Raiders' defense forced a three-and-out on the Chiefs' next offensive possession. Las Vegas' offense registered an eight-play, 60-yard drive that netted another field goal. However, Mahomes worked his magic one more time late in the fourth, completing a 55-yard pass on third down.
The long completion mirrored a play the Chiefs completed for a big gain earlier in the game. It was the difference-making play, as the completion put Kansas City on the Raiders' three-yard line with just over three minutes remaining. Kansas City scored a touchdown shortly after.
Las Vegas fumbled the ensuing kickoff, and the Chiefs scored a touchdown one play later, ending any chances of a comeback. The Raiders put up a fight at the end of the contest, but ultimately fell to Kansas City.

title: Raiders Stock Report: Who's Rising, Falling After Tough Chiefs Loss
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders' Week 4 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs was the latest opportunity to see how far the team has come under head coach Klint Kubiak. After starting the season 3-0, Las Vegas faced a Chiefs team that has dominated the yearly series between the two for a decade.
For the Raiders, Week 4 was the best chance to confirm, for better or worse, many things about Las Vegas' new-look team, with the first quarter of the regular season now in the books. As expected, Sunday was the most telling game of the four Las Vegas has played this season. The Raiders may have lost, but there is a lot to take away.
It is no secret that the Raiders have one of the league's best tight end groups. As talented as Brock Bowers is, the group is solid overall because they have talent beyond him. Bowers is arguably the best tight end in the NFL.
However, Michael Mayer and Ian Thomas give the Raiders a sizeable trio of tight ends who can make an impact in the passing game or as blockers. Sunday was the perfect example, as Thomas was wide open on the game's opening touchdown. Four of Kirk Cousins' first five passes were to tight ends.
The Raiders plan to handle the wide receiver position by committee. It was clear on Sunday that the committee included Las Vegas' tight ends. The loss of Jack Bech was notable early, as Las Vegas' receiving corps, with or without Bech, needs additional help.
On Sunday, Las Vegas used one of its deepest position groups to help compensate for its short-handed group of wide receivers.
Las Vegas' offense faced the best defense yet under Kubiak. They did so without Bech and starting offensive guard Jackson Powers-Johnson. Still, the Raiders' offense had several plays where their pass-catchers were wide open, in addition to Thomas' touchdown.
The Raiders' ability to draw up, call, and execute plays at a high level helped compensate for Las Vegas' missing players. In each of their first four games, solid play-calling has helped the Raiders' offense get players open down the field, and plays have worked to perfection.
This confirms the Raiders accomplished their offseason goal of finding a coach and offensive play-caller who can compete in today's league. Kubiak had already done so as an offensive coordinator with the Seattle Seahawks, but he has now done so as the lead man for the Raiders.
Kubiak and offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko have worked well together so far.
Few people have as high hopes and expectations for Masses as I do. His skill set matches what the Raiders need, and the type of players Las Vegas needs to fill out their secondary moving forward. However, because of my expectations for him, I will also be tough on the rookie.
He has the potential to have a long career in the Silver and Black, especially as they continue building out their defensive backfield in future seasons. One day, Masses could be to the Raiders' defensive backfield what veteran cornerback Eric Stokes currently is.
Last week, I listed Masses in this category, despite his interception and several good games overall. I  know it may not have made sense at the time. However, Chris Olave had several nice routes against the rookie, but the game's result and a wild fourth quarter overshadowed those plays.
As I expected, the Chiefs' offensive staff took note. Mahomes and the Chiefs went at Masses. This time, he allowed a touchdown, along with other completions. After winning the AFC Defensive Player of the Week Award in his very first start, Mahomes was bound to attack the rookie.
His struggles against good route runners and solid play calls from opposing offenses designed specifically for him are not glaring. However, Sunday's matchup against the Chiefs was a reminder that, like all rookies, Masses still has a lot to learn, much of which can only come with experience.
Las Vegas' offense didn't have Powers-Johnson, but overall, they still looked about the same as they did with him. Powers-Johnson's talent is not in question, but his durability is. Caleb Rogers being serviceable may or may not be a literal changing of the (starting) guard. Pun intended.

Kansas City has largely dominated the AFC West and the league since Patrick Mahomes became the team's starter. Las Vegas has been at the bottom of the totem pole. Entering this season, the Raiders had started seven different quarterbacks dating back to the 2023 season.
The Raiders and the Chiefs have been opposites for most of recent history, which is part of what makes Week 4 such an interesting matchup . Despite how different they are, the Raiders and the Chiefs have shared similarities through the first three weeks of the 2026 regular season.
It has been a while since claiming the Raiders and Chiefs had anything in common was even possible. That alone shows how far the Raiders have come in a short time. Yet, both teams average the exact same number of points on offense. Both teams have featured stout defenses that create turnovers.
Raiders veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins has led Las Vegas to an undefeated record through three games. It is a small sample size, especially for a quarterback who has played as long as Cousins has. Still, Cousins' familiarity with Kubiak and Cousins' steady play on the field have paid off so far.
“I think quarterbacking is all about, first of all, protecting the football. But so much of it is team. I think you got to remember that some of our fourth quarter success against the Saints was because our defense was giving us such short fields and getting us the ball back, and so they put the wind at your back."
“I don't know that suddenly we as an offense were playing a totally different game in the fourth quarter. It was just that we were put in a great position by our defense. So, team always helps and then the guys around you always helps. But it's really your unit."

title: Why Raiders Glad To Have Treydan Stukes Back in Action
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders are looking to remain undefeated as they battle the Kansas City Chiefs in a crucial divisional showdown.
If Klint Kubiak's crew wants to beat a resurgent Chiefs team, they'll need to execute on the defensive side of the ball. Rob Leonard has been excellent scheming things up on defense, and he'll need a major performance from all three levels of his unit.
The Raiders got good news this week: rookie safety Treydan Stukes has no injury designation. He is expected to be good to go for this game after missing last week due to concussion protocol.
What will Stukes bring to the Raiders now that he's back, as the team battles a division rival?
The Raiders have played well without Stukes, but getting a versatile defensive back back in the lineup matters a lot. The team has big plans for Stukes moving forward, and they need him healthy for them to come to fruition.
Through two games, Stukes has posted 11 total tackles and one pass defended. The team named him a starter at the beginning of the season, a sign that they believe in his ability to be an impactful player immediately.
When he was out against the New Orleans Saints, the Raiders allowed 255 receiving yards and four touchdowns through the air. It was clear that Stukes' presence was missed, and they'll need him against a Chiefs offense that ranks third in the league in total yards.
Although he is only a rookie, the Raiders need Stukes to be a big part of their plans. They have taken the league by surprise early this season, and if they want to keep it up and be a serious contender in the AFC, Stukes needs to be healthy and present.
The Chiefs look as explosive as they have been in the last half-decade, having reinvented their offensive approach with Eric Bieniemy back in the fold. It will take the Raiders' best defensive effort to pull off the win.
That includes Stukes, who has impressive ball-hawking skills and high-level football intelligence. They'll need him to put it to use against a quarterback like Patrick Mahomes, who has made a career out of destroying elite defenses.
Stukes is key to beating the Chiefs, and the Raiders should be happy he is back and out of concussion protocol. They need him to come up big in this game.

title: Predicting Raiders’ Offensive Leaders Against Chiefs
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders have been one of the biggest surprises of the 2026 NFL season so far, jumping out to a 3-0 start.
On Sunday, the Raiders host the likewise 3-0 Kansas City Chiefs at Allegiant Stadium at 4:25 p.m. ET. Facing a division rival speaks for itself, but sole possession atop the AFC West is also on the line. This matchup is one of the most electrifying games on the Week 4 slate. Here are projections for Las Vegas' offensive players' statistical outputs.
The 38-year-old quarterback has thrown three touchdowns in each of the first three games, but that streak will end on Sunday. Kansas City's defense is the best the Raiders have faced all season, and defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo's blitz packages could cause issues for Cousins.
That said, the 15-year veteran quarterback is excellent pre-snap and is quick to get the ball out of his hands. In a game that could be filled with points, Cousins could be in for another big outing.
The second-year running back has been marginalized in the last two games, averaging less than three yards per carry in each outing. Jeanty has an opportunity to bounce back against the Chiefs, who can be susceptible to the run.
Jeanty could cede opportunities to Mike Washington Jr., who has earned more work after his strong outing last week:  five carries for 54 yards, including a 36-yard touchdown. Nonetheless, Jeanty should see a substantial workload in a pivotal divisional matchup.
Bowers made his season debut in Week 3 against the New Orleans Saints, recording 10 receptions for 116 yards and one touchdown. Under Spagnuolo, Kansas City's defense typically takes away the best receiving option by doubling that player. We should see Bowers operate against bracket coverage consistently, which is why head coach Klint Kubiak moving the superstar tight end around pre-snap will be pivotal.
Nevertheless, as Bowers proved last week, it's virtually impossible to contain him, and he's always due for an explosive play. Kubiak should line Bowers up in the slot or near the line of scrimmage as much as possible to create linebacker matchups for the third-year tight end. Regardless of what the Chiefs throw at Bowers, expect a busy day for him in the passing game.
