title: Four Winners And Four Losers From Week 4 Dolphins Loss
full_text:
In their third road contest in four games, the Miami Dolphins had one of their best chances to win this season, but could not get the job done, falling to Minnesota 15-10.
It feels like there was genuine progress made by Miami. After being blown out by Las Vegas and San Francisco, the Dolphins hung around longer than expected against Kansas City and were a TOE away from a possible win against the Vikings.
Bottom line? This "progress" is too slow, and even though the list of winless NFL teams is shrinking, the Dolphins are firmly on that list no team wants to be on. Some players stood out for the Dolphins on both sides of the ball for good and bad reasons, but the same problems persist.
The biggest what-if of the season occurred in the second quarter when Bell caught a 68-yard touchdown to give the Dolphins the lead — except it didn't count because Bell BARELY stepped out of bounds before catching the ball, leading to an illegal touching penalty and wiping the score off the board.
Knowing how the game transpired, it's a brutal mistake for Bell to make. Every play matters more in a game that was this close. But if you were to take away that play, Bell was still a non-factor in this game, targeted three times but not recording a single catch. He was expected to build on a solid performance against Kansas City, but it didn't come close to happening.
One of the biggest negatives of Miami's season up to this point was the lack of a pass rush; opposing quarterbacks' jerseys were way too clean. However, the Dolphins found their groove against the Vikings, and Sieler was the poster boy of the group with three tackles, two tackles for loss, and, most importantly, TWO SACKS.
It's his best overall performance this season, hands down. He set the tone with his first sack, which came on the first play of the game. There was genuine synergy between him and some of the other Dolphins in the trenches, like Chop Robinson and Jordan Phillips.
Don't think this is a sign that Miami's pass rush is "fixed," and that they can continue this moving forward. But they found success against a really solid Minnesota offensive line, and will now take on a historically shaky Cincinnati O-line back in Miami Gardens, so let's see where they go from here.
Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores had his way in terms of getting to Miami's quarterback. Willis had an abysmal 85 passing yards, lost a fumble, and was sacked twice. While he didn't throw an interception, he shucked some questionable throws that could have been picked off.
When he had some solid completions here and there, he couldn't keep it going for back-to-back plays, or there was a penalty that wiped it off the board. In terms of being a dual-threat QB, he wasn't a threat at all in the run game.
I've tried my best to keep Willis off these lists so far this season, but his performance against Minnesota was the breaking point. Miami's offense had opportunities in this game to win, but it genuinely looked like Willis held the offense back at times.
The keys to the run game were given to Gordon following Achane's injury, and he didn't disappoint with 100 yards and a touchdown off nine carries.
His 53-yard pick-up coming out of halftime gave the Dolphins the spark they needed on offense, though it sadly led to a field goal. He could have even done better if one long-distance run hadn't been called back because he was "supposedly" touched at the line of scrimmage after stumbling down, though no TV angle was provided that actually showed that.
Regardless, Gordon was electric in this game and had to put the offense on his back at times. The flashes of speed, agility, and ability to break tackles in prior games culminated in one of his best performances in the NFL, and it was well needed.
In Paul's defense, the officiating crew for this game didn't give the Dolphins any favors, but players eventually need to adjust when they're getting hammered with penalties. Paul did not do that and was hit with three holding penalties. He negated a few quality plays from the offense, including the best run of the game for Willis in the second quarter.
It's a shame, because Paul did look good when blocking for Gordon and company. He had a great game against Kansas City and genuinely looked like he was turning into a quality pass blocker.
However, he regressed against Minnesota and visibly looked frustrated, not just with the officiating, but also with how the O-line struggled — Austin Jackson wasn't any better; it's just the matter of three holding penalties by Paul that put him on this list.
There needs to be a serious discussion about Rodriguez and how he deserves to be in the running for the NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year Award. He's done everything asked of him by Miami and then some, and seems to only be getting better as the weeks pass.
His performance against Minnesota was his best so far—- 18 total tackles (nine of which were solo) on 78 defensive snaps, leading the team in all three categories (tied in snaps). His 18 tackles in a single game are the most by ANY defensive player in the NFL this season in the NFL so far.
Rodriguez always seems to find his way to the football. His ability to wrap up quarterbacks, running backs, and wide receivers is currently unmatched in the NFL, especially considering he's 24 years old. Getting by Rodriguez with the ball in your hand has become a near-impossible task, cementing him as one of the brightest spots on the team this season.
On one hand, this was a decent game for Brooks by the numbers with 13 tackles. However, this slot truly represents everyone who attempted to contain TJ Hockenson, who had one of the best games of his career. Postgame, Brooks claimed ownership of the defense's struggles to keep up with the eighth-year tight end.
With Justin Jefferson not playing, there was hope that Miami's defense could silence Minnesota's passing game, but Hockenson turned out to be the hero that the Vikings needed. He racked up 13 receptions for 119 yards, including some of their biggest plays on offense as the game progressed.
The cherry on top was the final play before the two-minute warning, with Hockenson going down at the 1-yard line to ice the game as Miami had no more timeouts. Jordan Addison and the rest of Minnesota's wide receivers had mediocre performances in comparison; Hockenson was at the right place at the right time to become one of the most unexpected reasons why the Vikings won.
So far, Uche has had a pedestrian season for the Dolphins, but he provided solid snaps for Miami against the Vikings, finishing the day with six tackles and a sack in the second quarter.
He did some of his best work in the second half, including one of the most critical tackles of the game. On 3rd & 8, he stopped Aaron Jones dead in his tracks for a gain of three yards. Minnesota had to settle for a field goal, giving the ball back to Miami's offense, trailing by five points with just under seven minutes to go.
The Dolphins' offense didn't come through, but you can't say the defense didn't give them the opportunity needed to win the game.

title: Miami Dolphins 2026 Week 4 Snap Counts Stories: (Overly) Busy Day for the Defense
full_text:
What stood out regarding play counts in the Miami Dolphins' 15-10 loss against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday:
We'll start with the list of inactives, where the biggest news involved two players again being out with injuries — Caleb Douglas and Robert Beal Jr.
The only Dolphins players who were active but did not play were backup quarterback Kyle McCord, offensive lineman Andrew Meyer and running back Carlos Washington Jr., who was signed to the 53-man roster off the practice squad Saturday.
Since we've been keeping track every game, the starting lineup was back to seven rookies after tight end Will Kacmarek joined Week 3 starters Chris Bell at wide receiver, fullback DJ Herman, guard Kadyn Proctor, linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, cornerback Chris Johnson and safety Michael Taaffe.
-- What stands out here is the ridiculously low number of offensive snaps the Dolphins got, which was 39. That was exactly half the number of plays run by the Minnesota offense.
-- Jaylen Wright got the start at running back with De'Von Achane on IR with a torn ACL, but he quickly gave way to Ollie Gordon II, who ended up with a 22-12 snap advantage and clearly established himself as the current RB1 after rushing for exactly 100 yards.
-- For the first time this season, Kacmarek got more snaps at tight end than Greg Dulcich, with 24 compared to 20.
-- Veteran Jalen Tolbert was active for the second time, but he again barely was a factor on offense as he played only six snaps, two more than special teams specialist Ryan Miller. The Dolphins did use three wide receivers at the same time quite a bit, but this is where we point out that Malik Washington is more like a utility player on offense — a halfback/receiver, if you will — than a pure wide receiver.
-- The Dolphins used a sixth offensive lineman again, though this time it was only one snap for Caedan Wallace.
-- Four players were on the field for all of Miami's 78 defensive snaps: linebackers Jacob Rodriguez and Jordyn Brooks, Taaffe and Johnson.
-- This not surprisingly was a season/career high for the three rookies. The previous high for both Rodriguez and Johnson came in the season opener when both played all 68 snaps against the Las Vegas Raiders. Taaffe's previous high was 52 snaps against Kansas City. It was the second-highest total of Brooks' career, topped only by his 81 snaps for the Seattle Seahawks in a 33-13 victory against the Houston Texans in 2021, his second year in the NFL.
-- The Dolphins opened the game in the nickel and played most of the game with that five-DB alignment. JuJu Brents got 69 snaps at cornerback and Jason Marshall Jr. got 60.
-- Dante Trader Jr. again started at safety alongside Taaffe, but he left the game with a knee injury before returning, and Zayne Anderson wound up playing 29 snaps in Trader's place.
-- On the defensive line, what stood out was Josh Uche, who was very active, getting the most snaps on the edge with 55, five more than Chop Robinson, who also had his moments rushing quarterback Kyler Murray.

title: Five Instant Overreactions to Dolphins-Vikings Matchup
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins battled back late, but lost a 15-10 decision against to the Minnesota Vikings. Let’s overreact to the fourth straight loss to begin the Jeff Hafley era.
For the third time in four weeks, Miami was dominated in the third phase. The Dolphins gave up multiple big returns to Myles Price, and muffed three kicks of their own.
In a game that ultimately was decided by one score, having the worst special teams group in the league is going to keep moral victories from translating into material ones. The unit is sloppy, consistently out of place, and hasn’t shown any redeeming qualities outside of a nice Jaylen Wright return in Week 1.
An argument can be made that continuity will help this group over time, but Miami’s offense and defense don’t look nearly as out of place as its kicking game, despite also being made up of plenty of new players. This unit feels substantially worse than the rest of the team, and churning whatever you can of that portion of the roster seems like the best way forward.
The Dolphins' passing game was awful against Minnesota. Malik Willis finished 9-of-17 for 85 yards, and the team went 2-for-9 on third downs. Their biggest play, an out-of-structure touchdown from Malik Willis to Chris Bell, was wiped off the board due to the rookie stepping out of bounds before making the catch.
Outside of Malik Washington making a couple of nice plays in space and finishing with 67 yards, the receiving corps feels razor thin. Bell and Kevin Coleman Jr. missed out on crucial chemistry-building time this offseason, but have been vaulted into vital roles in the absence of Caleb Douglas.
Douglas’ return would not only re-adjust the pecking order, but also add some much-needed size and verticality to an aerial attack that seems insistent on pushing the ball deep down the field a few times a game.
Week over week, Miami is watching its rookies find increased comfortability, and several of them made major impacts on this game.
Jacob Rodriguez was all over the place, logging 18 total tackles, while Kadyn Proctor flashed on some big runs by Ollie Gordon. Michael Taaffe, Chris Johnson, Chris Bell, and Will Kacmarek all also had individual moments that showcased their potential.
Each have missed assignments, and the overwhelming amount of youth on this team is a major factor in Miami’s 0-4 record, but in a season where the team is looking for flashes, they’ve certainly gotten them so far.
Week One’s defensive woes seem like a distant memory compared to the most recent exposure we got against Minnesota. The team grabbed their first four sacks of the season , held Minnesota to zero touchdowns, and held their own on the backend for a majority of the game.
The front four had their best game of the season. Chop Robinson and Josh Uche were impactful, and the interior duo of Zach Sieler and Jordan Phillips appear to have settled in, with both making highlight plays.
The last couple of drives were rough, as Minnesota iced the game on the back of TJ Hockenson, but Jeff Hafley and Sean Duggan have this unit playing hard consistently, and their ascension has kept Miami in their last two games.
For as many individual high-points as there were in this game, there were just as many lows. For instance, following Miami’s lone touchdown drive, they allowed Minnesota to drain over eight minutes of clock, and after rallying to force a field goal, Jaylen Wright struggled to come up with a knuckling kick, knocking Miami’s offense back for their potential comeback drive.
This has been one of the major stories of this season. Penalties inside opposing territory, flags negating game-changing plays, and crucial clock and personnel gaffes late. These moments are to be expected of a young team, but the quantity and timing of them are becoming unacceptable. Whether this is simply the youth or a potential coaching problem is something that needs to be sorted out as soon as possible.

title: Dolphins Week 4 Instant Takeaways: So Close, Yet So Far
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins continue to be a tough out, but they still can't get that elusive first win under head coach Jeff Hafley.
In many ways, the Dolphins let one slip away against the Minnesota Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium, dropping a 15-10 decision that moved their record to 0-4.
The Dolphins gave the undefeated Vikings all they could handle, though in fairness Minnesota is a pretty unimpressive 4-0 team on offense, but again mistakes and missed opportunities made the Dolphins come up short.
And that's the plight of a team overloaded with young and unproven players, though some of the culprits on this day were not rookies but rather young veterans with starting experience.
While running back Ollie Gordon II proved a bright spot with his work in the absence of De'Von Achane, the bottom line is the Dolphins once again failed offensively with a fourth consecutive game with fewer than 14 points.
The defense gave the team a chance to win until the end, but then couldn't get the stop needed to give the offense a final opportunity to pull out a late victory.
-- The Dolphins don't have to hear about not having any sacks on the season anymore and they took care of that issue right from the start, courtesy of Zach Sieler. By the time they were done, the Dolphins had four sacks, two by Sieler and one each for Josh Uche and Chop Robinson.
-- Robinson ended with a game-high three QB hits, including back-to-back pressures in the first half and a sack like we haven't seen from him before where it wasn't about his speed and get-off but rather about pushing back right tackle Brian O'Neill into the lap of Kyler Murray.
-- The legend of Jacob Rodriguez continues to grow, this time with a game-high 18 tackles, which is the highest total in the NFL this season. What was lacking from his game this time was a tackle for loss or an impact third-down play. In other words, his performance was good, but maybe it was overblown a bit if you were to believe the folks at FOX and the gushing they were doing.
-- For all the good work of the defense — and it was a good performance, albeit against a mediocre offense missing its best player (Justin Jefferson) — it failed to deliver in the clutch. Needing the ball to try to come back, the Dolphins defense gave up four first downs on each of Minnesota's final drives, the first of which ended in the field goal and the second ending with kneel-downs to end the game.
-- Meanwhile, the Dolphins went three-and-out the only time they had the ball in the fourth quarter, which led to a time of possession advantage for the Vikings in that fourth quarter of 14:00 to 1:00.
-- Covering quality tight ends is not easy for any defense, but the Dolphins must do better than letting T.J. Hockenson completely own the game down the stretch, including the game-sealing third-down reception where he could have scored but instead gave himself up at the 2-yard line to run out the clock.
-- This is a recurring theme, but one we should get used to when we're dealing with so many young players.
-- It also sure looked like the Dolphins couldn't catch a break from the officials the entire game on a day when there seemed to be blown calls or questionable calls all over the place.
-- There were three significant close calls that all went against the Dolphins in this one, the most notable the call that Chris Bell's got a piece of the sideline to nullify his 68-yard touchdown off a brilliant off-structure play by Malik Willis. There also was the replay-assisted decision to rule that the Minnesota player had tipped the ball and therefore the roughing-the-punter penalty that would have given the Dolphins a first down had to be erased. And lastly there was that run where Ollie Gordon II stumbled at the line, got up and raced down the field, only for the officials to rule he was touched before getting up when TV replays didn't clearly show that at all.
-- And we won't talk about the three holding penalties called on left tackle Patrick Paul, all on plays where similar circumstances didn't produce a flag. Let's just say the Dolphins got a flag-happy crew on this day.
-- Willis' final stats again won't look very good for him without telling the real story because he was under duress. But maybe the Dolphins can take some comfort in holding the Vikings to two sacks after they had at least four in each of their first three wins.
-- Back to Gordon, that was some impressive running by the second-year tailback, and it sure looked as though his success came up the middle or over the left side.
-- Malik Washington showed once again why he's the most reliable and dependable wide receiver on the team and his work after the catch was some kind of impressive.
-- We addressed this in our halftime observations, but yes the special teams were rough, but that often happens when you have a talent-defiicient roster and the players on the back end of that roster are those playing in the kicking game.
-- So now the Dolphins are 0-4 for the sixth time in franchise history, the first time since that 2019 season. This 0-4, though, continues to look nothing like the 0-4 of 2019 when they lost by 20 or more points each time.

title: Breaking Down the Week 4 Dolphins Inactive Info
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins ' inactive list for their Week 4 matchup against the Minnesota Vikings once again was led by rookie wide receiver Caleb Douglas.
The list included the team's other injured player, edge Robert Beal Jr., along with the usual group of young players.
Tight end Justin Joly, who the Dolphins claimed off waivers from the Denver Broncos after they released the fifth-round pick from N.C. State, returned to the inactive list after making his NFL debut against the Kansas City Chiefs last week.
With Douglas out for a second game because of his ankle injury, veteran wide receiver Jalen Tolbert again will be active after not being in uniform for the first time two games of the regular season.
As expected, running back Jaylen Wright will be active after missing the Kansas City Chiefs because of his stinger/foot issue.
He'll be joined at running back by Ollie Gordon II and new 53-man roster member Carlos Washington Jr., who was signed off the practice squad Saturday.
We hit on all of our inactive list projections for the second time in four games.
Edge defender Rodney McGraw has a chance to become the 12th Dolphins rookie to make his NFL debut after being elevated from the practice squad Saturday. The Dolphins have 14 rookies on their roster, with Kenneth Grant and Trey Moore on injured reserve, and sixth-round pick DJ Campbell is the only rookie on the active roster yet to make his NFL debut. Practice squad member Max Llewellyn got playing time in Week 2 when the seventh-round pick was elevated for the game in San Francisco.
Campbell and fellow offensive lineman Chukwuebuka Godrick will be inactive for a fourth consecutive game, with Brady Cook once again serving as the emergency third quarterback.
Cornerback Marcellas Dial Jr. will be inactive for a third straight straight week after playing in the season opener against the Las Vegas Raiders.
Godrick and Campbell also were expected inactives based on the fact the Dolphins are carrying 10 offensive linemen on their active roster and the normal number is eight for game day, and they're the two least established of the group.
The Vikings' inactive list is headed by wide receiver Justin Jefferson, who was ruled out Friday because of the ankle injury he sustained in Week 3.
The list also includes B Max Brosmer, S Jakobe Thomas, P Brett Thorson, CB Chuck Demmings and DL Elijah Williams.

title: UDPATE: Why It Was the Right Time for the Dolphins to Kick the Tires on Another Former First-Round Pick
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins, at the risk of repeating ourselves, are on a quest to find core players for the future this season as much as they are looking for wins.
This is not bold statement because we've seen it manifest itself time and time again through the personnel transactions the team has made going back to the spring where the only newcomer of significant or financial commitment the team added was Malik Willis — and that in and of itself should be the only evidence anyone needs to understand he's not just a bridge quarterback.
Among the many new players brought in were a couple of former first-round picks looking to revive their NFL career and after the first experiment failed, the time has come to see about the second one.
Specifically, it's time for the Dolphins to find out what they have in defensive tackle Mazi Smith, and that's just what they made happen Saturday when they announced he was one of the two practice squad players elevated for the Week 4 game at Minnesota — just like we had suggested minutes before the move became official (and, no, we didn't get advance notice).
Also elevated was edge defender Rodney McGraw, who'll be in line to make his NFL debut, while running back Carlos Washington Jr. officially was signed to the active roster off the practice squad.
Smith failed as a first-round pick of the Dallas Cowboys in 2023 out of Michigan before he was included in the trade with the New York Jets that sent defensive tackle star Quinnen Williams to Dallas.
After they saw him for three games last year, the Jets cut Smith this offseason and the Dolphins signed him to their practice squad in the hopes that he perhaps could rediscover the form that had made him a disruptive force for the Michigan defensive line, where in 2022 one of his teammates up front was Kenneth Grant.
Smith started 17 games for Dallas in 2024, but never became that presence in the middle of the defensive line for the Cowboys.
The Dolphins' current interior defensive line group is down to three players after Kenneth Cooper Jr. was waived this week, though Grant could be back pretty soon from injured reserve with the Week 4 game at Minnesota being the last one he has to sit out regardless of health.
For that game against the Vikings, it was difficult to envision or rationalize the Dolphins going with only three IDLs — Zach Sieler, Jordan Phillips, Zeek Biggers — because just one injury would have put an unfair burden of the other two.
That meant the Dolphins likely needed to elevate a defensive tackle from the practice squad.
The Dolphins certainly could elevated Cooper since he did play in the first three games and was re-signed to the practice squad after clearing waivers, but the mere fact they were willing to expose him to waivers in the first place suggests his long-term future with the team isn't overly solid.
And since the 2026 season is about evaluation, why not get a look at Smith?
Head coach Jeff Hafley said Friday that Smith had made steady progress since joining the practice in the first days of September.
"He keeps getting better, and hopefully we'll be close to seeing him on a Sunday," Hafley said. "But he's making improvement, learning the defense and doing everything that (DL coach Austin) Clark asks him to do. I think he's getting himself in better shape, which is important. I've seen improvement, and I'm excited about the progress that he's made and eventually we're going to see him on a Sunday."
This Sunday will be that day.

title: Setting the Stage for the Dolphins-Vikings Week 4 Matchup
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins again will be looking for their first victory of the Jon-Eric Sullivan/Jeff Hafley era when they face the Minnesota Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium on Sunday.
Here's all the pertinent info for this Week 4 Dolphins-Vikings matchup:
DATE: Sunday, Oct. 4, 2026
SITE: U.S. Bank Stadium; Minneapolis, Minnesota
Announcers: Kevin Kugler (play-by-play), Daryl Johnston (color analyst), Allison Williams (sideline)
FanDuel line: Vikings by 10.5 (over/under 38.5)
Dolphins — EDGE Robert Beal Jr. (hamstring), WR Caleb Douglas (ankle) and CB Storm Duck (knee/Achilles) are OUT
Vikings — CB Charles Demmings (hamstring), WR Justin Jefferson (ankle) and P Brett Thorson (right hamstring) are OUT
Regular season series history: Dolphins lead 7-6
Oct. 16, 2022 at Miami — Vikings 24, Dolphins 16
Dec. 16, 2018 at Minnesota— Vikings 41, Dolphins 17
Dec. 21, 2014 at Miami — Dolphins 37, Vikings 35
Sept. 19, 2010 at Minnesota — Dolphins 14, Vikings 10
Nov. 19, 2006 at Miami — Dolphins 24, Vikings 20
Dolphins' largest margin of victory: 17 (1988 at Miami; Dolphins 24, Vikings 7)
Dolphins' largest margin of defeat: 24 (2018 at Minnesota; Vikings 41, Dolphins 17)
Highest-scoring matchup: 73 points (1994 at Minnesota; Vikings 38, Dolphins 35)
Lowest-scoring matchup: 20 points (2000 at Minnesota; Vikings 13, Dolphins 7)
Former Vikings players with the Dolphins:
Former Vikings coaches with the Dolphins:
Former Dolphins players with the Vikings:
LB Andrew Van Ginkel, OLB Kyle Van Noy, pass game coordinator/QB coach Josh McCown
Former Dolphins coaches with the Vikings:
Defensive coordinator Brian Flores, assistant head coach Frank Smith, defensive pass game coordinator/DB coach Gerald Alexander
The Vikings are one of the five 3-0 teams around the NFL and it's pretty astounding how they've gotten there considering their offense is ranked last in the league after failing to reach even 250 yards in any of the games. Minnesota is winning because of its defense, which has produced 14 sacks, 37 QB hits and six takeaways in those three games against the Green Bay Packers, Chicago Bears and Tampa Bay Buccaneers. QB Kyler Murray returned to action after missing the Week 2 game against the Bears because of a concussion, but again it's the defense orchestrated by former Dolphins head coach Brian Flores that's been the big story.
-------------------------------------------------------------------
The Dolphins are double-digit underdogs for a third consecutive game, but there might be reason to question that line here given the Vikings' porous showing on offense — particularly with Justin Jefferson ruled out Friday. After a lightning-quick first touchdown drive, the Dolphins defense pretty much controlled the high-powered Kansas City offense last week, so there's reason to believe it could duplicate that performance over a full game. The Dolphins still don't have a sack on the season, but they're due and maybe even just pressure on Kyler Murray creates a key turnover or two. It's really hard to picture the Dolphins winning this game with their offense, but simply not turning the ball over could help keep them in the game.
-------------------------------------------------------------------
The matchup between the Vikings defense and Dolphins offense looks pretty scary at first glance, in large part because of the absence of running back De'Von Achane to keep Brian Flores from maybe all-out attacking as he likes to do. QB Malik Willis was pressured pretty regularly in the first two games, though the line did a much better job against Kansas City last week. Still, the Dolphins haven't seen the kind of relentless blitzing and pass rushing they're likely to see in this game. The Dolphins have yet to top 13 points so far this season, and it's really difficult to see them doing it against the Vikings.
Just looking at a 3-0 team going against an 0-3 team, the initial reflex is to predict an easy victory for the Vikings. Except that the Vikings aren't necessarily a great 3-0 team with all their offensive issues. So the idea that they're going to blow out the Dolphins, as talent-deprived as Miami might be, just doesn't fly from here. Minnesota likely will win, but it says here the Dolphins manage to keep it close. Final Prediction: Vikings 13, Dolphins 10

title: Big Wins for Dolphins on Final Week 4 Injury Report
full_text:
The final determination of injured players for the Miami Dolphins and Minnesota Vikings ahead of their Week 4 matchup definitely favored the team from South Florida.
Each team ruled out three players for the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on Sunday, though the best player of those six was Vikings star wide receiver Justin Jefferson.
And the one player the Dolphins not only didn't rule out but also had no game status designation on was center Aaron Brewer, whose status became a bit of a concern when he was listed as a limited participant in practice Thursday because of a hand injury. Brewer was a full participant in practice Friday.
It also should be noted that one of the three players the Dolphins ruled out wasn't even eligible to play against Minnesota, and that's Storm Duck who still had to sit out a minimum of one more game after starting the regular season on the Reserve/PUP list.
Because he return to practice Wednesday and his three-week window opened, Duck still somehow wound up having a game status designation. After being limited in practice Wednesday and Thursday and then having an Achilles adding to his knee injury, Duck wound up being a full participant Friday, which obviously bodes well for his imminent return to the active roster.
The two players who would be eligible to play but won't also missed the home opener against the Kansas City Chiefs last Sunday, and that's rookie wide receiver Caleb Douglas and edge defender Robert Beal Jr.
Because the Dolphins elevated edge Clelin Ferrell against the Chiefs last week, perhaps it's safe to assume that rookie seventh-round pick Max Llewellyn will be elevated from the practice squad for a second time this season.
The other elevation figures to come at the running back position, where the Dolphins have only two players on the active roster — Jaylen Wright and Ollie Gordon II — now that De'Von Achane is on injured reserve with the left knee injury he sustained against Kansas City.
The question is whether the choice at running back will be Carlos Washington Jr. or Jarquez Hunter, who the Dolphins acquired in a trade with the Los Angeles Rams over the summer.
Edge Chop Robinson was added to the injury report Friday with a foot issue, but he was a full participant in practice and didn't get a game status designation.
The only player who was limited Friday was long-snapper Tucker Addington, who continues to deal with the shoulder injury he sustained against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 2.
For Minnesota, Jefferson didn't practice all week, so his absence shouldn't be very surprising, though it's significant considering he's easily his team's best offensive player.
This will mark the second time in four games this season the Dolphins will face a team missing its best offensive player, the first coming in the season opener when the Las Vegas Raiders were without star tight end Brock Bowers.
Along with Jefferson, the Vikings ruled out cornerback Charles Demmings and punter Brett Thorson. With Thorson, Minnesota will use veteran Johnny Hekker, who was waived but re-signed to the practice squad this week.

title: Three Bold Predictions for the Miami Dolphins Against the Minnesota Vikings
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins are set to face off against the 3-0 Minnesota Vikings on Sunday. Here are some bold predictions heading into this matchup, based on how both teams have performed so far this season.
Miami’s passing offense has been aggressive through three weeks, with quarterback Malik Willis ranking first in pass attempts of 20+ air yards, per NFL Pro.
That volume hasn’t translated to efficiency, though, as Miami is four of 17 on long throws, including an abysmal one of nine performance against Kansas City.
Watching the tape back, though, tells a story of near misses, and real opportunities over the top. Led by defensive coordinator Brian Flores, Minnesota plays an aggressive brand of defense that sometimes leaves downfield gaps in coverage as they expect the ball to come out fast.
They’ve been burned on this a few times, giving up a 20+ yard passing play in each of their first three games, and ranking seventh-worst in EPA per play allowed on deep attempts. I would expect Miami to try to force the issue, and if Willis and his receivers are on the same page, it could swing this game in the Dolphins’ favor.
The battle between the Vikings’ offense and the Dolphins’ defense is one between a stoppable force and a moveable object. Minnesota’s -0.19 EPA per play is tied for the fourth-worst mark in football through three weeks, while Miami’s 0.15 EPA per play allowed is dead last among defenses.
However, this matchup may be more favorable to Miami than meets the eye. The Dolphins’ defensive front played their best game of the season in week three, and are facing off against a bottom-five unit in terms of yards per carry. If Zach Sieler and Jordan Phillips can continue their ascension and lead a strong run-defense unit, it would free up their second-level defenders to get to their zone landmarks quicker.
Minnesota’s passing game is already fluttering, and now will be without star wide receiver Justin Jefferson because of an ankle injury. Recent trends are favoring Jeff Hafley’s defense to hunker down, and I wouldn’t be shocked if it happens.
Through Miami's first three games, third-year wide receiver Malik Washington’s touches have steadily increased, from just three in week one to seven in their most recent game against the Kansas City Chiefs.
Washington spent the entirety of the offseason building chemistry with Malik Willis, unlike his receiving corps counterparts Chris Bell, Kevin Coleman Jr., and Ryan Miller, and it’s shown up on multiple big occasions this season.
Without De’Von Achane and rookie standout Caleb Douglas, familiarity is going to be a key against a blitz-happy Brian Flores defense , and Washington has been Willis’ security blanket in out-of-structure and pressure situations so far this year. Miami has been creative in aligning Washington just about everywhere, and with their most dangerous weapon now out for the season, the versatile receiver will have to pick up the slack.

title: Christian Darrisaw Injury Concerns Could Force Vikings to Throw Caleb Tiernan Into the Fire
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings' bid for a perfect season continued with Sunday's win over the Miami Dolphins ; however, the Purple and Gold's latest victory didn't come without some loss. Minnesota's offensive line is featuring a couple of potential absences from key contributors. Left guard Donovan Jackson exited Week 4 with a knee injury, while starting left tackle Christian Darrisaw also sustained a concussion in the win.
What's even more concerning about Darrisaw's issue is that he was allegedly cleared from the in-game concussion protocol, only to be removed again after still showing symptoms (h/t Vikings), according to head coach Kevin O'Connell. Minnesota's head coach added that the team "will continue to evaluate" Darrisaw before hopefully providing an update on Monday.
In addition, OT Christian Darrisaw is in the NFL’s concussion protocol. https://t.co/hLlOv93wYR
Given how tricky concussions are, plus the fact that all players must clear the five-stage protocol before returning, Minnesota could be in trouble. The good news for the Vikings is that their bye week comes after their Week 5 showdown with the New Orleans Saints, giving Darrisaw (and Jackson) ample time to recover.
That said, a potential absence (even for just one game) might lead Minnesota to turn to the next man up, which might be 2026 third-round pick tackle Caleb Tiernan.
After Darrisaw left Sunday's game, the Vikings slotted free-agent addition Ryan Van Demark into the LT1 role. Although the Connecticut product had a solid performance as a run blocker, his pass protection left something to be desired, allowing three pressures across 22 pass-blocking opportunities —good for a 51.9 grade on Pro Football Focus .
Considering how Van Demark has been average at best in pass protection throughout his career, it's not unfathomable to imagine the Vikings giving some of the available LT snaps to Tiernan, too. They made him a Day 2 selection and have him on the 53-man roster for a reason , right?
Despite his high draft selection and the potential he possesses, Tiernan wasn't activated for the Vikings' first three games .
That changed in Week 4, though, when he finally made his debut in the win over the Dolphins, playing eight offensive snaps as an inline tight end rather than a tackle, according to PFF . Still, he made the most of his first NFL opportunities, finishing with grades of 70.3 for run blocking and 75.7 for pass protection.
Drafted 97th overall in April, Tiernan is a 6-foot-7, 323-pound blocker coming off a second-team All-Big Ten nod at left tackle. He played to an 84.3 PFF pass-block grade in 2025 . He allowed only nine sacks throughout his five-year run at Northwestern and surrendered 13 pressures in each of his last two years, compared to 26 total in 2023.
That doesn't mean he'll find similar success as a pro player, but the Vikings won't know until they try, either.
As mentioned before, the Vikings only have one game left before their bye week, and the upcoming showdown against the 1-2  Saints could be a solid measuring stick.
Even though they're below .500, the Saints' pass rush has looked solid heading into Week 4's Monday Night Football, clocking in at a PFF grade of 74.4 —seventh-best in the league. Five New Orleans players have at least six pressures this season, headlined by Chase Young's team-leading 12 (which includes five sacks).
Assuming the unit keeps playing that way, it could be an opportunity to assess what Tiernan (and Van Demark) is made of heading into the week-long break.
Then, whether Darrisaw is healthy or not, the Vikings will know whether to feel confident in their backup LTs coming out of the bye or need to explore the trade market for a potential solution.
The Vikings have been taking their time with Tiernan as he acclimates to the NFL, but they might have no choice but to throw the third-rounder into the fire if Darrisaw isn't good to go in Week 5.

title: 3 Studs & 3 Duds From Vikings' Week 4 Win Against the Dolphins (Hockenson Shines, Jennings Remains a Concern)
full_text:
The Vikings remain undefeated after their Week 4 victory over the winless Dolphins, but the 15-10 win wasn't the one-sided game many fans expected based on their records heading into the game.
Miami scored the only touchdown of the game, but Minnesota's defense and kicking kept the Vikings ahead for the entire contest. The crowd at U.S. Bank Stadium was quite vocal about their displeasure with the offense, which seemed to improve as the game went on.
Some Vikings players had better games than others. Sadly, there were a few players who struggled to contribute in Sunday's win.
Let's take a look at Minnesota's studs and duds from the game against the Dolphins.
Someone needed to step up as a pass-catcher with Justin Jefferson on the sidelines. While he recovers from his ankle injury, T.J. Hockenson had a great day. He caught all 13 of his targets from quarterback Kyler Murray, gaining a team-high 119 yards through the air.
Hockenson would have had a touchdown, but he slid before crossing the goal line, so Minnesota could have let the clock expire by taking knees with the lead instead of giving the ball back to the Dolphins. While it was a smart play, a lot of fans would have loved to have seen the touchdown scored.
With Jefferson out, this was a huge opportunity for Jauan Jennings to finally have a breakout game for the Vikings. Coming into this game, he had one catch for one yard on the season, and he continued to struggle on Sunday afternoon, catching one pass for eight yards.
The $8 million Minnesota paid to sign the former 49ers touchdown machine as a free agent this offseason feels like highway robbery at this point , and he may not get many more opportunities to change that impression.
Another week, more praise for kicker Will Reichard. Once again, he had a perfect day for Minnesota, making all five field goal attempts, including one from 50 yards out. Every point the Vikings scored this week came from Will the Thrill's leg.
To put into perspective how good Reichard has been, his last missed kick was in Week 8 of the 2025 season. Considering that he hasn't been kicking many field goals from close to the uprights, that makes it even more impressive and helps to build his All-Pro case .
Minnesota once again turned to veteran punter Johnny Hekker with starter Brett Thorson sidelined with a hamstring injury. Typically, the 15-year pro is as reliable as a special teams player can be, but his punting in Week 4 left a lot to be desired.
Hekker punted four times against Miami, averaging only 37.8 yards and getting one touchback. Considering his longest punt of the day was 52 yards, that shows how inconsistent he was with the depth of his kicks. Hopefully, Thorson doesn't miss much more time.
Starting running back Aaron Jones Sr., 31, is playing through a knee injury and could have used some help to get things done on the ground. Instead, head coach Kevin O'Connell made him their bell-cow rusher, and Jones cashed in on those opportunities.
Jones ran the ball 20 times for the Vikings, gaining 94 yards while adding four catches for 34 yards. Having 128 yards of offense come from a player who probably should have been on a snap count is big, but he shouldn't be asked to do that often .
As previously stated. Jones shouldn't have to carry the burden of Minnesota's run game alone. With Jordan Mason on injured reserve while he recovers from thumb surgery, the Vikings needed Demond Claiborne or DeeJay Dallas to step up .
Claiborne only had three rushing attempts and gained 12 yards, while Dallas didn't record a single carry. Dallas had one catch for 10 yards, but the duo having only four touches, compared to Jones's 24, is not a productive or healthy ratio for the season.

title: Vikings Week 4 Report Card: Grading Every Position After Grinding Out Win vs. Dolphins
full_text:
Maybe someday Vikings fans will get to witness a pretty win. That day was not Sunday, but now, at 4-0, it's best not to look a gift horse in the mouth.
The Vikings took down the Dolphins 15-10 with their tried-and-tested formula: elite defense combined with questionable offense . It hasn't been the most beautiful start to the season, but each week, Minnesota has somehow found a way, with contributions from everywhere.
So, with that being said, let's get into how each Vikings position group performed in the Week 4 win.
Kyler Murray was noticeably better this week, but mostly just took advantage of his available checkdowns to running backs and tight ends with a pedestrian 6.7 yards per completion. After a rough first half, Murray settled in during the fourth quarter and showed what could be possible in this offense. It was an encouraging performance, even if it was against what is probably the worst team in the league.
Still, despite the lack of scoring plays, Murray protected the ball, and as long as the Vikings don't turn the ball over, there's always a chance to win.
Aaron Jones Sr. has carried the load admirably without Jordan Mason , nearly notching his second 100-yard game of the season against Miami. The Vikings are playing with fire, though, running the injured 31-year-old at a high clip, and the tread is certainly wearing on the tires. Do they really have a choice, though?
Not really, as neither DeeJay Dallas nor Demond Claiborne have shown much juice. Claiborne did have his biggest day of the season with three carries for 12 yards.
Without Justin Jefferson, the Vikings needed a big game from Jordan Addison. Despite the win, that didn't happen, as Addison finished the day with a modest four catches and 52 yards. Jauan Jennings is also a clear afterthought in the Minnesota offense after notching just his second reception of the year, and it's safe to say that his offseason acquisition was extremely overhyped.
The Vikings have had just one wide receiver touchdown since Jefferson's two-score outburst in Week 1, and this group must start ascending soon.
Have a day, T.J. Hockenson.
The Minnesota tight end had a career performance, racking up 13 catches for 119 yards and what could have been a late touchdown had he not slid to run out the clock. Murray found a favorite target, at least for this week, and it was a good day for a unit that played its first game without their No. 2 guy , Josh Oliver.
After going three straight games to start the season without a sack, the Dolphins dropped Murray on his first dropback of the game. Miami got to him three more times in the contest, and penalties and injuries to both Donovan Jackson and Christian Darrisaw stacked up to make it the worst game (h/t Vikings) of the year for the Vikings' offensive line.
Christian Darrisaw is being evaluated for a concussion and his return is questionable.
The solid run game was about the only redeeming factor in this one, while the injury concerns are certainly a huge factor to monitor moving forward.
The interior defensive line had a down day overall, but it felt more like an anomaly than a sign of things to come. The Dolphins ran the ball well, putting up 121 yards on the ground, and there wasn't much push inside on Malik Willis dropbacks either.
Ultimately, they did allow the edges and linebackers to shine, though, too.
Dallas Turner continued his push for a possible Defensive Player of the Year award and now has 5.5 sacks after getting two more on Sunday. Fans also got their first look at rookie Jake Golday, who took his first defensive snaps of the season, and Blake Cashman continued his 15-game streak of performances with seven or more tackles.
The edges and off-ball backers for the Vikings have been arguably some of the best in the NFL through four weeks, and it's an incredibly fun group to watch.
The secondary was fine, but never really got tested by a struggling Miami offense. Malik Willis attempted just 17 passes, but also only threw for 85 yards. The Vikings dropped a few potential interceptions and could've had a bigger day if they reeled in even just one of them.
This team might very well be 1-3 without Will Reichard, who has now accounted for 49% of the Vikings' total points this season. Reichard continued his All-Pro bid by scoring all 15 of Minnesota's points on Sunday afternoon, including a game-high 50-yarder. Meanwhile, Myles Price was electric once again with a 47-yard kick return and a 36-yard punt return.
The only real blemish was the poor performance by Johnny Hekker, who shanked a few punts on the way to a 37.8-yard average, but hopefully Brett Thorson is on the mend anyway.

title: Will Reichard Powers Undefeated Vikings  to 15-10 Win Over Dolphins (and What Mattered Most in Week 4)
full_text:
MINNEAPOLIS, MN — The undefeated Vikings welcomed the winless Dolphins to the Twin Cities for some Week 4 action on Sunday afternoon.
At stake for the Vikings? Continuing their undefeated start, showing competence in the passing game, and helping defensive coordinator Brian Flores exact brutal revenge against the franchise he once coached. For the Dolphins? Proving they can win a football game and maybe sack a quarterback while they’re at it.
Turns out, things would be a little more interesting than many expected.
The 15-10 win for the Purple and Gold followed a familiar script, as the Vikings offense kept it much closer than it should have. The Dolphins, to their credit, came out motivated and feisty. Minnesota looked to be a far cry from a team that’s undefeated on the season, as offensive incompetence nearly derailed their undefeated start to the season.
Luckily, the Vikings' defense and special teams once again did just enough to keep them afloat. With one more game to go before a much-needed bye week, let's dive into what truly mattered from Sunday's win.
Will Reichard may be the best thing to ever happen to this team, and I’m only being partially hyperbolic. He nailed five field goals with a long of 50 for the day and is now a perfect 12-for-12 for the season. He's now outscored the rest of Minnesota's special teams and the entire offense 32-12 since Week 2 (h/t VikingzFanPage).
#Vikings points scored since week 2: Will Reichard: 32 Special teams: 6 Rest of offense: 6 (Per the broadcast) pic.twitter.com/8eYXtHiIzb
This is now the second time this season that Reichard has accounted for every point scored by the Vikings. Reichard’s reliability has been a bright spot for a Vikings team whose offense seems incapable of finding the end zone. While his performance has been incredibly impressive, the irony of the Vikings’ kicker being their most reliable scoring threat should not be lost on any of us.
The Dolphins entered the game without a single sack on the season. That would change on Kyler Murray’s first snap of the game as Zach Sieler got into the backfield, bringing him down (h/t Dolphins Wire's Jason Sarney). From there, the offense couldn't find consistent footing, and boos rang out at multiple points throughout the afternoon.
And Zach Sieler gets the first sack of the season for the Miami Dolphins. On the games first snap. pic.twitter.com/XcfV3KTzAF
Murray looked rough, but Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell’s play calling did him zero favors whatsoever. To this point, the marriage between Murray’s skill set and O’Connell’s scheme seems incompatible. He would end the day with only 247 passing yards on a 27-for-37 (73.0%) completion rate and no touchdowns. He did, however, find a flow late in the fourth and seems to be building a connection with T.J. Hockenson, who had 13 catches for 119 yards on the day.
The offensive line would take a beating as the Vikings lost left guard Donovan Jackson with a knee injury. Later, left tackle Christian Darrisaw left the game with a neck injury before returning to start the second half... and then exiting again to be examined for a concussion, per the Vikings.
Running back Aaron Jones once again fought valiantly to give the offense some form of life, running for 94 rushing yards on 20 carries (4.7 yards per attempt) on the day.
The fact that a 31-year-old RB who has already faced a knee injury this season is their most reliable offensive player should indicate just how poor the passing game has been.
General manager Nolan Teasley may soon be faced with some difficult decisions as the trade deadline approaches. The team is winning games, but the offense is simply unsustainable. The unit needs either an injection of explosiveness in the run game or a QB who can run the offense the way O’Connell wants.
It turns out that 2026 is the year of Dallas Turner. His two first-half sacks set the tone for a defense looking to inject energy into their home crowd while the offense struggled mightily.
The third-year pass rusher tallied an additional two sacks to bring his season total to 5.5, with his five pressures bringing that number up to 29. He also forced a fumble. Not only was Turner awarded an 86.1 overall grade on Pro Football Focus for his efforts, but his pass rush grade of 92.9 was a new season high, beating his previous best set in Week 1 (90.4).
Turner's emergence after the Jonathan Greenard trade has been one of the best storylines of the season. It would be shocking if he isn't on an All-Pro team at the end of the season, potentially even challenging for 2026 NFL Defensive Player of the Year honors, too.

title: Vikings vs. Dolphins: Who Wins and Why in Week 4
full_text:
Minnesota has as good of a chance as any to improve to 4-0 this Sunday as they take on the 0-3 Miami Dolphins. It's the classic trap game, as Miami does actually posses some competency in certain areas, but the Vikings will likely be licking their chops in this one.
While the Vikings come in with the perfect record, they haven't played anywhere near perfection on the field. Meanwhile, the Dolphins are hoping to end a three-game skid to start the year by taking advantage of a lackluster Viking offense. There's a lot to dissect in this matchup, so let's get into who wins and why.
Despite entering the matchup 0-3, the Dolphins defense isn't actually too terrible (hang the banner). They boast a potential Rookie of the Year winner in linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, who has 28 tackles and one interception on the year, and a solid run-defense. That's about where the compliments end, however, as Miami remains the only team in the league yet to register a sack, and has allowed a blistering 80% completion rate to opposing quarterbacks.
The Minnesota offense may not be the picture of dominance through three games, and the absences of Jordan Mason and Justin Jefferson likely ensures that they won't be this week either. Still, Kyler Murray hopefully got the first ugly game--and it was ugly--out of the way, and should settle in a bit back at home.
The Vikings will rely heavily on Jordan Addison and Aaron Jones to be the difference-makers in this one, and if Murray can protect the ball, there's no reason the offense can't put up points. Still, the Vikings have yet to throw for more than 175 yards in a game, and if things aren't clicking against a Dolphins team that has only forced 6 incompletions over the past two weeks, serious alarm bells should start going off in Minnesota.
The Dolphins will go the rest of the way without their best player after De'Von Achane tore his ACL in the first quarter of last week's loss. Without Achane, the Dolphins offense managed to score just three points the rest of the game, and they'll need to get creative to get past a Brian Flores defense playing some of it's best football.
Miami has the lowest-scoring offense in the NFL, and has yet to eclipse 13 points in any game. Malik Willis has been sacked four or more times twice, and the Vikings absurd 70% blitz-rate may have a chance to add to that number again.
Flores surely won't hold back facing the team that fired him , and that blitz-rate could even climb higher. Willis is mobile, though, and like Murray, may be able to use that ability to escape some would-be tacklers. Still, without Achane, it's hard to see Minnesota getting scared off with any play-action, and Dallas Turner and company may just pin their ears back all game.
Ultimately, this boils down to a top-five defense taking on a bottom-five offense that just lost their best player. If Willis, can avoid pressure and use his legs, Miami may stand a fighting chance. Otherwise, this is just going to further cement the budding idea around the league that Flores is the best defensive coordinator in the NFL.

title: Jauan Jennings Could Be a Vikings Lost Cause If He Doesn't Capitalize on Justin Jefferson's Absence
full_text:
On Friday, the Minnesota Vikings announced that superstar wide receiver Justin Jefferson will sit out Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins while he recovers from an ankle injury sustained against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 3.
In his absence, other pass catchers will need to step up. Jordan Addison rose to the occasion last week to help the Vikings remain undefeated this season, but he will need help in Week 4 from someone like Jauan Jennings to keep the streak alive.
So far this season, Jennings has been a massive disappointment. He signed a one-year deal worth eight million dollars to play for Minnesota but has not offered much in terms of a return on investment in three weeks.
Jennings missed the Vikings' game in Week 2 for personal reasons, but played 78 snaps for Minnesota in the other two games. He turned those opportunities into one catch on three targets for one yard. One of those targets was an interception, which led to a passer rating of 2.8 when throwing the ball his way this season.
The potential is there for Jennings to be a major weapon for the Purple and Gold. Last year with the San Francisco 49ers, He led all wide receivers on his team in targets (90), receptions (55), and receiving yards (643), while leading the team in receiving touchdowns (9) and tying for most receptions of 20 yards or more (9).
With Jefferson out of the lineup, Addison will slide into the WR1 role with Jennings acting as the WR2. The 29-year-old receiver will have an opportunity to play more offensive snaps on Sunday, and he needs to turn that workload into a contribution for the offense.
Jennings is trending dangerously close to being a free-agent signing bust. He still has time to turn his season around, but there may not be a better opportunity for him to get back on track than against the 0-3 Dolphins this weekend.
The bad news for Minnesota is that if Jennings can't provide value on offense, the Vikings' WR4 hasn't been able to do anything offensively. Benching Jennings for Tai Felton wouldn't make sense since Felton hasn't caught a pass all season after being targeted twice on 35 offensive snaps.
The Vikings need to find a wide receiver to take pressure off Addison on Sunday. If that doesn't happen, it might be time to consider Jennings a lost cause.

title: Kyler Murray Needs to Be Vikings' X-Factor vs. the Dolphins
full_text:
Only the Minnesota Vikings could be 3-0 under an offensive head coach with zero offense. This team continues to find new and unusual ways to keep us on the edge of our seats. By all measures, Sunday’s matchup against the Dolphins should be a clear-cut opportunity to reach 4-0 to start the season.
Back at home, against a winless opponent, with an extra-motivated Brian Flores. Miami may be in for quite the weekend. That is, of course, as long as the Vikings offense, namely quarterback Kyler Murray, doesn’t derail the game.
Murray’s start to the season hasn't been ideal by any measure, but Sunday will be a big chance to find a flow after playing a full game of football last week for the first time in a year. General manager and coach Kevin O’Connell will be watching closely, as Murray’s performance could shift their plans both this season and in the long term.
Murray needs to put together a strong showing on Sunday to find his rhythm and prove to his teammates that he can be the guy. The stage is his alone after the team traded his training-camp competition, J.J. McCarthy, to the Giants this week. Now Murray must prove the team is right to keep endorsing him. The good news is that Miami may just be the perfect opponent for Murray to thrive against.
The Dolphins have totaled zero sacks so far this season, showing a complete inability to hit home on opposing QBs. Murray, who’s still working through the timing of Minnesota’s offense, could benefit greatly from less pressure or urgency to take off running before plays fully develop. The impatience and jittery feet we saw against the Buccaneers should settle into better fundamentals and pocket presence.
Even with Justin Jefferson officially ruled out with an ankle injury, Murray should have plenty of opportunity to find his weapons downfield. Based on how things have started for the former Sooner star, he desperately needs a strong performance if he wants to be in Minnesota’s long-term plans. (h/t: VikingzFanPage)
#Vikings QB Kyler Murray on the offensive struggles today: “I mean, it's only Week 3. That’s my first game realistically. And (Jefferson) went down. I think we're going to get better each week. Obviously, we didn't feel like we played our best game today.” pic.twitter.com/tkAo8e8CX1
It’s impossible to make definitive claims about Murray’s performance or fit with the Vikings this season due to the lack of available data and reps.
Last Sunday’s game in Tampa was Murray’s first full game of football since Sept. 25, 2025 (Murray played 96% of snaps the following week per Pro Football Focus ), It makes sense that his Week 1 concussion and the loss of star wideout Justin Jefferson would slow down his acclimation to O’Connell’s notoriously tricky offense. But Murray is running out of time to prove to fans and the front office that he can steer the ship.
While Murray’s performance in Tampa was obviously rough to watch, the advanced data makes it clear just how bad it truly was. His single-game passing success rate of 15.6% was the worst of any QB in O’Connell’s 73 games leading the Vikings (h/t: Ian Hartitz). Murray, who is on a one-year league minimum deal, needs to get his game on track quickly if he hopes to earn a lucrative contract from the Vikings or any other team, for that matter.
Kevin O'Connell has coached 73 games since taking over as Vikings head coach in 2022. Nobody has posted a worse single-game passing success rate than Kyler Murray in Week 3 (15.6%).
The discourse around Kyler Murray, both in Minnesota and during his time in Arizona, suggests many NFL observers simply don't see him as a QB with high-end potential. I’d argue that we are talking about a former Heisman-winning, number-one overall draft pick who had the opportunity to go pro in two sports, not an undrafted project. There is something there; we just don't know if O'Connell's offense is the stage to show it.
He may not have proven to be a fit with the Vikings and O’Connell yet, but he is certainly a talented player capable of making an impact. With all eyes squarely on him, he’ll need to deliver to change the narrative this Sunday. He may be costing himself the trust of the team, and a large chunk of money, if he does not.

title: Confidence Meter: How I Feel About the Vikings Heading Into Week 4
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings host the Miami Dolphins in Week 4, and many fans are expecting the game to be a lopsided affair in favor of the Purple and Gold. However, this game won't be an easy win for head coach Kevin O'Connell and crew.
Minnesota may be 3-0 with two division wins this season, but the Vikings have some serious issues that could have a major impact on the outcome of Sunday's game. Last week, the team needed a punt return touchdown to put away the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and this week might require another big play to move to 4-0.
Let's take a look at each phase of the Vikings' game and evaluate the positives and negatives of each heading into Week 4.
The scariest part of the Vikings' season so far is their offense. Struggling quarterback play and struggling receivers have led to the team being last in offensive yards per game (238.3) and passing yards per game (137),
To make matters worse, superstar wide receiver Justin Jefferson will sit out Sunday's game to recover from an ankle injury that he sustained last week, forcing Jordan Addison, Jauan Jennings, or Tai Felton to step up in Week 4 .
The running back situation isn't any better. Jordan Mason is on injured reserve after thumb surgery, and backups Demond Claiborne and DeeJay Dallas have not made an impact in his absence.
The run game has fallen on the shoulders of veteran rusher Aaron Jones, who played through a knee injury and required rest in practice earlier this week. He played 47 offensive snaps last week compared to 12 for Claiborne and Dallas. Minnesota can't continue working Jones like that.
Tight end is not great either. Starter T.J. Hockenson is good to go, but Josh Oliver is now on IR with a torn bicep, which will require Gavin Bartholomew or Hockenson to play a lot more blocking snaps than usual this weekend.
The good news is that the offensive line has been okay. There are no major injuries within the unit, but neither any of the linemen nor fullback Max Bredeson has a Pro Football Focus grade over 70. They will need to be at their best to help quarterback Kyler Murray and Minnesota's other skill players.
The Vikings' aggressive defense under coordinator Brian Flores has made throwing the ball miserable for opposing quarterbacks this season. The impressive part is that Minnesota is holding opponents to the fourth-fewest rushing yards per game (85.7) while allowing the second-fewest points scored against them (41).
Rookie cornerback Charles Demmings will miss this game, which would push Zemaiah Vaughn onto the active roster. Otherwise, the Vikings should be at full strength on defense against Miami, and they should be able to control the pace of the game if they can limit explosive plays.
Will Reichard is one of the best kickers in the league, and he should continue to look great at home against Miami. Myles Price has looked great as a return man and brought a punt to the house last week.
Punter Brett Thorson will miss this game with an ankle injury, but the Vikings will elevate veteran Johnny Hekker from the practice squad. With that move, there shouldn't be a drop-off in production at that position.
On paper, the Vikings should win this game. However, the offense will need to put points on the board, or at least get into field-goal range.
It is hard to be confident in this team moving the ball on offense, since they have punted 14 times and converted only five of their 28 third-down attempts in the last two games

title: Vikings Week 4: 3 Most Important Things to Watch for as Dolphins Come to Town (Brian Flores's Revenge Edition)
full_text:
The Vikings finally return home on Sunday for their first game at U.S. Bank Stadium since Week 1. They’ll welcome a winless Dolphins team struggling to find its footing. Minnesota is balancing a multiplicity of truths: they're undefeated, with an elite defense, but they also have one of the NFL's least productive offenses .
Sunday offers a chance to finally put together a strong performance across all three phases.
The Vikings are a talented team playing winning football, but can they finally silence the criticism that's followed them to this point by decisively handling an inferior opponent? Here are three things to watch as the Purple and Gold fight for a 4-0 start.
As if the Vikings’ defensive coordinator needed more motivation to torture an opposing offense, this game may just unlock a new level of chaos from Brian Flores . There is certainly no love lost between Flores and the Dolphins organization after his tenure as their head coach ended in 2022. The reasons behind the firing and the allegations surrounding his time there are major factors in Flores’s ongoing lawsuit against the NFL.
Sunday will be the first time Brian Flores calls a defense against the franchise that fired him as their head coach. Miami’s offense is in for a long afternoon. pic.twitter.com/jbkxdZVM4L
The Vikings' defense is already attacking opposing offenses at an astounding rate.
Their league-leading 71% blitz rate through three weeks is 25% higher than the second-place Bucs at 46% (h/t: Doug Clawson of CBS Sports ). Minnesota also leads the league with 14 sacks, while Miami has not sacked an opposing quarterback so far this season.
Let's just say, Flores will look to widen that gap even further. Miami losing its best offensive player for the season—star running back De'Von Achane—certainly doesn't help its chances against Flores's stacked defense.
So far, the Vikings offense has been wildly concerning. They currently average a league-low 238.3 yards per game through three games, and while there are plenty of explanations so far, they simply have to start producing. The Vikings offense will need to take advantage of a Dolphins defense that has proven to be incapable of generating pressure on opposing QBs.
The Vikings will be without their best offensive weapon , as Justin Jefferson missed practice this week with an ankle injury, but there should still be plenty of opportunity . Jauan Jennings in particular will need to step up. In two games of action so far, he’s totaled one catch for one yard on three targets.
That simply won’t cut it if he’s asked to be WR2 on Sunday, regardless of how great he is at blocking.
While the Vikings offense has largely struggled, two special teams players have emerged as some of the most reliable scoring options on the roster. Kicker Will Reichard and WR/returner Myles Price have proven to be incredibly valuable so far in the Vikings’ 3-0 start.
Price has had a week of recognition, earning NFC Special Teams Player of the Week on Wednesday and NFC Special Teams Player of the Month on Thursday after his massive 86-yard punt-return TD in Tampa (h/t: Vikings). This follows teammate Isaiah Rodgers winning the NFC’s weekly honor for his blocked field goal in Chicago after Week 2.
Strong start to the season 💪 @Myles_price3 has been named NFC Special Teams Player of the Month! 📰: https://t.co/qtgyCmZl3e pic.twitter.com/OwPqFA4ooX
Reichard, meanwhile, has been automatic this season. He’s currently 6-for-6 on extra point attempts and  7-for-7 on field goals, including 2-for-2 on kicks of 50 yards or more.
If the Vikings' offense continues to struggle again on Sunday, the special teams unit may need to step back up to generate points.

title: Chargers Emerging as Ideal Trade Partner to Help Vikings Solve RB Depth Concerns
full_text:
Not a whole lot of people had the Vikings entering October undefeated on their 2026 Bingo card, but here we are. Head coach Kevin O'Connell and his staff are sitting at 3-0 as they enter Sunday's clash with the Dolphins, but even though their record is flawless, it's safe to say the Purple and Gold can still improve certain roster areas , especially the backfield.
Aaron Jones Sr. is still a solid starting running back, with 203 rushing yards and a touchdown on 62 carries this season, but the situation behind him isn't ideal. Top backup RB Jordan Mason is still on the injured reserve and has to miss at least two more games before he returns, leaving Demond Claiborne and DeeJay Dallas—who've combined for 11 rushing yards on six carries—as the next men up.
Claiborne and Dallas aren't showing signs of turning things around, and recent practice-squad additions Audric Estime and Devin Neal aren't guaranteed to move the needle, either. If no one emerges as a viable No. 2 option behind Jones, the Vikings could be interested in bringing in another set of legs before the Nov. 10 trade deadline, especially should Mason suffer any setback.
If that's the case, the Chargers could be one potential trade partner option to help the Vikings put their backfield concerns in the rearview.
Heading into Week 4, the Chargers are 0-3, ranking dead last in the AFC West behind two 3-0 teams (Chiefs, Raiders) and the 2-1 Broncos. Unless something drastic happens, Los Angeles is on track to miss the playoffs ( 90% chance of missing , per NFL) and could wind up as sellers before next month's deadline.
Of course, the Chargers won't be looking to move either of their top runners—Omarion Hampton or Keaton Mitchell—but they might be willing to make Kimani Vidal available to RB-needy teams like the Vikings.
Drafted 181st overall by the Chargers in 2024, has fallen out of favor ever since Mike McDaniel took over as offensive coordinator this offseason. The 25-year-old RB has only seen one carry for six yards while being limited to 28 offensive snaps. Meanwhile, Vidal has already played 19 special teams snaps compared to 37 combined in the previous two seasons, further illustrating just how Los Angeles views him.
If the status quo remains, it isn't absurd to think that the Chargers would be open to trading Vidal. His contract is up after the season, and even though he'll be a restricted free agent, that doesn't mean that Los Angeles will tender him in the offseason. Certain partnerships just run their course, and that's all a part of the NFL.
The Vikings should be all over Vidal if he becomes available.
He hasn't done much this season, but it was only last year that the Troy product averaged 4.1 yards on 155 carries in 13 games (10 starts), finishing with 643 rushing yards and three touchdowns, as well as a 16-136-1 line in the passing game. Averaging 59.9 scrimmage yards put Vidal on pace for 1,018 in 17 games, which is a respectable output for any backup RB.
Let's also not forget that the Vikings had a front-row seat to one of the best games of Vidal's career last season. He converted 23 carries into 117 rushing yards and his first-career touchdown in a 37-10 road win for the Chargers in Week 8, showing just how at home Vidal might feel at U.S. Bank Stadium.
Taking all of the above into consideration, it's easy to see why the Vikings should be interested in Vidal if he becomes available. He's young and underused, making the perfect storm for Minnesota to unlock his potential. Claiborne and Dallas have had their chances to fill in for Mason, but they aren't producing enough to stick around on a legitimate playoff contender.
Vidal could be that guy for the Vikings, though, making him a name worth tracking from now until November.

title: Patriots Don't Have Immediate Injury Update on WR Mack Hollins
full_text:
FOXBORO — The New England Patriots, already down A.J. Brown for at least one more week, suffered another hit to their wide receiver room.
Mack Hollins left Sunday's 29-26 comeback win over the Buffalo Bills with a calf injury. The veteran got banged up during one of the team's drives in the third quarter, and walked off the field. He would pace around on the sideline for a brief time before heading into the Patriots locker room with members of the medical staff.
On Monday morning, head coach Mike Vrabel was asked about Hollins' status and if where he stands health-wise as the team prepares for Week 5.
"I think we’ll probably know more here in a little bit," Vrabel said. "I don’t know if he’ll be able to practice here for a couple days, but again, I don’t have every detail.
"I’ll get in there with (head athletic trainer) Jim (Whalen) here afterwards and kind of see where we are, and then make sure we have guys that are ready to go, and everybody’s preparing as a starter, and we know the energy that Mack brings, and next guy has to be ready to go."
Hollins has stepped up to be the Patriots' top target since Week 1, and he caught three of four passes for 53 yards before leaving the game. Through four games, he has 20 targets, 15 receptions and 209 yards.
After Hollins went down, the Patriots leaned on Efton Chism III a lot more in the passing game. A close friend with Hollins, Chism grabbed two passes on the team's game-winning drive — including a one-handed, 23-yard touchdown to reclaim the lead .
Chism could be a player who gets a larger role without Hollins on the field. The Patriots could also look outside the organization for someone to fill that hole left by the 33-year-old. Currently, the Patriots have Chism, Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas and Kyle Williams on the active roster, and Cameron Dorner, Kyle Dixon an Chandler Brayboy on the practice squad.
Brown will remain on injured reserve for at least one more week as he works his way back from a high-ankle sprain suffered in the season opener.
"Sure. Anybody that can help us, we'll go explore in here shortly," Vrabel said when asked about potentially adding another receiver.
One name that's sure to draw attention? Tyreek Hill , who's reportedly been in conversations to sign with a team after a prolonged time on the open market. The former Super Bowl champion was released by the Miami Dolphins after a gruesome leg injury a season ago.
The Patriots could also kick the tires on Brian Thomas Jr. (Jacksonville Jaguars) or Marvin Harrision Jr. (Arizona Cardinals) via trade.
The Patriots are off both Monday and Tuesday, and will return to the practice field Wednesday for their home bout with the 3-1 Las Vegas Raiders.
