title: Patriots' Mike Vrabel Claps Back at Bills CB After Postgame Dig
full_text:
FOXBORO — Mike Vrabel , one day after the New England Patriots' 29-26 upset win of the Buffalo Bills , talked some smack after an opposing veteran made a comment postgame.
The Patriots walked out of Buffalo winners after Efton Chism III snared a one-handed touchdown in the final minute to give them the lead. Chism, who had just one touchdown to his name before that game, became the hero in Western New York.
It drew comments from Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson, referring to Chism as an elevated practice squad player. Chism has never played on the practice squad in his two-year career, making the 53-man roster each season out of training camp.
That led Vrabel to make some funny remarks about the Bills defensive back's own career path.
"For a guy that’s been on eight teams in four years? I mean, I guess he knows the drill," Vrabel quipped on his weekly radio hit on WEEI's The Greg Hill Show.
Gardner-Johnson, however, has bounced around from team to team since arriving in the NFL in 2019. He finished with four tackles in what turned into the Bills' first loss of the season.
"We’re not getting into no bulletin board material," Gardner-Johnson said in the locker room. "An elevated guy made a helluva catch. Probably won’t hear from him again. Respectfully. I say that with a lot of confidence, because it’s like (Drake Maye) didn’t put his confidence in his best player. He would have thrown to (Romeo) Doubs or somebody, but they won the game.
The Patriots went onto the road to beat the Bills in an offensive showing that was a complete change from the previous weeks. Maye threw for three touchdowns in their second win of the season. Chism's touchdown helped give the Patriots a one-point lead, and a successful two-point conversion bumped it to three.
"Whatever, they didn’t do (expletive) better than us. We gotta play better. They can mark that, we’ll be back to see them again. So, they better have that same energy," Gardner-Johnson continued. “They put up what? Twenty-something points? They barely scored. They struggled all game. … A practice squad player made a helluva play. You do it again, he probably won’t make it again. Simple."
Chism had two catches in the win. Earlier in the game-winning drive, the 24-year-old caught a 19-yard pass that forced hi to leap into the air. It was a big showing from the young receiver, who might be in line for more targets in the coming weeks.
"Guys continue to take advantage of their opportunities," Vrabel said Monday to reporters. "(He) certainly did a lot of things well, and I know that he'll continue to do a lot of things well for us."
Gardner-Johnson and the Bills will travel to Gillette Stadium to face this same Patriots team in Week 13.

title: 5 Winners, 2 Losers from Patriots' Upset Win Over Bills: Young WR Saves The Day
full_text:
After an ugly loss a week ago, the New England Patriots are back in the win column after a divisional upset over the Buffalo Bills. A season ago, the Patriots' win over the Bills was a chief catalyst for the team to carry momentum.
For now, it remains to be seen if this year's win will do the same.
Until then, here are the five biggest risers, and two biggest fallers, from New England's 29-26 win over Buffalo.
Cbism's role for 2026 was expected to be a minimal one. The second-year receiver was a healthy scratch in Week 1, a trend which quickly changed once A.J. Brown went down with injury.
Fast forward a few weeks and Chism has finally earned his place in the receiver room. On Sunday, he made a pair of acrobatic catches, including the go-ahead touchdown , to help New England take home the win.
"When I'm out there and you know the ball's in the air, I kind of black out," Chism said when asked abut his go-ahead grab. I'm kind of in that little flow state. I saw it in the air. Drake gave me an opportunity and I just, you know, you got to come down with with with those opportunities. You don't know how many you get. So just trying to take advantage of all of them."
Campbell has grown accustomed to seeing his name as a riser on this list. Sunday, not so much.
The second-year left tackle had his struggles on Sunday, allowing five pressures in the first half and one more in the second. The LSU product didn't have his best day against the Bills defensive line, plus was called for two penalties.
Prior to this week, Campbell's performance at left tackle has been impressive. He has been a force to be reckoned with at the tackle positon, a clear step up from last year's playoff performances.
Although Maye had a pair of turnovers , but both could be argued not to be his fault. The first, a fumble, came due to the entirety of the offensive line collapsing. The second, an interception, simply took an unlucky bounce through WR Romeo Doubs' hands.
Other than that, the young quarterback was surgical. Maye gained more than 320 yards through the air and ground, plus threw for three touchdowns.
"He just (was) extremely prepared)," head coach Mike Vrabel said. "Focused. And a good week of practice."
Heading into the day, Woodson had been awaiting the first regular season interception of his career.
He wound up grabbing what may end up being the most important video of that play. The second-year player tallied three tackles on the day in addition to his forced turnover.
The interception could not have come at a more perfect time. With a minute left on the game clock, Bills quarterback Josh Allen tried to play hero-ball. With his intended receiver blanketed in double coverage, it does not work. Woodson got the easy interception to take home the win.
Although Wishnowsky has performed acceptable in lieu of Bryce Baringer, who is aiding an injury, today was a signifcant step in the wrong direction. The 34-year-old punted four times on Sunday for a season-low average of just 38 yards.
Wishnowsky also added multiple touchbacks to his catalogue, struggling to flip the field against a high-powered Bills offense.
As per usual, Ponder makes the winners-losers list as a riser. He finished the day with a sack and a trio of tackles. The 2025 undrafted free agent has also marked a half-sack in each of the Patriots' past three matchups.
The most important part about Sunday for Ponder? He was able to do so in a near-healthy Patriots edge rusher room. Even with starter Dre'Mont Jones back in the lineup after missing a game-plus due to a shoulder injury, Ponder still stepped up to the plate.
Although Maye was marked for an interception on a drop by Doubs , the turnover was simply a stroke of misfortunate for the pass-catcher. Other than that, the former Green Bay Packer played near-perfect football on Sunday.
Doubs tallied six receptions on his nine targets, racking up 58 yards and his first two touchdowns of the year. WIth Brown still out for at least the next week, New England will certainly continue to need to lean on its receiver.

title: Patriots Secondary Overjoyed after Sealing Bills Win with Interception
full_text:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. — The New England Patriots locker room, fresh off a thrilling 29-26 win over the division rival Buffalo Bills , was elated. Everyone seemed to be in a good mood after the team's second win of the season.
But there might not have been a happier bunch of players than the secondary — a group that battled injuries before and during the game before a Craig Woodson interception ended the game in the final seconds.
"God empowered me for moments like this," Woodson told reporters after the game. "Moments to make plays like this. To have the opportunity to go out there and put the skillset he gave me on display, and go out there and give him the glory. That's all I thought about.
"Once the play happened, the ball went in the air. It was like it was slow motion, honestly."
His interception — coming just a few plays after the Patriots reclaimed the lead with a 23-yard touchdown from Efton Chism III — quieted the Highmark Stadium crowd. It was Woodson's first interception since his one against the Houston Texans in last season's AFC Divisional game.
This one, though, handed Josh Allen and the Bills their first loss of the season. That made it a little bit more special.
"We needed this win," cornerback Carlton Davis told Patriots On SI. "We needed this win for the division, so the urgency. It was an urgency win. ... That s--- was f------ huge, bro.
"We needed players to step up. Like having lost our best corner, having lost C-Woods ... It's that next man up mentality."
This was not a secondary that was at his best. Dell Pettus was placed on IR a week ago after suffering an ankle injury. Christian Gonzalez missed the game with a shoulder issue . Charles Woods left the game in the fourth quarter after suffering what he called a "stinger" in his shoulder.
And yet, this unit battled against an offense that has been at the top of its game all year.
"That's a team win," Woods told Patriots On SI. "That's what you call a team win right there. Just guys playing complimentary football, special teams, o(ffense), defense. Beautiful."
Some things will need to get cleaned up from this unit. The Bills grabbed the lead in the fourth quarter after Allen connected with Keon Coleman for a 34-yard laser down the middle of the field. Khalil Shakir had a 50-yard gain, while Joshua Palmer would have had one if he hadn't dropped the ball.
But ultimately, this unit was happy to be the ones to clinch it.
"I'm very psyched," Woods said. "That's our mentality. We always preach next man up, so you know, very excited. I'm very happy for (Woodson)."
It was Woodson's first game back after missing the team's Week 3 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. He suffered a shoulder injury the week prior, and his absence clearly hurt this team. Now that he's healthy and ready to go, he hopes to build on what the Patriots put on tape in Western New York.
"Just because we were 1-2 doesn't mean anything," Woodson said. "We can win as many games as we want."

title: Mike Vrabel Explains Unusual Unsportsmanlike Conduct Penalty in Patriots Win
full_text:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. — With the Buffalo Bills driving at the end of the first half, New England Patriots cornerback Marcus Jones was called for a holding penalty. After that, Jones' head coach was also issued a penalty — but for a different reason.
Vrabel , sharing with reporters after the Patriots' come-from-behind 29-26 win over the Bills, said that he swore at a member of the officiating crew as he voiced his displeasure with the call.
"I told him it was a terrible — I'm not going to say — effing call," Vrabel said, also sharing it's something he's probably said around 87 times during his career as a head coach. "There was nothing derogatory. You'd have to ask him. I think he was a little sensitive.
"Once I get the word from upstairs that it wasn't what we felt like was a good call, which I'm going to trust Stretch (vice president of football operations and strategy John Streicher) with my life."
The penalty added 15 yards to the Bills, who eventually would go down and punch it into the end zone on a Josh Allen two-yard quarterback keeper. That touchdown would tie the game at 14-14, and the Bills would head into the locker rooms at halftime leading by a field goal after a Drake Maye interception that bounced out of the hands of wide receiver Romeo Doubs.
"I probably shouldn't have swore," Vrabel continued. "But I can tell you that in my history of being on the sidelines as a head coach, I've said that. And I apologized to him."
ESPN's Mike Reiss, who is the Patriots pool reporter , spoke with Vinovich after the game about what led to the infraction.
Q: What led to Mike Vrabel being assessed an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty?
Vinovich: "He was out of the box, came up to the official and said, "That was a (expletive) terrible call."
Q: In a situation like that, is there any warning given?
Vinovich: "I don't know how you're going to give a warning. It's not something that is going to happen twice. When you use language like that, it's pretty much a given."
The Patriots were penalized six times for 35 yards, while the Bills were penalized five times for 31 yards. Those 15 yards didn't end up costing the Patriots the win, as Drake Maye connected with Efton Chism III on a 23-yard touchdown in the final minutes to give them their second win of the season.
"And again, players responded," Vrabel said. "It was unfortunate and I have to be better in those moments."

title: Efton Chism's 'Snag of the Year' Helps Patriots Grab Important Division Win
full_text:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. —  It felt eerily similar to Kayshon Boutte's touchdown grab in last year's playoffs. Streaking down the right sideline, covered by a defender, Efton Chism III got a step on Buffalo Bills rookie cornerback Davison Igbinosun.
The result? A one-handed, game-winning, 23-yard touchdown from Chism to help the New England Patriots knock off the home Bills 29-26 . The catch — one of just two Chism had on the day — helped the Patriots get back to .500.
It was Chism's second-career touchdown . But this one had a lot more excitement around it compared to his Week 17 grab against the New York Jets a year ago.
"Just trying to make a play," he said postgame.
Chism wasn't supposed to be on the field for that play. During practice this week, he was on the sideline when that play call was being run. But after Mack Hollins left the game with a calf injury , it was Chism's opportunity to answer the call.
"Shoot, when I'm out there and the ball's in the air, I kind of black out. I'm kind of in that little flow state," said Chism, who got a game ball after the game. "I saw it in the air and Drake (Maye) gave me an opportunity and you got to come down with those opportunities."
Chism also had a 19-yard catch where he was flipped into the air with three minutes remaining. That helped set the table for the 24-year-old's highlight reel catch.
The Patriots had an offensive showing that looked a lot more productive than the three previous weeks. They put up a season-high in points on the previously-undefeated Bills, Maye threw three touchdowns and they had guys, like Chism and right guard Ben Brown, step up.
Sunday was just another day of Chism's coaches and teammates seeing all his hard work pay off.
"Nobody works harder," Mike Vrabel said. "There are plenty of guys who work hard, but I mean, Chiz is literally in (wide receivers coach) Todd Downing’s office before 6 o'clock every morning, if not 5:30, getting the game plan down to know every position. He’s an extremely hard worker.
His toughness, his routine, it’s really cool to see guys like that take advantage of their opportunities and obviously stepping up in a critical situation is what this league is about."
"You guys see it every year for two years now in training camp," Maye said. "He just keeps on doing the right thing. He stays after every day in practice. 'Hey Drake, you need anything? Hey, I'm here.' There's guys, late in the building that I see late at night. It's Chiz. He loves this game, and you get what you put into it. I think you saw that with Chiz."
Romeo Doubs, who had two touchdowns of his own, put it pretty plainly.
"That was a snag," he said. "Snag of the year, man."
But for Chism, he's just happy that he was able to impact the game in a positive way.
"I'm just blessed," Chism said. "I'm just so happy to have all the hard work that we put in as a team and as a group, and for things to go as well as they did."

title: 7 Takeaways From Patriots' Gutsy Come-From-Behind Win over Bills
full_text:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. — It's like last season's lightning struck again.
With the New England Patriots heading in a tough environment against the undefeated Buffalo Bills , they got several big plays to put out a thrilling victory. Nearly one year later, it happened again, as this year's iteration scored four times to the tune of a 29-26 upset win.
It wasn't pretty by any stretch of the imagination. But a win is a win, and the Patriots are back at .500 after what was a sloppy first month of the season . After a 34-yard touchdown from Josh Allen to Keon Coleman gave the Bills a five-point lead, an impressive one-handed snag from Efton Chism III gave the Patriots a thrilling victory.
Here's what happened, and what it means moving forward:
On the Patriots' first drive of the game, both Drake Maye and Romeo Doubs had big roles to play. The team was driving down the field, picking up four first downs. Then came a fourth-and-three deep into Buffalo territory. The Patriots decided to keep the offense on the field, and Maye hit a wide-open Doubs for 15 yards.
One play later, Maye just got the ball out of a collapsing pocket and found Doubs leaping up over Bills cornerback Maxwell Hairston for the touchdown. It was Doubs' first as a Patriot, and it wouldn't end there.
On the Patriots' first drive of the second half, Doubs caught three passes — including one on fourth down — and capped off the series with a two-yard touchdown on a fade route. He ended the day with six receptions for 58 yards and those two scores, and started to put together some productive plays after a relatively quiet start to the season.
After a couple weeks of getting gashed on the ground, the Patriots were able to settle in and control the line of scrimmage. But that didn't last forever.
Bills running back James Cook ran his way to 75 total yards (with one touchdown). Josh Allen also added a two-yard sneak in the closing moments of the first half to tie the game at 14, but wasn't much of a factor using his legs in the second half.
The Bills finished with 87 rushing yards, and Cook sprinted his way to three carries of more than 10 yards in the second half. His speed, dormant in the first half, was a big reason why Buffalo had the lead so late.
It's plagued the Patriots for the first three games of the season, and it didn't get any better this week. Maye — c oming into the game with an NFL-leading seven turnovers — made another poor play. With the offensive line getting pushed back, Maye tried to cock his arm and throw his way out of pressure.
That idea didn't work. There were too many Bills defenders in the area, and Maye's arm hit the back of left tackle Will Campbell. The ball falls to the ground (the strip sack was credited to T.J. Parker) and the Bills took over.
It was Maye's second lost fumble in as many weeks, and he almost lost another on the next drive (it was overturned after a review showed it was an incomplete pass instead of what would have turned into a Bills scoop-and-score).
But with 16 seconds left and the ball, another turnover came back to bite the Patriots. Maye tried to hit Doubs on a slant, and a low throw forces the receiver to head towards the ground. As Doubs tried to secure it, the ball pops out of his hands and into the waiting arms of Dee Alford. Maye's seventh pick of the season. When it rains, it pours.
With the Bills down 21-20 with 6:36 left in the fourth quarter, they started to gain some momentum. Cook rushes for 16 yards up the gut and then Allen did MVP things. A 34-yard touchdown strike to Coleman deep across the middle sent Highmark Stadium into a frenzy.
They wouldn't be able to convert on a two-point try (Allen tried to find Joshua Palmer), so the lead would remain at 26-21 when the Patriots took over. On their ensuing drive, the Patriots had a big drive of their own.
The result? A gorgeous ball from Maye to Efton Chism III — who snagged it one-handed to score his second-career touchdown. Tack on a two-point conversation, and the Patriots reclaimed the lead once more.
The Bills could have had a shot to win the game, but under duress, Allen heaves up a prayer that Patriots safety Craig Woodson came down with. It was Woodson's second career pick, and first in a regular season game. It couldn't have come at a bigger time.
The second-year offensve tackle has been really good to begin this 2026 season. Sunday was not his best performance.
Campbell allowed five pressures in the first half and had a costly holding penalty to negate a Maye rushing first down. The Bills defensive front had a productive game, limiting New England's running backs to just 3.2 yards per carry.
Personally, it was a great day for the Patriots running back. He entered the game with 3,785 rushing yards, and after a six-yard run in the first quarter, Stevenson moved past Hall of Famer Curtis Martin (3,799) for fourth-most in franchise history. He ended the afternoon with 47 yards, boosting his career total to 3,832.
He also moved up on the Patriots all-time scoring leaderboards, as his one-yard score (and 29th in his carer) in the second quarter tied BenJarvus Green-Ellis for eighth-most in franchise history.
With a long injury report heading into this game, and two big names already out with shoulder injuries ( Barmore, Christian Gonzalez ), the Patriots couldn't afford more bad luck in the health department. In the first quarter, fullback Reggie Gilliam headed to the locker room and was later listed as questionable to return with an ankle injury. He had come into the game carrying a questionable designation for a knee injury.
Gilliam would return to the game and help lead block for Rhamondre Stevenson on the team's second score.
Later in the game, Mack Hollins would leave the game with a calf injury. He wouldn't return after being listed as questionable. Charles Woods (shoulder) and Eli Raridon (ankle) would also get banged up in the fourth quarter.

title: Patriots Week 4 Inactives vs. Bills: Several Key Names Won't Be Playing
full_text:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. — The New England Patriots are back on the game field, and they have a massive opportunity to wash away last week's brutal 35-6 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. They're set to do battle against the 3-0 Buffalo Bills, who've gotten out to the best start out of any team in the AFC.
But the Patriots won't be at full strength. Quarterback Drake Maye — who was on the injury report with a right shoulder ailment — will remain on the field, but several other big names (primarily on the defensive side of the ball) won't suit up.
Here's all the players on both the Patriots and Bills that won't be dressing for their Week 4 battle:
QB Behren Morton (emergency third QB)
OG Ar'maj Reed-Adams (elbow)
DT Christian Barmore (shoulder)
CB Christian Gonzalez (shoulder)
CB Channing Canada (hamstring)
CB Christian Benford (toe)
The biggest losses are Gonzalez and Barmore, who missed all three of the Patriots practices this week . Gonzalez was spotted in the locker room on Wednesday, but his weekly media availability was canceled as reporters waited for him to speak. He would later chat with Mike Vrabel at his locker.
Barmore's absence will mean a larger workload for Cory Durden and DaQuan Jones. It also means that Leonard Taylor III — who was inactive the last two weeks — will return to the field for game action.
Morton has yet to see the field this season, and will only get snaps if both Maye and backup Tommy DeVito leave with injuries.
Against the Steelers, the Patriots lost several players to injuries (Dre'Mont Jones, Mike Onwenu, Craig Woodson, Eli Raridon, Dell Pettus). All of those players didn't end up playing the next week, and both Onwenu and Pettus were placed on injured reserve.
Now, after a good week of practice, Raridon (thigh), Jones (shoulder) and Woodson (shoulder) are all active. All of them came into the game with questionable designations, but didn't miss a practice this week. Additionally, fullback Reggie Gilliam, offensive tackle Morgan Moses and linebacker Christian Elliss will all play after being listed as questionable.
Jones was a big loss last week when the team traveled to Jacksonville, as his power off the edge was missed. He didn't give a 100% answer when asked if he would play on Thursday, but was happy how he progressed in his recovery.
"I'm feeling great," Jones said in front of his locker. "Feeling better and better every single day. Our training staff gas done a great job of rehabbing me, making sure I'm good."
Woodson's return might cut into the playing time of Jaylen Reed, who stepped up last week in his place. With Raridon's return to the field, he could also add another element to a passing attack that has struggled to open the year. The rookie tight end remains the only player to catch a touchdown pass this season.
Without Gonzalez and Canada, the Patriots will have to rely a lot more on Woods — who's filled into his role as the team's top cornerback backup. He stepped up into a larger spot after Carlton Davis missed Week 2 with a neck injury. He's up to the task, according to Davis.
"(He's) just more mature, understanding how to be a better professional," Davis said on Friday. "He's coming in the facility earlier. He's put more time into his craft and showing up."
The Patriots also have Karon Prunty and Kindle Vildor ( elevated from the practice squad ) on the game day roster. They'll be tasked with stopping a passing offense that features D.J. Moore, Keon Coleman, Joshua Palmer and Khalil Shakir.
The Patriots and Bills will officially kick off at 1 p.m. EST from the new Highmark Stadium , the first time the Patriots will place in the newly-built stadium. The $2.1 billion stadium originally broke ground in 2023 and officially opened its doors in Week 2 for the Bills home opener. The Patriots had plenty of success in the last Ralph Wilson/Highmark Stadium, going 32-20 all time — and they were the only team to play there at least 10 times to finish with a winning record.

title: 4 Storylines For Patriots' Matchup With Bills: Drake Maye, Josh Allen Take Center Stage
full_text:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. — The New England Patriots and Buffalo Bills. Two of the AFC's top teams. Two of the league's top quarterbacks.
It should be a fun Week 4 matchup from the brand spanking new Highmark Stadium.
The Patriots haven't gotten out to the best start to the season . There's a real shot — just like a season ago — to turn their year around in Western New York.
"I think you have to be willing to go through some difficult times," Mike Vrabel said this week . "Again, you put everything you have into each week, whether you're on the road or you're at home. If you lose, you have to quickly try to get back to neutral and then figure out who you have available the next week."
Here are four things I'll be watching when the ball is kicked off at 1 p.m.
There’s a real shot that Drake Maye totally breaks out this week. After all, he showed it all last season.
But at the end of the day, I said that going into the Pittsburgh game and the Jaguars game. Until I see it happen with my own eyes, it’s hard to imagine a pure 180 out of the Patriots quarterback against a stout Bills defense.
Something will need to happen from Maye if the Patriots want to win. He’s gone three-straight games with more turnovers than touchdowns to open the season, and something looks off when it comes to decision-making. A turnaround outing against the undefeated Bills could be just what the doctor ordered.
Josh Allen and James Cook combine for one of the NFL’s most lethal rushing pairs. Whether it’s the running backs quickness or the quarterback’s brute strength with the ball in his hands, they are a tough duo to get down.
The Patriots have a great run defense to help minimize damage , or at least they did before Christian Barmore was ruled out with a shoulder injury. A defensive unit that didn’t really plug many gaps against the Jaguars could be in for a real tricky day.
Milton Williams — who’s without a major play three games in — could be called on a lot more as a pass rusher, opening the door for Cory Durden and DaQuan Jones to try and stop the barrage of rushing yards.
Barmore is a big loss, as is superstar cornerback Christian Gonzalez — who’s dealing with a shoulder injury himself. Two of the Patriots’ best are sidelined for a game that they really can’t afford to miss.
They’re also down rookie corner Channing Canada, who had a hamstring injury. They elevated cornerback Kindle Vildor and safety Mike Brown from the practice squad to give them some additional depth in the secondary.
Not an ideal situation for the Patriots, who are going up against arguably the league’s top offensive unit.
The Bills are 3-0. The Patriots are 1-2. If New England loses and drops the first head-to-head game, that could put a dent in their chances for the division.
Now of course, it’s a long season. Plus the Patriots have favorable matchups against the Las Vegas Raiders and Miami Dolphins, both at home. And yet, seeing the Bills race out in front for the AFC East lead could be a little disheartening.
This game could be a precursor for how the standings shake out, as well as a team’s hopes for the wild card.

title: 5 Patriots to Watch in Divisional Clash vs. Bills
full_text:
The beginning of the 2026 season hasn't fared too well for the New England Patriots . Last season's AFC champions have just one win under their belts, alongside a pair of particularly ugly losses.
An AFC East battle against the Buffalo Bills could be the perfect antidote ... or a recipe for disaster. With that, here are the five most important Patriots to watch when the team takes on the Bills at 1 this afternoon
Through three games this season, Maye has been far from the best quarterback in the NFL. In fact, he may be the worst. The 23-year-old has tossed a league-high six interceptions and only one touchdown. His 585 passing yards also ranks just 25th.
"I think it's disappointing," Maye said last Sunday when asked about his performance against the Jacksonville Jaguars . "You know, I think the ball starts rolling like that, we can't get out of our own way, can't get out of my own way personally. So I gotta look myself in the mirror and take this as a turning point."
Before Williams missed the Patriots' latter matchup with the Bills last season due to injury, he played a significant role in the team's 23-20 win over Buffalo earlier in the year. The 27-year-old recorded a half sack and four tackles en route to the victory.
Now, on Sunday, New England may need an even better performance from Williams to have any chance at winning. The defensive tackle is yet to record a sack this season and will need to step up big with co-star Christian Barmore ruled out due to a shoulder injury.
As the Patriots continue to struggle with injuries, Woods is likely to have an increased workload on Sunday, as superstar cornerback Christian Gonzalez has been ruled out with a shoulder injury . Woods stepped into a similar role against the Pittsburgh Steelers two weeks ago with Carlton Davis III out. In that battle, he tallied eight tackles and deflected a pass.
"I mean, I think Charles will get some snaps in there," head coach Mike Vrabel said Friday. "I think we'll mix around some guys. Marcus (Jones) will play outside, inside a little bit. I think Karon's (Prunty) done a really nice job on special teams and so if he's asked to play on defense, he'll be ready to go.
No surprise here. Yet another Patriot who will need to step up due to an injury at the position. Heading into the season, Brown was New England's fourth-string right guard. After injuries to starter Mike Onwenu and backup Greg Van Roten, plus poor play by third-stringer Walter Rouse, Brown is expected to start on Sunday .
"I would probably anticipate Ben Brown starting out there," Vrabel said Friday. "I think Walter (Rouse) will have to be ready to go. I think that we will see where we are with Matt Pryor coming over from Arizona, whether we feel like he could potentially help us at the game or be available for the game."
Last season, the Patriots' first matchup against the Bills was the tide-turner for Borregales. After having missed a field goal and a pair of point-after attempts through the first few weeks of the year, the then-rookie connected on his trio of kicks and duo of PATs in Buffalo. The final of the day may have been the best of his young career thus far , a 52-yarder to win the game.
Borregales has now missed a kick in each of the past two weeks, including an ugly 38-yard attempt. Can this year's matchup against the Bills have a similar effect as last season's did?

title: Saints vs. Falcons: 3 Keys to Victory for New Orleans on Monday Night
full_text:
Sign up for the daily Saints Newsletter by clicking here .
As NFC South action kicks off on Monday Night Football, the spotlight turns to the Crescent City for one of the NFL's most heated rivalries.
At the Caesars Superdome, the New Orleans Saints welcome the Atlanta Falcons . Both teams hold 1-2 records, making this divisional showdown a key chance to get back to .500 and seize early momentum in the division.
The Saints are eager to recover from a disappointing 35-27 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders , a game in which four consecutive second-half giveaways squandered a double-digit lead. The Falcons, meanwhile, arrive in New Orleans buoyed by a convincing 35-14 victory over the Green Bay Packers .
Monday's contest represents the Saints' initial Monday Night Football home game since hosting the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2022. It also marks their first night game overall since an Oct. 17, 2024, clash against the Denver Broncos —a pair of games that both ended in New Orleans losses.
If the Saints want bragging rights and to stay on the right path, here are three keys to victory against the Dirty Birds.
While Atlanta boasts the league's top-ranked run defense—yielding only 47.7 yards per game without allowing a single rushing touchdown—their secondary has proven to be a major vulnerability.
With the Falcons surrendering 263 passing yards per game (29th in the NFL), New Orleans has a strong tactical edge. The Saints enter averaging 281.3 yards through the air, ranking third overall.
This presents a clear opening for quarterback Tyler Shough . Instead of stubbornly challenging Atlanta's stout front line, New Orleans should capitalize on Shough, Chris Olave , and the aerial attack to generate downfield shots against a struggling Atlanta secondary.
And with Travis Etienne Jr . out for the foreseeable future, the Saints’ rushing attack will take a hit, so they might just need to throw the rock around.
Atlanta running back Bijan Robinson enters the NFC South matchup as one of the NFL's most productive offensive players. Through three games, the Falcons running back has rushed for 349 yards and two touchdowns on 66 carries, averaging 5.3 yards per attempt. Add his 13 receptions for 118 yards and a touchdown, and Robinson leads the NFL with 467 yards from scrimmage.
The Saints also will be dealing with a player coming off his best performance of the season. Robinson shredded Green Bay for 194 yards and two touchdowns on 29 carries, including a 55-yard run, while adding two catches for 19 yards. Atlanta finished with 242 rushing yards and controlled possession for more than 37 minutes in its 35-14 victory. Robinson was subsequently named NFC Offensive Player of the Week.
This one should be straightforward after what happened against Las Vegas.
New Orleans committed four consecutive turnovers in the second half of its 35-27 loss to the Raiders, turning what had been a double-digit Saints advantage into a frustrating defeat. The Saints enter Monday with a minus-4 turnover differential, ranking near the bottom of the NFL.
Atlanta has its own turnover problems — the Falcons enter at an NFL-worst minus-6 — making possession potentially one of the biggest deciding factors Monday night.
The Saints have shown they can move the football and score. They simply cannot give Atlanta extra possessions, especially in a rivalry game that could come down to one or two critical mistakes.

title: Saints-Falcons Staff Predictions: Will New Orleans Bounce Back on Monday Night?
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints will take on the Atlanta Falcons in another clash between the two longtime rivals on Monday Night Football in New Orleans.
New Orleans (1-2) is coming off a tough 35-27 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders in a game the Saints held a double-digit lead in the third quarter. Meanwhile, the Falcons are coming off a 35-14 upset win over the Green Bay Packers on Monday Night Football.
Here are the staff predictions.
Despite the Falcons having the best run defense in the NFL, allowing just 47.7 yards per game and zero rushing touchdowns, they have been extremely vulnerable through the air.
Atlanta ranks 29th in pass defense at 263 yards allowed per game, which creates an enticing matchup for Tyler Shough and a Saints offense averaging 281.3 passing yards per game, third best in the NFL.
That might be exactly how New Orleans has to win this game, especially considering the state of its backfield. The Saints’ rushing attack hasn’t been the strongest, rushing for 101.3 yards per game, tied for 16th in the league.
On top of that, Travis Etienne Jr. was placed on injured reserve with a hamstring injury, leaving Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller to carry the load against the NFL's best run defense. Starting left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. also remains sidelined after undergoing ankle surgery, making pass protection another concern.
The bigger reason I expect a shootout, however, is what's happening on the other side of the ball.
New Orleans will be without Kaden Elliss , Carl Granderson and Anfernee Jennings , while Pete Werner is questionable after missing all three practices with a shoulder injury. That leaves an already vulnerable Saints defense potentially without four significant pieces of its front seven against an Atlanta offense built around Bijan Robinson and one of the NFL's most productive rushing attacks.
Atlanta enters the game averaging 173 rushing yards per game, second in the NFL, while New Orleans ranks 27th against the run at 128.7 yards allowed per game. That's a bad matchup before even accounting for the Saints' injuries.
Moreover, Michael Penix made his first appearance in more than 10 months, and completed 18 of 25 passes for 256 yards, one touchdown and one interception in Atlanta's 35-14 victory. He averaged 10.2 yards per attempt, posted a 101.4 passer rating and wasn't sacked as the Falcons piled up 498 total yards.
So I don't expect New Orleans to shut Atlanta down. I expect the Saints to have to outscore them.
The Falcons should be able to move the football on a depleted New Orleans defense, but Atlanta's inability to consistently stop the pass gives Shough an opportunity to answer. If the Saints can protect him and avoid the turnovers that doomed them against Las Vegas, I like their chances of producing enough explosive plays through the air to survive.
Emotions were high in the Superdome last weekend when the Raiders visited New Orleans. None of it counted, as Las Vegas left the Crescent City the same way they arrived: undefeated.
Of course, the fourth quarter was the undoing for the Saints in their home opener. In Week 1, it was a slow start in Detroit that led to defeat. In Week 2, it was a win in Baltimore despite an even slower start than Week 1.
Though not the most hobbled of teams, the Saints still have 10 players on injured reserve, the latest of which is Travis Etienne Jr., plus two more on the Designated to Return IR.
The Falcons got back Michael Penix Jr. at quarterback after the debacle of QBs in the first two weeks of the season. He has never played against the Saints, after sitting behind Kirk Cousins in 2024 and tearing his ACL in 2025, missing the entire season. Running back Bijan Robinson is solid, but in the Superdome last season, Robinson ran 14 times for 70 yards and no touchdowns. He did even worse at home against the Saints, getting 15 carries for a measly 33 yards.
With that said, the question that keeps popping in my head is will the Saints learn from these mistakes they've made this season?
They learned from their slow starts in Games 1 and 2, turning that around against Las Vegas last weekend. Will they learn from that fourth-quarter letdown? Tyler Shough says they have. By the way, he said the same thing about the slow starts in the first two weeks of the season, and sure enough, he was right.

title: 2 Saints Whose Stock Is Falling Entering Monday Night vs. Falcons
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints don't have much time to dwell on what went wrong against the Las Vegas Raiders .
Now they must shift their attention to their game against the Atlanta Falcons on Monday Night Football, who come to the Caesars Superdome for the Saints' first NFC South matchup of the season. With both teams sitting at 1-2, New Orleans has an opportunity to not only get back to .500 but claim bragging rights over its longtime divisional rivals.
But there are a few individual performances from that loss that become even more concerning when looking ahead to Atlanta.
Here are two Saints whose stock is down — and who will be under the microscope against Atlanta.
It was a difficult afternoon for Justin Reid , and the numbers backed it up.
Reid received a 28.2 overall grade from Pro Football Focus, the lowest among Saints players who logged at least 20 snaps. His biggest struggles came in coverage, where PFF gave him a 29.6 grade.
PFF charted Reid as the nearest defender on six completions for 74 yards and a touchdown, with opposing quarterbacks producing a 150.3 passer rating when targeting his coverage. That doesn't mean Reid was at fault for each completion because coverage assignments can make nearest-defender statistics imperfect, but it does show how frequently Las Vegas found success in his area.
Reid also drew an unnecessary roughness penalty in the end zone, adding another negative play to an already difficult outing.
The veteran safety was brought to New Orleans to provide stability and experience and, for the most part, has been on the back end, but Week 3 was easily one of those performances he would like to shake off.
While Chase Young continues to generate pressure from one side of the Saints' defensive front, Cameron Jordan hasn't been nearly as productive from the other.
Jordan finished with a 45.6 overall PFF grade, the second-lowest mark among Saints players who played at least 20 snaps. His 24.8 tackling grade was the lowest defensive grade in any individual category highlighted by PFF's Week 3 numbers.
The pass-rush production was also limited. Jordan rushed Kirk Cousins 21 times but generated only one pressure, according to PFF.
The contrast with Young was noticeable. Young recorded two sacks and earned an 81.1 overall grade and 87.1 pass-rush grade, while Jordan struggled to consistently affect Cousins.
At 37, the Saints aren't asking him to carry their pass rush anymore, but they still need more impact from one of the most experienced players on the defense.

title: Saints Stock Report: 3 Players Trending Up Despite Raiders Loss
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints' fourth-quarter collapse against the Las Vegas Raiders overshadowed several encouraging individual performances.
New Orleans surrendered an 11-point second-half lead in its 35-27 loss, committing four turnovers in the fourth quarter as a winnable game quickly unraveled. But while the final result was disappointing, several Saints continued to strengthen their cases as key pieces on both sides of the ball.
Here are three players whose stock is rising coming out of the loss.
Chase Young continues to look like one of the Saints' most disruptive defenders.
The veteran edge rusher recorded two sacks, giving him his third career multi-sack game and second since joining New Orleans. Young now has 3.5 sacks on the year, the most on the Saints and is tied fifth in the NFL.
That production was particularly important because the Saints weren't consistently affecting Kirk Cousins otherwise. Young supplied some of their best individual pass-rush moments and continues to make a strong case for being one of the centerpieces of this defensive front.
Young picked up a 81.1 defense grade and a 87.0 pass rush grade according to Pro Football Focus (PFF) . Young has a 79.4 overall grade (16th best among edge rushers) and a 90.3 pass rush grade, the third-best among edge rushers.
There wasn't much flashy about Chris Olave 's performance, but the production was undeniable.
Olave caught nine passes on 12 targets for 107 yards, accounting for more than 40% of Tyler Shough 's passing yardage. Olave did not drop a pass for the second consecutive game and caught three passes on the four contested targets thrown his way.
Perhaps more importantly, he provided Shough with a reliable option throughout a game in which the Saints repeatedly moved the chains, as seven of Olave’s catches resulted in a first down. Olave continues to look like the clear centerpiece of the passing game.
Noah Fant' s emergence might be one of the more interesting developments through three weeks.
He caught four passes for 33 yards and two touchdowns, including a 16-yard score immediately after New Orleans recovered a Raiders kickoff fumble.
The Saints scored only four touchdowns through tight ends during all of last season. They scored four against Las Vegas alone and already have six this year.
With Juwan Johnson also catching two touchdowns, Kellen Moore suddenly has legitimate flexibility at tight end.

title: Saints Face a Much Different Falcons Offense With Michael Penix Jr. Back
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints face a transforming Atlanta Falcons offense ahead of Monday night's game.
Atlanta struggled in its first two games, averaging just 262 yards and eight points while committing seven turnovers. However, everything shifted with Michael Penix Jr. 's return in Week 3, as the Falcons erupted for 498 yards and 35 points with only one turnover against Green Bay.
Although Atlanta enters averaging 17 points per game, that stat is misleading. The Saints' challenge is preparing for the potent Penix-led offense rather than early-season metrics.
Here is a breakdown of the Falcons’ offense.
Penix missed two games recovering from last November's torn ACL. This forced Atlanta to start veteran Cooper Rush after initial starter Tua Tagovailoa suffered a preseason oblique injury.
Under Rush, the offense struggled severely as he threw foir interceptions in Atlanta’s losses to the Pittsburgh Steelers and Carolina Panthers . During those two games, the Falcons averaged only eight points and 262 yards while failing to reach the red zone.
Penix's return against Green Bay immediately changed the complexion of the offense, and possibly was a season-changing game
Making his first appearance in more than 10 months, Penix completed 18 of 25 passes for 256 yards, one touchdown and one interception in Atlanta's 35-14 victory. He averaged 10.2 yards per attempt, posted a 101.4 passer rating and wasn't sacked as the Falcons piled up 498 total yards.
Penix also helped unlock Drake London . The Falcons' No. 1 receiver caught nine passes for a career-high 194 yards against Green Bay, giving Atlanta the explosive passing element it had been missing during the first two weeks. Through three games this season, London has 15 catches for 274 yards.
There is still an obvious caveat for the Saints: Penix has played only one game since undergoing ACL surgery.
Atlanta doesn't need Penix to carry the team alone. Supported by Bijan Robinson and a run game that posted 242 yards against Green Bay, Penix can rely on play-action and manageable situations.
Even so, his return changes how New Orleans must prepare.
Unlike the unit that scored three points against Carolina, New Orleans faces a healthy Penix leading a 498-yard offense. The Saints must now evaluate if Atlanta's breakout performance is a temporary spark or a lasting shift.
Speaking of Robinson, he will be New Orleans’ biggest threat.
Robinson enters the NFC South matchup as one of the NFL's most productive offensive players. Through three games, the Falcons running back has rushed for 349 yards and two touchdowns on 66 carries, averaging 5.3 yards per attempt. Add his 13 receptions for 118 yards and a touchdown, and Robinson leads the NFL with 467 yards from scrimmage.
The Saints also will be dealing with a player coming off his best performance of the season. Robinson shredded Green Bay for 194 yards and two touchdowns on 29 carries, including a 55-yard run, while adding two catches for 19 yards. Atlanta finished with 242 rushing yards and controlled possession for more than 37 minutes in its 35-14 victory. Robinson was subsequently named NFC Offensive Player of the Week.
The basic formula against New Orleans should be straightforward: establish Robinson, force the Saints to devote extra bodies to the run, manufacture easy throws/screens for Penix and then attack vertically or over the middle with London.
The biggest secondary concern for New Orleans is that Atlanta doesn't necessarily need Penix to throw 35-40 times. Against Green Bay, the Falcons attempted just 25 passes against 41 rushing attempts and still generated 498 yards.

title: Braxton Berrios Headed to IR With Foot Injury
full_text:
New York Giants receiver and return specialist Braxton Berrios, who suffered a foot injury late in the first half of the team’s 36-24 Week 4 win over the Arizona Cardinals, is being placed on injured reserve , according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.
Berrios, who joined the 53-man roster last week after spending the first three weeks of the season on the practice squad, served as the Giants' main return specialist on punts and kickoffs.
In four games this season, Berrios returned four punts for 10 yards, including a 7-yard return, and had five kickoff returns for 138 yards (27.6 avg.).
As a receiver, he had one pass target, which came in the game against the Cardinals (the pass attempt falling incomplete).
With Berrios out for at least the next four weeks, receiver Charlie Jones, who was signed to the 53-man roster last week after spending time on the team’s practice squad, is believed to be the next man up.
Jones replaced Berrios in the second half of Sunday’s game. He returned two punts for 29 yards (14.5 avg.) and had a fair catch. On kickoffs, he returned three for 69 yards (23.0 avg.).
The Giants have two receivers on their practice squad, Jalin Hyatt and Dalen Cambre. Of the two, Cambre has special teams experience.
The other possibility is that if defensive lineman/outside linebacker Chauncey Golston’s neck injury is something that might keep him sidelined for a while, the team could look to sign outside linebacker Trace Ford, who was elevated from the practice squad last week for the first time this season, to the 53-man roster.

title: Giants Offense Film Review: Winston's Three TDs and Nabers' 112 Yards Contribute to 36-24 Win
full_text:
The New York Giants offense didn’t look pretty, but it got the job done.
Big Blue topped the Arizona Cardinals 36-24 (the offense scoring 27 of those points). In doing so, they also bested the Cardinals in total yards (319 to 270), time of possession (32:13 to 27:47), and average yards per play (5.2 to 4.3) — all despite running two fewer plays.
Again, it wasn’t a work of art, but it was a gritty showing in which the Giants leaned more into 11-personnel this week, something they’ve gradually done ever since losing Jaxson Dart to a season-ending knee injury.
Here are this week’s player grades.
Winston has had plenty of up-and-down games since entering the league, this week included. He started very skittish in the pocket, unable to come off his initial read, holding onto the ball and contributing to two first-half sacks.
Winston looked shaky early on. Then he found himself in the second quarter with two touchdown throws: a 12-yarder to Malachi Fields on a scramble, and his best throw of the day, a 25-yard deep middle throw to Malik Nabers made with great anticipation and accuracy.
Then he finished off the first half with a classic bonehead decision, an interception with the offense approaching field goal range.
The Cardinals then used the 24 seconds Winston gave them to kick their own field goal, the Giants finishing the half with a narrow 19-17 lead.
On his first drive of the second half, Winston gifted Arizona his second interception at the Giants' 37. Arizona converted the turnover into a touchdown and a 24-19 lead.
Winston then responded with an 11-play drive, finishing with a dart to Theo Johnson in the end zone for the 27-24 lead. The Giants never relinquished the lead.
On the day, Winston went a respectable 18 of 29 for 250 yards. His three touchdown throws were big. His two interceptions hurt. Several of his sacks seemed to stem from his poor feel in the pocket.
One thing about Winston is you can never count him out. The bad plays may come, but they never seem to get him down. He kept plugging away and gave his team a chance to win.
Skattebo ran a lot of tough inside runs, per usual, plus a couple of ill-advised bounce-outs that didn't work. One drew the inevitable holding call on a Giants tight end.
Skattebo threw a couple of positive pass blocks but also missed a couple more, one of which became a sack. He's got to get better.
His best play was the third-and-2 wide toss, which was well-schemed but still required him to plant his foot, turn it upfield, and get the yards, which he did.
His production was a typical: 18 carries for 58 yards (3.2 avg.) with a long of 8 yards.
One of his better snaps was a checkdown pass for 8 yards on a third-and-7. We'd love to see him used more in the passing game, where he has the skills and instincts.
One other thing about this kid: even though he lacks speed, he sure knows where the marker is, and he sure knows how to get past it.
Harris also had lots of tough inside running, including the two-point conversion he took hard into the end zone.
Harris had only nine carries for 30 yards (3.3 avg.) on a day that he nearly ruined with a lost fumble (punched out by an Arizona defensive back) early in the fourth quarter, but fortunately the defense held.
Harris has to be more reliable than that.
Tracy got 12 snaps and only one touch, a run that had no chance of succeeding given the way he ran it. There was a cutback seam, but he totally missed it.
Tracy did very well with a stout blitz pickup, a good sign.
Giants Nation held its breath when Nabers went up for a contested 39-yard catch and came down hard on his shoulder.
He stayed down, made it to the sideline under his own power, and eventually returned to the field three plays later to catch a pass, then went on to record his best game of the young season.
Nabers caught six of seven targets for 112 yards (18.7 avg.). He ran a seam route and caught a touchdown from 25 yards out, giving the Giants a 19-14 second-quarter lead.
Nabers also made a couple of contested catches, showing off his strong hands.
After Arizona took a third-quarter lead, on the first play from scrimmage the coaches schemed Nabers open deep left for a big 28 yards. This play jump-started the offense on a touchdown drive that retook the lead.
Notably, on the failed two-point conversion to Malachi Fields, the quarterback missed Nabers on a wide-open crosser, choosing to look away from the team's best receiver. That one should get a hoot in the film room.
Continuing to bring a physical presence every time he's on the field, this big rookie also made two big catches, both on broken scramble plays, that were as important as any of Nabers' catches.
On a third-and-4 late in the second quarter, Fields did well to turn his route upfield as the quarterback broke the pocket. Fields then presented himself to his quarterback and smoothly took in the 12-yard pass for the touchdown that got the trailing Giants back in the game.
On the offense's final scoring drive of the day, Fields once again found space against the deep Arizona zone on a scramble play and hauled in the 40-yard throw.
This kid has shown very reliable hands so far on his limited targets.
His only other target of the day turned into the team's second interception when the well-covered Fields was undercut in the deep middle by the defensive back on a terrible throw.
Targeted just twice, Mooney was wide open on a deep crosser, but the ball sailed over his head. His other target was a "hospital ball," a short crosser right into the teeth of a waiting strong safety.
Mooney couldn't hold onto the ball against the immediate contact. This speedy vet remains a reliable complement to the team's WR1.
Berrios got a rare target out of the slot in the first half, but the throw was way off. Berrios left the game with a foot injury at the end of the first half and did not return.
The team's sure-handed receiving tight end caught seven of his 12 targets for 66 yards. At least three of those misses were off-target throws as Likely and his quarterback left significant yards on the field.
Another miss in Likely's direction became an interception, again on a terrible throw with Likely open. The tight end's best moment came on another scramble play, where Likely worked his way open and leaped high to haul in a difficult throw that might have become a turnover if not for his great leap and hands.
This player has the best hands on the team, bar none.
Continuing to get a majority of the run-game snaps, Manhertz has never blocked better than he has in this, his third year on the team.
Manhertz also found himself the target on the failed scramble-drill two-point try in the end zone, but he could not shake free, and the throw was easily knocked away.
Despite Manhertz eating up his snaps, Johnson still got 15 or so snaps on offense, and he really came up big when his number was called.
His 11-yard touchdown catch on a second-and-10 gave the team a third-quarter 27-24 lead that they held the rest of the way.
Not known for catching balls against contact, Johnson showed strong hands in going up for the short seam throw despite tight coverage and bringing it in for the important score.
Continuing to get his fair share of run-blocking snaps, Ricard was sharp, physical, and reliable throughout. He even got a schemed checkdown throw as his first target of the year in the passing game, but the throw was high, and he could not bring it in.
The lower-body injuries that Thomas is dealing with are affecting his run-blocking more than his pass-blocking.
Though his pass blocks have been effective (but hardly dominant), his run-blocking this week was more hit-and-miss because of clumsy, at times uncertain footwork.
He's just not sustaining contact very well while he struggles with his health.
The veteran's pass-blocking was superb, but his run-blocking was mediocre.
Dominating his edge in pass pro kept his pocket relatively clean (one lone edge pressure).

title: Four Moments That Defined the Giants' 36-24 Win Over the Cardinals
full_text:
New York Giants fans expected their team to get bigger, more physical and fundamentally sharper under Super Bowl-winning head coach John Harbaugh, but there was still some uncertainty regarding the team's ability to close out games.
The Baltimore Ravens' bad habit of blowing fourth-quarter leads was a topic of conversation entering this new era of Big Blue football.
It isn't right now, though. The Giants thwarted a comeback effort for the third time this year, trusting their defense to stymie the Arizona Cardinals and clinch a 36-24 victory on Sunday afternoon.
Although the competition has been less than fierce, New York is thriving in the clutch. This latest crunch-time triumph propelled the team into solo possession of first place in the NFC East. Given what the Giants have endured already, the franchise deserves to feel good about itself.
There is always stuff that can be improved, but this is ultimately a results-based business. Let's take a closer look at the four moments that defined this winning effort .
The Giants finally figured out how to score in the red zone, posting their first touchdown since Week 1 with 4:30 remaining in the second quarter. They fortified their momentum on the next drive, courtesy of a 35-year-old defensive tackle and a rookie 21-year-old linebacker .
Facing third-and-2 on the Cardinals' 35-yard line, Shelby Harris brought the pressure and batted a Jacoby Brissett pass. The tipped ball landed in the ready hands of Arvell Reese, who exploded in MetLife Stadium during this Week 4 matchup.
The Giants took over at the 26-yard line, and Jameis Winston connected with Malik Nabers for a 25-yard touchdown two plays later. Harris and Reese joined forces for a difference-making turnover that ultimately allowed their team to take the lead with 2:25 left in the half.
Trailing 24-19 with less than six minutes remaining in the third, Jameis Winston was staring down a third-and-20 on his team's own 42-yard line. He had thrown picks on his last two drives, which resulted in 10 Arizona points, but true to form, the veteran gunslinger unexpectedly fired a beauty into the heart of Cardinals territory.
Winston scrambled out of trouble and completed a 40-yard pass to rookie wide receiver Malachi Fields. The backup-turned-starter following Jaxson Dart's season-ending knee injury can make some head-scratching throws, but if you wait long enough, he will blow your mind with gutsy, excellent plays.
Winston did plenty of both on Sunday, but the positives edged out the negatives. His average depth of target was 11.3 , per Pro Football Focus , nearly twice as much as last week's number. This dime to Fields was a big reason for the spike, and it preceded another pivotal completion that occurred on the same drive.
Five plays after the Winston-Fields link-up, the Giants found themselves in the unfortunate position of settling for a 34-yard field goal attempt. Dominic Zvada, who remained perfect in his first NFL campaign, drilled it and brought New York within two points of the Cardinals. Or at least that's what everyone thought.
The officials called Arizona for a defensive holding penalty, granting the Giants a welcome first down. Following a Najee Harris run that went nowhere, Jameis Winston zipped an 11-yard TD pass to tight end Theo Johnson and Big Blue grabbed a 27-24 lead with 1:44 left in the third quarter.
Winston was 18-of-29 for 250 yards and three touchdowns, but perhaps just as important as his passing heroics, New York won the penalty battle.
The Giants were flagged six times for 44 yards, while their opponent accrued 55 penalty yards on seven flags.
If someone was going to emerge from the telephone booth and lift the Giants to a W, there should have been no less likely candidate than Deonte Banks.
But not in this game. The fourth-year cornerback enjoyed what fans earnestly hope is a breakout performance, putting on the cape shortly after he was issued a questionable pass interference flag on third-and-6.
With the Cardinals advancing to the 4-yard line, Banks had to quickly move past the penalty.
DOTS of the Deonte Banks game-winner pic.twitter.com/KDnI8qIWkI
And did he ever. The 2023 first-round draft pick totaled four passes defended, including a stellar one on All-Pro tight end Trey McBride with 14 seconds remaining on the game clock.
Four plays later, Banks put the game firmly in the win column when he snagged Jacoby Brissett's pass intended for Michael Wilson and raced to the opposite end zone for a 98-yard pick-six as time expired.
The road to redemption is a long one and cannot be completed with just one excellent showing, but this 25-year-old has dramatically changed his fortunes.

title: Giants-Cardinals Winners and Losers: Arvell Reese Arrives, Deonte Banks Gets Redemption
full_text:
The New York Giants were an offseason darling after hiring John Harbaugh and making intriguing roster additions. Although the campaign has already packed some brutal lows, this squad is validating the preseason optimism.
The Giants emerged from a thrilling showdown at MetLife Stadium as 36-24 victors over the Arizona Cardinals and now occupy sole possession of first place in the NFC East.
They won't win any beauty contests. Still, a 3-1 record is worth celebrating, especially for a franchise that has been extremely unsuccessful and extremely unlucky for the better part of a decade and a half.
We're going to shine the light on some of the players who thrived on Sunday , and a few who stumbled a bit. Here are Big Blue's Week 4 winners and losers.
There were some scuffles over the first two weeks, but Arvell Reese has officially arrived. The rookie linebacker left an indelible mark on this game, disrupting the Cardinals' plans throughout the afternoon and across the field.
Reese forced a Jacoby Brissett interception with overwhelming pressure, and then recorded a pick himself that led to a go-ahead touchdown late in the first half, posted nine solo tackles and totaled nine stops. Simply put, he was an all-encompassing presence.
The No. 5 overall pick flashed promise in his first two games and made a noticeable impact against the Tennessee Titans. On this day, he became an absolute game-wrecker. While it can be tricky for rookies to maintain consistency, Reese proved plenty with this performance.
The defense will once again steal the headlines, but Malik Nabers cannot fly under the radar after what he accomplished in front of the home crowd. The dynamic wide receiver posted his first truly big game since suffering a season-ending knee injury last year in a Week 4 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
Nabers recorded six receptions for 112 yards and scored his first touchdown since returning from his ACL injury . He was an igniting force for a passing offense that remains erratic with Jameis Winston under center. Those understandably worried about that duo's chemistry got a delightful surprise.
No. 1 formally reintroduced himself as a star pass-catcher who can elevate those around him. The next step is stacking show-stopping performances.
Arvell Reese arrived, Malik Nabers returned to form, and Deonte Banks had his huge comeback moment. From draft bust and potential roster cut to Week 4 hero, he's finding new life under John Harbaugh and Dennard Wilson.
The stats will not do Banks justice. Although he allowed two touchdowns and was called for a questionable pass interference penalty with 27 seconds remaining, Banks looked like a team's No. 1 cornerback. Fans should be mighty grateful that the G-Men gave him another chance.
Banks posted four pass breakups against Arizona. Directly after his last one, which came on third-and-goal against All-Pro tight end Trey McBride, he clinched the win with New York's second consecutive game-ending interception.
After missing the last two weeks with a calf injury, Banks enjoyed possibly his best outing to date. He needed this, and so did the Giants.
You will not find a sack in his stat line, but Abdul Carter was easy to notice. The second-year outside linebacker kept Brissett on his heels for much of the fourth quarter.
Eight of his nine pressures came in less than 2.5 seconds , according to Next Gen Stats, perfectly illustrating his elusiveness and relentlessness. Dennard Wilson blitzed Arizona more than 50 percent of the time, enabling Carter to do what he does best.
The sacks will come. Meanwhile, fans should still take pleasure in watching No. 3 make opposing QBs squirm.
It looked like fans' worst fears were coming true through the first three weeks of the season. Shelby Harris played fewer than 30 defensive snaps per game and performed far below his career standard. Well, the 35-year-old is not in Father Time's grasp quite yet.
Harris is responsible for one of the most important plays of the game, batting down the Brissett pass that directly led to an Arvell Reese interception and, by extension, a crucial Big Blue touchdown. His game went beyond that one impactful down, though.
The veteran defensive tackle stayed active on run defense, recording two stops, and was a key reason why New York settled down after the Cardinals began the game with back-to-back scoring drives.
There will be quiet days, but Harris' tank is obviously not empty.
Center Bryan Hudson started ahead of John Michael Schmitz, a player arguably considered the weak link on the line, and Hudson flourished.
He allowed no sacks, hurries or pressures in 67 offensive snaps , per Pro Football Focus, giving fans a glimpse of the type of play they could potentially see in the middle of the offensive line.
Undrafted out of Louisville in 2024, Hudson finally got a chance to carry a legitimate NFL workload.
The third-year running back definitely left an imprint as a kick returner.
Following a Tyler Allgeier rushing score that put the Cardinals up 14-3 in the first quarter, Tyrone Tracy Jr. immediately injected energy into the Giants' offense with a 55-yard return. New York had to settle for a field goal, but the explosive play let the team keep pace with the visitors.
Tracy has more burst than any current Big Blue ball-carrier, so it is good to know that former special teams coordinator John Harbaugh can still utilize his talents.
Although the offensive line shares in the blame for an inexcusably inefficient New York rushing attack, the running back room had a collectively brutal afternoon in East Rutherford, New Jersey.
Cam Skattebo logged 18 carries for only 58 yards and is now averaging 3.5 yards per attempt this season.
Najee Harris failed to build on a standout showing against Tennessee, logging nine carries for 30 yards and fumbling in the fourth quarter in Cardinals territory.
(Tyrone Tracy received just one touch on offense, for minus-1 yard.)
In short, the results weren't anything to write home about. With Jaxson Dart sidelined for the rest of the year, this squad must establish the run to manufacture points consistently. Greg Roman will have to adjust the game plan this week.
It feels wrong to slot the 27-year-old center here after he and his wife welcomed their first child, but it is hard to view his current standing with the team in a positive light.
Because he missed a couple of practices due to the birth of his baby, Harbaugh played Bryan Hudson instead. The Giants head coach assured the media that this development is not a long-term thing, but nobody can argue with the results. Hudson stepped up and now deserves more consideration.
Schmitz hasn't put together a strong enough body of work to guarantee himself the starting position for the rest of the season. Will he get another chance this season? That's hard to say, but as one of three active players to ride the bench this week, Schmitz has officially been put on notice.
It is hard to evaluate a rookie properly after just a couple of weeks. However, with a quarter of the campaign nearly complete, it is fair to critique Francis Mauigoa's latest performance.
The young right guard has arguably been one of the best offensive linemen in his class so far, but he struggled against Arizona . Mauigoa surrendered one sack, three hurries and five pressures, per PFF.
The former Miami mauler had a "welcome to the NFL" experience at MetLife, and he will need to learn from it moving forward.
Don't expect him to spend much time on this list, however.

title: Deonte Banks Predicted He'd End Up with INT Against Cardinals
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. – New York Giants cornerback Deonte Banks waited patiently for the Arizona Cardinals offense to play into his gridiron intuition during their Week 4 matchup at MetLife Stadium.
As he lined up on fourth-and-goal from the Giants' 4-yard line with virtually no time remaining, the fourth-year defensive back knew the defense needed a "big play" to give New York its third win of the season.
Once he recognized Arizona's offensive alignment, Banks knew he could deliver.
"They were giving me a tight end and a receiver set all day, but I was thinking slant," Banks told reporters after the game. "They hadn't given it to me all day. So that time, I just knew they were gonna give it to me."
Banks' assessment proved correct. The 25-year-old read Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett's slant pass attempt, jumped the route (intended for receiver Michael Wilson) and secured the interception. The Maryland product then returned the pick 98 yards for a touchdown, handing New York a 36-24 victory in Week 4 .
For Banks, the outcome was inevitable.
"It was just a matter of time because they kept running it; on film they kept running it," he added. "I knew I was going to take it. I've been calling it all week, like, I'm going to pick a slant this week. I played it as I thought they would run it, and I just took it."
BANKS CLOSED ON SUNDAYS 📺: CBS/Paramount+ pic.twitter.com/Adh3ijHUwo
Initially selected by the Giants in the first round (24th overall) of the 2023 NFL Draft, Banks' NFL tenure has been up and down. After an impressive rookie campaign, he struggled to live up to expectations in his second and third seasons. As a result, the Giants declined Banks' fifth-year option in the offseason, making 2026 the final year of his rookie contract.
Despite his recent struggles, Banks used a strong training camp performance to regain the starting spot at boundary corner. His perseverance, along with a newfound passion for the game, has him playing some of the best football of his career. As such, he is determined to move forward without looking back.
"I'm not worried about last year or any of that," Banks said. "I just know what I'm capable of and I want just to prove myself right … just keep proving myself right."
In the meantime, the victor is content to enjoy the spoils. Having earned his first pick-six since his days at Edgewood High School in Maryland, as well as his longest touchdown since a 95-yard kickoff-return score against the Las Vegas Raiders in December 2025, Banks will take a memento from this Week 4 field of battle.
"I have the ball," he exclaimed. "I'm going to get it customized to say 'game-winning pick' on it."

title: Jameis Winston, Giants "Found a Way" Against Cardinals as QB Chatter Swirls
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. – New York Giants quarterback Jameis Winston has seen enough during his 12 years in the NFL to know that nothing should ever be taken for granted.
Despite playing every snap at the position since incumbent starter Jaxson Dart's season-ending knee injury in Week 2, Winston's future as Big Blue's QB1 has drawn plenty of speculation. After all, he and the Giants were about to enter Week 4 having failed to score a touchdown in either of their last two games.
Moreover, the 32-year-old's job security was called into even greater question after the Giants acquired quarterback J.J. McCarthy in a trade with the Minnesota Vikings on Sept. 28.
Still, Winston remained confident that the tide could be turned with a solid performance in Week 4 against the Arizona Cardinals at MetLife Stadium. Though his showing displayed both the "bad" and the "ugly" aspects of his game, his "good" was enough to help New York win 36-24.
Winston finished 18 of 29 for 250 yards, throwing three touchdowns and two interceptions as the Giants improved to 3-1 for the first time since 2022. After the game, he was less concerned about staking his claim to the job and more focused on praising the legions of Giants fans in attendance for their support.
"Every week I go in and prepare to be my very best," Winston told reporters after the game. "And I'm just happy we were able to go out there and apply it and pull out a win for our fans today.
"It means a lot to us because the fans are a big part of this entire organization," he continued. "Without their support, without their commitment to coming to the games and being loud … we wouldn't be here. We love that. That's what we do this for.
"That's why you want to win games, because of that vibrational frequency, it's beautiful when you say the Giants find a way, and so far we have been finding a way, and I'm so proud of our team for doing that. And I think it's definitely because of our fans."
To say that New York found "a way" to win in Week 4 might be an understatement. The Giants' defense withstood a last-gasp effort from the Cardinals on fourth-and-goal from the Giants' 4-yard line with just seconds remaining in the fourth quarter. Cornerback Deonte Banks intercepted Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett and returned it 98 yards, lifting New York to victory.
Given the circumstances, Winston wisely shared some gratitude with his teammate for not only securing the win but also improving his chances of keeping the starting job.
"To see Tae (Banks), man, someone who has faced his trials, man, but still finds a way to persevere," Winston said. "And for that to happen to him, and for him to finish in the end zone with that ball, I was so proud of him."
With a Week 5 showdown against the Washington Commanders fast approaching, Winston is preparing to lead his team as its starting quarterback.
No matter what comes his way, the 12-year veteran knows his focus must stay on what he can control. His Week 4 performance was far from perfect. However, he is determined to build on the improvements he made as he hopes to keep New York in sole possession of first place in the NFC East.
Until then, Winston will take it one day at a time.
"I'm just grateful for the opportunity I have now," Winston said. "And right now, I get to smile and say I'm the starting quarterback for the New York Football Giants. So, what I would love is winning games with my team and being the best I can be. And I feel like that, man, I'm heating up and I'm starting to get better, better, and better."
"Last week, I was questioning if I could even throw," he added. "This week, I've got people talking about the Jameis Winston experience again. So I'm still curious, and I'm inspired to be the best me every single day. And that alone pushes me. Not another man, not another teammate, just my desire to be what I would love."
