title: Odell Beckham Jr. Disagrees With Harbaugh's Explanation for His Giants Release
full_text:
Nearly a week after his release by the New York Giants , receiver Odell Beckham Jr. decided to break his silence on the move that sent a shockwave through the fanbase.
Beckham, who signed with the Giants ahead of training camp and worked hard to make head coach John Harbaugh's first 53-man roster, saw his reunion last just three games with 13 total pass play snaps, one target and zero receptions in that span.
That clearly wasn't the impact that either side was expecting the Giants' 2014 first-round pick to have in his return to the team's receiving corps, and it led to the decision to part ways that Harbaugh said was purely in the best interest of his football team and had nothing to do with a personal matter with Beckham.
It seems the 33-year-old Beckham, who took to the comment section of a fan's Instagram account to air his side of the story, doesn't agree with his coach's explanation, suggesting he was wronged by the franchise.
OBJ reacts to the Giants releasing him 😬 pic.twitter.com/W2imDyJlFI
“I’m super smart !!!!” Beckham said in part of his comment. “But I didn’t see this one my brotha! They got me!!!"
"They won on top of the money you talking about I made them. I came in HUMBLY, took the vet min then EARNED my spot and didn’t say nothing about no (money) which I (know I) make for everybody.
Beckham added that he didn't understand why the Giants "gave me the run along" because he felt he could have "been playing this year elsewhere and making an impact."
The Giants' move to reunite with Beckham came during a period of uncertainty for the wide receiver room during the summer, when fellow LSU alum and the team's No. 1 option in Malik Nabers was still in the process of rehabbing from his ACL injury suffered in 2025 and Darius Slayton was on the comeback from an offseason core muscle repair.
In search of depth, they turned towards a familiar face with ties to Harbaugh, who coached Beckham during his stint with the Ravens in 2023, and a guy whose NFL career had seen it all and could serve as a resource for the younger players in the building.
Once he made the roster, Beckham was the Giants' fourth receiver in the positional order, and given their larger reliance on heavier personnel packages to fit the run-first style of offense, it became difficult to get Beckham into the mix and routes where they could get the ball into his hands.
Hence, Harbaugh was adamant that the failed second partnership in New York came down to a lack of a feasible role in the Giants offense and the need to create more value in that roster spot, which was subsequently used to sign receiver Braxton Berrios, who had run out of practice squad elevations.
“I did hope he would get more chances, and he didn’t,” Harbaugh said on Wednesday following Beckham's release.
“That’s where we stood, so I felt like that being the case, we’re not going to be able to get it done roster spot-wise. We need more out of that spot, and that’s what we’re going to do. Nothing about Odell that he could do in that sense.'
What was so odd about Beckham's inability to get involved in the offense wasn't that he had lost the speed he once had or route running, but that the Giants had missed more than a few chances to connect with the receiver.
During the preseason especially, Beckham was frequently burning past opposing cornerbacks or getting left unaccounted for, leaving him alone and striding towards the endzone for potential huge plays and touchdown scores.
Sadly, the quarterbacks seemed not to catch Beckham wide open amid their read progressions. The result was a lack of receptions column for a player whose had to overcome multiple injuries just for the chance to compete for a spot on an NFL roster and show he can still contribute as a pass catcher.
With no new production from his second stint with the team, Beckham's career numbers remain at 7,987 receiving yards and 59 touchdown catches. He holds five 1,000-yard seasons, including four with the Giants in his first three years (2014-16) and the last in 2018 before he was traded to the Cleveland Browns in the offseason.
While Beckham believes he can still offer something to another franchise, no team has jumped on his availability since clearing waivers, even with having the proof of making the Giants roster this summer on his recent resume.
It will remain to be seen if Beckham finds another opportunity before he chooses to hang up his cleats one day. When he does, many Giants fans would love to see him do it with the organization that first took a chance on him when they drafted him twelve years ago.
They would have to hope that Beckham doesn't reject the possibility from any ill feelings towards the Giants. Beckham seems to have matured a lot over his years as a pro, but his latest public statement brings into question whether his relationship with the franchise will look the same after the most recent ending.

title: Arvell Reese Delivers Best Game of Rookie Season in Giants' Win Over Cardinals
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. – New York Giants linebacker Arvell Reese had himself a day in the team's 36-24 victory over the Arizona Cardinals at MetLife Stadium in Week 4.
The No. 5 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft turned in a defensive masterpiece against the Cardinals, logging nine solo tackles, one tackle for loss, three passes defensed, one quarterback hit, and one interception, which was one of the game's pivotal turning points in the Giants' favor.
He also became the fifth Giants rookie with three or more passes defensed and an interception in a game and the only Giants rookie since 1994 with nine or more tackles, three or more passes defensed and at least one interception in a game.
With just over three minutes remaining in the first half, Reese intercepted Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett after defensive tackle Shelby Harris batted the pass at the line. On the Giants' ensuing drive, quarterback Jameis Winston threw a 25-yard touchdown pass to receiver Malik Nabers to give New York its first lead of the day, 19-14.
For Reese, it was routine.
"I was just the man on the back," Reese said of his interception. "I saw the ball coming my way. He's there, and I look at the quarterback (Brissett), and I see the ball coming my way."
As a former standout at Ohio State, Reese is no stranger to playing under the weight of great expectations. The 6-foot-4, 243-pounder became the first player Harbaugh drafted in the top five during his nearly two-decade run as an NFL head coach.
After a stellar performance throughout training camp and into the preseason, Reese earned the starting spot on the weak side of Harbaugh's defense. Given his triple-threat skill set, which allows him to stop the run, drop into coverage, and rush the passer, Reese has found comfort playing all over the field.
This week he joined select company, becoming the third rookie in the NFL since 2010 to record nine or more tackles, three or more passes defensed and one or more interceptions, joining Dee Milliner (Dec. 22, 2013) and Kerby Joseph (Nov. 6, 2022).
Still, Reese refuses to acknowledge it as anything but doing his job.
"I think it's just being in the moment," Reese said. "Being poised and knowing, having that 'win the game' on-defense mentality. Just trying to show up, play for the person beside me, and not play selfishly.
"I think it's just playing unselfishly," he continued. "Really trying to win and playing for the person beside you. Like I just said, bro, I play because I don't want to let the person beside me down. I do my job and try to dominate so he can know I've got his back."
As the Giants turn their attention to a Week 5 showdown with their division-rival Washington Commanders, Reese will look to add to his season totals of 34 tackles, four passes defensed, and the aforementioned interception.
He'll have his teammates' support, and he will also find added strength in knowing he had his best game as a pro in the presence of arguably the greatest defender in NFL history.
"Man, that means a lot," Reese said when told that Hall of Fame linebacker Lawrence Taylor was in attendance as part of the team's honoring of the 1986 Super Bowl championship team.
"With a guy like that in the building, him setting the standard for how that position is supposed to be played back in the day, it definitely means a lot to play a decent game like that."
"Yeah, a bunch of plays I left out there," Reese answered with a grin.

title: Why the Giants Had J.J. McCarthy Active Despite Less Than a Week in the Offense
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. – The ' decision to keep quarterback J.J. McCarthy active despite having completed less than a week getting up to speed on the offense raised eyebrows and raised questions about whether McCarthy or Jake Haener, a standard practice squad elevation, was QB2 behind starter Jameis Winston.
"We thought we could do it with the kind of way we were set up for special teams," head coach John Harbaugh explained after the game.
"We had enough guys playing special teams, and it just gave us an option in case we wanted to put J.J. out there to run certain plays that we had prepared for him, but to think that he was going to be the backup for the whole game was unrealistic.
"So we had, we had Jake (Haener) up too, and that was our thinking. We just felt like we needed three guys for the two roles."
Despite the Giants' victory, Winston had an up-and-down day that included two interceptions that thankfully didn't cost the team in the long run. He also threw three touchdown passes.
"I thought he played well except for the turnovers, and that's the thing he's going to tell you," Harbaugh said of Winston.
"So that's something to clean up."
Harbaugh added that the coaches had no thoughts about putting McCarthy into a package.
With the 36-24 win, the Giants moved to 3-0 at home this season. It marks the eighth time since the 1970 merger, and the first time since 2008, that they have started the season 3-0 at home.
Harbaugh is the sixth Giants coach in franchise history to win his first three home games, joining Dan Reeves (1993), Alex Webster (1969), Jim Lee Howell (1954), Steve Owen (1931) and Roy Andrews (1929).
The Giants' defense recorded three interceptions and 14 pass breakups. The last time they had three interceptions in a game was against New England on Nov. 26, 2023. The defense's 14 passes defensed are the most by a Giants team since Dec. 29, 2013, when they totaled 16 against Washington.
Linebacker Arvell Reese produced nine total tackles, three passes defensed, one interception and one tackle for loss. He is the fifth Giants rookie with three or more passes defensed and an interception in a game and the only Giants rookie since 1994 with nine or more tackles, three or more passes defensed and at least one interception in a game.
Reese is also the third rookie in the NFL since 2010 to record nine or more tackles, three or more passes defensed, and one or more interceptions, joining Dee Milliner (Dec. 22, 2013) and Kerby Joseph (Nov. 6, 2022).

title: Giants Report Card: Defense Stars as Giants Top Cardinals to Take NFC East Lead
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. - Grading the New York Giants ' 36-24 win over the Arizona Cardinals.
The Jameis Winston experience had its ups and downs this week, starting with two interceptions (both on late throws) and a touchdown drought that lasted nine quarters.
It finally ended in the second quarter when Winston found Malachi Fields on a 12-yard touchdown pass, making it a 14-12 game in favor of the Cardinals.
A little later in the quarter, Winston threw his second touchdown pass, this time to receiver Malik Nabers, who caught his first touchdown pass in a regular-season game since tearing his ACL last year, also during Week 4 of the regular season.
The Giants' rushing game had its issues, finishing with 87 yards on 28 carries (3.1 yards per carry), with no runs going beyond nine yards, led by Najee Harris. Harris also fumbled, the fifth fumble by the Giants' running backs this season.
Things started rough for the Giants defense, particularly against the run, when the Cardinals rushed for 92 yards on 15 carries in the first half.
But credit the Giants for battening down the hatches and adjusting, as Arizona gained just 31 yards on 11 rushing attempts in the second half despite the closeness of the game.
What can be said of the defensive secondary, particularly on the last drive? The Cardinals began the drive on their own 33-yard line.
They benefited from two Giants defensive penalties, including a very questionable defensive pass interference call against cornerback Deonte Banks that gave the Cardinals 1st-and-goal on the Giants' 4-yard line.
DOTS of the Deonte Banks game-winner pic.twitter.com/KDnI8qIWkI
But Banks and the Giants, with their backs against the wall, came up big. Jacoby Brissett threw three straight incomplete passes.
On 4th down, Banks atoned for the DPI by intercepting Brissett and returning it 98 yards for the score that put the game away.
It also put the Giants in sole possession of first place in the NFC East, thanks to the Giants' win and the Eagles' loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
The kickoff coverage unit allowed too many leaky yards. Jalen Brooks returned a kickoff for 37 yards, and Devin Duvernay returned one for 39 yards.
Otherwise, the dynamic duo of punter Jordan Stout and kicker Dominic Zvada were money again, with Stout finishing with a 44.7 net average and Zvada nailing all three field goals from 39, 50, and 52 yards.
Charlie Jones took over for Braxton Berrios on punt returns in the second half when Berrios went down with a foot injury. Jones finished with a 14.5-yard average, a 23-yard return, and one fair catch.
On kickoff returns, Tyrone Tracy Jr. delivered an impressive 55-yard return behind pristine blocking from the return unit in the first quarter, setting up Zvada's second field goal of the day.
Kudos to defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson, who made adjustments to the run defense that shut down the Arizona rushing attack and produced three tackles for loss (4 yards total).
On the other side of the ball, why offensive coordinator Matt Nagy keeps insisting on running plays wide in the red zone remains a mystery. The Giants finished 2-of-3 in the red zone this week, but at times they made it harder on themselves with slow-developing plays that went wide (four, per the game film, none of which gained more than two yards).
Wilson's second-half adjustments helped the Giants close out the win, but Nagy's red zone play-calling continues to be an area that can be better.

title: Jets Have a Clear 53-Man Roster Decision to Make After Braiden McGregor's Season-Ending Injury
full_text:
Another disappointing effort in Week 4 has the New York Jets tumbling down the standings, now sitting at 1-3 as they prepare for a Week 5 showdown against the Cleveland Browns. Losses like the 23-12 defeat to the Chicago Bears on Sunday are demoralizing for a young team , especially one that's been plagued by injuries on both sides of the ball.
If another lopsided loss wasn't enough, New York's injured reserve is another player bigger heading into the rest of the season.
Early Monday afternoon, ESPN 's Adam Schefter reported that Jets defensive end Braiden McGregor's season is officially over . The former undrafted free agent out of Michigan left Sunday's loss with a chest injury and didn't return, with the reported diagnosis now being a torn pectoral muscle.
Jets DE Braiden McGregor tore his pec and now will be out for the season, per source. pic.twitter.com/WEMVEzx6ZR
Although McGregor has been in a backup role for the Jets since 2024, his absence will be felt. He's played 49 defensive snaps and another 46 on special teams this season, tallying seven solo tackles. His 74.4 tackling grade on Pro Football Focus is also the fifth-best among New York defenders who've played at least 40 snaps this season.
With McGregor being a big part of the Jets' five-man pass-rush rotation (David Bailey, Joseph Ossai, Will McDonald IV, and Kingsley Enagbare), someone will need to step up for the rest of the season. That could mean calling up a practice-squad member for help—specifically preseason darling Nate Lynn.
With McGregor's season over, the Jets officially have an opportunity to see what Lynn can do in regular-season action.
The 24-year-old EDGE joined the Jets as a free agent in mid-August after being released by the Tennessee Titans earlier in the offseason. Lynn needed a fresh start after failing to make a regular-season appearance with the Titans in 2025 and the Detroit Lions in 2024. The Jets seemed like the perfect team for that opportunity, given their pass-rushing woes.
He may have arrived in Gotham late in the offseason, but it didn't take Lynn long to win over Jets fans. He debuted for Gang Green against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 2 of the preseason, generating four pressures (including two sacks) and an impressive 85.9 pass-rush grade on PFF . He followed that up with another two-pressure performance against the New York Giants in the exhibition finale, seemingly doing enough to make the 53-man roster in some fans' eyes .
That's why it was somewhat shocking when Lynn wasn't part of the initial 53-man roster and instead landed on the practice squad. Joseph Ossai not ending up on the injured reserve or Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list likely played a role in that decision, per Sports Illustrated's Nick Faria, leaving the former UDFA in limbo.
But now that McGregor's season is over, Lynn could be a potential 53-man roster candidate. He's already familiar with Glenn, who was his defensive coordinator during the 2024 season in Detroit, and he also knows assistant defensive line/outside linebackers coach Cameron Davis, who coached the Lions' D-line while Lynn was in the Motor City. Those connections could lead to a spot in the edge rush rotation.
Whether he's promoted to the 53-man unit or used as a game-day elevation, Lynn's first chance to impress the Jets post-McGregor injury could come against the Browns in Week 5. Cleveland might be 3-1, but quarterback Deshaun Watson is completing 48.5% of passes for 173 yards, one touchdown, two interceptions, and a 34.2 passing grade when under pressure , per PFF .
If Lynn plays a role in the Jets' defense getting to Watson, Gang Green will be in a great spot to beat the Browns. Additionally, it would also boost Lynn's chances of remaining in the pass rush rotation not just for the rest of the year, but perhaps in 2027, too.
Needless to say, his situation will be interesting to monitor in the coming days.

title: Faria's Focus Week 4: Key Jets Takeaways After Bears Loss, Losing Skid, Biggest Concerns & More
full_text:
Another game, another disappointing Jets defeat . Gang Green needed a victory over the Bears and backup quarterback Tyson Bagent to build momentum heading into the middle parts of the season.
Instead, New York looked lifeless for most of the afternoon and fell to the Bears 23-12 in a game that looked much closer than it actually was.
As with any loss like this (New York's third in a row), there are plenty of takeaways to break down . At the end of the day, though, the Jets' biggest issues reared their ugly heads in the worst ways on Sunday.
It's time to highlight them now.
No reason to hide it. The Jets were thoroughly outplayed on Sunday at each facet of the game. The defense gave up 492 yards of total offense and over 230 rushing yards. Offensively, they ran just 32 plays and were 0-for-7 on third down.
The only reason the game was even close was because Chicago turned the ball over multiple times.
New York's total points scored off of those turnovers: six.
"We have to be opportunistic," Glenn said. "We have these opportunities on the pick and on the fumble. I think it was in range to get points. And again, we got six points out of it; we have to do a better job at that and get seven."
It's good that the Jets were able to end their interception drought. It's even better that they recorded multiple interceptions during that time as well. But the reality is that this team took a major step back on Sunday after three straight weeks of competitive football.
What makes the performance even more alarming , though, is that the Jets ran into many of the same problems that have plagued them over the years. They were penalized 15 times, their defense missed too many assignments, and Gang Green looked completely outmatched schematically.
It's the type of game that raises questions for every major decision-maker in the front office. If it isn't fixed soon, it could bring disaster for the Jets throughout the remainder of the year.
Some head coaches change how the team looks and plays depending on the opponent. Others choose to run things a specific way that focuses on certain principles and intangibles.
The Jets' coaching staff is one based on the latter. They want to play and coach in a specific way that they believe will work for the future. Their biggest problem, though, is an unwillingness to adjust to aspects of the game as they come.
Take Sunday's loss as a great example. Chicago's offense was going up and down the field against New York's defense all game. Conversely, the Jets tried and failed to do much on the offensive end in their own right. They wanted to be a team that could run the ball effectively and be efficient in the passing game. They looked at Chicago's run defense being ranked 22nd in the league and decided to focus on targeting them in that way.
The final tally: 14 carries for 59 yards and just 4.2 yards per carry. Not good enough.
Conversely, the Jets' limited number of offensive snaps also meant fewer opportunities for Garrett Wilson and Kenyon Sadiq—the remaining lifeblood of New York's passing offense. Wilson and Sadiq finished with just eight targets and three catches for 27 yards, all by Wilson. Inexcusable.
New York was without starting running back Breece Hall and other talented players like wideouts Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper Jr. The Jets should have fed the ball consistently to their best players. Instead, they were more focused on making sure their principles stayed true.
It left Wilson fresher than he's been after a game in years.
"I take a lot of pride in when the ball does come my way, making a play on it," Wilson said. "I want more on my plate, for sure. ... I feel good. I ain’t take no hits.”
After the game, Glenn was asked about the lack of targets, citing the reality that New York needed to do a better job.
But the real reason is that the Jets are so focused on running the ball; it effectively took them out of rhythm in the passing game. With so few reps, it ultimately sunk the entire group.
Defensively, it wasn't much better. Gang Green's secondary continues to compete hard despite any true star talent at corner, but their linebackers have been a mess. Jamien Sherwood and Demario Davis both struggled throughout the contest when it came to undisciplined play.
Whether due to injuries or coaching focus, the team isn't close to making a swap at that position, though.
Coaching is not the only reason the Jets lost. In a 23-12 blowout like the one suffered on Sunday, it is never the lone reason, but New York's unwillingness to adapt, especially in the modern NFL, is a major hindrance to the team, and it's something Ben Johnson and the Bears used to their advantage.
Through four games, the Jets' biggest on-field problem is the same as it was last season.
They don't have a pass rush.
Chicago has one of the best offensive lines in the game. It was always going to be a challenge for New York. But the lack of production over the last few games has been downright alarming.
Against the Bears, the Jets' edge rushers recorded just a single collective pressure. The player with the most pressures on the team ended up being defensive tackle Harrison Phillips... with two. The only sack the Jets enjoyed came on another blitz, which highlights the fact that the team can't get consistent pressure on a QB unless they send extra men at the point of attack. That's not a recipe for success.
Will McDonald IV has seemingly taken a major step back , while second overall pick David Bailey was the third-lowest-graded starting defender (57.0) for the Jets on Sunday, and Kingsley Enagbare wasn't even available because of an injury.
This collective group must play better. Giving up nearly 500 yards to a Bears offense on their third different starting quarterback this season is concerning, especially since this was the big issue last season that has yet to be resolved.
I said before the season began that New York's entire roster has greatly improved when it comes to baseline talent. Through three games, that statement rang true. Gang Green looked far more competitive than they had at any point last season.
One thing changed that, and it wasn't a coaching decision or front office pick.
Sometimes a year gets derailed not by coaching, but because the talent on the team is simply not on the field due to a myriad of physical issues. On Sunday, here is who the Jets were without and lost at one point during the game:
In total, that is eight starters on the roster missing or lost on Sunday. Over a third of the team's starting lineup is dealing with injuries. With each passing week, it seems like New York is getting more banged up.
No one likes to make an excuse regarding injuries. They happen to every team after all. But when you are a rebuilding organization like the Jets, the first thing to improve is the starting talent, not the depth of the roster. That's why, when starters go down en masse like this, these organizations don't have the depth necessary to keep playing at a specific level.
Until the Jets get healthy again, it's hard to say when this losing streak will end. That's just a fact.

title: Jets Week 4 Report Card: Grading Every Position After Bears Hand Gang Green a 3rd Straight Loss
full_text:
A slow start out of the gate paved the way for a 23-12 loss to the Bears on Sunday, handing the Jets a third consecutive defeat. Even though they were without nearly half of their offensive starters in the Windy City, it was another disappointing performance from Gang Green.
To make matters worse, the Bears were still without starting quarterback Caleb Williams (Grade 2 hamstring strain), and there appeared to be some favorable matchups for the Jets to exploit going in. That said, the Jets never established any momentum early on and struggled to keep pace with the Bears throughout the game, even against backup QB Tyson Bagent.
With three straight losses to their credit since a Week 1 win over the Titans, injuries and slow starts continue to plague this Jets team. Fresh off a frustrating Week 4 loss to the Bears , let's hand out some grades for each unit ahead of a Week 5 home matchup against the Browns.
Although the Bears have been solid against the pass to begin the season, this was a key matchup coming into the game to see what Jets QB Geno Smith could do against them. Smith finished just 8-of-15 for 119 passing yards and one touchdown, and the Jets could not sustain any momentum by punting on five of their eight drives.
Granted, he was without running back Breece Hall (quad), wide receiver Adonai Mitchell (right finger) and tight end Mason Taylor (thumb) and hardly had any reliable options to turn to, but he did post a respectable 101.8 passer rating and kept the Jets in the game with a late two-play, 72-yard TD drive in the fourth quarter.
That said, Smith's worst completion percentage (53.3%) since 2023 was nowhere near the efficiency the Jets needed from him with so many players injured.
The overall volume was low, with Smith completing just eight passes the entire game, but the Jets certainly looked like a team that was shorthanded in the receiving corps. The lone bright spot, however, was Isaiah Williams, who had two catches for 73 yards and a 58-yard TD in the fourth (h/t NFL), which at least gave the Jets a spark that was nonexistent for the rest of the game.
Isaiah Williams 58-yard TD! NYJvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/TRgGogeLyP
Aside from that, this was an opportunity for others to step up in light of the injuries, and they did the exact opposite.
Garrett Wilson only had three catches for 27 yards while Sterling Shepard was only targeted once after being signed to the practice squad just last month. Being without two of their top-three receivers did not help, as rookie Omar Cooper Jr. continues to deal with a high ankle sprain as well, but the 100 combined yards from Williams and Wilson on just five total receptions is not going to cut it.
Even though Taylor was sidelined once again, rookie Kenyon Sadiq's breakout performance in Week 3 and the overall statement from the TE group set a high bar moving forward. While the priority should have been on feeding Sadiq more and keeping him involved in the offense, that was far from the case on Sunday, with zero catches on four targets, one week after coming down with seven receptions for 105 yards and a TD against the Lions.
In fact, Jelani Woods (one reception, 11 yards) was the only TE with a catch in the game as the TE unit looked like a shell of itself in the Windy City. Again, Smith only had 15 total pass attempts the entire game, but that is no excuse for this group to have little impact and struggle over the middle of the field when the WR room was already depleted coming in.
All the attention turned to Braelon Allen in the backfield as Hall sat out with a quad injury. He had been relatively quiet through the first three weeks with just 19 carries for 61 yards and a TD, but Allen was solid with 59 rush yards on 14 carries and emerged as one of the biggest winners from the game in a Jets uniform. Allen played 30 offensive snaps for the Jets, per Pro Football Focus , and averaged a respectable 4.2 yards per carry, up from his average of 3.2 for the season.
Allen didn't have enough explosiveness to take the pressure off Smith, with his longest run being just 10 yards. That made this offense essentially one-dimensional for the majority of the game and contributed to the lack of rhythm the Jets' offense was able to put together. It was an encouraging showing from Allen, but not nearly enough for a team that mustered only seven first downs and went 0-of-7 on third down.
This was another letdown from the offensive line, which was without Dylan Parham (left knee) and once again struggled to establish its will in the trenches. The Jets had just 157 yards of total offense, never found their identity from the opening kick, and could not keep Smith protected, allowing three sacks.
Given Parham's impressive play so far, his absence was certainly felt , but there is more to this simply than just his injury.
The Jets only possessed the ball for 17:15, which was their fewest since 2005, and simply put together a dreadful performance. The lack of playmakers is one thing, and it was not entirely the O-line's fault that Smith held onto the ball too long at times. Still, it is hard to see this team doing much better until those issues are resolved and the offense develops a better flow.
It was difficult to find many positives regarding the performance of the  defensive line on Sunday. Aside from finding some success when blitzing, it was an inexcusable outing from this group after allowing 232 yards on the ground and more than four yards per carry. Even No. 2 pick David Bailey, who was viewed as an X-factor entering the game by Sports Illustrated's Nick Faria, failed to record a pressure in 27 pass-rush snaps.
This was also an opportunity for someone like Joseph Ossai, who had a chance to erase any doubts in Kingsley Enagbare's absence (knee). He tied for the third-most solo tackles (five) on the team and had seven total, but his impact was minimal aside from that. It was one thing to allow 232 rush yards, but the fact that Bagent went off for a career-high 268 yards speaks to how poorly the Jets played up front.
From Jamien Sherwood's forced fumble on Bears RB D'Andre Swift and13 total tackles (five solo) to Demario Davis' 10 total tackles and the only sack of the game for the Jets, there were a lot of positives to take from the linebacker corps. That said, Davis was called offside on a play that would have been an interception—one of three instances in the game where a potential interception was negated due to a penalty for Gang Green—and was constantly picked on in coverage.
Sherwood has also struggled and has slowly become a concern himself. Overall, this group performed well compared to other units, but it still had difficulty finding any answers to New York's dominant rushing attack. Some of the blame can go to the line up front not holding up its end of the bargain, but with Kiko Mauigoa (quad) sidelined once again, the LBs left some room for improvement going forward.
At long last, the Jets finally ended a 21-game drought without an interception (h/t NFL) when All-Pro safety Minkah Fitzpatrick jumped a route on a poor throw from Bagent in his first game back from a groin injury. He also led the team with 16 total tackles (eight solo) and remains the most reliable part of this unit despite a few missteps in coverage.
Minkah Fitzpatrick gives the Jets their first INT in 636 pass attempts NYJvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/CQUCl4JVnt
However, the Jets had three more interceptions besides Fitzpatrick's, but all three were taken away due to penalties. Brandon Stephens and rookie D'Angelo Ponds were each penalized. Ponds ultimately stepped up for Jarvis Brownlee Jr. after he exited the game with a concussion, and Dane Belton was solid again with 14 total tackles, but the overall coverage from this group was inconsistent and still posed some concerns against a backup QB.

title: Jets Week 4 Awards: 8 Winners After an Uninspiring Loss to the Bears in Chicago
full_text:
Woof. There are not many ways to describe how poorly the Jets played on Sunday .
Gang Green needed a victory to get to .500 heading into the month of October. Instead, all three phases struggled, and the Jets lost 23-12 to the Chicago Bears in a game that wasn't nearly as close as the scoreboard said.
"Very disappointed on a number of different levels," Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said. "This was about not playing complementary football. ... We have to do a better job of complementing each other, and that did not happen today."
There's certainly a lot to take in after Sunday's loss, and, as always, I have my weekly Jets awards to give out.
It finally happened. New York finally recorded an interception after 637 days, and 20 games.
Minkah Fitzpatrick was the player who picked off Tyson Bagent on a gorgeous jump route (h/t NFL). He has been an excellent addition to the team, even if he missed the last two games with a groin injury. New York could have gotten at least four interceptions on the day, but three were called back by penalties.
Minkah Fitzpatrick gives the Jets their first INT in 636 pass attempts NYJvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/CQUCl4JVnt
The good news is we don't have to ask anymore when the Jets will finally force a turnover. The bad news is what happened after that interception.
There isn 't much positive to say about the Jets right now after a loss like that. Their offense failed to do much of anything, but the defense was easily the worst part of the game. New York's edge rushing group recorded just a single pressure in Sunday's loss. Only Harrison Phillips recorded two pressures along the defensive line in total.
Jamien Sherwood and Demario Davis both looked old and slow as they were picked apart by Chicago. New York had five turnovers recorded, but only two counted due to mental mistakes and pre-snap penalties.
Worst of all came on the final drive. Chicago held onto the ball for the final nine minutes of action and ran 18 plays. They were picked off twice on the drive, but Davis was called for being offsides on one and for a defensive hold on the other.
The Jets gave up 492 total yards (that's nearly 500 yards of offense), and over 230 yards rushing. Nothing the team did this week was good. And there will need to be a lot of questions going forward about the effectiveness of the group.
Last season, Glenn made it clear that the final four minutes of every half belonged to the head coach. It is up to the coach to have his team prepared to get off the field on defense and then score points on offense  before the half ends.
While the Jets' interception drought may be over, a new drought has begun.
New York has yet to score a single point in the final two minutes (h/t ESPN 's Rich Cimini) of both the first half and the end of the game this season. In the first half, the Jets simply went three-and-out this time around instead of some mental mishap in the closing seconds. They didn't get the ball with a chance to score in the fourth.
Here's a chance for the Jets to end another drought -- scoring in the final minutes of a half. Eight straight games without pts in the final 4 minutes of the first/second halves. #Jets
We'll talk more about Glenn in a little bit, but it's clear that the Jets offense is only hindering themselves by being unable to put up points in a no-huddle and two-minute situation.
Eighty-nine. The Bears' offense ran 89 plays during their beatdown win over New York.
The current league average is just 62 plays per game for offenses across the league. Chicago was so efficient, and New York bailed them out with multiple penalties, that the Bears were able to do whatever they wanted offensively.
It's honestly a miracle the Jets were not beaten by more. A big play recorded offensively and a few turnovers evened out what ended up becoming a blowout. Glenn has preached himself to be a quality defensive mind. While player execution was poor throughout, it's on the coaching staff that they weren't able to get off the field on that side of the ball.
Eighty-nine plays is an absurd amount. Inexcusable across the board.
Glenn was one of seven coaches hired during the 2025 cycle. Here are the records of all seven coaches through 21 games:
Glenn's record? 4-17 after the loss on Sunday. Just a note: here are the records of the coaches who were hired this past offseason.
Glenn has just one more win than a coach who was one-and-done during their first years. Five new hires this offseason nearly have as many wins.
Something needs to change. And fast.
In the modern NFL—and with rules built in favor of helping offenses—teams should be pretty good on third down. No one should ever have a game in which they fail to convert on third down.
Somehow, the Jets accomplished that feat, going 0-for-7 on third down. New York only ran 32 plays on the day, and while much of that can be blamed on the defense giving up big plays of their own, it's also an example of how bad the entire offensive unit was at sustaining drives. Going 0-for-7 should never happen on an NFL field, especially with a quality starting quarterback like Smith leading the way.
That's what happened, though.
Somehow, the Jets' third-down offense wasn't the worst across the league. The Eagles went 0-12 on third down in their 24-20 loss to the Rams.
Progress? The Jets weren't as bad on third down as the Eagles? Yikes.
New York made many nice plays during Sunday's loss. Most of them were called back due to penalties.
One play that did stick was a 58-yard touchdown (h/t NFL) from Smith to Isaiah Williams. Williams blew through his one-on-one matchup and caught a nice throw. Williams finished with two receptions for 73 yards and the score, which led all receivers. The outcome wasn't in doubt when that touchdown throw was made, but it's still a nice play.
Isaiah Williams 58-yard TD! NYJvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/TRgGogeLyP
I'll call out good plays when they happen.
Ok, now back to the bad stuff.
Through the first three weeks of the regular season, it felt like the 2026 Jets were different than last year's team that finished 3-14. They were better offensively and defensively. Even some coaching metrics had improved.
After Week 4, though, it's fair to wonder whether this team is just the same exact one from last year. Despite all the positive looks over the last few weeks, the Jets are still 1-3 and are dealing with a plethora of injuries in key areas.
They are too often outcoached and outprepared where it matters most. Players are also making the same kind of mental mistakes we saw last season.
Until the Jets prove fans wrong and actually win football games, this will remain a bad football team. And Sunday's loss did nothing to give anyone hope that things were going in the right direction.

title: 6 Duds & 2 Studs in Jets' Disappointing 23-12 Loss to Bears in Week 4
full_text:
Through the first three weeks of the season, Jets fans could take a glass- half-full mindset. Sure, the organization was 1-2, but they had fought hard in each contest. There were significant improvements on the roster that made Gang Green better than their 2025 counterpart.
On Sunday against the Bears, the Jets reverted back to what the 2025 team looked like .
The score may have read 23-12, but the Jets lost to the Bears in such a fashion that the score didn't do it justice. Every level of play seemed to collapse for the Jets. They were outgained in yards, 492-157, and didn't record a third-down conversion all game.
In a game where there weren't many positives , it's time to go over some of the Jets' biggest studs and duds from Sunday's loss.
There were two key positives throughout Sunday's loss. At the top of the list was the Jets ending a 21-game drought without an interception (h/t NFL). That came courtesy of All-Pro safety Minkah Fitzpatrick early in the second quarter. Fitzpatrick jumped a route on a poor throw from Tyson Bagent and made a great play on the ball. His return also set the Jets up with a chance to put up points, while leading the team in tackles with 16.
Minkah Fitzpatrick gives the Jets their first INT in 636 pass attempts NYJvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/CQUCl4JVnt
Of note, the Jets actually had four interceptions recorded during Sunday's loss, but three were called back due to penalties. Fitzpatrick had a couple of missteps in coverage, but he remains a high performer who can make plays in the back end.
We'll get more on the penalties later, but this was a good day for Fitzpatrick, who wasn't able to play over the last two weeks with a groin injury.
The first three weeks show improvement from the Jets. Sunday was a complete disaster, and it will weigh on head coach Aaron Glenn going forward. Chicago had over twice the yards against the Jets offense, but they also ran 89 plays.
That's right. 89 plays from Chicago's offense. That is a failure of the Jets' defense and their ability to get off the field. They also had several turnovers forced, called back with penalties. Add in an offense that did not record a single third-down conversion, and the Jets were a complete disaster from the opening kickoff.
New York had shown improvement to begin the year. But they are now 1-3 this year, and 4-17 under Glenn as head coach. If things don't turn around quickly, things could get very ugly later this year.
New York made one play offensively today: a 58-yard strike from Geno Smith late in the contest (h/t NFL). The Jets were down 23-6 at the time, so it's not like it had any major impact on the outcome of the game, but it's nice to see Williams make a deep play like that.
Isaiah Williams 58-yard TD! NYJvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/TRgGogeLyP
Keep in mind, he also had a bad drop early in the game, but this was an improvement for Williams. As the Jets continue to be without Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper Jr. at wide receiver, the Jets will need to be relying on Williams moving forward.
We've talked about two of the main positives for the Jets in this game. Now it's time to talk about the long list of negatives.
And we have to start with the defensive line. For the second straight week, the Jets failed to get any pressure rushing with just their down linemen. The only time the team was able to get any form of pressure was when the team blitzed. It's not a good pathway to success to continue to ask the secondary to make plays deep when you can't get pressure on the quarterback.
It also doesn't help that the team gave up 232 yards on the ground and over four yards per carry. Chicago did whatever they wanted to do up front. While they have one of the best offensive lines in the game, it's inexcusable that the Jets weren't able to put up more of a fight.
Second overall pick David Bailey was nonexistent at times, rushing the passer. Going up against Darnell Wright is a tough matchup for any young pass rusher, but Bailey's didn't even manage a pressure in 27 pass rush reps.
In fact, the entire defensive line recorded just a single pressure during the game.
Last week, it felt like Geno Smith could do no wrong . This week was far different.
New York's offense was only able to run 32 plays. Much of that is because the defense was unable to get off the field in any situation. But they did little to help themselves either. New York was 0-7 on third down. Smith was just 8-for-15 passing for 119 yards, which were greatly helped by the deep touchdown to Williams. His 53.3% completion percentage was the worst for him in a game since 2023.
Smith also took three sacks that had more to do with him holding the ball too long than with the offensive line getting beat. The injuries are a problem, but the quarterback certainly deserves blame, as this wasn't the kind of performance New York needed from him.
First, it was T'Vondre Sweat's interception called back for a penalty. Then it was Brandon Stephens' pick called back for a penalty. After that, it was a D'Angelo Ponds interception called back for—you guessed it—a penalty.
New York was called for 12 penalties during the game. Many of them were crushing, including twice in the final quarter when the defense needed a stop, got it, but were called offsides because a player jumped early.
This, of course, is a reflection of coaching. Penalties don't sink teams in totality, but when they change how a team plays, it's indicative of a roster that is undisciplined. New York needs to be better across the board. Penalties are a microcosm of that.
New York's linebackers were a disaster on Sunday. While the defensive line was a weak link of the group, the duo of Jamien Sherwood and Demario Davis weren't much better. Sherwood made a couple of good run stops and forced a fumble that the Jets recovered. For the rest of the game, he was picked on outside and in the pass .
Davis wasn't much better. As captain and face of the Jets' defense, New York expects more than being called for offsides on a play that would have been an interception. It also doesn't help that the Bears picked on Davis in coverage.
This group looks slow and unsure of where to go. They'll need to bounce back in a major way.
I said last week that the Jets were playing better , but the rash of injuries over the last several weeks posed a major problem for the organization. For starters, the team may have improved its talent during the offseason, but if their talent isn't on the field, then how are they going to be able to compete?
Sunday looked like a game in which the injuries suffered before really caught up with the organization. New York may be improved, but they aren't deep enough to make do with the kind of injuries that keep out five starters on either side of the field.
Unless these players return, it could be even worse for New York moving forward, too. Jarvis Brownlee suffered a concussion when he was run into by a teammate. That's a key part of the Jets' secondary who may be unable to play next week.

title: 3 Jets Postgame Quotes That Matter After 23-12 Loss to Bears (Aaron Glenn, Garrett Wilson & More)
full_text:
It's back to the drawing board for the Jets after suffering a 23-12 loss to the Bears at Soldier Field in Week 4. Sunday's loss marked the third straight for head coach Aaron Glenn & Co. Navigating defeat is a part of the learning experience, but that doesn't change the fact that the Jets aren't exactly leaving much room for optimism when they fail to reach 200 total yards of offense while the opposition almost hits the 500-yard mark.
It's safe to say that Jets fans have plenty of concerns on both sides of the ball after being outplayed by the Bears throughout the trip to the Windy City. That's why many were looking forward to what Glenn and his players had to say after a third straight loss made a potential playoff berth that much tougher to challenge for.
As the Jets try to figure out how to stop the bleeding before it's too late, here are the three most important quotes to come out of Sunday's postgame press conference, starting off with the bench boss himself.
There wasn't a lot to cheer for on Sunday afternoon, but the Jets did accomplish one thing: ending their interception drought. Gang Green went 20 consecutive games without a pick, finally ending that run when Minkah Fitzpatrick played the role of Brock Lesnar to the streak's Undertaker, coming down with an interception early in the second quarter (h/t NFL).
Minkah Fitzpatrick gives the Jets their first INT in 636 pass attempts NYJvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/CQUCl4JVnt
Although it's nice to put that drought in the rearview, ending the INT-less streak doesn't mean as much without a win at the end of the day, and no one knows that better than Glenn (h/t The Athletic 's Zack Rosenblatt).
"We got an interception. Great. We lost the game," Glenn said without much enthusiasm. "We lost the game. That’s what I’m thinking about.”
Seeing Fitzpatrick come down with a pick in his post-injury return was great, but it would've been a bad look for Glenn to praise that moment immediately after a disappointing loss. It'd be one thing if Fitzpatrick's interception sealed a victory or shifted the tide in the game, but that wasn't the case. Instead, the Jets' head coach is likely overwhelmed by the fact that he's " very disappointed on a number of different levels ," per Rosenblatt.
Assuming Glenn is as disappointed as he says, he needs to put his money where his mouth is throughout practice this week. A loss to the Browns in Week 5 would all but certainly put the Jets behind the eight ball in their hunt to challenge for a playoff spot, potentially ending their bid altogether.
There's no denying just how important Garrett Wilson is to the Jets, as proven by Sports Illustrated 's Nick Faria naming him the team's No. 1 player back in the offseason . That said, you wouldn't know how important Wilson is, judging by how inconsistent his usage has been this season.
The fifth-year WR was targeted only 14 times for 11 catches,136 receiving yards and a touchdown in the Jets' first two games, resulting in fans demanding more action for the former Offensive Rookie of the Year. Those fans' hopes were answered against the Lions in Week 3, as Wilson left Ford Field with an impressive 10-107-1 stat line on 13 targets.
So, everyone should've expected more of the same against the Bears, right? Wrong. Wilson finished Sunday tied for the team lead in targets (4) with rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq, recording 27 receiving yards without doing much else.
After the game, he made it clear that he wants to be more involved (h/t SNY Jets ).
"I take a lot of pride in when the ball does come my way, making a play on it. ... Being one of the guys that the organization believes in," Wilson said. "When the ball comes my way, I gotta make the play. ... I want more on my plate, for sure."
"I take a lot of pride in when the ball does come my way, making a play on it...I want more on my plate, for sure" - Garrett Wilson pic.twitter.com/zwXuEnR6rM
The Jets need to start peppering Wilson with targets, given that he's their WR1 for the foreseeable future. The 26-year-old playmaker has only been targeted more than seven times once this season, compared with surpassing that mark in six of his seven appearances last season.
Throw in the fact that WRs like Adonai Mitchell, Tim Patrick, Arian Smith and Omar Cooper Jr. are banged up or on injured reserve (along with starting RB Breece Hall's injury), and the Jets have even more reason to make Wilson the offensive focal point moving forward.
As mentioned earlier, Fitzpatrick finally made his return from injury after suffering a groin issue in Week 1. It didn't take long for him to make his impact felt outside of his drought-ending INT, as he also had 16 tackles (eight solo) and a broken-up pass, as well as strong Pro Football Focus grades when it came to tackling (88.7), run defense (86.6) and overall play (81.8).
Despite the big day, the veteran safety isn't letting his personal success cloud the fact that the Jets have significant improvements to make, telling SNY, " I don't think we did anything well that we wanted to do well ."
He also made it clear that New York can't ignore the glaring issue in front of the team .
It's only taken two games with the Jets for Fitzpatrick to feel it's necessary to, essentially, put his teammates and coaches on notice. It wasn't aggressive or direct—just the exact type of steady message young players need from a veteran voice who's been around the league for a minute.
Will the Jets listen to Fitzpatrick? If they know what's best for them, they should.

title: Jets' Snap Count vs. Bears: Biggest Winners, Losers & Role Changes in Sunday's Loss to Bears
full_text:
The Jets opened October by falling further below the .500 mark with a 23-13 loss to the Bears on Sunday afternoon. It was a struggle for Gang Green on both sides of the ball at Soldier Field, as the Bears outpaced them 492-157 in total yards while the Jets went an uninspiring 0-for-7 on third downs, all while tallying more penalty yards (76) than offense on the ground (59).
Even though New York was missing key offensive playmakers, that doesn't matter—a 1-3 record after four games leaves more questions than answers. The Jets' snap count from their third straight loss helps address those concerns, highlighting who might deserve more playing time and whose should be slashed for the betterment of the team.
That said, here are the biggest winners and losers of the Week 4 snap count, as well as one Jet whose role changed and might look different moving forward.
Braelon Allen found himself as the Jets' de facto No. 1 running back with Breece Hall missing Week 4 due to a quad injury. The 22-year-old RB entered the weekend with only 61 rushing yards and a touchdown on 19 carries (3.2 yards per carry), but the fact that he had previously started twice gave New York fans hope Allen could handle what head coach Aaron Glenn needed him to do.
He didn't find the end zone, but Allen did look solid with 59 rushing yards on 14 carries, all while playing 30 offensive snaps , according to Pro Football Focus . Even though that number is lower than last week's (34), that has a lot to do with how the Jets' offense struggled to stay on the field.
When you break things down, Allen played 93.8% of offensive snaps (30-of-32) compared to 51.5% (34-of-66) in Week 3.
That workload won't remain when Hall returns, but continuing to capitalize on the bumped-up snap count will help Allen remain a key part of the Jets' offensive plans, no matter who's healthy.
The Jets' defense was given a boost with offseason acquisition Minkah Fitzpatrick's return to the secondary on Sunday. While getting a proven performer like Fitzpatrick back was welcome by fans and coaches, his return naturally meant someone else would lose opportunities. That player ended up being Andre Cisco.
Cisco was the biggest beneficiary from the moment that Fitzpatrick went down in Week 1. The Syracuse product finished the season opener with 44 snaps before that jumped to 59 in Week 2, followed by a season-high mark of 65 against the Lions last week. But with Fitzpatrick back, Cisco ended Sunday's game with only three defensive snaps.
For reference, he had never played fewer than 48 in an appearance with the Jets since the start of the 2025 season. Fitzpatrick and Dane Belton are terrific starting safeties when healthy, but the NFL season is long, and New York shouldn't want to tire them out, so finding a way to get more snaps to Cisco could be in the team's best interest.
Jack Heflin's 2026 has been a rollercoaster ride. He went from signing a reserve contract in February to being waived and added to the practice squad in the summer, only to be promoted to the 53-man roster in Week 2. He made his debut with a quiet performance in last week's loss to the Lions, making it interesting to see how he'd be used moving forward.
Well, it only took one game to find out.
After fellow defensive lineman Braiden McGregor was ruled out with a chest injury in the second half , Heflin's playing time increased, as he finished Sunday's loss with 16 defensive snaps—including seven pass-rush opportunities—which was an increase from the eight he saw in his Jets debut in Week 3. He didn't record any meaningful stats, but it's clear that New York sees Heflin as a viable fill-in option.
If McGregor misses time (whether that's a game or more), expect Heflin's snap count to continue growing.
Without Hall leading the backfield against the Bears, the Jets turned to Allen and Isaiah Davis as their lead running backs on the day. Although Allen had a solid day, given how New York's offense looked throughout the loss, Davis's performance could be described as anything but notable.
Despite the lack of Hall, the Jets didn't look Davis's way, as all 14 carries out of the backfield went to Allen. It'd be one thing if he'd at least been on the field a decent amount, but that wasn't the case either. Davis went from playing zero offensive snaps in the first three weeks to two on Sunday, which isn't exactly an encouraging increase. It means that even when Hall isn't playing, the Jets don't see giving him the ball as much of a priority.
Jets fans have been clamoring to see D'Angelo Ponds unleashed. The rookie cornerback's NFL career has started slowly, mainly due to the offseason injury situation that limited his availability. Ponds finally made his debut to the tune of two defensive snaps against the Lions last week, leaving those around Gotham hoping to see more.
Week 4 appeared to be another quiet outing for Ponds until fellow slot defender Jarvis Brownlee Jr. exited and didn't return due to a concussion (h/t Jets). Glenn then tabbed Ponds as the next man up, using the ex-Indiana Hoosier for 18 defensive snaps, with 14 coming in the slot. Although the rookie didn't come up with a pick or defended pass (he wasn't targeted), he did record a run stop and finished with PFF grades of 75.2 for run defense and 74.0 for tackling.
There's still a lot to learn about Brownlee's situation as he prepares to navigate the NFL's concussion protocol. In the meantime, the Jets will likely lean on Ponds as their No. 1 slot CB, with the upcoming Week 5 showdown vs. the Browns marking his first potential NFL start.
If that happens and Ponds looks more like a veteran than a first-year pro in the middle of the field, the Jets might have no choice but to increase his role for the rest of the season.

title: Jets Have 3 Advantages Over Bears in Week 4 (Here's Why It Matters)
full_text:
On paper, the New York Jets should feel confident going into their Week 4 showdown against the Chicago Bears. Despite a rash of injuries to nearly half of their starting offense, New York will play a backup quarterback for Chicago, who is also dealing with a slew of banged-up players.
Of course, just ask the Philadelphia Eagles if playing against a backup quarterback is actually beneficial.
Chicago's demolition of the Eagles on Monday with a third-string quarterback shows 1. How prepared they are each and every week, and 2. Injuries mean little to them.
For the Jets, their three matchup advantages will need to show out early and often on Sunday if they are to pull off an upset. Let's get to those matchups now.
Geno Smith has played some of the best football of his career through three games with the Jets. He hasn't made many mistakes, and looks the part of a viable starting quarterback. After torching the Lions in Week 3, he gets a Bears defense that has given up just 10 combined points in the last two games.
So why in the world is Smith an advantage over the Bears when Chicago's pass defense is ranked 12th in the league?
The reality is, despite missing several key starters, New York's offense can still move the football. They proved that last week in Detroit. While Chicago is a different beast, the Jets still have Garrett Wilson on the field. New York is also expected to have Kenyon Sadiq, who was the first tight end in team history to record over 100 yards receiving in a game since Dustin Keller.
Without Breece Hall, the Jets are going to need to rely on their passing offense to stay on schedule. Smith showed last week he could do it. And against a Bears defense that has played well, but doesn't have the talent to match Wilson or Sadiq, this is a game New York should still put up points in.
Some Jets fans are going to take this part the wrong way. I am not saying Aaron Glenn is a better head coach than Ben Johnson. Obviously that is a foolish thing to expect.
What I am saying, though, is that Glenn's defensive scheme is actually the perfect counter to Johnson's going into Sunday.
One of the reasons why the Eagles' defense was torched last week was due to the fact they run primarily zone concepts. Cover-4 and Quarters looks can be beaten with a patient quarterback who is in rhythm.
How do defenses get those signal-callers out of their comfort zone? By playing man coverage and disrupting receivers at the line of scrimmage. That is something Glenn has shown a willingness to do.
Chicago still has advantages across the board on offense. They run the ball well, and Johnson is creative enough to adjust to what other teams are doing. But when you play a backup quarterback, you want to blitz a heavy amount, and pound receivers at the line of scrimmage.
New York has done that through three weeks. That could give them an advantage.
Sadiq is listed as questionable going into Week 4 with a back injury . New York did, however, talk as though they expected him to play. If he doesn't it will be extremely difficult for the team to pull out an upset in Chicago.
For this exercise, we're going under the assumption that he will play. And if he does, he is a matchup nightmare for whoever the Bears throw at him.
Sadiq's breakout game against Detroit came in a lot of different ways. The crux of the issue, though, came because he was too big going up against nickel corners, too fast for linebackers, and too athletic for safeties. He is a true matchup nightmare that the Jets need to find a way to get the ball to.
If Sadiq plays, he becomes a central cog in a potential Jets upset. Chicago's linebackers, while good, aren't athletic enough to contain him.

title: Why David Bailey Is Jets' X-Factor vs. Bears in Week 4
full_text:
Through the first quarter of the season, the New York Jets should feel confident about their 2026 rookie class .
Each player who has seen the field, however how little of time they have been given, has made at least one play to show their potential. Chief among that production is 16th overall pick Kenyon Sadiq and second overall selection David Bailey.
Sadiq became the first Jets tight end to record 100 yards receiving in a game since Dustin Keller over a decade ago in New York's Week 3 loss to Detroit.
Bailey, meanwhile, leads the team in pressures and has two sacks and a forced fumble to his name already.
But as the Jets prepare for another contest against a playoff contender in the Chicago Bears, the organization knows they will need more production out of Bailey. The kind that is normally reserved for some of the top players at his position.
The stats surrounding the Jets defense have been impressive going into Week 4. They rank second overall in total yards allowed, third in passing yards allowed, and seventh against the run. New York has even improved in their pass rushing ability—sitting at 11th in the league.
Sacks aren't the only tally that proves if a defensive line is good, though. Gang Green has struggled mightily to get sustained pressure on opposing quarterbacks to start the season. They currently are ranked just 28th in the league in pressure rate.
It means that while the Jets are getting sacks, most of those are coming from blitzes, not in basic rushes with their four or five down linemen.
That needs to change going into Week 4, and Bailey must be the one to spearhead it.
It just so happens that Chicago's offensive line didn't give up a single sack and 10 light pressures last week in their Monday night win over the Philadelphia Eagles. If the Jets are going to be successful this week, even without Caleb Williams playing for Chicago, the team will need to bump those numbers up significantly.
Bailey will have his own challenge on the right side of the line. Darnell Wright is the game's highest-ranked right tackle by Pro Football Focus . Left Tackle Theo Benedet is considered league average, but is coming off another strong game.
Bailey will need to start winning one-on-one matchups faster than he has so far. If he can get consistent pressure on whoever is starting for the Bears on Sunday, then it could open the door for other pass rushers to get home as well.
New York's big problem is their players aren't winning one-on-one matchups across the board. It's caused a cascade of issues including forcing just one turnover as a collective defense this year.
Bailey dominated one-on-one matchups all camp. It's time for him to the very thing that he was brought in for.

title: McMullen: No More Hedging; The Eagles Need To Commit  On Offense
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA — Nick Sirianni said the quiet part out loud after Sunday’s 24-20 collapse against the Los Angeles Rams.
An offseason of hype had some casting Sean Mannion, a relative novice, as the next great offensive mind in the NFL. If anything, the Eagles have taken another step back from the version of this offense Kevin Patullo was vilified for running.
“Obviously, it hasn’t been good enough,” Sirianni understated . “... You’re trying to make sure as you find out who you are that you’re playing with detail and you’re playing together and you’re playing with toughness, and we’ve still got a ways to go there and it’s obvious that we’re still trying to figure [an identity] out.”
Four games into a season quickly losing steam that sentiment felt more like a confession than a nod to a process with light showing at the end of a tunnel.
The numbers from Lincoln Financial Field made the confession unnecessary.
The Eagles managed 172 total yards, their lowest in a dozen years, and 68 net passing yards, their lowest in a regular-season game in 23 years. They went 0-for-12 on third down, the first time they have failed to convert a single third down since at least 2000, and they have now failed on 17 straight third downs dating to the second half in Chicago.
Quarterback Jalen Hurts finished 12-of-27 for 93 yards. The two touchdowns to Darius Cooper were gift-wrapped by the defense and special teams. The Eagles' second-half offense continues a historically poor run and ranks last in the league in points, yards, yards per play, and expected points added.
Hurts’s answer, repeated until it lost any real meaning, was “poor execution.” Execution is real, but it only matters when the plan is sound and the players fail to carry it out. What is happening to Philadelphia right now does not look like that.
Mannion’s scheme was sold as a Shanahan/McVay-like wide-zone, under-center attack that would keep defenses honest and better marry the run and the pass. Through four weeks, it is a disjointed mess and those coaches may want to sue for libel for being connected to this disaster.
The Eagles’ under-center snaps have produced negative EPA that ranks near the bottom of the league. Defenses stack the box when Hurts is under center. When Philadelphia falls into obvious pass downs, it is getting blitzed as if Brian Flores had been cloned by every opponent.
The deeper problem is the gap between the roster and the idea.
This is still a team that needs to be built around Hurts’s dual-threat ability, Saquon Barkley’s gravity, and a line that has been among the league’s best when healthy. Mannion has not yet turned any of that into anything viable in his version og whatever you want to dub this offense.
Until the Eagles decide who they are — a wide-zone team that lives under center, a Hurts-centric spread attack, or something in between — the “poor execution” line will be used as cover for the more basic failure. Nobody is sure what this is even supposed to look like.

title: Grading Each Position After Eagles Loss To Rams: Bad Marks Across The Board
full_text:
If Philadelphia Eagles losses couldn't get any worse, Nick Sirianni's team found a way .
The Eagles blew a 10-point fourth quarter lead in Sunday's loss to the Los Angeles Rams, a game they somehow led despite not having five starters on offense. This was a game the Eagles weren't supposed to win , yet they found a way to lose in the worst of ways.
The defense collapsed and the offense was worse. Nick Sirianni made questionable decisions , and the Eagles are 2-2 as a result.
The report card for this week is ugly, and it might be the ugliest report card of the year. Here are the position-by-position grades for this week:
This may be a generous grade for Jalen Hurts, given he finished 12-of-27 for 93 yards. Hurts averaged just 3.4 yards per attempt, but he also threw for two touchdowns and ended up with a 78.2 passer rating.
Hurts was 2-of-9 for 10 yards and a 39.6 passer rating in the second half -- 1.1 yards per attempt. He couldn't get anything moving on offense, but was also without DeVonta Smith, Dallas Goedert, Saquon Barkley, Landon Dickerson and Lane Johnson on offense.
While Hurts has to elevate the offense, this offense is an absolute mess. Hurts is a square peg in a round hole right now, and teh Eagles don't have the personnel to help him out.
The Eagles have failed Jalen Hurts with the way this offense was built, and Hurts has struggled to adapt.
When Saquon Barkley is out for the game on his second carry, it's going to be a poor day for the running backs. Tank Bigsby didn't have a bad day (14 carries, 55 yards), but the explosiveness isn't there without Barkley and a healthy offensive line.
Even if the offensive line were healthy, the holes weren't there for the backs outside of one drive. Will Shipley had six carries for 23 yards and the two combined averaged 3.9 yards per carry.
The Eagles are what they are at running back without Barkley.
Without DeVonta Smith, the wide receiver position isn't strong. Dontayvion Wicks is a good player, but the mindset changes as a WR1 compared to a WR2. He finished with just three catches for 18 yards, and couldn't make a play to get the pass game going.
Darius Cooper could, as his two touchdown catches are the only reason this grade is as high as it is. Makai Lemon was also open on a few plays, but Jalen Hurts couldn't get the ball to him due to the offensive line not protecting him.
The Eagles needed Smith on Sunday. They won't have him for a few games, so this group will be tested.
This position isn't good, relying on 36-year-old Zach Ertz to even be competent. Ertz had two catches for 13 yards, while Johnny Mundt and E.J. Jenkins had a goose egg in the box score.
Mundt played an overwhelming majority of the snaps (80%), compared to Ertz's 21% and Jenkins' 20%. Known as a good blocker, Mundt wasn't good at doing that Sunday either.
This is a bad tight end group that really needs Goedert.
Somehow this unit gets worse and worse by the week.
Without Lane Johnson, Markel Bell is called upon to start in emergency duty -- and his first start didn't go well. Bell allowed six pressures and an 18.8% pressure rate allowed per dropback, completely being exposed on the right side.
Cam Jurgens allowed five pressures and a 12.5% pressure rate allowed per dropback. Drew Kendall allowed three pressures and a 9.4% pressure rate allowed per dropback. All three players were awful in pass protection on Sunday, and they're the different players from the Week 1 offensive line.
The Rams blitzed Jalen Hurts obsessively because they could. Bell and Jurgens weren't stoping them , as the right side and interior of the offensive line were exposed. The push up front wasn't good either on run plays as Bigsby averaged 0.57 yards before contact per carry and Shipley was at 0.67.
This is a bad offensive line, and will be slightly better if Johnson does decide to come back.
The pass rush just don't get enough pressure on the quarterback, no matter when it occurs in the game. Nolan Smith did have a sack, but he also had two missed tackles and a 5.7% pressure rate. Jalyx Hunt had three pressures and a 7.7% pressure rate.
Jonathan Greenard is a difference maker, and his pressure did lead to the Andrew Mukuba interception in the first half. Greenard did have a 21.4% pressure rate, but this unit took a major hit once he left with an ankle injury.
Greenard is a good player, but it's fair to question that contract. He just can't stay on the field.
The wrist injury is affecting Jalen Carter, who had three pressures in 52 pass rushing snaps. Carter wasn't a difference maker on Sunday, although the Eagles are paying him to be one. He did have a quarterback hit for what it's worth.
Jordan Davis played 25 snaps and didn't have a pressure, not even seeing close to as many snaps as Carter and Moro Ojomo. While Ojomo had a 9.1% pressure rate, his plays doesn't make up for the lack of production the Eagles are getting from Carter and Davis.
This is an overpaid, underperforming group.
The missed tackle on the Kyren Williams touchdown late in the game is the play that highlighted Jeremiah Trotter Jr. -- but he had a good game. Trotter Jr. finished with 15 tackles, five of which were against the run (10 were solo tackle).
Jihaad Campbell had nine tackles and two pressures, and has shown he can rush the passer. Now for the coverage numbers for both...
Campbell was targeted 12 times and allowed 80 yards, as Matthew Stafford had an 85.4 passer rating targeting him. This was better than Campbell has performed in previous weeks. Trotter. Jr. allowed 7-of-8 passes targeted his way for 49 yards and a 92.2 passer rating -- but no 20+ yard completions.
Trotter Jr. deserves to be on the field somewhere.
Seeing the fire from Quinyon Mitchell on Davante Adams was excellent to see, but the Rams passing game challenged the outside cornerbacks. Mitchell allowed just three catches for 27 yards, but Tariq Woolen was picked on throughout the game.
Woolen allowed three catches for 91 yards and a 99.8 passer rating when targeted (one touchdown), with two 20+ yard completions and one coverage penalty. This was Woolen's worst game with the Eagles, but he's been very good through four games.
Cooper DeJean had an interception and allowed a 0.0 passer rating in coverage. DeJean has either been great in the slot -- or horrible. The Eagles got a great game from DeJean Sunday.
Surprised to see a grade this high? That's because the safeties played well on Sunday.
Mukuba did have two missed tackles, but he also had an intercpetion and allowed just two yards in coverage. He was all over the field, and not getting exposed as much.
Perhaps that's because Michael Carter was playing next to him. Carter was targeted three times and allowed just seven yards in coverage. His range in coverage showed when targeted and appeared to get more comfortable playing safety as the game went on.
The safeties were good on Sunday, which is way better than they've been the first three games.
Jake Elliott hit a 56-yard field goal and was 2-of-2 on field goal attempts, remaining perfect on the season. Britain Covey averaged 19.7 yards per punt return, including a 41-yard return that led to a touchdown two plays later.
Smael Mondon made plays on kickoff coverage to prevent big returns and Kelee Ringo had a good tackle in punt coverage. Braden Mann was his usual self, having two punts inside the 20-yard line and averaged 43.8 net yards per punt.
The Eagles may have been awful Sunday. Their special teams were not.
