title: Eagles Stock Report After Rams Collapse:  How Offense Is Affecting Jalen Hurts' Future
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA - What looked like a story of perseverance turned with a Nick Sirianni gamble with 7:32 left in the game and the Eagles leading the Los Angeles Rams by a 20-10 margin.
Instead of taking a chip shot Jake Elliott field goal and extending the lead to 23-10, Sirianni went for the kill shot. Philadelphia's problematic passing game came up empty leaving the door for a talented but underachieving Rams team, which took the momentum shift and sling-shotted it to 14 points over the final 7:26, culminating with a tremendous Kyren Williams 7-yard run with 70 seconds remaining.
The collapse ruined a storybook ending in which the Eagles' lost three of there top stars. Right tackle Lane Johnson was ruled out 90 minutes before the game due to a personal matter while running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) and All-Pro cornerback Quinyon Mitchell (knee) were lost to injury. Philadelphia had also come in knowing it would be without star receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and All-Pro linebacker Zack Baun (knee).
Six days ago the Eagles could do nothing to stop Case Keenum during an ugly loss to the Chicago Bears. On Sunday, Philadelphia made the reigning MVP and future Hall of Famer Matthew Stafford looks like a third-string quarterback for most of the game, stunning the overhyped Rams for 53 minutes of football.
You have to play 60, though.
A mistake prone LA offense, featuring two interceptions by Stafford and two mind-numbing personal fouls calls that wiped out positive plays was complemented by an awful special teams performance and a defense without Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald that allowed just enough big plays to falter.
Aesthetic football has rarely been the Eagles thing in the Sirianni/Jalen Hurts era but winning has and no other number proved that more that Sirianni's personal record of 4-0 against the highly-regarded Sean McVay.
That formula almost worked again until it didn't
Turnovers: The Eagles defense forced their first turnover of the season on the Rams' first drive when a ferocious Jonathan Greenard rush resulted in a Drew Mukuba interception. The takeaway drought marked the second most defensive snaps before the first turnovers for a Vic Fangio unit since 2016. The longest came in 2019 when Fangio was the head coach in Denver, which did not have a defensive takeaway until Week 5 that season.
The idea that turnovers come in bunches was boosted later when Cooper DeJean hauled in a no-look Stafford pass that set up the Eagles to steal a late touchdown right before halftime. Winning the turnover margin only goes so far when you're outgained by a 415 to 172 margin.
Coop! - No, not that Coop. DeJean certainly played well and is starting to come out of his early-season funk but Darius Cooper was the one receiver Hurts seemed to trust without Smith and Dallas Goedert. The 2025 undrafted free agent saved Hurts from an interception by high-pointing the football over Quentin Lake for one TD, and then uncovered in the back of the end zone for the second consecutive week for No. 2.
Jake the Make: Jake Elliott looks back to the old Jake Elliott. He's 2-for-2 outside of 55 yards so far this season. Overall he's now 4-for-4 on FGs on the season and hasn't missed an extra point.
Being Bold: While Sirianni will take plenty of heat, the analytics argue that the Eagles would have only needed a 13% chance to convert the fourth-and-two that kickstarted the Rams. The value of leading by 13 vs. 10 is negligible and actually would have given the Rams far better field position on the subsequent kickoff with the goal of two touchdowns only clearer for Los Angeles.
Third-downs: The Eagles were a dismal 0-for-12 on high-leverage downs and dating back to Chicago, they've failed to convert their last 17 tries on third down. Sirianni noted everything is contributing but the hear is growing on the idea of hiring a first-year offensive coordinator with no play-calling experience.
The Tush Push: Philadelphia failed on a fourth-and-one tush-push attempt despite super-charging it with the presence of Willie Lampkin to push Hurts. The Eagles should transition to spreading out opposiing defenses who are now plugging the A-gaps and allowing the powerful Hurts to pick and choose.
The pass rush: Greenard provided some juice early but at the end of the day the Eagles had just one sack by Nolan Smith and are on pace for just 17 sacks this season.
Right-Handed: Hurts has always had a propensity to flush right when in trouble and that default setting is only increasing. The Eagles' QB1 is flushing right on his dropbacks 16.7% of the time through four weeks, according to SumerSports. That number was 11.9% last season, 12.8% in 2024, 10.5% in 2023 and 10.4% in 2022.
Blitzkrieg: Hurts was just 5 of 15 for 46 yards when blizted by the Rams. The lack of effiency was glaring and it's been consistently bad so far this season. This was Hurts second-lowest EPA performance against the blitz out of the 89 games where he was blitzed at least five times. Week 1 was his sixth lowest EPA performance and Week 3 was his ninth lowest per SumerSports.

title: 4 Biggest Takeaways From Eagles Collapse: Letting Jeff Stoutland Go Was A Mistake
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles collapsed. There's no other way to describe a blown 10-point lead midway through the fourth quarter,
There are many ways to digest the latest defeat that put the Eagles to 2-2, a game that wasn't expected to be a win at kickoff put played its way into a potential victory. Only to see the win taken away from them.
Nick Sirianni is partially to blame . So is the offense, along with the defense allowing 14 points in the final 7:31. Let's focus on the offensive incompetance in the biggest takeaways from this loss, and why this offense is a major problem.
The Eagles tried to downplay Stoutland's impact on this offensive line. The new scheme was easier and favorable to players, a few of the offensive linemen said this summer.
That doesn't mean the scheme is better. That doesn't mena the players are coached up better, or developed.
Markel Bell allowed five pressures in his first start, a late entry at right tackle after Lane Johnson couldn't go for personal reasons. His pressure rate allowed per dropback was 15.6%.
Cam Jurgens isn't a left guard, as he allowed three pressures on Sunday -- a pressure rate allowed per dropback of 9.4%. Through three games, Jurgens has allowed a pressure rate allowed per dropback of 7.5%.
Drew Kendall has been okay at center, but he had a pressure rate allowed per dropback at 6.3% on Sunday. Tyler Steen was at 6.3% too, not taking the next step from last season.
This offensive line was mediocre last season -- with Stoutland. The Eagles partially blamed him for the struggles and the development of players, thinking Chris Kuper was the answer.
We're seeing why Kuper was available, and why his contract wasn't renewed. The proof is in the pudding.
Evaluating Jalen Hurts is hard enough, whether he has the personnel around him or not (he doesn't this year). Take away the Eagles' RB1, TE1, WR1, LG1, and RT1 and the puzzle is even harder.
Hurts was bad on Sunday, there's no sugarcoating it. He was 12-of-27 for 93 yards and two touchdowns -- somehow finishing with a 78.2 passer rating despite 3.4 yards per attempt. He was 2-of-9 for 10 yards in the second half -- 1.1 yards per attempt.
Hurts is 2-of-10 for 18 yards on third and fourth down. He was 5-of-16 for 46 yards and a touchdown in the pocket -- 2.9 yards per attempt (61.5 rating).
While Hurts was bad, what chance did he have to execute at a high level -- especially after Barkley injured his hamstring on the first series? Zach Ertz wasn't even on the team two weeks ago, and he was the best receiving tight end. Makai Lemon just isn't ready for a starting role at wide receiver either.
Dontayvion Wicks is a good player, but he's not a WR1. Darius Cooper was the only playmaker on offense, and that includes Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley (who are backups for a reason).
The offensive line is bad and can't protect Hurts either. It was impressive Hurts threw for two touchdowns given the circumstances. The Eagles can't even run the offense they want to run given the personnel they have on the field.
Hurts just disn't have a chance to make plays with what he had on Sunday. That's the reality.
Prior to the game, there were plenty of questions when it came to how this football team was built. The Eagles had three quarterbacks active for the game, and already made a change at QB2 with Tanner McKee taking over for Andy Dalton.
With Lane Johnson out, the Eagles had just two tackles on the active roster -- Jordan Mailata and Markel Bell (Fred Johnson was also out). The Eagles also had four tight ends active, two of whcih weren't even on the team two weeks ago.
The Week 1 center is now the left guard. The current cneter played guard all summer. The right tackle played just one snap in his career.
The first-round draft pick isn't ready for the role he's in. The second-round draft pick is on injured reserve, and was poor when he was on the field in training camp. The third-round pick was the right tackle on Sunday, as he's learning a new position this year.
More than fair to criticize what Howie Roseman give Nick Sirianni and his coaching staff to work with. The depth on this offense just isn't there and there are too many players at certain positions that aren't necessary.
The Eagles were hoping Makai Lemon would be the WR3 or the primary slot option. They traded up for him to specifically play that role. Lemon had three catches for 27 yards in his 42 snaps, good for him but not what the Eagles thought they'd get when they drafted him.
Lemon was supposed to make an instant impact, not have 10 catches for 65 yards through four games. he hasn't helped this passing attack -- or lack thereof.
Eli Stowers was bad in the spring and in the summer. He was placed on injured reserve with a hamstring and quad injury, but he wouldn't have helpe dthis tight end room immediately either.
Stowers was supposed to be the TE2. The Eagles had to keep four tight ends, and expose this offense to Johnny Mundt and E.J. Jenkins more due to Stowers' lack of development.
Markel Bell learned right tackle this summer, but immensely struggled in his first start. A 15.6% pressure rate allowed per dropback shows Bell wasn't ready to fill in on short notice.
This is only chaper one of their careers. but the Eagles banked on Lemon and Stowers to help this team immediately. This is the result of that reliance.
The offense is bad, and both are playing a major role in that.

title: Why Eagles Believe They Can Respond After Fourth Quarter Collapse
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – The Eagles may have arrived at an early crossroads in their season.
There is still plenty of season remaining, but after losing two straight games – one in a blowout last Monday to the Bears, the other in a meltdown on Sunday to the Rams – there is definitely a whiff of desperation as they head to London looking to beat a Jaguars team that moved to 3-1 by beating the Bengals in Cincinnati on Sunday.
“Here's what I do know is there's gonna be panic on the outside, and there's gonna be understandably a lot of frustration on the inside, but we were 2-2 in the Super Bowl year, and there's kind of like a sigh of relief in a way when everyone writes you off, where you just say, ‘OK, now the only thing that matters is everyone in this room,’ and I have a feeling that's probably gonna happen,” said Eagles punt returner Britain Covey, whose 41-yard punt return into the red zone set up a touchdown that gave the Eagles a 13-3 lead with 5:44 to play in the second quarter.
“You're gonna get written off as a team and, and in a way it's kind of a unique situation. You wish it wasn't needing that, but it's a unique way to come together as a team because you're all you have.”
Right now, though, there’s little to hang a hat on, though some players saw things a bit differently.
“I think there's a lot of things we can take away from this game,” said Cooper DeJean, whose interception late in the first half set up a touchdown with three seconds to go. “I don't think anybody's worried. I still feel like there's a lot of confidence in, in this locker room. There's definitely things we can build off of that we did in this game, and obviously things that we can clean up. The biggest thing is finishing the game.”
-The Eagles were banged up coming in and got even more banged up during the game, losing Saquon Barkley, Jonathan Greenard, and Quinyon Mitchell. Lane Johnson wasn’t available due to a personal matter just hours before kickoff, a move that left the Eagles with 47 available players, not the 48 allowed by the NFL on game day.
-The Eagles have been dreadful in the third quarter through four games, going three-and-out on nine of their 11 possessions in that quarter.
-On Sunday, they were 0-for-12 on third down and 1-for-4 on fourth down. They had just 12 first downs.
“I've got a ton of confidence in [Offensive Coordinator] Sean [Mannion] and he's going to wear a lot of this,” said head coach Nick Sirianni. “There's no doubt. I'm going to wear a lot of this. Our offense is going to wear a lot of this. You win together, you lose together. I have no complaints on what happened there today. There's opportunity for us all to grow following this game, win, lose, draw.”
While the Eagles were 2-2 in their 2024 Super Bowl season, they emerged from their bye week with a renewed emphasis on the running game. Saquon Barkley reeled off a 2,000-yard season.
Jalen Hurts said they need to “double down” on the work.
“This is a team that is building and finding its way,” said the quarterback. “It's obviously a work in progress. I have the utmost confidence in this team. I have the utmost confidence in this group. We just have to remain endured, be persistent, and keep committing to one another, keep committing to the work of becoming a better group together.”

title: Inside The Eagles Collapse: How Nick Sirianni Instigated The 4th Quarter Disaster
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles had a 10-point lead over the Los Angeles Rams with 7:31 to play.
Nick Sirianni was facing a fourth-and-goal at the Rams' 2-yard line. His offense had 81 yards in the second half to this point, coming off three striaght possessions involving a three-and-out and a turnover on downs.
The Eagles didn't have Saquon Barkley, Lane Johnson, Dallas Goedert, Landon Dickerson, and DeVonta Smith -- five of their starters from Week 1 not on offense. The center (Drew Kendall) didn't start in Week 1 and the left guard (Cam Jurgens) never played left guard before Week 2 of this season.
Sirianni mad ethe decision to make it a three-score game. Build a 20-10 lead to 27-10, and put the Rams in a "true backed up" situation. Those were his words.
There was nothing wrong with Sirianni's decision in the moment. Going for it is perfectly acceptable.
The circumstances called for the conservative decision.
Take the points. Take the 13-point lead with 7:31 left. Force the Rams to score two touchdowns, which they would had needed regardless if the Eagles kicked a 20-yard field goal.
The decision made by Sirianni was fine. He wa sgoing for the win, the three-score lead. A touchdown makes it 27-10 and makes the Rams have to score two touchdowns and kick a field goal. There's no guarantee if they even get three possessions in the final 7:31.
If the Eagles weren't down their WR1, TE1, RB1, RT1, and LG1, it make plenty of sense to trust the analytics and go for it. The analytics don't put that into the equation.
Sirianni won't use injuries as an excuse. No coach will, as they'll play with the hand they're dealt.
Coaches trust their personnel, but they have to be observant of what's in the room. The Eagles lost Barkley in the game -- and Johnson before it. They were already down Dickerson, Smith, and Goedert heading into Sunday.
The Eagles lined up Makai Lemon on the outside, Darius Cooper in the slot and E.J. Jenkins in the slot. Tank Bigsby was the running back and Markel Bell was the right tackle.
Lemon rarely plays outside. Jenkins hardly plays at all.
Bigsby is the RB2 and Bell wa splaying in his first career game -- and had his struggles. How did Sirianni think this was going to work?
The Eagles couldn't run the ball in on three plays. The offensive line struggled to block all afternoon. Dontayvion Wicks -- who was lined up on the right side -- was shut down the entire second half. The pass game was shut down the entire second half, as Jalen Hurts had 5 passing yards at that point.
For some reason, Sirianni was oblivious to what he had surrounding him. Or he flat out ignored it.
The personnel available was the signal to kick. Go up 13 and take the shot with a defense taht had two takeaways and looked like a top-5 defense for the first 52:30 of the game.
The Eagles went for it, and didn't conver. Even though the Rams were backed up at their own 2-yard line, they had life.
There was no guarantee the Rams would have scored two touchdowns if they were down 13. Knowing you need two touchdowns compared to a touchdown and a field goal is a completely different mindset.
The Rams have professional football players, but professionals are human too. Players do press when they need two touchdowns with limited time left, chasing the big play as the clock ticks down.
Once the Rams got the first touchdown, they needed a field goal and the mindset changed. If the Rams were down 13, they needed two touchdowns in two possessions. They score the first touchdown -- they still need to score the second.
The game changed once the Rams got into field goal range with 1:37 left. If the Rams still needed a touchdown, they're forcing their way into the end zone -- and the Eagles defense is playing different towards keeping them out.
Even if the Rams get the second touchdown, the Eagles only need a field goal -- even with all the offensive struggles. A play can change the complexion in the final minute, and Jake Elliott was 2-for-2 on 50+ yard field goals this season.
There are so many variables at play being up 13 as opposed to 10, just like being up 17 as opposed to 13. The field goal seemed like a safer bet than converting a 4th-and-goal.
Sirianni's decision was understandable. He just didn't think it the whole way through in the short amount of time he had.
That's why he's the head coach. He made a decision that has a lot of layers, whether he went for it or kicked.
Given what Sirianni had in front of him? He should have kicked.
This offense just isn't good enough, whether they had those players available or not. Given the Eagles were missing five starters, the decision to kick should have been an easy one.

title: Instant Obvervations From Eagles Collapse To Rams: What Were They Doing?!
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – The Eagles will jet across the Atlantic Ocean later this week, dragging a heavy anchor into their Week 5 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. That anchor is a two-game losing streak, following a 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday.
The Eagles, now 2-2, led 20-10 when Jalen Hurts threw an incomplete pass on fourth-and-goal from the 2-yard line with 7:26 to play.
The Rams kicked it into high gear from there. Their offense ripped off a 98-yard drive that needed just nine plays and used 3:27 of clock. Their defense then forced a three-and-out from the Eagles’ offense – nothing new about that – to get the ball back with 2:55 left. The offense then went 79 on 10 plays in just 1:45 to win the game and get back to .500 at 2-2.
The win was Sean McVay’s first against Nick Sirianni. He is now 1-4 against the Eagles’ head coach.
The Eagles made a questionable call to go for it on fourth-and-goal midway through the fourth quarter to go up six. Perhaps had they kicked a chip shot field goal, they would have only needed a field goal when they got the ball back with 65 seconds.
Not that it mattered. Hurts was sacked twice on their last possession, and Philly couldn’t get a first down. The Eagles were 0-12 on third down and had just 12 first downs. Hurts threw for just 93 yards, and the Eagles had just 172 total yards.
This was a game the Eagles weren’t supposed to win. They had an injury list as long as an arm coming in, then added to it when running back Saquon Barkley went out early with a hamstring injury in the first quarter, and cornerback Quinyon Mitchell was lost with a knee injury and outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard went out with an ankle injury, both in the third quarter.
Even oddsmakers installed them as three-point underdogs. In their own home.
So, it was a loss not entirely unexpected. Except they played well enough to steal it.
The Eagles entered the game without receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and linebacker Zack Baun (concussion). Smith will reportedly miss another game or two.
Tight end Dallas Goedert and safety Marcus Epps also missed the game with injuires.
The Eagles were stung when Lane Johnson couldn’t play due to a personal matter. With Fred Johnson already ruled out with an injury, the Eagles had to start Markel Bell and hope both he and Jordan Mailata made it through the game healthy because they had only seven linemen active. They did.
The Eagles only had 47 players active for the game. The league allows 48 players to dress, but Philly called up two tight ends on Saturday, not knowing Johnson would not play.
Despite the loss, the Eagles did some decent things.
The Eagles finally got their first two of the season and scored 10 points off them. They were interceptions by Drew Mukuba and Cooper DeJean. Mukuba's first-quarter pick led to a 29-yard field goal from Jake Elliott, the first points the Eagles scored in the first quarter all year. DeJean’s pick came late in the first half and led to a 10-yard touchdown catch from Darius Cooper, giving the Eagles a 20-10 lead at the break.
Darius Cooper’s 10-yard touchdown catch in the back of the end zone with three seconds left in the first half was reminiscent of his 3-yard TD catch with nine seconds left in the game against the Titans in a Week 2 win. Cooper also had a nifty TD catch when he seemed to rip the ball away from Rams defender Quentin Lake in the end zone from 18 yards out. He now leads the team in touchdown catches with three, passing injured Dallas Goedert, who has two.
Yes, the Eagles got one, and they now have four. Nolan Smith got home and has two of those this season. He would have had another one, but it was erased by a holding penalty against Quinyon Mitchell. Smith played a strong game from his edge post, logging several pressures.
Without Zack Baun, Jeremiah Trotter, Jr., made just the second start of his career, which is in its third year. Trotter made 15 tackles. Jihaad Campbell stepped up in Baun’s absence, too. He helped break up a pass on fourth-and-8 early in the fourth quarter to get the Eagles the ball back on downs. Campbell had nine tackles. He was picked on in the pass game, though. Credit McVay for exploiting matchup involving the second-year linebacker.
THIRD DOWNS AND THIRD QUARTERS
The Eagles were 0-for-9 on that down through three quarters. And speaking of the third quarter, the Eagles' struggles continued. They went three-and-out twice and four-and-out once. They have now gone three-and-out nine times in 11 third-quarter possessions this season. The result was the Eagles were shut out of the scoring column in the second half on Sunday.
Markel Bell did some good and bad, about what you’d expect after not learning that he would start until Sunday morning when Johnson could not play due to personal reasons.
Bell made some blocks that stood out, but there was also one play when he didn’t block anybody, and Hurts ended up getting sacked. The thinking is that the third-round draft pick is only going to get better, especially if he can prepare during the week as the starter. Hurts was sacked four times overall.

title: Eagles Projected Offense Starters In Major Trouble With Lane Johnson Out Against Rams
full_text:
Add Lane Johnson to the list of offensive starters the Philadelphia Eagles won't have on Sunday.
Johnson is out of Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Rams due to personal issues. He was dealing with some personal issues with his parents during the summer and admitted this is likely his final NFL season, but why he's missing Sunday's game is unknown.
Withpout Johnson, Markel Bell will start at right tackle -- and the Eagles will be down three starters on offense.
Not ideal for a football team that won't have it's starting wide receiver (DeVonta Smith) and starting tight end (Dallas Goedert) this week. Dontayvion Wicks will be the WR1 and Zach Ertz -- who wasn't on the roster two weeks ago -- will be the TE1.
This isn't ideal at all for the Eagles, who already have their problems scoring points and moving the ball. Due to personnel issues, offensive coordinator Sean mannion hasn't been able to run the offense he wanted -- and it's showing in the statistics.
The Eagles are 23rd in yards per game (302.3), 14th in yards per play (5.3), and 22nd in offensive points per game (18.3%). They are seventh in the NFL in plays run from shotgun (67.4%) and 30th in the league in three-and-out percentage (3.4%). They lead the NFL in plays running "11 personnel at 76.7% due to the lack of depth at tight end.
This is the projected starting lineup the Eagles are going with on Sunday. How will they find ways to score points?
The Eagles are down three straters, inlcuding their best wide receiver, tight end, and offensive lineman. They're also down their WR4, so they're thin at that position as well.
Elijah Moore -- who played just six offensive snaps all yeear -- is the WR4. Makai Lemon -- who has struggled to catch up and get acclimated to the speed of the NFL game, is the WR2. Darius Cooper, -- who the Eagles won't play over Lemon for whatever reason -- is the WR3.
Ertz didn't even get the most snaps at tight end last week. Johnny Mundt and E.J. Jenkins -- who both have a combined 3 catches for 12 yards this seaosn -- are the TE2 and TE3.
Markel Bell -- who has played one offensive snaps in his career -- is starting at right tackle. Even Fred Johnson is out this week.
How the Eagles will score points against the Rams is anyone's guess. Same with Jalen Hurts being able to protect himself.
This could be ugly on Sunday, but we'll have to wait and see.

title: The Three Matchups That Should Decide Eagles-Rams
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA — The Eagles’ margin for error in Week 4 was already small after a 27-7 loss in Chicago. Arguably, it’s gotten even thinner against the talented Los Angeles Rams, with DeVonta Smith and Zack Baun both ruled out.
Three matchups should decide whether Philadelphia can bounce back at Lincoln Financial Field.
Smith (hamstring) and Dallas Goedert (knee) are already ruled out, which strips Jalen Hurts of his two most reliable pass-catchers and leaves Dontayvion Wicks, rookie Makai Lemon and Zach Ertz to carry the majority of receiving load.
Those Eagles' absences change the math for Chris Shula and the LA defense, which is without superstars Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald.
The Rams typically live in sub packages — an NFL-high 36.3 percent of their defensive snaps have come in dime — and they have yet to allow a rush of 20-plus yards. They rank No. 11 overall in rush defense.
Saquon Barkley is the counter for Philadelphia. He has 174 yards on 34 carries through three games, a 5.1 average, but the production has been front-loaded: 137 yards on 21 first-half carries, 37 yards on 13 in the second half.
Barkley has a strong history against the Rams as an Eagles, topping the 200-yard barrier against LA on two occasions in 2024.
Without Smith stretching the field and forcing extra attention on the perimeter, Philadelphia’s best path is a heavy dose of Barkley that makes Los Angeles come out of dime and play more base.
If the Rams stay light in the box and still bottle Barkley up on early downs, the Eagles’ already uneven offense that is near the bottom of the league in three-and-out rate has little else to hang its hat on.
Matthew Stafford is coming off a night in Denver in which he was sacked four times and pressured on 45.8 percent of his dropbacks.
Against a clean pocket, the reigning MVP has looked like himself. Under pressure he has been ordinary, including 5-of-18 for 61 yards and an interception against the Broncos.
The goal has to be speeding Stafford up and getting him off his spots. However, the Eagles’ pass rush has been been pedestrian so far with only three sacks in three games, 28th in the league.
Jonathan Greenard is expected to play a larger role after a pitch-count debut in Chicago, Jalyx Hunt has been generating some pressure without finishing, and Jalen Carter is playing through a hairline wrist fracture.
In the two 2024 wins over Los Angeles, Philadelphia sacked Stafford five times each. Last year’s meeting produced only one sack, and the Eagles still needed a blocked field goal on the game’s final play.
A four-man rush that actually moves Stafford off his spot will be the difference between persevering against Puka Nacua and Davante Adams in coverage vs. getting overrun.
Baun, an All-Pro who’s one of the better coverage linebackers in football, is in the concussion protocol and ruled out.
Jeremiah Trotter Jr. will start next to Jihaad Campbell and wear the green dot. Trotter’s only prior starts came in Week 18 games when the Eagles rested starters. He is regarded as a high-IQ, instinctive player who is best when going downhill. However, Trotter is not the athlete or playmaker in space that Baun is.
That will matter against a Rams offense that leads the league and ranks second in passing, with Nacua back alongside Adams and Kyren Williams.
Baun’s absence will almost put more of the intermediate and crossing game in Sean McVay’s crosshairs.
The Eagles are also without veteran safety Marcus Epps, so the communication burden in the middle of the field is shared by a thinner group than the one that held Stafford under 200 yards last September — a night Baun opened with an interception.

title: Six Thoughts And A  Prediction For Eagles-Rams: Overcoming Injuries Will Be Challenging
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – Six players are out for the Eagles, four of whom are starters. So, of course, they’ll beat the Rams, right?
They still have Jalen Hurts, and the quarterback gives the Eagles a chance to win most weeks, but without two receivers, DeVonta Smith and Hollywood, without tight end Dallas Goedert, and backup offensive tackle Fred Johnson. The defense wasn’t spared, either, and will be without starting linebacker Zack Baun and starting safety Marcus Epps.
It’s remarkable, really. It’s only Week 4 and the Eagles health is in shambles. Sitting at 2-1 and coming off a blowout loss in Chicago, the Eagles need to find a way to get back on track, but it won't be easy.
Perhaps this bears remembering: Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni is 4-0 against the Rams’ Sean McVay. The last time L.A. beat the Eagles was in Doug Pedersons’s final season as the head coach, on Sept. 20, 2020.
Here are six thoughts on the game with a final score prediction:
ZACH ERTZ AND JONATHAN GREENARD
Sirianni was fond of saying that his offense runs through 6, 11, and 88 – Smith, A.J. Brown, and Goedert. Brown is gone and Smith and Goedert are injured. Ertz played 19 snaps after signing with the Eagle days before they went to Chicago. Expect more this time out and he could have more than the one catch he had against the Bears.
Greenard played 18 snaps. It was a good start, but his role should increase, especially with two starters gone.
Ready or not, the backup linebacker who had an excellent summer will make his third career start in two-plus years.
It’s been a mess for the Eagles, with seven of their nine drives over the third quarter ending in three-and-outs, and they have scored just six points in that span through three games. Will they have this game-killer fixed by kickoff?
“As a staff and as a team, we're working through getting better there,” said OC Sean Mannion. “You hate to do a lot of nice things in the first half of some of these games and kind of fall into a rut in the second half. It's something we've been discussing each week, looking to get sharper and sharper as a unit and as a staff. I think we got some good things to work on there, some good thoughts moving into this week of how to improve on that.”
If the underdog Eagles hope to pull an upset, it could be with a big play in this part of the game. Look at last year, when the Eagles blocked not one, but two field goal tries from Joshua Karty. The final kick would have given L.A. a walk-off win, but Jordan Davis swatted it, scooped it, and scored it.
The Rams brought in a new kicker halfway through last season, replacing Karty with Harrison Mevis.
“I think Mevis has done a really good job ever since he came in halfway through the season,” said Eagles special teams coordinator Michael Clay. “He does a really good job with the elevation. They've done a really good job of shoring up their field goal pro, but there's always things we're going to try and look at in terms of where can we possibly dent and get around it.”
That’s the number of turnovers and sacks, respectively, the Eagles defense has. The three sacks are the 29th-worst in the league. At least they aren’t the Dolphins, who don’t have any sacks, but the teams are close. If Greenard’s role grows, he could be the one to add to the total.
As for the 0 turnovers, well, Matthew Stafford just broke an NFL-record after throwing his 34th pick-6 interception in this, his 18th season. Maybe the Eagles can get one.
The Eagles have it up three times on Monday night and are now 0-5 in takeaway/giveaway. That’s not the recipe for a successful season. Tank Bigsby’s fumble at his team’s 15 is hard to forgive. He only played two snaps in Chicago, and none after he coughed it up.
Sirianni was asked during the week would be required to handle a Rams team that is talented and motivated after falling to 1-2 last week with a loss against the Broncos.
“We're motivated also, and I have a lot of respect for this football team,” he responded. “We're going to have to play our best game to date.” The Eagles could do that, and it might still not be enough. Without the Injured Six, the task is a lot bigger.

title: What Steelers Are Getting in Marte Mapu
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have made a few veteran additions on the defensive side of the ball after their Week 4 loss on Thursday Night Football to the Cleveland Browns.
Prior to signing cornerback Sean Murphy-Bunting to their 53-man roster from the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' practice squad, KPRC 2 Houston's Aaron Wilson reported that the Steelers also added linebacker Marte Mapu to their practice squad.
Given the struggles of Pittsburgh's inside linebackers over the past season-plus in addition to the tackling issues that have plagued the team, perhaps Mapu could eventually come up from the practice squad and provide a little bit of a spark in the middle of the defense.
A third-round pick by Bill Belichick and the New England Patriots in the 2023 NFL Draft, Mapu played in all 17 of the team's games as a rookie and made one start. Over that span, he logged 18 tackles and a forced fumble while garnering 204 snaps on defense and 217 on special teams.
In 2024, Mapu was on the field for 486 of New England's defensive snaps and 113 of their special teams reps over 10 games (nine starts) after spending the early part of the season on the reserve/injured list with a calf injury.
Mapu also dealt with a neck injury that year, though he did log 46 tackles, three forced fumbles and an interception when he was out on the field.
During the 2025 campaign, Mapu largely filled a special teams role for the Patriots in Mike Vrabel's first year as the team's head coach.
He played 120 defensive snaps and 255 on special teams, closing out the season with 25 tackles, a forced fumble and an interception while also adding a tackle during New England's run to Super Bowl LX, where they lost to the Seattle Seahawks.
Mapu was later traded to the Houston Texans this past offseason, but was waived from IR before final roster cuts with an injury settlement.
He worked out for the Steelers on October 2, and now he'll have a chance to potentially make an impact for them this season.
At 6-foot-3 and 230 pounds, Mapu is not a thumper or much of a difference-maker against the run. His tackling took a major step forward in 2025, as Pro Football Focus credited him with having a missed tackle rate of 0.0 percent, though his career mark is still dubious in that regard at 13.5 percent.
Mapu's greatest quality is both his usefulness as a special teamer as well as his versatility on the defensive side of the ball, particularly in coverage.
A hybrid defender who can spend time at both inside linebacker and safety while also having the ability to play in the slot, Mapu is a Swiss Army knife who could move around Patrick Graham's defense.
He's likely not going to come in and threaten to take playing time away from Patrick Queen and Payton Wilson, though if he is ever elevated from the practice squad or even signed to the 53-man roster at some point, Graham could get more creative with some of his looks and overall packages with Mapu on the field given his flexibility and coverage ability.

title: Steelers Sign Bucs Veteran Cornerback
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are adding a veteran cornerback to their 53-man roster ahead of their Week 5 matchup at home against the Indianapolis Colts.
According to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero, the Steelers have signed Sean Murphy-Bunting off the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' practice squad.
The Steelers are signing veteran CB Sean Murphy-Bunting off the Bucs' practice squad, per source. Murphy-Bunting has played in 82 NFL games (65 starts) and has 11 career interceptions. Some experienced depth for Pittsburgh after the Joey Porter Jr. trade. pic.twitter.com/waUZp7F8Jg
After trading Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys last week for a 2028 second-round pick and 2027 conditional sixth-rounder, the Steelers were in need of another veteran corner.
Jamel Dean, a former teammate of Murphy-Bunting's during the latter's first stint in Tampa Bay, suffered an ankle injury in Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss to the Cleveland Browns that could keep him off the field for a couple of weeks as well, further pushing the team to go out and add to their cornerback room .
Murphy-Bunting has not appeared in a regular season game since 2024, as his entire 2025 campaign was wiped out due to a torn ACL he suffered that March.
The 29-year-old has plenty of experience, though, making 65 starts and playing in a total of 82 games. Over that span, he has posted 297 tackles, 11 interceptions and eight forced fumbles.
Given how massive of a hole Pittsburgh has at cornerback now that Porter Jr. is gone and Dean could be sidelined for a few games, Murphy-Bunting is a candidate to see the field on defense in some capacity for the Steelers right from the jump.
Asante Samuel Jr. and Daylen Everette figure to remain the starters on the boundary for the time being while Jalen Ramsey handles his usual duties between playing in the slot and at safety.
Murphy-Bunting will join Brandin Echols and Doneiko Slaughter, who took Porter Jr.'s spot on the 53-man roster, as Pittsburgh's reserve corners.
Though he was almost exclusively a boundary corner in 2023 for the Tennessee Titans and in 2024 with the Cardinals, which would give him the leg-up as the primary backup behind Samuel Jr. and Everette for now over Echols and Slaughter, Murphy-Bunting did spend a good amount of time in the slot at the beginning of his career with the Bucs.
Perhaps his positional versatility in that aspect will come into play for the Steelers down the line, and it'll become all the more valuable once Dean returns down the line.

title: Tyreek Hill News Puts Steelers on Watch
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers thought that they addressed their wide receiver issues in the offseason. Acquiring veteran Michael Pittman Jr. and drafting Germie Bernard was supposed to upgrade the depth chart and give quarterback Aaron Rodgers the weapons he needed to operate Mike McCarthy's West Coast offense.
Four games into the season, and the Steelers can concretely say they haven't quite solved one of their biggest issues on offense. DK Metcalf had a huge Week 4 performance, but he was also a nonfactor over the first three contests. Roman Wilson has made some big plays, but he's also made some costly mistakes that led to turnovers. Bernard hasn't made the impact some hoped he could as a rookie. Pittman Jr. was supposed to stabilize the group, but he and Rodgers have yet to get on the same page.
While the Steelers look for more help at receiver, one free agent is expected to sign with a team soon. According to NFL insider Adam Schefter, former Kansas City Chiefs and Miami Dolphins pass-catcher Tyreek Hill is currently speaking with multiple teams. His agent, Drew Rosenhaus, told Schefter that he's negotiating on his client's behalf and could finalize a deal for the former All-Pro before Week 5 action begins.
"I would anticipate Tyreek  potentially signing with a team over the next few days," Rosenhaus told Schefter.
Developing: Tyreek Hill’s agent Drew Rosenhaus said he plans to begin negotiating a deal for his veteran wide receiver with multiple teams today. One of those teams is the Chiefs, who have maintained contact with Hill. “I would anticipate Tyreek  potentially signing with a team… pic.twitter.com/RBn7ju28Ku
The Steelers need more talent on offense, there's no denying that. Even with the additions of Pittman Jr. and Bernard and the improved play from Wilson, Pittsburgh's passing game is underwhelming. When Rodgers has time in the pocket, the same problem emerges. No receiver can create separation on their own.
Tyreek Hill's career has been defined by his ability to create separation. One of the quickest receivers the game has ever seen in his prime, Hill was always open, even when it appeared like he wasn't.
Now 32 years old and coming off a major knee injury that included multiple torn ligaments, Hill can't be counted on to be the same guy who twice posted 1,700 receiving yards in a season. But the Steelers don't need him to be someone who catches 100 passes and makes it all happen. Sure, that wouldn't hurt, but the Steelers really need a player who can create a little space on his own and give Rodgers an open target down field.
The Steelers would love to land Hill, but it's extremely unlikely. Not only because the Steelers already have a crowded receiver room, but because the other options are much better for Hill personally.
Look at the Chiefs, for example. The consensus is that Hill will return to Kansas City, and it's hard to argue against that for one very simple reason: quarterback Partrick Mahomes. Mahomes is still in his prime and can bring a team to the Super Bowl. As historic a player as Rodgers is, the 42-year-old version of him with inconsistent offensive line play cannot deliver the same way.
But the Tyreek Hill watch is officially back on.

title: Steelers Solution to CB Problem is in Seattle
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers need a solution at cornerback , but they may not have one. Right now, they should simply be looking for all options, and the Seattle Seahawks may have one for them.
Pittsburgh's starters after the Jamel Dean injury are likely Asante Samuel Jr. and Daylen Everette, with Jalen Ramsey in the slot. Maybe they can test Brandin Echols as a starter, or move Ramsey to the outside. Although, playing with a broken wrist doesn't leave much hope that he'll be better as an outside corner than a slot corner.
Really, outside options are the best for the Steelers. They could consider a trade, and we've already named five possibilities there. Or, they could look at an easier move that doesn't require giving anything away, and may come with just slightly less potential to solve their problem.
Why not take a risk on Trevon Diggs? The Steelers could bring in a player their head coach has plenty of experience with and test him out.
Diggs is only 28 years old and is currently on the Seahawks' practice squad. That means the Steelers wouldn't be required to give up anything if they signed him. They would only need to create a roster spot on their 53-man team and keep him on their roster for a minimum of four weeks.
With Dean missing multiple weeks, they could consider putting him on Injured Reserve and signing Diggs. There's no give-and-take with that move, simply an option with a ton of ball production throughout his career and a player looking for an opportunity.
Diggs and McCarthy were together in Dallas for five years. McCarthy was the head coach when Diggs signed a five-year, $97 million deal with the Cowboys in 2023. He was also his coach when he recorded 11 interceptions during the 2021 season.
So, why not? The Steelers don't have a 100%, no-questions-asked solution to their cornerback issue. This group doesn't look nearly as strong without Joey Porter Jr. and Jamel Dean. They need help.
Diggs comes with a four-week commitment and no trade compensation. He's operating on a veteran minimum contract and got onto the field in Week 4 for the first time, meaning he's not going to be completely rusty when he signs.
It's the easiest answer for the Steelers. And they need answers.
Diggs should be a conversation Pittsburgh is having. One that could lead to them poaching the veteran from Seattle's practice squad.

title: Steelers, Porter Family Ties Officially Severed
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Porter name may finally be done in the city of Pittsburgh. As the Pittsburgh Steelers move on from Joey Porter Jr., the blood appears to be as bad as it can get, and his first win as a member of the Dallas Cowboys set the stage for plenty of shots to be taken.
The first came from Porter Jr. himself, posting on his Instagram after the win. The caption was simple a "W" after the Cowboys beat the Houston Texans 34-30. But the song playing in the photo was "Laughing to the Bank" by Chief Keef. And everyone knew that was intentional.
Dallas Cowboys CB Joey Porter Jr. took to Instagram to celebrate the team winning in his debut. pic.twitter.com/pR4uUqiMQm
Oh, but Porter Jr. wasn't alone. His father, Joey Porter Sr., also had words to say.
He released a video after the game saying, "They tried to take me away from football for four weeks. ... They held us down for three weeks... Football is back."
YIKES: Joey Porter Sr. takes a CLEAR SHOT at the #Steelers after his son Joey Porter Jr. was traded to Dallas. “They tried to take me away from football for four weeks.” “They held us down for 3 weeks… Football is back.” Porters are LOVING Dallas. 👀 pic.twitter.com/OPO6Bh2zCX
Porter Sr. is part of a mural within Acrisure Stadium. As players head back to the locker room, they pass a wall where Porter Sr. is amongst other Steelers legends wearing his uniform. He was also put into the team's Hall of Honor in 2025.
But it appears the relationship between the Porters and the Steelers is all but over. Fans want him removed from the Hall of Honor, and as for Porter Jr., many have voiced their opinions on social media about feeling good that he's gone.
It may not work in Pittsburgh's favor, as they need to recover from losing one of the best up-and-coming cornerbacks in the NFL, right before losing their other starter to an ankle injury.
Porter Jr. getting the first laugh of the trade doesn't mean anything, though. It's about the last laugh.
This can either look really good or really bad for the Steelers, and especially for general manager Omar Khan. If Porter Jr. skyrockets in Dallas and becomes a star, there's no defending Pittsburgh's decision not to try and give him a reasonable contract extension.
With their moves of DK Metcalf, Jalen Ramsey and others in the last two seasons, there wasn't a real explanation as to why they suddenly decided to cheap out on a big name. But they did.
If they can replace Porter Jr. and become successful without him, though, Pittsburgh wins. They look great in the process and walk away victors of a hostile situation.
There's a long time before we know who officially won the Steelers-Porter standoff. In the meantime, the ties between the family and Pittsburgh are officially severed. It'll be interesting to see what they do with Porter Sr.'s spot in the mural.

title: Steelers Can't Avoid Michael Pittman Jr. Disappointment
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have a potential issue on their hands with Michael Pittman Jr.
Upon acquiring Pittman Jr. and a 2026 seventh-round pick via trade from the Indianapolis Colts in March for a 2026 sixth-rounder, the Steelers signed the veteran wide receiver to a three-year, $59 million extension.
Pittsburgh's wide receiver room had been extremely thin for several years running prior to landing Pittman Jr., and he was viewed as a perfect complementary piece to DK Metcalf in Mike McCarthy's offense.
Given the way things are trending at the moment, however, it might be time to start worrying about Pittman Jr. and whether or not general manager Omar Khan is beginning to regret his decision to both land and pay him.
Pittman Jr. had a good debut for the Steelers, leading the team in receiving yards with 58 as they defeated the Atlanta Falcons by a score of 20-13 in Week 1.
He went on to miss Pittsburgh's Week 2 loss to the New England Patriots with a foot injury, though, before returning for a Week 3 win vs. the Cincinnati Bengals. Pittman Jr. garnered five targets in that contest and hauled in just two of them for a total of 16 yards.
It wasn't any better on Thursday Night Football in a defeat at the hands of the Cleveland Browns , either. DK Metcalf and Roman Wilson stole the show at receiver, combining for 189 yards and a touchdown on eight receptions.
Pittman Jr., on the other hand, finished with a measly two catches for 15 yards, which ranked sixth on the team.
The 28-year-old is still a physically-minded receiver who has strong hands, though he's really struggled to separate and offer any real upside in terms what he can do after the catch.
The fact that he's dealing with plantar fasciitis certainly has capped what he's capable of providing at the moment, but the outlook is still bleak.
Per Pro Football Focus , Pittman Jr.'s four penalties on the season are the second-most for any wide receiver in the NFL this season only behind Metcalf, who has five.
Furthermore, Pittman Jr.'s average depth of target (9.42, per SumerSports ) lags rather significantly behind both Wilson (15.33) and Metcalf (14.97).
The same can be said for Pittman Jr.'s yards per route run (0.9) when compared to Wilson (1.77) and Metcalf (1.26).
While the expectation was never that Pittman Jr. was going to stretch the field or be as explosive as Metcalf or even Wilson, the Steelers still haven't gotten nearly what they've expected out of the seven-year vet up to this point.
Again, his plantar fasciitis injury is hampering him, but how much confidence can Pittsburgh really have in a bounce-back for Pittman Jr.? Wilson is well on his way to surpassing him if he hasn't already, and second-round pick Germie Bernard is lurking in the shadows as well.
It wouldn't come as a huge surprise if Pittman Jr.'s usage is curtailed just a bit, and if he doesn't turn it around, perhaps the Steelers could look to move on from him in the offseason by either cutting or trading him with a post-June 1 designation and saving $18.5 million against the cap to go with $7.56 million in dead money for the 2027 campaign (per Over the Cap ).

title: No Need to Panic About Steelers' Nick Herbig
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have one of the better pass rushing units in the NFL, yet they've decided to deploy one of the top members of that group in a peculiar manner.
Upon signing Nick Herbig to a four-year, $100 million extension in early June, the expectations was that the Steelers were at least going to feature him more prominently moving forward.
That simply hasn't been the case, however. Herbig has been on the field for 52 percent of the team's defensive snaps through the first four weeks of the season, which is down from 60 percent in 2025, and he's only had 40 reps as a pass rusher in the process (per Pro Football Reference ).
It's not as though Pittsburgh hasn't gotten home and pressured opposing quarterbacks and thus needs Herbig to provide a spark, but his lack of usage in that role is still dubious and needs to change.
An interesting development for Herbig and how he's been ingratiated into defensive coordinator Patrick Graham's system is the uptick in his coverage reps.
Over 17 contests last season, Herbig finished with 54 total snaps in coverage (per PFF). Across four games so far in 2026, he has logged 20 reps as a coverage defender, meaning he's on pace to pass the mark he set in 2025 by a significant margin.
That's one of the reasons why he hasn't been utilized as a pass rusher as often as he has in the past, but the Steelers must pivot and ensure he has more opportunities to get into the backfield moving forward.
According to SumerSports , Herbig has the best pressure rate amongst Pittsburgh's EDGE rushers at 20.5 percent, meaning he's considerably outperforming Alex Highsmith (13.6 percent), T.J. Watt (12.1 percent) and Jack Sawyer (12.0 percent) on a rate basis.
The production hasn't been there for Herbig, as he has yet to record a sack this season, but they're going to come if he sustains his current level of play.
The Steelers' decision to extend Herbig has come back into focus after they couldn't agree on a new deal with Joey Porter Jr. and thus traded him to the Dallas Cowboys ahead of their Week 4 loss to the Cleveland Browns on Thursday Night Football.
It's easy to look at Herbig's stats and think that Pittsburgh may have made a mistake by potentially prioritizing him over Porter Jr., who played at a borderline elite level in 2025 and deserved a lucrative new deal from the franchise this past offseason.
While it's entirely possible the Steelers will look back at how they handled Porter Jr.'s situation and end up regretting it, paying Herbig was inarguably the correct course of action.
He's remained impactful to begin this season, and he will be a cornerstone of Pittsburgh's defense for years to come.

title: Injury News Should Push Steelers Toward Trade Market
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers fanbase wasn't expecting good news when Derrick Harmon and Jamel Dean left Week 4's game with injuries. Both players didn't look like their chances of returning anytime soon were great. Now, those concerns have been confirmed.
According to ESPN's Ian Rapoport, the Steelers expect both Harmon and Dean to miss multiple weeks with their injuries. Harmon was carted from the sideline to the locker room with a foot injury and Dean was limping on the sideline after an ankle injury. He was later seen in a walking boot in the locker room.
The #Steelers also could be without CB Jamel Dean for a couple of weeks as he works his way back from an ankle injury. https://t.co/HNQaQxgTWn
The news was the last thing the Steelers needed to hear. Right now, their defense is looking to find its footing again after struggling for the last two games. Harmon was a key piece of that turnaround, being their best run defender and making plays in crucial moments, like he did to seal the game against the Cincinnati Bengals.
Replacing Harmon isn't the most difficult thing in the world for the Steelers. They'll be able to play Keeanu Benton and Yahya Black more, and have Sebastian Joseph-Day coming off the bench. They may call upon rookie Gabe Rubio for the first time, but they won't need too much out of him as the last player off the bench.
Dean is the bigger issue. Obviously, everyone is going to bring up Joey Porter Jr. and how the team just traded their top cornerback, only for their other starter to go down. Now, they're stuck with Asante Samuel Jr., who has struggled, and third-round rookie Daylen Everette.
The Steelers may need to test all options in replacing Dean. Samuel Jr. and Everette will get the first go, but seeing if Brandin Echols can help on the outside may also need to be considered.
If nothing works, looking outside of the team should be on the table as well. Pittsburgh can't sit around and get beat on the outside in the passing game and just expect it all to be fine. They'll run into more issues than they may be able to handle.
Calling teams like the Los Angeles Rams, Houston Texans and maybe the Tennessee Titans should be on their mind . Names like Cam Hart, Kamari Lassiter and Cor’Dale Flott might be the route this team needs to go in order to fix their problem.
The Steelers weren't going to get Joey Porter Jr. back even if they didn't trade him. He wasn't going to play for them this season. But now they may need to make a second cornerback trade to validate the first. And if they believe the season is still wide open, they shouldn't be hesitating to see what's out there.

title: Steelers, Joey Porter Jr. Biggest Problem Revealed - And It Must Change
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers shipped Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys for a 2028 second-round draft pick after months of failed negotiations and plenty of drama, all leading to the end of one of the franchise's biggest disappointments in recent memory.
Fans wanted Porter Jr. to spend his career in Pittsburgh. The organization continued to preach the same things. But there was a hang-up in contract talks that the two sides couldn't figure out, and it was exactly what everyone thought it was.
According to ESPN's Ian Rapoport, the problem between the Steelers and Porter Jr. was the guaranteed money.
"There was significant money guaranteed for injury, but not fully in the second year, as the Steelers held firm on a stance they have used often over the past few years," Rapoport said. "They are among the few teams to avoid guarantees past Year 1, joining Green Bay and Cincinnati among those the clubs that (mostly) take that stance."
This isn't surprising. The Steelers refuse to adjust the way they go about contracts, unless they're dealing with big-name players like T.J. Watt. DK Metcalf, no one saw coming, and maybe shouldn't have happened looking back. But it did.
Why, you ask? Well, because negotiating with a franchise left tackle and center isn't going to be easy. And if Troy Fautanu and Zach Frazier look like they're worthy of extensions this season, the Steelers need to make sure they sign them.
They cannot - and that can't be stressed enough - mess up deals for two key pieces to their offensive line.
The team's philosophy seems outdated at this point anyways. Especially if they're going to pick and choose when they break it and when they don't. Giving Metcalf a ton of money for him to struggle and not paying a homegrown talent like Porter Jr. doesn't fit anyone's idea of the "right move," and it doesn't seem to be working out in Pittsburgh's favor.
The Porter Jr. stuff is over, but it's a great time to live and learn. Figure out how they can adjust and be better the next time. Because the next time, there will be two cornerstone pieces of your offensive line up for extensions, and if they prove worthy, signing them is an absolute must.
Botching Fautanu and Frazier in 2027 should be grounds for cleaning house in the front office. But again, it's a great time to readjust and figure things out.
Because these problems can't happen again. Not if the Steelers don't want to look like a team players shouldn't be negotiating with.

title: Steelers' OT Concerns are Way Overblown
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers ' offensive line has faced a ton of scrutiny early in the 2026 season, and for good reason.
After all, the unit has allowed 13 sacks, which is tied for the most in the league. That number is perhaps a bit skewed against the Steelers considering they've played four games while every other team besides the Cleveland Browns, who they lost to on Thursday Night Football in Week 4 , has played three.
Pittsburgh has allowed a pressure rate of 42.1 percent on the year, which is still rather poor but isn't nearly the worst mark in the league, instead coming in at No. 20 (per SumerSports ).
Again, the offensive line has been a problem, and that was especially the case when Spencer Anderson and Dylan were starting, but two players the Steelers shouldn't worry about moving forward are Troy Fautanu and Max Iheanachor.
After missing all but one game as a rookie in 2024 as a result of a knee injury he suffered ahead of Week 3, Fautanu returned last season and was a steady presence at right tackle while showing flashes of eventually becoming a franchise tackle for Pittsburgh.
Upon selecting Iheanachor in the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft, the Steelers opted to move Fautanu from right tackle to left tackle, where he played during a vast majority of his collegiate career at Washington.
There were some ups and downs throughout the summer as Fautanu switched sides and readapted to the position, and it hasn't necessarily been a completely smooth transition during the regular season either.
Fautanu, as is the case with the rest of Pittsburgh's offensive line, has faced plenty of scrutiny for the unit's shortcomings. Any excessive vitriol towards him feels unfair, though, as among 158 offensive linemen who have logged at least 100 snaps so far this season, Fautanu's allowed pressure rate of 5.3 percent ranks right around the middle of the pack at No. 86 (per SumerSports ).
He had arguably his best performance of the year vs. Cleveland as well, allowing a single pressure and shutting out Jared Verse along the way.
Has Fautanu played like a superstar this year? No, but he's still been reliable and seems to be growing on a weekly basis.
Iheanachor was viewed as somewhat of a project when Pittsburgh selected him No. 21 overall in this past year's draft. He had all the physical and athletic tools as a prospect to eventually blossom into a stalwart at right tackle, though he needed more experience and refinement in his technique before he could ever reach his ceiling.
He's made a ton of strides since entering the league, though, first making noise in training camp before an upper-body injury kept him out of the first two games of the preseason.
Iheanachor was later inserted into the starting lineup for the Steelers' Week 3 win over the Cincinnati Bengals, and he was as good as the team could've realistically hoped, allowing just two pressures and no sacks (per SumerSports ).
The Arizona State product did take a big step back vs. Cleveland, giving up five pressures and two sacks, though Isaiah McGuire's sack that was credited against Iheanachor was largely the result of Rodgers stepping up right into it.
That doesn't completely excuse Iheanachor's struggles, though it does add some needed context.
There are going to be growing pains for him as a rookie. For someone who came into the league as raw as he did, Pittsburgh has to take the good with the bad.
Iheanachor is still undoubtedly a better option at right tackle than Cook, however, and he has all the makings of a difference-maker for the Steelers. It's just going to take time for him to become a finished product.

title: Hanich Panic Meter: Seahawks' Offense Inconsistent After Chargers
full_text:
Week 4 against the Los Angeles Chargers was a chance for the Seattle Seahawks to develop some good habits before a brutal stretch of the schedule. The Seahawks may have scored 30 points for the third consecutive week, but there were still a lot of issues that plagued the team and allowed the winless Chargers to remain close.
From the poor play of the offensive line, lack of explosiveness in the running game and some concerns about the passing game, there are issues that Seattle must highlight this week in practice. The Seahawks must prepare for the San Francisco 49ers (4-0), at the Denver Broncos (2-2) on a short week due to Thursday Night Football, the Kansas City Chiefs (4-0) and the Chicago Bears (3-1) over the next four weeks. Now is the time for the Seahawks to get right on the offensive side of the ball.
Seattle’s offensive line isn’t quite up to the level it needed to be against the Chargers’ defense. The Chargers ranked in the top ten in run defense, but the Seahawks’ offensive line had the experience and the schemes to dominate. Instead, it feels like the offensive line played down to the level of the Chargers overall. They allowed quarterback Sam Darnold to be sacked three times and take nine quarterback hits.
The Seahawks’ rushing offense continued to struggle even with the understanding that rookie and starting running back Jadarian Price would be out . Outside of wide receiver Rashid Shaheed’s two runs for 33 yards and a touchdown, the Seahawks rushed for 105 yards on 31 carries, averaging 3.38 yards per carry.
Seattle is still inefficient at converting for third downs as the team only converted 3-of-12 on third downs. A good portion of those plays the offense couldn’t convert were run plays. While Seattle was better in the red zone, it still lacked the consistency to extend drives on third and short on the ground.
There is some discourse that offensive coordinator Brian Fleury and Darnold aren’t in sync yet. This may not be the case, but the two have to understand what makes the passing game more efficient. After three stellar performances from wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, it seemed clear that the Seahawks wanted to divert attention from JSN. Most of the first looks on the passing plays were to Shaheed or tight end AJ Barner.
JSN was targeted six times and caught five of them for 76 yards. The next highest targeted pass-catcher was running back Emanuel Wilson, who is a powerback targeted four times. Shaheed and Barner were targeted three times each, but could’ve gotten more if Darnold wasn’t under constant pressure.
​Ultimately, for Darnold, he has to trust his instincts and not force his passes in certain coverages just because the area of the field is open to a receiver. He needs to survey the entire area and avoid the turnovers. That interception on the first play of the Seahawks’ first drive was a tone setter.
Fleury, on the other hand, has to develop the offensive line’s ability to push the ball at the line of scrimmage. The offensive line has to play better, but Fleury must find a running back with explosiveness, whether it is Wilson with a new mindset, Zach Charbonnet back from his injury or Joe Mixon coming out of retirement . Finally, he has to find ways to make JSN the main focus of the offense; there is a reason he is one of the highest-paid players in the league.
The Seahawks have gotten better on offense under harsher conditions and challenges. The problem is that they have to do it again, this time with the 49ers in Week 5, who possess a defense that ranks third in the league in points allowed per game (16).

title: The Good, Bad, and Ugly From Seahawks Win Over Chargers
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks won had the ugliest 30-23 win in that final score's history of the league against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 4.
Both quarterbacks, Sam Darnold and Justin Herbert , respectively, threw interceptions on their very first plays from scrimmage. Seattle, let a three-touchdown lead turn into a one-touchdown lead by the final whistle.
It was that kind of day at Lumen Field.
Here is the good, the bad, and the ugly from a win Mike Macdonald and Co. may want to immediately forget besides one offensive skill-position player's well-timed breakout:
With Jaxon Smith-Njigba having a great, but not typically dominant outing (76 receiving yards on five catches), and Sam Darnold having a sloppy effort (13-of-22 passing with three interceptions) in his second game back from a glute injury, Emanuel Wilson had a much-needed breakout effort out of the backfield against Los Angeles.
The fourth-year undrafted product out of Fort Valley State had 81 rushing yards on 21 carries and another 39 receiving yards on three catches.
Wilson found the end zone on a 23-yard screen pass and an eight-yard run.
Wilson was elusive and explosive. With Jadarian Price on the IR with a chest injury , and George Holani gathering just 18 yards on seven carries, Wilson had the exact kind of day offensive coordinator Brian Fleury needed to see.
There were several truly head-scratching special teams mistake that could've cost the Seahawks this game.
A 15-yard unnecessary roughness penalty on Connor O'Toole helped give the Chargers better field position. That led to a 39-yard field before the half, which ended up keeping Los Angeles within two scores coming out of the break.
In the kicking game, Jason Myers's kickoff landed short of the dynamic kickoff landing zone after a score in the second quarter. Myers also missed an extra point.
Had the Chargers scored a touchdown on their last drive, an extra point would've sufficed to send the game into overtime because of that. All three phases would've been responsible for this loss, had Los Angeles been capable of completing the comeback.
Seattle broke the franchise record for the most penalty yards in a game with 150 on 14 flags. The Chargers, to their credit, had 130 penalty yards on 16 flags.
Playing with such a lack of discipline isn't how the defending champions will successfully defend their crown.
While it's a positive sign that the Seahawks are still winning in what can only be described as an early-season hangover, between this game and last week's 33-31 loss to the Commanders , Macdonald needs to clean this up before the schedule rachets up the difficulty level.
The 49ers, Broncos, Chiefs, and Bears are next on the schedule.

title: Seahawks' Penalty Total 'Unacceptable' in Win vs. Chargers
full_text:
Even in a win, Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald was visibly dissatisfied after a 30-23 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday.
The Seahawks allowed the Chargers to score 10 fourth-quarter points, had 14 total penalties and gave LA a shot to tie the game down the stretch after leading by 21 points in the third quarter.
Between both teams, 30 total penalties were called in the matchup between the Seahawks and Chargers. That's the most in one game this season in any game through Week 4 and made it an ugly matchup to watch. Seattle had multiple opportunities to seal the game, but couldn't.
“Well, we were [going to be] off the field multiple times, and we got penalties. So, it’s cut and dry,” Macdonald told reporters postgame . “That’s not how we’re going to do business. That’s not how we need to play. That’s unacceptable.”
Macdonald re-emphasized that the players' performance in terms of miscues on penalties was not to the team's standard.
“To have seven personal foul penalties is unacceptable on any level, however you slice it,” Macdonald added. “That’s not us, and that’s not going to be how we play football around here.”
The Seahawks had multiple roughing the passer penalties, late hits and facemask penalties. All of those culminated in extending key Chargers drives that kept them in the game and led to the game being as close as it was.
Had even one or two of those calls not happened, the final scoreboard could have looked much different.
“I would say the penalties is what made it close … We make a penalty and they get a free first down, or they get closer [on] third down,” Seahawks outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu said. “So, it’s just on us — the little mistakes that made it closer than it needed to be.”
Nwosu added that the Seahawks' defense didn't agree with many of the calls being made, but they were happy to at least get the win.
“What was being called out there, we thought it was a couple things that didn’t go our way,” Nwosu said. “We didn’t agree with the calls and we let our emotions get the best of us. But, like Mike [Macdonald] said in the breakdown, we’re going to learn from it; we’re going to attack it, and at the end of the day, we got the win. That’s most important.”
The Seahawks will have to be better when they face the San Francisco 49ers in Week 5. Similar mistakes or anything nearly as sloppy could cost them a critical game in the NFC West race.

title: Nick Emmanwori Back 100% Puts Seahawks' Defense at Eite Potential
full_text:
It took some time, but second-year nickelback Nick Emmawori got back to full speed for the Seattle Seahawks (3-1). Emmanwori showed why he is not only the Seahawks’ most pivotal defender, but also one of the NFL’s dynamic defenders in Seattle’s 30-23 win over the Los Angeles Chargers . Emmanwori played his third game of the season versus the Chargers, but Sunday felt like it was the first time that he truly felt back for Seattle.
Emmanwori accumulated nine total tackles, eight solo tackles, two tackles for loss, two quarterback hits, one sack and a pass breakup. This game felt like he played 100% for the first time since Super Bowl LX before he had a late offseason surgery on his ankle. There are signs that show not only is Emmanwori back, but he is even better than last season.
The Seahawks knew there would be some complications from his ankle surgery in July that made him miss all training camp and the Week 1 win over the New England Patriots. Seattle opted not to overuse Emmanwori in the next two road games at the Arizona Cardinals and at the Washington Commanders.
He only played nine defensive snaps (18%) against the Cardinals with 36 defensive plays (52.2%) against the Commanders. Although he made his first start of the season against Washington, he wasn’t up to game speed yet.
The Seahawks had a great feeling about Emmanwori’s availability as he practiced fully for the first time since before the ankle surgery. Emmanwori looked up to the task against the Chargers’ offense and played at full speed on Sunday. While the Dark Side Defense played great against the Patriots and Cardinals, Sunday’s game against the Chargers was potentially the Seahawks’ most complete defensive performance.
The Seahawks were determined to expand Emmanwori’s athleticism this season . The coaching staff had him learn under veteran edge rusher DeMarcus Lawrece and take part in edge rushing drills. Seattle looked to expand Emmanwori into a pass rusher on top of being a man-and-zone coverage player and blitzer from the secondary.
The Seahawks likely wanted Emmanwori to be at his healthiest or 100% before being utilized as an edge rusher. Seattle had a huge production boost in pass rushers in Week 4 against the Chargers compared to the previous games. Emmanwori’s increased reps and inclusion in the Seahawks’ pass rush were a key reason for the turmoil in the Chargers’ backfield. He was one of the more consistent pass rushers on Sunday thanks to his speed and tremendous athleticism.
Seattle can utilize Emmanwori throughout the field and in multiple schemes to make him one of the unpredictable defenders on an elite defense. The Seahawks can easily take the reins of the league’s most dangerous defense thanks to Emmanwori back at full health.

title: 3 Observations From Seahawks Ugly Win vs. Chargers
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are waking up victorious after beating the Los Angeles Chargers 30-23 at Lumen Field for their Week 4 matchup.
The Seahawks started off strong and even held a 30-13 lead at the end of the third quarter. The Chargers attempted a fourth-quarter comeback, but it wasn't enough. The Seahawks made a game-ending fumble recovery with less than two minutes to go to salvage the victory. Here's a look at three observations from the Seahawks win against the Chargers.
With Jadarian Price on injured reserve and Zach Charbonnet still recovering from his torn ACL, the Seahawks needed somebody to step up to the plate in the run game. Enter Emanuel Wilson, the team's free agent signing from the Green Bay Packers this offseason.
Wilson has had an inconsistent workload over the first three games, but he was given the RB1 status against the Chargers and ran with it. He finished with 81 rushing yards on 21 carries and also had 3 catches for 39 yards and a touchdown through the air. Those are the type of numbers that one would expect out of a starting running back, and him finding the end zone twice is a positive sign of what's to come.
The Seahawks should definitely feel more confident in Wilson moving forward with Price and Sharpe still out.
There was a lot of yellow on the field during the game between the Seahawks and Chargers. The teams combined for 30 penalties for 280 yards. The Seahawks were responsible for 14 penalties for 150 yards. That's simply unacceptable, and a win likely wouldn't have happened against most teams in the league with that kind of performance.
Luckily, the Seahawks were facing the Chargers , who have been one of the worst teams in the league so far this season and have been just as undisciplined as Seattle was today. This should be a massive emphasis going into Week 5 against the undefeated San Francisco 49ers.
All things considered, a win is a win, especially in the National Football League. The Seahawks coming out on top is important for keeping up in a very tight NFC West, with the Los Angeles Rams and 49ers both winning on Sunday. The Seahawks are firmly in second place with a 3-1 record. They will have a chance to take first place if they can be the first team this season to beat the 49ers, who have won all four of their games so far.
They know they will have to put together a better performance than they did in Week 4, and that should trigger a very focused week of practice ahead.
