title: Seahawks HC Mike Macdonald Delivers Good News on Leonard Williams Injury
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks were without one of their top defensive players for part of the second half of Sunday's 30-23 win over the Los Angeles Chargers once defensive lineman Leonard Williams suffered a lower body injury.
Williams limped off the field and did not return to the game. An already quiet day for the All-Pro defender ended early, but Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald had positive news about Williams after the game.
“He’s got an ankle [injury] … it doesn’t look serious right now, which is positive news, but we’ll see,” Macdonald told reporters .
Williams didn't log any tackles but did have one quarterback hit before his injury. He had logged 13 tackles, 3.0 sacks and five tackles for loss in the team's previous three games, helping lead a Seahawks defense that has remained one of the best in the league this season.
At 32 years old, Williams has continued to play at an All-Pro level in his 12th NFL season for a Super Bowl-winning defense. He earned his first-ever Second Team All-Pro nod in 2025 with 62 tackles, nine tackles for loss, 7.0 sacks and a pick-six.
Seattle's game plan would vary drastically if Williams isn't ready to go for Week 5 against the San Francisco 49ers. Williams is the heart of the team's defensive line next to Byron Murphy II and Jarran Reed, and he opens up rushes for the rest of the defense by requiring double teams to slow him down.
Mike Morris and Rylie Mills would likely see a large increase in snaps if Williams is sidelined. However, that may not be necessary if Macdonald's postgame verdict is correct.
The practice reports throughout the week will be key to Williams' status. Seattle needs to be as close to full strength if it hopes to beat a red-hot 49ers team next week that currently leads the NFC West with a 4-0 record.
The Seahawks held on against the Chargers, but it was far less impressive a win than expected. Ample penalties and overall miscues on defense made for a much closer game than anticipated, especially down the stretch. Those types of mistakes won't be as easy to recover from in Week 5, and that makes Williams' presence that much more important.

title: 3 Winners, 3 Losers From Seahawks Win vs. Chargers
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are back in the win column after their 30-23 victory against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 4.
Here's a look at the winners and losers from the matchup:
The star of the day is running back Emanuel Wilson, who ran for 81 yards and a touchdown while also catching three passes for 39 yards and a score. With Jadarian Price on injured reserve and Zach Charbonnet still not ready to return from a torn ACL, Wilson is very important to the team's depth. The fact that he's able to score both on the ground and in the air is a very positive sign of what is to come.
Seahawks defensive lineman Leonard Williams left the team's game early against the Chargers. He was on the sideline following the injury, which is a sign that it probably isn't a long-term or super serious injury. He will undergo more tests over the next couple of days, and we will know more once practice starts for Week 5.
Jones continued to flex his muscles and prove why he is the undisputed leader of the defense. He led the team with 12 tackles and a sack, and he also had an interception off Justin Herbert in the second quarter. Two plays later, the Seahawks scored a touchdown to go up 17 points, so his play definitely made an impact.
Darnold and Herbert both started the game with interceptions. Herbert threw one on the first play from scrimmage, and as soon as the Seahawks got the ball back, Darnold gave the ball right back to Los Angeles. It's the first time a game has started with back-to-back interceptions since 1978.
History! Per ESPN Research and Elias Sports, the Chargers/Seahawks game is the first game to start with consecutive interceptions (one by each team) since 1978 -- as far back as we have data.
Eventually, both quarterbacks found some success during the game, but Herbert still had four turnovers as an offense, including another interception later in the game. Overall, the quarterback play could have been better on both sides, but Seattle is the one walking away with the win.
Hall capped off the afternoon with a massive fumble recovery to end the Chargers' final drive that could have ended in the game tying at 30. It was the final of four turnovers the Seahawks defense forced, which led them to their third victory of the season.
Hall finished the day with just two tackles, but falling on the football when it mattered most is what he will be remembered for in this game. Those kinds of plays are what turn losses into wins, and the Seahawks couldn't be more thankful to have him on the defense.

title: Leonard Williams Injury Update: Latest On Seahawks Stud Defender
full_text:
A lot has gone wrong today in the week 4 bout between the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Chargers. The game is on track to challenge records for most total penalties in a single game, with many of them coming in the form of personal fouls. But for the Seahawks, they had managed to largely avoid injury scares until the fourth quarter.
Leonard Williams, the superstar defensive lineman who has been off to an excellent start so far this season, went down on a Justin Herbert run near the goal line. Star Chargers tackle Rashawn Slater went down on the same play, and both players headed to the sideline for the final play of the drive, where the Chargers scored a goal line touchdown.
Williams went to the blue tent, but then left it before the Seahawks defense took the field again, walking on his own without a limp, and still with his helmet. It’s an encouraging sign, and indicates the injury was ultimately minor, but I’m not sure we see him today with the Seahawks up by two scores later. We’ll await updates on his status with bated breath.
With not much time left in the game and the Seahawks trying to hold onto a lead, there may not be a significant need for Big Cat to return today. But next week, with the Seahawks due to take on the currently undefeated San Francisco 49ers, getting Leonard back on the field is going to be extremely important. Without him, this defense becomes much less dangerous.
Byron Murphy II, who has a sack today, is still among the best defensive tackles in football, and Jarran Reed is a good veteran. Rylie Mills is also a frisky reserve. But Leonard Williams is among the best in football, and he forms the foundation of a great pass rush and run defense. Luckily, early indications are positive that the injury is relatively minor, if such a thing exists.
Leonard Williams recorded a sack in each of the first three games this season, and has been his generally disruptive self at virtually all times. In what has been a hideous game for much of its runtime, hopefully things are not capped off with an injury to a crucial player. But for now, the Seahawks must focus in on trying to seal this victory, and then figure out Big Cat's situation.

title: George Holani, Rashid Shaheed Have Big Opportunities After Jadarian Price Injury
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks (2-1) have the tough task of having to play without rookie first-string running back Jadarian Price for at least four games after being placed on IR with a chest injury . The Seahawks were being patient with Price’s development after a rough three games to start the season. Now a huge part of their offense is out, and the Seahawks need some production to make up for Price's potential, especially if the running game suffers.
The Seahawks will have their first test without Price as they take on the Los Angeles Charger s (0-3). This will be an opportunity for two players to step up and become the players needed for the offense to remain efficient. These were players that had a big role before the start of the season, but their lack of contribution has lowered their potential. Price’s injury, however, is a chance for these two players to step up for the Seahawks.
The Seahawks likely aren’t trading for a running back, especially since Zach Charbonnet returns from his ACL injury soon. With Price out and Charbonnet not yet back, the Seahawks will turn to Holani, who came into the season as the No. 2 running back.
Holani, however, has only rushed for 52 yards on 15 carries, averaging 3.5 yards per carry in three games. He is behind Price and power back Emanuel Wilson in rushing yards for Seattle. He doesn’t have a run that accounted for a first down in three games played.
The Seahawks had a lot of faith in Holani this offseason to be a reliable player through all 17 regular season games. Outside of pass protection and six receptions for 50 yards, Holani hasn’t become the running back they expected him to be. He will likely make his first career start on Sunday versus the Chargers. This could be his chance to show he deserves the praise from the team at the beginning of the season.
One player that the Seahawks need to step up starting in Week 4 against Los Angeles is wide receiver/return specialist Rashid Shaheed. Of all the high-caliber players who are off to a slow start of the season, Shaheed has struggled the most . He has caught six receptions out of 12 targets for 53 yards. Only one of his plays was for a first down.
Shaheed has also been cautious in the return game to start the season. He has returned seven kickoffs for 190 yards, averaging 27.1 yards, and fumbled once. Shaheed returned seven punts for 67 yards, averaging 9.6 yards.
The Seahawks need him to be more reliable in the passing game and more reliable in the return game. He is averaging $17 million a year for three years. He needs to play to where his contract is justified based on his pay. With the Seahawks likely running the ball less, they can focus their targets on Shaheed, who is still one of the league’s most dynamic players.

title: 49ers Catch a Huge Break on Kyle Juszczyk's Knee Injury
full_text:
49ers star player Kyle Juszczyk exited the game against the Broncos in Week 4 after suffering a knee injury. It was a brutal hit he took, causing his knee to hyperextend.
The initial fear was that Juszczyk tore his ACL. A hyperextension can lead to that. Kyle Shanahan shared during his postgame press conference that the 49ers didn't believe Juszczyk tore his ACL.
Turns out, they were correct. ESPN's Adam Schefter has reported that Juszczyk underwent an MRI on his knee today, revealing a sprain and a bone bruise.
An MRI on Kyle Jusczyk’s knee revealed a sprain and bone bruise that now is expected to sideline him 2-3 weeks, per source. https://t.co/yhJytZ1XlR
That's a huge break for the 49ers and Juszczyk, given how rough the injury looked. Now, Juszczyk will miss some time. They're expecting him to be out for two to three weeks.
I don't imagine the 49ers will place him on Injured Reserve, especially since they haven't done that with Nick Bosa. Their I.R. list is incredibly long, so they can't afford it.
If Juszczyk is only out for two or three games, they'll be fine. They also have their Week 8 Bye to help them out. I think the 49ers will sit Juszczyk out for the next three games.
Rather, that is what they should do to allow him four weeks to heal before returning in Week 9 against the Raiders. It's a bummer they will be without him, but a greater relief that he's not lost for the season.
With Juszczyk out for the next few games, the 49ers will need to fill his spot, but with whom? It will probably be tight end Brayden Willis.
He played 10 snaps against the Broncos. He was the fullback during the preseason, so he's the most prepared for it. However, he's not the most trustworthy.
At times during the preseason, he had no clue who to block and ran without hitting anyone. Juszczyk's loss will sting the 49ers, especially since they don't have a viable fill-in.
Their entire offense relies on Juszczyk thanks to his motions. It helps Brock Purdy uncover the defense and sets up the play for timely success.
Maybe Luke Farrell can fill Juszczyk's role as well. Either way, you can't replace Juszczyk. I don't even think they can shrink the void left by him.
Shanahan is going to need to be extra creative to make up for his absence.

title: The Hypothetical Reason Why 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan Would Wear a Dre Greenlaw Jersey
full_text:
It's no secret that San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan adores linebacker Dre Greenlaw.
Greenlaw brings something unique to the defense with his intensity, eagerness and overall attitude toward playing football. Now, after a one-year absence with the Denver Broncos, he’s back in the City by the Bay and with a franchise where he feels he belongs.
Shanahan has always spoken highly of him. Playing Denver in Week 4 was always going to fire him up, and the stats backed this up: he recorded 12 tackles, almost double Fred Warner's , and had a forced fumble as well. It was his best performance of the season.
Speaking after the game, Shanahan spoke at length about Greenlaw's performance and his wider influence on the franchise.
"I think people know, but like if I had to wear a jersey, I'd probably wear his," said Shanahan post-game .
"Just the way he plays, what he's done for us over these years, going back to his rookie year and getting us the number one seed in Seattle with the play he made on the goal line.
"Just the way he inspires people because the way he plays. I think he's an intimidation factor for the other side of the ball because of the way he plays, and it's hard for us not to be as aggressive as possible with how he is out there.
"So, we missed him for the year, but it was good to, as we feel, get a family member back."
Shanahan believes that Greenlaw was more fired up for this game, likely due to his negative experience with the Broncos , resulting in him dominating the stat line.
"Yes, definitely. We knew he'd be excited going into this game. Dre's excited going into every game, but this one meant a little more to him. I was a little nervous there in the first half," he added.
"We told him, 'You can get close, but don't be so excited you give them an explosive with 15.' And I really thought someone was going to get one in the second half of one of the teams, just challenged our team to make sure it wasn't us.
"I don't think anyone ended up getting one, but Dre held his emotions good enough today and led the team in tackles and had an unbelievable game. He's had an unbelievable season so far and we're so happy to have him back at home."

title: 49ers LT Trent Williams Sounds Off on O-Line's Impressive Start to 2026
full_text:
It’s clear to see that the San Francisco 49ers’ offensive line is a position group that has improved greatly.
It would be fair to say it's the most improved position group on the entire roster. Aside from Connor Colby winning the left guard position in training camp, the rest of the unit remains the same.
So, what happened for the 49ers to go from having one of the NFL’s most mediocre offensive lines to one of its best? Trent Williams explains how the unit's self-belief has played a role in improving their game.
"I think everybody in the locker room goes through those times where you've got to be a little bit, I guess, for lack of a better word, crazy, in a sense to where you've got to believe that you're the best," shared Williams with the media after the 49ers' Week 4 victory against the Broncos.
"You've got to believe you have the best o-line. You've got to believe you have the best defensive line whether that's true or not. It's the belief and the confidence that allows you to play like you can be that.
"I've always thought we had the talent to be one of the best o-lines in the league. I always say I thought Colton [McKivitz] and myself were probably the best pair of Tackles in the league. With the way Dom [Puni] has been playing, obviously Jake [Brendel] has always been real solid for us, the heart and soul of our o-line.
"Connor [Colby] taking that big step, that's probably when you reference the question. I understand it's left guard, but we always had faith in him. He has the attributes to be really successful. We've seen that his rookie year and now he's putting on film."
The most striking stat from the Week 4 victory is that the unit has yet to allow Brock Purdy to be sacked this season. The last time this happened was in 2005, when Peyton Manning’s Indianapolis Colts finished the season with a 14-2 record.
The 49ers looked vastly better as the Broncos presented a step up purely because of their strong defense. Another big step follows in Week 5 against the Seattle Seahawks - the very team that defeated San Francisco twice last season.
Self-belief definitely helps, but coaching surely has played a key role too. The coaching staff deserve credit for this massive improvement. Long may it continue.

title: 5 49ers Whose Stock Is Falling After Week 4
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers moved to 4-0 with their win over the Denver Broncos in Week 4. While most players on the team continue to see their stock rise, there are a few players who did not perform well in the win. Who saw their stock drop?
Watkins could be a stock-up player because he played a career-high 16 snaps in Week 4. However, he did not see a target or catch a pass. It has been a bit of a one-step-forward-and-one-step-back type of progression for the 49ers' former fourth-round pick.
Stout struggled before he left the game due to injury. However, finishing the game with an unknown status for the next week is never good. Still, before that, he allowed a big catch and missed two tackles. He was arguably the 49ers' biggest liability on defense when he left the game.
When Stout left the game, the 49ers decided to play Deommodore Lenoir in the slot. Then, they played Jack Jones on the outside. Jones struggled, particularly in the run game. This is the second week in a row that injuries in the secondary caused Jones to play more than expected. This is also the second week in a row that Jones has struggled.
The 49ers are admittedly asking more from their fourth-round rookie than you would typically expect. However, he left Week 3 with cramps and saw his snaps reduced in Week 4, despite the team being thin along the interior.
Former UDFA and practice squad option Sebastian Valdez played more snaps and had a bigger impact than Halton in Week 4. It makes sense for the 49ers to limit Halton's snaps to keep him healthy for the full season. It is also a sign that Halton might not have the best conditioning.
When Black had 14 carries for 65 yards, it looked like he was going to have a real role in the offense as a rookie. However, he has been a minimal backup since then. He has 17 carries for 55 yards in the three games since Week 1. He also went from 28 snaps in Week 1 to averaging 14 per game in the three weeks since then.
Black was not expected to have a significant role, but it has been getting smaller in recent weeks, which is surprising.

title: 5 Biggest 49ers Risers After Impressive Broncos Win
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers had arguably their most impressive win of the 2026 season with their 24-14 victory over the Denver Broncos. Which players had their stock rise the most in the win?
If the MVP talk was not starting for Purdy after the first three weeks, it is going to get louder now. The thought was that Purdy beat up on weaker competition in the early portion of the season. However, the Broncos have a respected defense, and Purdy still performed. He only had 216 yards, but added two touchdowns and no interceptions. He is up to 11 touchdowns and one interception this season. The excuses for him being an MVP favorite are fading.
Evans came into the game questionable with a rib injury. Not only did he play, but he put up an impressive five catches for 76 yards. Evans is averaging 2.63 yards per route run this season. He averages 2.07 for his career. When he is on the field, he is as impactful as any receiver. The 49ers have to love what they are seeing through four weeks.
Kittle has been incredible since returning from his Achilles injury. He has 16 catches for 244 yards and four touchdowns so far this season. He is averaging 2.8 yards per route run this season after averaging 2.28 for his career.
Not only is he making an impact in the passing game, but he is still the best blocking option on the team. He is on an incredible tear.
Odighizuwa has been a highly impactful addition. The team is asking him to do a lot due to all of the injuries along the interior defensive line. In the first week of the season, he played 59% of the defensive snaps. The following week, he was up to 69%.
Then, in Week 3, he shot up to 82% due to the lack of depth on the line. This week, he played at 79%. The team is leaning heavily into him getting a strong workload. So far, he has taken advantage.
Greenlaw was fired up, and this game obviously meant something to him given the history he has with the Broncos. Greenlaw led the team in tackles and forced a fumble in the win. He looked great and the 49ers got the win.

title: 49ers Grades After 24-14 Win Over Broncos: Brock Purdy Bails Out Kyle Shanahan
full_text:
SANTA CLARA -- The 49ers just beat the Denver Broncos 24-14 . Here are the 49ers' grades for this performance.
Brock Purdy kept the 49ers offense afloat all game without much help from anyone else, save the offensive linemen. They were excellent. The weapons were not -- they were banged up, and Kyle Shanahan's game plan and play calling were subpar for most of the game (more on Shanahan in a minute). When Purdy dropped back, his receivers generally weren't open until late in the second half when both of the Broncos' starting cornerbacks got injured. Until then, the pass game was anemic, partially because Purdy wasn't seeing the field particularly well. So, he bought time and extended drives with his legs until the passing game opened up. The 49ers wouldn't have won without his improvisation. He has been their best player all season. The 49ers need to help him out.
Christian McCaffrey scored a touchdown, but averaged just 3.5 yards per carry and caught only three passes for 18 yards. The Broncos essentially held him in check, just like the Dolphins did two weeks ago. He wasn't even dangerous as a receiver, which was surprising. He simply isn't the player he was three years ago. These days, he's good for just a couple exciting plays per game. His backup, Kaelon Black, averaged just 2.2 yards per carry. And their lead blocker, Kyle Juszczyk, left the game with two catches and a knee sprain. The 49ers used to have a dominant running game. Now, they don't. In fact, their most effective runner today was a wide receiver.
Deebo Samuel had just 26 receiving yards, but he caught a touchdown pass and averaged 14.7 yards per carry on three attempts. He still struggles to get himself open and catch passes down the field, but he's as difficult to tackle as ever, and he seems to score a touchdown every week, which makes him extremely valuable. The 49ers need to get him the ball even more often. I can't believe I just typed that. The other starting wide receiver, Mike Evans, heroically played through broken ribs and caught five passes for 76 yards. What a pleasure it is to watch him work, even when injured. Still, the receivers struggled to get open, which is why the passing game struggled until the Broncos' starting cornerbacks left the game. The 49ers seriously miss Demarcus Robinson and De'Zhaun Stribling. Stribling can't even put weight on his injured ankle yet. He's using a special scooter to get around. Don't expect him back any time soon.
George Kittle caught just four passes -- they should have targeted him much more frequently -- but he put the game away with a 56-yard touchdown catch off a screen pass from Purdy late in the fourth quarter. Better late than never. It's incredible how Kittle has been able to regain almost all of his speed and explosiveness fewer than 10 months after tearing his Achilles.
These guys haven't given up a sack yet this season, which is incredible. Trent Williams is playing as well as he's ever played, which is remarkable considering he's 38. Still, the run game struggled, and that's partially the fault of the offensive linemen. They'll have a huge test next week against the Seahawks.
They stopped the run, which is impressive considering how many players are injured, but they can't rush the quarterback without Nick Bosa. They sacked Bo Nix zero times. But they didn't have to sack him to make him play poorly -- he did that all on his own because he's not good. The 49ers simply had to keep him in the pocket, which they did for the most part. Nix finished the game with just two rushes for 10 yards. He's not good enough to beat the 49ers from the pocket, which he proved today.
Dre Greenlaw made the Broncos pay for letting him go this offseason by recording a team-high 12 tackles and a forced fumble. Sean Payton must have been so upset that Greenlaw never played like that for the Broncos last season. Fred Warner also had seven tackles and two pass breakups in this game. He was a terrific sidekick to Greenlaw, who was the star for a change.
They held Bo Nix to a minuscule 5.1 yards per pass attempt without a pass rush. That means they just blanketed the Broncos' receivers all game. Not an easy thing to do. The only time the Broncos really moved the ball effectively was when Upton Stout left the game with a shoulder injury. After the game, he had ice wrapped around his shoulder, and he couldn't move his arm. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said Stout has an AC sprain, which sounds painful. The 49ers defense is so much better with him on the field than without him. His replacement, Jack Jones, gave up a touchdown catch almost immediately.
Eddy Pineiro had a 54-yard field-goal attempt blocked. He hasn't been nearly as good this season as he was a year ago. He's someone to monitor. Fortunately for this position group, Siran Neal recovered a muffed punt deep in Broncos territory, and this set up a touchdown for the 49ers. Neal is playing like a Pro Bowl special teams player.
Raheem Morris was the best coach on the field today. He shut down the Broncos offense with half a defensive line. Morris is rolling right now because opposing coaches don't know his tendencies with this defense. Teams are still learning how he's calling plays for this group, which is a huge advantage for the 49ers. Meanwhile, Kyle Shanahan produced his worst performance of the season, partially because his offense is so banged up and Denver's defense is good. Still, he didn't leverage his biggest advantage -- Purdy's mobility -- until the fourth quarter. Shanahan had Purdy dropping straight back all game. Purdy had to call his own number and run when he saw openings. Finally, in the fourth quarter, Shanahan called a play-action pass that was designed for Purdy to roll to his left. He hit Evans for 17 yards, and the 49ers scored a one-yard touchdown on the next play. Finally, Shanahan called a brilliant screen pass for Kittle that put the game away. Which means when Shanahan had to be at his best, he was, even though he struggled for three quarters. That's impressive. Does this win mean the 49ers are the best team in the NFL? Not necessarily, no. They can prove that next week against the Seattle Seahawks. But for now, the 49ers are undefeated, and their team hasn't even gotten healthy yet. If it ever healthies up, watch out. This could be their year.

title: 9 Biggest Takeaways From 49ers' Week 4 Win Over Broncos
full_text:
Well, that was a close one.
The San Francisco 49ers gut out a tough 24-14 win over the Denver Broncos to improve to 4-0. Let's dive into the nine biggest takeaways from the game.
Aside from the perfectly called screen pass to George Kittle in the fourth quarter, Kyle Shanahan was confusing in this game. The first half was atrocious for the 49ers' offense.
You can credit that to Denver's defense, but many of the offensive woes were due to poor play calls. Shanahan wasn't in his bag this game. He needs to bounce back next week against a tougher opponent.
Unlike his last two games, Brock Purdy wasn't on fire against the Broncos. It was to be expected since he wasn't facing a poor defense. He still played well, but he definitely cooled down.
Shanahan didn't do him any favors in this game either. Purdy did have a few sweet plays, like a perfect pass to Mike Evans in the second quarter.
The first touchdown of the game was thanks to Purdy going off script. It wasn't a good play call by Shanahan, so Purdy had to bail him out by flushing out of the pocket to hit Deebo Samuel for a wide-open touchdown.
Overall, Purdy is playing at a high level. While he did cool down in this game, he was still fairly sharp and took care of the football. He'll need a game like this or better next week against Seattle.
It seemed like Purdy was under a bit more pressure in this game, but he was mostly comfortable in the pocket today against one of the best pass-rushing units in the NFL.
He still hasn't been sacked yet, which is insane. After this game, I think it's safe to say that the 49ers' offensive line is legit, if not a great unit in pass protection. They proved themselves today.
Similar to last week's takeaways, I'm using this as a George Kittle appreciation post. He essentially iced the game with his 56-yard touchdown run from a screen pass in the fourth quarter.
Kittle looks like he's never lost a step, even though he's 32 and tore his Achilles less than nine months ago. This guy is special. Generational even.
It was nuts for the 49ers to play Mike Evans today when he most likely has fractured ribs. But they clearly needed him out there. Their receivers are lacking in quality outside of him and Samuel.
He put on a gutsy performance, tallying five catches for 76 yards. You could see he was in extreme discomfort on every target—a round of applause for his toughness and ability to ball out still.
Denver has one of the worst run defenses in the league, which made it low-hanging fruit for the 49ers to attack with Christian McCaffrey. However, their run defense was sound today.
McCaffrey barely saw any daylight, as the Broncos made sure to cover any rushing lanes. Either the Broncos stepped up huge today, or their run defense is only skewed badly from Week 1.
One player who never misses games is Kyle Juszczyk. Unfortunately, he suffered a brutal hit to his knee, causing it to hyperextend. He needed help from trainers to walk off the field. The fear right now would be a torn ACL, so fingers crossed it isn't anything too signficant.
Without Nick Bosa , the 49ers' pass rush is nonexistent. The defense as a whole played well for most of this game, but it's clear they need to add a pass rusher.
John Lynch needs to be on the phone with the Chargers immediately to see what it'll take to acquire Khalil Mack. I'd imagine they'll be interested now that they're 0-4.
One of the main reasons the 49ers won this game was thanks to Bo Nix . He's an awful quarterback. The only way he can succeed is if his first read is there or if he turns it into backyard football.
Nix is Jimmy Garoppolo 2.0. All he was missing was a turnover in his performance today to emphasize how awful he played. Denver won't go far this year because of him.

title: 49ers' George Kittle Becomes All-Time Franchise Touchdown Leader by a Tight End
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle made history in Week 4 after securing a 24-14 win against the Denver Broncos.
Kittle sealed the game with a 56-yard touchdown, sprinting into the end zone to surpass Vernon Davis and become the 49ers' all-time touchdown leader among tight ends.
Davis recorded 55 touchdowns during his tenure with the team, while Kittle's latest achievement was his fourth of the season, taking his total to 56.
It's only Week 4 into the season and Kittle has already sealed the record. It's incredible and almost unthinkable that he's in this position because of the Achilles injury he picked up in January.
He missed the entire offseason but managed to be fit for Week 1, just eight months later, well ahead of the realistic recovery timeline for such a severe injury. He was evidently rusty in Week 1, but it didn't matter as the 49ers dominated the Los Angeles Rams.
But in Week 2 against the Miami Dolphins, Week 3 against the Arizona Cardinals and now Week 4 against the Broncos, Kittle has been simply electric. Across those three games at Levi's Stadium, he has recorded four touchdowns, 232 receiving yards and several crucial catches. Kittle is playing at a ridiculous level.
He's blown away every realistic expectation placed on him so far this season. But that's exactly what deserves praise. At 32, soon to be 33, his physicality remains unquestionable, and this injury has seemingly only made him better. He's come back looking even stronger than before.
It's even fair to say the Broncos would present the toughest challenge yet because of their defense. It's one of the best in the league for a reason. Yet his game-winning touchdown looked effortless.
And now, wth this touchdown feat, Kittle's legacy with the 49ers is all but complete. He has the most receptions and touchdowns by a tight end and will now go on to set new records that will be tough to surpass.
Without question, he is one of the most influential draft picks of the Kyle Shanahan era, and how fitting that he produced when the 49ers needed him most, on the occasion of Shanahan becoming the longest-serving head coach in franchise history.
It's Year 10 and Kittle has shown no signs of slowing down or any regression in his game. A place in the 49ers museum and franchise Hall of Fame awaits.

title: Star Buccaneers Defender Out For Multiple Weeks After Week 4 Injury
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers lost their Week 4 matchup against the Green Bay Packers 17-14 in Week 4, but the loss wasn't the only fallout.
The Buccaneers' star safety, Antoine Winfield Jr., went down on the field toward the back half of the game holding his abdomen, and he did not return to action. Head coach Todd Bowles told media after the game that the team was running tests on Winfield Jr.'s injury, and those tests didn't come back the way Bowles or Winfield likely hoped.
Bowles confirmed to reporters on Monday that Winfield Jr. fractured his ribs, and he's expected to be sidelined anywhere from two to four weeks with the injury.
"We won't have Winfield Thursday. He has a slight rib fracture — he'll be out two to four weeks probably, from what I'm hearing."
Winfield is Tampa Bay's starting safety, and as a former All-Pro, he's crucial to the defense. Winfield signed a four-year, $84.1 million extension with the Bucs after a dominant 2023 season, and he's been playing alongside safety Tykee Smith for the last two years.
So far this season, Winfield has netted 15 solo tackles and one forced fumble. With him out of the picture for the next few weeks, the team will turn to safety Ifeatu Melifonwu to take his place — Melifonwu played for Miami last year and came to Tampa Bay in the offseason.
The depth behind Winfield remains precarious. With both Melifonwu and Smith starting, the only other safety on the roster is Miles Killebrew, who is mainly a special teams player. The Bucs have two safeties on the practice squad in JJ Roberts and Silas Walters, so the team may be forced to elevate one of those two players to replace Winfield.
The Bucs also have a spot on the practice squad open after defensive back Sean Murphy-Bunting (who could also play safety) was signed to the Pittsburgh Steelers' 53-man roster. The Bucs may look to add another defensive back there, too.
Tampa Bay is set to play the Dallas Cowboys in just three days on Thursday Night Football.

title: Buccaneers Lose Super Bowl Champion Corner to the Steelers
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers' defensive back depth got a little thinner on Monday, just one day after the Bucs lost to the Green Bay Packers in Week 4.
The Buccaneers brought on defensive back Sean Murphy-Bunting at the beginning of the season to the practice squad to shore up cornerback depth and add a veteran presence to the roster. Through the first four games, Murphy-Bunting, who won a Super Bowl with Tampa Bay in 2020, was not elevated.
Keeping a player on the practice squad has some risks, and the Bucs faced the brunt of that on Monday when Murphy-Bunting was signed away from the team.
The Pittsburgh Steelers have signed Murphy-Bunting to their active roster, per The Ringer's Tom Pelissero.
The Steelers are signing veteran CB Sean Murphy-Bunting off the Bucs' practice squad, per source. Murphy-Bunting has played in 82 NFL games (65 starts) and has 11 career interceptions. Some experienced depth for Pittsburgh after the Joey Porter Jr. trade. pic.twitter.com/waUZp7F8Jg
The move gives Pittsburgh some cornerback depth after the Joey Porter Jr. trade, where the Steelers sent Porter to the Cowboys. Another reason why Pittsburgh is bringing on Murphy-Bunting has to do with another Super Bowl-winning Buccaneer who played alongside Murphy-Bunting in 2020.
The Steelers signed cornerback Jamel Dean in free agency after the Bucs let him walk this year, and just like in Tampa Bay, Dean has had some trouble staying healthy. Murphy-Bunting is an option for the Steelers while Dean recovers, and he may be thrust into a playing role sooner than later.
Murphy-Bunting recorded no stats in Tampa Bay this year, but last year, he had three interceptions with the Arizona Cardinals and recorded five pass deflections. The Bucs have been using a rotation of Benjamin Morrison, Jacob Parrish and Zyon McCollum on the outside, so Murphy-Bunting has never needed to be elevated so far this season.
Now that he's off the practice squad, however, the Bucs could find another corner to fill his spot. Morrison recently injured his quad in practice and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. is also dealing with an oblique injury, so another defensive back — perhaps one who can also play safety — could be a good move for general Jason Licht and the Bucs after Murphy-Bunting's departure.
The Bucs play the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday Night Football on the road, and it will be interesting to see if they replace Murphy-Bunting's spot on the squad before that game in just three days.

title: Buccaneers Suffer Multiple Injuries After Loss to Packers
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers had a tough go of things on Sunday in Week 4 against the Green Bay Packers. The team wasn't able to do enough to stave off Green Bay, falling 17-14 and moving to a dreadful 0-4 on the season.
That loss did come with some injury to insult. The Buccaneers had two defensive players injured in this contest, and they're both names to monitor as the Bucs turn around and play the Dallas Cowboys in just three days.
Safety Antoine Winfield Jr. and linebacker SirVocea Dennis both got injured during the team's loss to the Packers.
Dennis played mostly on special teams Sunday, and he injured his ankle a little over halfway through the contest. Dennis was ruled out and did not return to the game — fellow linebackers Christian Rozeboom and Josiah Trotter played in spurts throughout the game.
The more significant injury, however, is to Winfield. Winfield is one of Tampa Bay's two starting safeties, and he went down toward the end of the game. Head coach Todd Bowles referred to the injury as an oblique injury, and any potential absence from Winfield would be a dangerous prospect for the Bucs.
Tampa Bay started out the season with just three safeties on the 53-man roster. The team officially signed safety Ifeatu Melifonwu before Sunday's game, so now they have four — one of those safeties is the other starter Tykee Smith, one is Winfield, one is Melifonwu and another is safety Miles Killebrew.
Killebrew is largely a special teams player who doesn't have much value playing safety, so the Bucs would be in a tough spot if Melifonwu were the only option to replace Winfield. Unfortunately, that may be the case — the Bucs have to play the Cowboys three days from now, so any injury to Winfield might be too much to overcome until then.
Bowles will speak to the media at 1:45 p.m., which is when he'll update the media on Winfield and Dennis' condition. The Bucs will look to beat the Cowboys in search of their first win of the 2025 season.

title: Buccaneers' 0-4 Start Puts Them in Line for No. 1 Pick
full_text:
It's a disaster in Tampa Bay.
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have now started the season 0-4 for the first time since 2013, and it doesn't appear that things are going to improve.
If the Bucs continue on this route, they are in line for one of the top picks in the 2027 NFL Draft.
If things hold, and the season continues the way that it has gone, the Bucs will be in a situation where they are in line for a high draft pick, if not the first overall pick in next year's draft.
They will have plenty of options.
As things stand now, the Bucs would have the third overall pick behind the Houston Texans and the Tennessee Titans.
Both of those teams don't necessarily need a quarterback, so the hype surrounding Arch Manning, Dante Moore or another quarterback will be a hot topic of conversation if things stand.
That brings into question whether or not Jeremiah Smith would be available, or the opportunity to trade back and accumulate tremendous draft capital in the process.
The interesting aspect of it all will come down to who the Buccaneers will decide to employ for both the head coach and general manager positions. Jason Licht likely has a bit more comfort in his role, but the likelihood of Todd Bowles remaining the head coach is reaching a point where it's almost a foregone conclusion that he won't return.
If both Bowles and Licht get the axe at some point, then the strategy for the Bucs could completely change depending on how the new powers that be want to build the roster.
There are a ton of games left on the schedule, so this whole thing could be moot by the end of the season. But the reality is that the Buccaneers are not a good football team and are well-positioned to have a top pick in the draft.
If that does indeed come to fruition, then the likely new staff will have plenty of options at their disposal.
One thing is for sure — something has to change. But the question is, how will it and who will do it?

title: Grading Every Buccaneers Position Group From Their Week 4 Loss to the Packers
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers lost another game and fell to 0-4 on the season after a 17-14 loss to the Green Bay Packers.
This team continues to find more ways to lose football games and simply cannot and will not be able to do anything of real note this season. Let's go ahead and take a look at what grades the Bucs' position groups earned in this matchup.
All things considered, I thought that Jalon Daniels was a very pleasant surprise for the Buccaneers in this game. Yes, he did throw two interceptions, but he also was able to make some good throws and was an absolute threat on his feet with 55 rushing yards during the contest as well.
Daniels didn't have much help in this game with an offensive line that simply couldn't block for him, but I think he showed enough to be intrigued by what he could do against Dallas on Thursday night football.
Bucky Irving had 16 carries for 61 yards, and Sean Tucker and Kenny Gainwell had touchdowns in this matchup. While all of those things were great, this group still is not doing a good job of picking up blitzing players, which will continue to lower their grade until proven otherwise.
We know that all three of these running backs do some good work with the football in their hands. Now, it's just a matter of doing the dirty work and helping protect the quarterback when needed.
Chris Godwin Jr, and Emeka Egbuka combined for eight catches on 11 targets for 44 yards and no touchdowns in this game. Both have looked like an absolute far cry from expectations this season, and it doesn't seem to matter whether it's Baker Mayfield or Daniels — these guys are not getting the football.
Ted Hurst III and Tez Johnson had a couple of nice catches in this game, but overall, the wide receiver room continues to be one of the bigger disappointments this season.
Starting tight end Cade Otton had another drop in this game, but he did lead the team with 37 receiving yards on four catches. Honestly, it looks like the Bucs made a mistake bringing back Otton at the contract they did, as he looks like a very replaceable player at a position that simply is not giving the team a lot of value.
Payne Durham and Bauer Sharpe didn't do anything of note in this game, as both were on special teams duty, with Ko Kieft missing this matchup due to injury.
The Bucs offensive line continues to be one of the worst units in the entire NFL. They get a D here because they were actually able to hold up well in run blocking. However, They've got to be one of the worst interior units in the entire NFL, and regardless of who is out there at quarterback between Daniels and Mayfield, they cannot get any type of protection to help them.
Jordan Love felt comfortable throughout the game today as the Bucs only finished with two quarterback hits and zero sacks in this matchup. We even saw the run defense of the Bucs give up multiple gashes for big gains throughout this contest that helped spell defeat for the team.
I am still of the mindset that Christian Rozeboom needs to play more. It's not that Alex Anzalone and Josiah Trotter played terribly today, it's just a matter of Rozeboom playing better than both of them when he is on the field. There were a couple of missed tackles by Trotter in this game early on, but overall, we've seen much worse from this unit this season.
Jacob Parrish had an interception today, and Tykee Smith forced a red zone fumble for this Bucs defense. It's still pretty wild that this is the far and away best position group on this team week in and week out, but here we are.
Not really anything to say on special teams today, Chase McLaughlin made his kicks and Riley Dixon was average at punting, just as they've been during their time in Tampa Bay.

title: Overreactions From Buccaneers' Loss to the Packers
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers couldn't get it done on Sunday during Jalon Daniels' first start. Tampa Bay lost its game against the Green Bay Packers 17-14, dropping to 0-4 on the year.
The Bucs have a lot of season ahead of them, and some people may be inclined to overreact — and that's exactly what we're doing after this disastrous start. Here are three overreactions from today's loss:
The Bucs defense didn't seem to play too poorly in this game on points alone, but this Packers offense was very, very bad heading into this game. The Bucs generally allowed Green Bay to do what it wanted, showing that the defense's performance against the Vikings was more a fluke than the truth.
The Packers' rushing record this season heading into Week 4 was a measly 66 yards, and the Packers broke that record and put up 98 net yards against the Bucs. Green Bay went for three fourth-down conversions on the day, and they converted on all of them, the last of which was a touchdown.
The Bucs let a paltry Packers offense score two touchdowns and let Jordan Love be quite efficient on the day. There will be much, much greater offenses to contend with down the line, and this Bucs defense still won't be able to contain those offenses.
Running back Sean Tucker can make things happen when he gets the football, and he showed that on Sunday. He scored a touchdown to give the Bucs their first six points, and he powered through on a fourth-and-one play to extend that drive.
The problem? He only had three carries the entire game. Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell didn't average many more yards than he did (Irving 3.8 to Tucker's 3.3, Gainwell 1.7), and he showcased his motor in the limited time he got.
Gainwell ended up catching a passing touchdown, so he's still valuable, and Irving has shown himself to be the lead back. But it may be time to let Tucker get the ball more and see what good things happen when he does.
The Bucs have fallen to 0-4. There's only been one team to make the playoffs in NFL history after a start like that — the 1992 Chargers, a team that rattled off 11 wins in their next 12 games to make the playoffs that year.
This Bucs team, quite frankly, does not have that in them. Daniels isn't ready to be a starting quarterback in the NFL — he'll have to play a Dallas Cowboys team next week and a Pittsburgh Steelers team the week after that, and both of those teams are better than this Packers team the Bucs just lost to.
This is likely it for the Bucs. They are not making the playoffs, and they'll probably lose enough games this year to have a very high pick in the 2027 NFL Draft in April.

title: Is Baker Mayfield Trying to Come Back Earlier Than the Buccaneers' Timetable?
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are on a quest to get their first win — and save their season — in Week 4 against the Green Bay Packers. It'll be a tough task given how poor the team has looked over the first two weeks, but it'll be even harder with a backup quarterback.
The Bucs are rolling with undrafted free agent rookie Jalon Daniels at starter after incumbent signal caller Baker Mayfield dislocated his thumb at the end of the game against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 3. When asked what Mayfield's timetable was, Bowles confirmed that following Monday that the team expected him to be out for at least three weeks.
Mayfield is no stranger to playing through injury, though. And a new report from The Ringer's Tom Pelissero may indicate that Mayfield is trying to beat his timeline.
Pelissero reported on Saturday that Mayfield is getting the stitches removed from his thumb on Monday, which he added is part of his quest to beat his initial three-week timeline.
Bucs QB Baker Mayfield is scheduled to have stitches removed from his thumb Monday — an important step as he pushes to beat the three-week timeline for returning. More in The Sweep: https://t.co/1GBRb85fBa pic.twitter.com/mhL84q6M7B
What exactly does that mean, though? The first thing to note is that three weeks do not equal three games in this instance.
The Bucs have a unique scenario in the next few days where they'll play the Packers on Sunday and then travel to Dallas to play the Cowboys on Thursday Night Football just four days later. The Bucs then do not play the following Sunday, of course, and then they'll play the next Sunday against the Pittsburgh Steelers at home.
Because of that, that Steelers game will be three weeks after the Sunday when Mayfield dislocated his thumb, which would be just two games missed. Mayfield may be shooting for this benchmark — alternatively, he could be trying to come back faster.
Mayfield playing against the Cowboys seems like a very tall task, however, so expecting that may be misguided. That Steelers game looks to be the best target. But Mayfield has played through injury before and could be trying to make it back way before then — especially if the Bucs win on Sunday against the Packers.
For now, the Bucs have to go with Daniels against the Packers in Raymond James Stadium at 1 p.m. on Sunday. If the Bucs fall to 0-4, their playoff chances are almost entirely squandered . A win could keep them alive in the NFC South, though, and that may be exactly what Mayfield is thinking when it comes to his return timetable.

Give me the Bucs to finally get a win.

I have a bold prediction: Daniels will take care of the ball and not turn it over, but in the end, the Packers will win. I think there will be more juice in this offense just from how Daniels can operate and utilize his scramble ability and using his live arm.

title: 3 Key Areas Buccaneers Have Advantage over Packers: The Run Game Difference
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are struggling. They're 0-3 to start the season, and what's worse, they're set to start a backup quarterback in UDFA rookie Jalon Daniels on Sunday. The Bucs have faltered in numerous areas this season, but despite what some may think when watching the team, they aren't the worst squad in the NFL.
That team may very well be the Green Bay Packers, whom the Bucs play on Sunday. The Packers do have a win, but via advanced metrics, there's almost nothing they do right — and that means there are plenty of areas the Bucs have an advantage.
Here's where the Bucs triumph over the Packers heading into Sunday's matchup at 1 p.m. in Raymond James Stadium:
It cannot be understated how bad this Packers run game is.
The Packers are dead last or tied for dead last in every NFL volume stat for rushing (3.0 yards per rush, 48.7 yards per game). They run the ball at a league-low rate, too, rushing a staggering 26.67% of the time. Their advanced metrics are not better, obviously — per SumerSports, they're putting up a ridiculous -0.407 EPA/play on the ground (32nd) and have a success rate of 33.3% (30th).
Conversely, Tampa Bay has a better run game. They're 12th in the league in yards per rush (4.3) but just 23rd in rush yards per game (94.3). Even still, they have a rush EPA/play of -0.056 (13th) and a success rate of 40.9% (20th). That might not sound impressive, but that's leagues better than what Green Bay is producing.
The Bucs will need to lean on the run game to help Daniels in his first NFL start. But they certainly won't have to worry about Green Bay's.
Tampa Bay has had some big struggles on defense, but letting teams score in the red zone has not been one of them.
Tampa Bay has allowed opposing teams in the red zone to score a touchdown on just 37.50% of attempts, good for No. 4 in the league. Tampa Bay is putting up a defensive EPA/play of -0.169 in the red zone — negative numbers here are good for the defense, and that ranks eighth in the league so far.
The Packers, meanwhile, have certainly not been effective in the red zone. They've converted red zone trips to touchdowns on just 41.67% of their drives, good for 29th in the NFL. They put up an astounding -0.485 EPA/play in the red zone, which is 31st of 32 teams in the NFL.
Scoring points down in the red zone wins football games, and the Packers might have a particularly tough time doing that on Sunday.
The Bucs are very fortunate to have Chase McLaughlin. When McLaughlin kicks, points go on the board.
McLaughlin has yet to miss anything this season, hitting every field goal he has been asked to and every extra point for a 100% efficiency. He's hit a long of 59 yards this year and scored 32 points for the Buccaneers, which is tied for first in the league.
The Packers, meanwhile, can't quite say the same about their own special teams. Green Bay's kicker Trey Smack has already had a kick blocked this year, and he has also missed an extra point, putting him at 83.3% for both regular field goals and extra points this season.
With McLaughlin at the helm, the Bucs only need to get in striking distance before they can put points on the board.

title: Multiple Key Buccaneers Players Out vs. Packers
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers face a must-win game against the Green Bay Packers on Sunday in hopes of avoiding a dreaded 0-4 start on the year. The team will be down their starting quarterback Baker Mayfield and will turn to undrafted free agent Jalon Daniels to try and guide the offense to a win.
Mayfield isn't the only Buccaneers player hurt, though. The team is dealing with a few different injuries heading into Sunday, and it will have to overcome them to beat the Packers and try to get what has been a disastrous season so far back on track.
Here's what Tampa Bay's injury report will look like on Friday:
The Buccaneers have a number of players out for Sunday's matchup against the Packers.
Todd Bowles confirms that Baker Mayfield, Benjamin Morrison, Ko Kieft and Rueben Bain are OUT. Josiah Trotter and Yaya Diaby should be good to go Sunday. pic.twitter.com/xiFoyJnem5
The most notable players out are cornerback Benjamin Morrison, dealing with a quad injury, and outside linebacker Rueben Bain, dealing with a groin injury. Morrison appears to have injured his quad during practice Thursday and will not play, while Bain has been recovering from a groin injury he suffered in Week 2 against the Cleveland Browns.
Morrison played just one defensive snap in Tampa Bay's Week 3 loss to the Vikings, but he still provides strong depth for the unit. With Bain out once again, edge rushers like Anthony Nelson and David Walker will certainly get more time as starter Yaya Diaby deals with a calf injury — Bowles said Friday that Diaby should be fine.
Additionally, tight end Ko Kieft will be out with an elbow injury. As frequently discussed, Mayfield isn't on injured reserve, so he will also be listed as out with a thumb dislocation on the injury report.
CB Jacob Parrish and linebacker SirVocea Dennis both returned to practice after taking personal leaves, and linebacker Josiah Trotter should be good to go for Sunday. Parrish was absent for two days due to a personal matter, and while he will almost certainly play, his absence for the first two days of practice could see the Bucs elevate a defensive back from the practice squad or have CB Ayden Garnes active for the first time this season.

title: Titans Stock Report: 3 Players Rising and 2 Falling After Defeat vs. Ravens
full_text:
Looking at an 0-4 team, the Tennessee Titans can really only be positively viewed on an individual spectrum. Yesterday's 24-18 loss to the Baltimore Ravens yielded many of the same team-wide worries that have plagued Robert Saleh's first season.
Yet, a select few players still found ways to grow. There are pieces that are working on their own within this Titans team, it's just a matter of finding the right fits for those pieces on a regular basis.
Until then, here are three players rising (and two unfortunately falling) after Tennessee's defeat in Week 4.
Tate was comfortably Tennessee's best player on the field yesterday. Even taking in his notable downfield fumble, the rookie WR had his best game of the season so far. He appears to be Ward's favorite target already, and is only improving with every passing week.
The fourth overall pick hauled in nine receptions for 145 yards - both season-highs - and caught a two-point conversion late in the fourth quarter. It's hard to scold Tate for his individual mistake in light of the team's dire overall struggles.
If anyone gets a pass up to now, it's Tate. The rookie has already begun to make good on Tennessee's first-round investment. A big, big riser after Week 4.
For the second straight week, Spears nearly missed a game due to being questionable with an ankle issue. For the second straight week, Spears was barely involved on the ground or through the air. He has to occupy a falling spot following Week 4.
Against Baltimore, Spears had just two carries for seven yards. He caught one pass for a loss of a yard, and that was Spears' only target. Rookie back Nick Singleton even outpaced Spears in carries, with three.
Tony Pollard has become the only reliable rushing option on this Titans team. If you'd have said that going into the year, some folks may have scoffed. Tennessee's backfield is slowly growing thinner every Sunday, and Spears' recent cold stretch definitely plays a part in that.
EDGE Jermaine Johnson has quietly become a consistent contributor on defense for Tennessee. In yesterday's duel with Baltimore, the 27-year old veteran finally broke through.
Johnson leveled four tackles in total, two of which went for a loss. He also managed to secure his first sack of the season on a play that helped bottle the Ravens' driving offense before the half. Johnson finally looked the part of someone worth trading for.
Tennessee needs reliable pressure from the EDGE moving forward, but Week 4 marked a step in the right direction for Johnson. He's a certified riser on this list.
Barton may have led the Titans in tackles (tied with Anthony Hill Jr. with eight), but the veteran LB was in over his head facing the Ravens' offense.
WR Zay Flowers flamed Barton when the LB was forced to cover him vertically. That was just one of many plays in which Ravens OC Declan Doyle was able to take advantage of Barton. On another, Barton bit on Mark Andrews motioning to the right, which led to a wide open Devontez Walker right behind him. Credit to Turron Davenport for that spot.
Hill has proven his worth as a starter alongside Barton, but the argument that Cedric Gray should be in the latter position instead is growing stronger. Barton simply looks a step behind in Saleh's defensive system.
Ward deserves a slight positive mention on this list. As vocal as we've been about criticizing him when need be, for the most part, Ward improved yesterday.
Is he inconsistent? Yes, especially on dink-and-dunk attempts. However, Ward's 222-yard showing came with more than a few impressive balls. Part of Tate's breakout is due to Ward finding him downfield and through some tight windows, at that. You also have to mention his fourth-quarter scoring drive, which saw Ward complete a touchdown and a two-point conversion in the air.
Ward's first-drive interception falls more on Tony Pollard than it does him, and that was his only egregious mistake of the day. Not a great outing, but an encouraging one nonetheless. Titans fans should be excited to see if Ward can continue to build on this promise moving forward.

title: Titans Mill: Does Blame For Offensive Woes Fall on Cam Ward, Brian Daboll, or Both After Week 4?
full_text:
Against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 4, the Tennessee Titans' struggles once again came down to an inability to keep up with the opposing offense. Lamar Jackson is a two-time MVP - few teams can keep pace with him - but he exited for most of the second half with an ankle injury.
Tyler Huntley checked in for the Ravens, didn't score a single point in the final two quarters, and Baltimore still won. Tennessee's offense once again failed to generate enough momentum to fully turn the tide, even if their numbers looked better on paper.
Entering Week 5 without a win, who is to blame here? Cam Ward and Brian Daboll are really the only two names that belong in this discussion. The lame answer, but the true one, is that each of them have responsibility to shoulder here.
On a play-to-play basis, Ward still has to be better. His 222 yards on 20/31 passing vs. the Ravens may be his best performance of the season, and the interception he threw on the first drive was hardly his fault.
But a series of three-and-outs in the second half, as well as another batch of inaccurate passes, signal that Ward still isn't where the Titans need him to be. His footwork appears a step slow, and misses on short- single-yardage routes stack up against a player.
Carnell Tate ( who had a massive day of his own ) had a potential score on a wide open route in the second quarter, only for Ward to sail the ball over his head. You just can't have that.
But you also can't have an OC that doesn't trust your passer, and that's Daboll's issue.
For the perfect example, look no further than Daboll dialing up four straight running plays on first and goal. That decision came after Tony Pollard had already gotten in for a score, and it cost Tennessee an expected game-tying touchdown before the half.
The Titans didn't trust Ward in the red zone until Tennessee was two scores behind in the fourth quarter, when he delivered on a quick scoring drive that resulted in a Wan'Dale Robinson touchdown. Daboll dug Tennessee a hole, and he and Ward as a duo couldn't climb out of in in the second half.
Daboll did open up the playbook downfield to some extent. Ward reached a new passing peak this year, and the aforementioned Tate secured nine receptions for 145 yards. But when it mattered - the shots on goal - Daboll fell short.
There's no specific split of the blame here. However, Ward is now 3-18 as a starter. Brian Daboll has yet to spur this Titans offense past 20 points, or to a victory. Each of them have to improve fast, and they'll have to find a way to do it together.

title: Postgame Quotes That Matter From Robert Saleh and What They Reveal About Titans' Week 4 Loss to Ravens
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans will have to wait at least another week for their first win of 2026, as the team fell to the Baltimore Ravens 24-18 on the road.
Despite Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson sitting out the second half with an ankle injury, the 24-7 halftime deficit was too much for Tennessee to overcome in the end. The Titans are now 0-4 and have lost each of the last three games by one score.
Head coach Robert Saleh spoke about Tennessee's loss in his postgame press conference and had some interesting things to say.
Saleh was asked about failing to come away with the victory despite shutting out Baltimore in the second half, and the Titans head coach said it was frustrating before eventually stating that Sunday's contest was goofy.
"It was frustrating overall from a viewing standpoint," Saleh said. "Offense came out with a lot of juice. It was a goofy game. It didn't feel like 24-7 at halftime. But I do appreciate the fact that everyone came out and fought. But overall disappointing."
Tennessee had a bunch of missed chances on Sunday that doomed them in the end. The Ravens are a premier contender in the AFC, but the Titans beat themselves in multiple aspects and basically gave themselves no chance to pull off the road upset.
Saleh was also asked about the offensive play calling, especially in the red zone. The Titans ran the ball seven times in a row in the red zone during the second quarter, and came away with no points after getting stuffed on fourth-and-goal. Saleh defended his offensive coordinator, Brian Daboll, and commended the coaching staff for working hard to call the best possible play in any situation.
"Felt like we were running the ball pretty well," Saleh said. "That's something I'll defintely have a conversation with Daboll about. In those situations, the guys work their tails off to call the best plays in that situation based on what we've seen on tape. I'm pleased with the preparation that goes into it. We'll figure out what we have to do better."
Tennessee's conversative offensive play calling has plagued them all year. It doesn't seem like Daboll has full trust in quarterback Cam Ward to operate in key situations , and it's completely killing the offense as a result.
One of the major bright spots for the Titans in the loss Sunday was rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate. Though the Ohio State product committed a fumble, Tate hauled in nine receptions for 145 yards and looked like the player Tennessee drafted with the No. 4 overall pick in April.
Saleh praised his rookie receiver and said Tate will be a good player in the NFL for a while .
"He's a young kid and he's going to get better. He's going to get more consistent. He's going to be a good player for a while."
Tate has been gaining momentum over the last two weeks and has been stepping up as the Titans' top receiving option. The 21-year-old has all the tools to be a No. 1 receiver for years to come, and it was awesome to see him stand out in Week 4.
The Titans will return home next week to face the winless Houston Texans at Nissan Stadium. One AFC South team will tally its first victory of the year, and we'll see if it is Tennessee.

title: Cam Ward in Titans' 24-18 Loss to Ravens: Tennessee Still Can’t Find Consistency
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans dropped their fourth consecutive game of the season, losing to the Baltimore Ravens 24-18.
The game wasn’t as close as the score would indicate, but credit to the Titans for fighting until the very end in a game that got away from them relatively quickly. Tennessee’s offense showed signs of life throughout the first half, but two turnovers ultimately killed promising drives.
The first came on an ill-advised play in which QB Cam Ward tried to make something out of nothing. In an attempt to avoid a sack, Ward flicked the ball to RB Tony Pollard, who didn’t seem like he was expecting it.
The ball then went through his hands, subsequently falling into the grasp of Ravens LB Trenton Simpson for an interception — Ward’s second pick over his last three passes dating back to the Giants game. The Titans signal caller discussed the early turnover shortly after the game.
“I just think I can make it easier for him (Pollard). Me and Tony, we’ve hit on that play a lot of times last year… I know he wants that play back. I want it back. But if I can put it on his chest and make it easier for him, then he’ll have a chance to get upfield.”
Tennessee then turned the ball over again on what should’ve been the final drive of the half. Rookie WR Carnell Tate fumbled the ball on a play that would've resulted in a big gain. Instead, Baltimore got the ball back in prime position to set up a last-second field goal to end the half with a 24-7 lead.
Despite the rocky ending to the half , the blossoming connection between Ward and Tate was evident throughout the game. The Titans clearly prioritized getting the two top five picks involved, and it paid off. Tate finished the game with nine catches for 145 yards — the highest total in a single game by a Titans wide receiver since AJ Brown.
Impressive numbers no doubt, but there was undoubtedly still a lot of meat left on the bone. An encouraging sign for Tennessee’s top tandem going forward, nevertheless.
Outside of their budding connection, Ward wasn’t able to get much going with anybody else. WRs Wan’Dale Robinson, Elic Ayomanor and Calvin Ridley combined for just 54 yards on five catches. It's clear he needs more help outside of Tate, but at least we started to see the flashes from Ward that made him an intriguing prospect to begin with.
The Titans QB was asked how he evaluates a game where plays were made, but not enough to realistically have a chance to win at the end:
“[We have to] br critical on the good plays, but we have to really hone in on the bad plays and how we can limit that. That’s what’s holding us back, offensively. That’s what’s holding the team back. We have to limit the bad plays on both sides of the ball. But I think once we do that, we’ll put ourselves in good situations to win games.”
Another encouraging sign for Tennessee was Ward‘s patience in the pocket. He touched on that topic after the game, giving the bulk of the credit to his offensive line for holding up against a talented Ravens front.
“Yeah, I for sure was (more patient). That’s just me trusting the o-line, continuously feeling the pocket — not letting one rush affect me for the rest of the game," said Ward.
"I think I stood tall to that. I think the o-line did a fantastic job protecting me. Even on the sack, I feel I should’ve been able to get out of that. But at the end of the day, those guys keep us in the ballgame.”
Despite the solid days by the offensive line and their rookie receiver, there were still far too many drives that stalled out, either through turnovers or because they never got going altogether. At one point, the Titans had three straight three-and-outs between the end of the second quarter and the start of the third.
The two right after halftime were especially disappointing, because it was clear Ravens QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) wasn’t likely to return to the game, so the opportunity to get back into it was there for the taking. But in typical Titans fashion, they fail to capitalize on it, and instead, wait until the very end to make it close.
However, the Ward-Tate connection is definitely something to build on going forward. If those two can consistently connect like they did today, then better days are undoubtedly ahead for this offense.
But for this team to reach its true potential, they got to stop finding ways to beat themselves. Until that happens, losses will continue to pile up, because it’s clear that this team doesn’t have the talent or experience needed to overcome those kinds of mistakes.

title: 2 Winners and Losers From Titans' Week 4 Loss to Ravens: Carnell Tate's Big Day Not Big Enough
full_text:
Different week, same result. The Tennessee Titans are 0-4, falling 24-18 to the Baltimore Ravens in yet another familiar defeat.
The offense turns the ball over on the first drive, puzzling red-zone play-calling suffocates rare momentum, and an explosive offense on the other side of the line picks apart Robert Saleh's defense in chunks. The new head coach remains without a victory with Tennessee.
We've got winners and losers from today's contest as the Titans brace for a Week 5 matchup with the division-rival Houston Texans. Believe it or not, there are a couple of positive things to write home about. We won't start with those, however.
Ridley's sideline chuckles aren't doing him any favors right now. In the process of gradually losing touches to second-year WR Elic Ayomanor, Ridley once again had another dud of a day in this Titans offense.
With just one reception for 13 yards today (on just two targets), Ridley continues to fall behind in an offensive rotation that is likely to forget about him in the coming weeks. His fall from opening the season as a snap-heavy starter to being essentially being buried in just two weeks is almost surprising.
Except, when he disappears on the field like this, Titans fans just have to shrug. It wasn't a total loss on offense today, but Ridley's role is inarguably almost gone.
Look, I know Carnell Tate's fumble toward the end of the first half stripped the Titans of any momentum they had at that point. You can't let that happen.
But the rookie was by far and away the best player in this offense today. His 9 receptions led by the team by a country mile, translating to 145 yards and multiple big plays over the middle. It was simply a big day for Tate, turnover set aside.
Tennessee's offense has more questions to answer right now than ever. Tate, regarding his investment and future in Nashville, is not one of them.
This spot probably could've gone to either Ward or Daboll, but Daboll arguably cost the Titans this game with his egregious goal-line play-calling in the first half. Today was another uninspiring offensive showing from Tennessee, and that traces back in large part to the OC.
Generally, it was familiar look after familiar look. The Titans carried the ball - times, the bulk of which went to veteran RB Tony Pollard. Pollard again had a fine day, including a score of his own, but Daboll is treating the 29-year old like he's Derrick Henry in this offense.
Between treating a journeyman rusher like a workhorse and failing to ignite an offensive spark given multiple chances in the second half, the Titans' OC lands on the loser list today. Daboll has more to prove than anyone on Tennessee's sideline.
Our lone defensive name from today's game lands in the winner's circle. Jermaine Johnson was a veteran trade acquisition that Saleh previously coached in New York. He's been fair for the most part up to now, but Week 4 finally saw some worthwhile life out of the EDGE.
The main note from Johnson's showing today was him finally leveling a sack. On the whole, Johnson finished with four tackles (two of which went for a loss) and a generally promising showing on the defensive line.
If the Titans could get this kind of outing from their defensive veterans every game, we could be looking at a much different Titans team. A defeat is a defeat, but all Tennessee can do is shrug and accept a positive uptick from Johnson.

title: Titans' First Half vs. Ravens: 1 Poor Decision on Goal Line Tanks Tennessee's Chances
full_text:
At 24-7, the Tennessee Titans first half started promisingly and went quickly sour. Robert Saleh's 0-3 team is still in this game, but battles like these are decided in between the lines.
Tennessee has caused some disruption (credit to Jacob Martin, Marcus Harris, and Jermaine Johnson for two sacks) to give the offense chances to produce, and that Titans' offense looks a little better today - save for Carnell Tate's late-half fumble. That's another complaint for another day.
However, when push came to shove midway through the second quarter and the Titans had a chance to tie on the goal line, OC Brian Daboll decided to run with Tony Pollard five straight times. Small gain gave way to small gain, and Pollard ultimately came up short on fourth down.
Baltimore then got the ball on a turnover on downs, marched down the field, and scored on a touchdown pass to Mark Andrews. Everyone has been harping on the Titans' offense to take more risks heading into Week 4, and it's not that there's an issue with going for it on fourth down. But running the same guy up the gut over, and over, and over again... well, that's bound to result the way it did.
What could've been a 14-14 contest went the opposite direction in a matter of minutes. Daboll deserves the whole of the blame in this instance, and that one call could be the reason the Titans can't get out of a hole today.
Ravens defense holds strong at the goal line! TENvsBAL on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/2OnAvcVySy
Although, this outcome isn't necessarily surprising. It was a goal-line interception in the fourth quarter that lost the Titans last week's game against the New York Giants. Call it cold feet in the booth or hesitancy in the huddle, but in trying to play it safer in scoring position, Tennessee lost out entirely.
This isn't even an argument that the Titans should've thrown on fourth down. It is, however, an argument that the passing game should've been used at some point in those five plays to throw the defense off.
Setting aside Ward's fluke interception on the first drive of the game, his 135 first-half yards represents the highest mark through two quarters this season. Pollard's 13 carries for 38 yards and a score on the ground have helped define a bettered offense up to now.
But it's almost as if the Titans got too comfortable that something was finally working in the first half. Daboll leaned on it too heavily at the worst possible time, and Tennessee's odds reversed in the aftermath.
We've still got two quarters, but don't be surprised if this is a decision we're regretfully revisiting in the coming week if Tennessee comes up short.
